I had no idea this game existed until today (I totally misread the release date and thought it was new) but as a fan of both the IP and Metroidvania's, I decided to purchase based on the mostly positive reviews. The concept for the game is great, being a human attempting to survive Kaiju destruction is great and I'd like to see more games use it. The gameplay is where issues start to rear their head. The combat is awful, you'll be doing the same repetitive attack block combination nearly every encounter and occasionally trying to decide if its worth using some of your limited ammunition to speed things up. The story is very mediocre with some of the worst voice acting I've heard in a video game in recent memory. The puzzles and exploration are incredibly shallow and the "realistic platforming" can lead to accidentally taking damage pretty frequently.
So why do I recommend this game? While its incredibly mediocre there is some fun to have here if you want a breezy Metroidvania. You can complete the game in just a few hours and I think if you're a fan of the Monsterverse you'll get something out of it. The sequences where you need to evade Kong or the other monsters are the highlight, some returning characters from the movies were a nice touch, and the visuals are pretty nice to look at.
So this isn't really an enthused recommendation, but if you're looking for something simple to waste a few hours and are a fan of the Monsterverse or Kaiju in general, I think you'll enjoy this game.

This game excels at building atmosphere and showcasing the titans a real dangers to human life. It provides a more realistic and down to Earth view of the Monsterverse than are typically seen in the films. This, along with the lore details and connections to the films make this an excellent compliment to the film series. While the cinematic puzzle platformer game play is enjoyable, the game is unfortunately dragged down by some odd design decisions, especially later on. There will frequently be long and treacherous trial and error stretches with no checkpoints, forcing constant repetition. Checkpoints, health, and ammo pickups become very sparse in the late game, often forcing you to walk long distances to retry a combat encounter. Combat itself is repetitive and bland. Overall, this game is excellent for fans of the Monsterverse, and of the cinematic platformer genre, but should be avoided by a wider audience.

Essentially wants to be Alien Isolation with dinosaurs, which is a very cool concept. It's early access so its hard to tell yet if it'll achieve that goal. So far, it has its pros and its cons. The introduction level is nicely crafted, with some cool moments. The dinosaur designs for the limited species in the game so far are slick. Theres a toggle feathers option for both the Utahraptors and Compy's which is a nice touch. The T.rex and Allosaur arent really in the game yet, but the tease the intro level has with each of them is cinematic enough. Now for the not so good yet parts. Alien Isolation featured one of the most advanced and organic enemy Ai systems in gaming history. The Xenomorph felt like a living, unscripted ,breathing creature. Actively hunting you while learning your patterns and actions. Deathgrounds dinosaurs at present fall very short of that. The Utahraptors follow a scripted path around the areas you have to carry out your objectives. Repeating those same paths, unless disturbed. If you run and hide in a vent, they briefly hang around the area until they return to their scripted routes. While beautifully modeled, their current animations leave allot to be desired. They walk extremely stiffly and robotically, hardly feeling like a living creature. The Compy's are midly more interesting. They will hound you the second you try to hide or pass through vents and their animations are more lifelike. 
The game has a class system, which enables a team of friends to fill each role as they try to accomplish objectives on a selection of maps. The maps are nicely created, with clear aesthetic themes and variety. But the classes feel very much the same to play. The only real difference is loadout. 
There is a skeleton of a narrative behind the games setting and while its nothing very fresh in the dinosaur game genre, It does have potential.
At this point I hope the devs stick to it and continue to improve their product. This can definitely be a rad dinosaur game if given the continued love and work it needs to flourish. 
Rooting for it.

Ys I & II Chronicles+ — Review

Ys I & II Chronicles+ is where it all began — the foundation of everything that makes the Ys series so beloved today. These two games, remade and bundled together by Falcom, are old-school to the core: simple, fast, and full of heart. But even after all these years, they still have that special spark that newer action RPGs often miss — a pure sense of adventure.

This collection includes modernized versions of the original Ys I: Ancient Ys Vanished and Ys II: Ancient Ys Vanished – The Final Chapter, rebuilt with improved visuals, remastered music, and smoother controls. It’s the definitive way to experience the origins of Adol Christin’s legend.

Story and Setting

The story begins with Adol — a young, red-haired adventurer drawn by tales of a mysterious land called Esteria, cut off from the outside world by a supernatural storm. When he arrives, he’s swept into a quest involving ancient goddesses, lost civilizations, and a growing evil threatening to consume the land.

Ys I is a straightforward, almost mythic story — simple, heroic, and full of mystery. Ys II continues directly after, expanding the world into the floating land of Ys and deepening the lore behind the goddesses and their ancient power.

While the storytelling is minimal by modern standards, there’s a certain sincerity to it. The tone is adventurous and optimistic, and the pacing is tight — no long cutscenes, just quick dialogue, exploration, and action.

Gameplay

These games are famous (and a little infamous) for their “bump combat” system — you don’t press an attack button. Instead, you damage enemies by running into them off-center. It sounds strange, but it actually creates a rhythm — positioning and timing become key, and battles feel fast and snappy once you get used to it.

In Ys II, things open up even more. Adol gains magic abilities, allowing for ranged attacks and more strategic fights, which makes combat feel more dynamic and modern.

Both games are all about movement, speed, and risk. You rush through dungeons, make snap decisions in battle, and rely on quick reflexes. The design feels archaic but honest — every victory feels earned, especially during boss fights, which are surprisingly intense for such old-school mechanics.

The Chronicles+ version adds quality-of-life improvements: smoother movement, controller support, multiple difficulty settings, and selectable soundtracks (you can even use the classic PC-88 music if you’re nostalgic).

Presentation

The remastered visuals are charming — simple but colorful 2D sprites over detailed backdrops, with Falcom’s distinctive art style shining through. It’s not flashy, but it feels timeless in its simplicity.

The real star, though, is the soundtrack. Falcom’s Sound Team JDK delivers some of their most iconic tracks here — “Feena,” “First Step Towards Wars,” and “Palace of Destruction” are legendary. The remixed and orchestral versions add even more power and emotion, making the whole experience feel grand despite the small scale.

What I Liked

Classic, fast-paced gameplay that’s still surprisingly fun

Gorgeous, remastered soundtrack (one of the best in JRPG history)

Simple but heartfelt story and characters

Tight pacing — no filler, pure adventure

Great modern improvements in the Chronicles+ version

What I Didn’t Like

The bump combat can feel awkward at first

Some dungeons are maze-like and confusing

Old-school difficulty spikes, especially in Ys I

Storytelling is minimal compared to later entries

Final Thoughts

Ys I & II Chronicles+ isn’t just a nostalgia trip — it’s a look back at how a series built its soul. It’s fast, sincere, and full of energy. Even with its quirks and simplicity, it captures that feeling of stepping into an unknown land and pushing forward no matter what.

These games may be relics of the ‘80s, but in this remastered form, they still feel alive — carried by their brilliant music, brisk pace, and that timeless sense of adventure Falcom has always done best.

If you love Ys, this is essential history. If you’re new to the series, it’s a charming and surprisingly exciting place to start — just be patient with the bump combat for the first hour or two.

My Score: 8.5/10

Что ж... это безумно своеобразное произведение. Я прошёл его впервые ещё лет шесть назад, но с того момента забыл абсолютно всё, посему смог насладиться им как в первый раз.

1. Персонажи. Это, пожалуй, самое главное, что меня обычно интересует в хоть сколько-нибудь сюжетных играх. Здесь с ними очень сложно. Как минимум поначалу авторы пытаются представить каждого из них в очень напускном виде. Каждый до безумия «ultimate». Каждый очень склоняется в крайность и однобокость. Если персонажа показали глупеньким, он будет глупым глобально до последнего. Если персонаж излишне социальный, он будет абсолютно таким же тупым ослом от начала и до конца. Эта проблема всё так же душит общение с героями даже вне основного сюжета. Хочешь пообщаться с Селестией? Готовься, что из 5 раз она все разы будет говорить что-то про казик и удачу. Хочешь с Асахиной поболтать? Вы каждый раз будете говорить про спорт и плавать (за кадром, конечно же). Это касается всех кроме Киригири. В этой игре ты не ищешь наиболее интересных и приятных тебе персонажей среди многих прикольных персонажей, ты ищешь чуть меньший сорт кринжа среди навозной ямы. Но, пусть до этого всё и звучало критично, к этому привыкаешь, а глобальный сюжет форсит персонажей хоть сколько-нибудь казаться более приемлемыми.

[spoiler]Таким образом Саяка, казавшаяся миленькой девочкой, грубо предала Макото. Сакура, казавшаяся молчаливым огром, оказалась в целом рассудительной и по-хорошему эмоциональной. Селестия, пусть и кринжово мыслящая только о стереотипном в рамках неё мусоре, выказывала интересные мысли вроде той, что, может, им и не стоит покидать школу (лгала!), удивлялась безразличию Бьякуи несмотря на собственную хладнокровность. Чихиро захотел стать сильнее. Прикольно. Отдельно стоит упомянуть Киригири, на которую авторы очевидно делали большую ставку. Она наиболее привлекает внимание, кажется более всего рассудительной, но страшно напрягает тем, что совершенно не хочет доверять и раскрываться. Можно понять в таких условиях, но всё же тяжело. На фоне этого я буквально хлопать начал, когда она, малость смутившись, признала, что «maybe I overreacted a bit». Важно не забыть и про Монокуму, юмор которого вытягивает огромное количество диалогов. Слушать же Хифуми, Токо или ставшего гулём Таку — нереально в любой момент игры. Абсолютно отвратительно.[/spoiler]

2. Детектив и геймплей. Самое душное в них — необходимость по очереди ручками прокликивать каждую улику, каждую мелочь. Ещё, конечно, есть огромные претензии к тому, как выстроена временами логика правильных выстрелов в сражении аргументами. «Правильное» решение далеко не всегда было самым очевидным, а некоторые аргументы вполне могли массово подходить под много фраз и наоборот. Ещё из минусов.. мм.. иногда низкая вариативность. Рассказать ли [spoiler]Кёко о битве Сакуры с Монокумой?[/spoiler] «Ну да, расскажи», — выбираю я. «Не, не стоит обвинять, не подумав». Разрабы дали выбор, чтобы не дать выбор, чтобы я [spoiler]не доверился Кёко[/spoiler] и затем видел эти детские глупости.

В остальном же детективные истории здесь очень интересные. Да, некоторые улики приходится слишком разжёвывать по ходу «class trial», но в целом к каждой из глав есть большой интерес. Мотивы, цепочка событий, орудие, время — всё это мы узнаём и каждый раз в этом есть интерес. Новые локации, новые взаимодействия персонажей, раскрытие глубины хотя бы некоторых из них. Если бы некоторые из них не были тупыми дебилами, которые бросаются словами, не думая головой, было бы вообще прекрасно. Ещё с точки зрения геймплея прикольно, что в рамках игры можно передвигаться по школе. Необычно для такого жанра.

3. Атмосфера. Авторы всё время сталкивают «hope» и «despair», и я бы докопался до этой софистики (особенно в финале), но с каждым «class trial» этот самый «despair» чувствуется всё сильнее и сильнее. Приближение к разгадке никоим образом не наполняет школу радостью, напротив — чем ближе разгадка, тем меньше живых персонажей. Коридоры пустеют, подарки давать некому. Персонажи, дававшие смысл заходить в игру, буквально умирают. Это очень своеобразно, наполняет одновременно и интересом, и ощущением пустоты, словно реально кого-то потерял. Атмосферность этой игре не занимать, с этим тут всё сильно.

Это хороший детективчик, в который вписали безумно экстравагантных персонажей. Иногда это плюс, но чаще — огромный минус. Лишь по ходу истории к некоторым персонажам взгляд теплеет, но другие же остаются такими же занозчивыми, бесячими и однобокими. Глобальный сюжет про школу отчаяния порадовал, детективные истории тоже, Кёко — легенда, атмосферность неплохая. Но можно было сильно лучше, сделав персонажей адекватнее. Впрочем, возможно, это визитная карточка всей серии Ронпы.

Out of all the classic style FPSes, This is one of them. Ridiculous, outrageous, and punishing.

When you find a Secret in any other FPS game, you're usually treated to a nice little boost of health, maybe a new gun or a power up, or maybe just ammo.

In Serious Sam, the secret is +1 armor and when you pick it up the game grabs you by the lapels and screams "HOW DARE YOU" in your face and demands you explain yourself to the 410,757,864,530 Kleer skeletons that just spawned in the bathroom stall sized room you're in.

Secret levels are the same way. You'll walk in from the last level shoving your appendix back inside your gut, get full health and ammo, and leave clutching your appendix yet again after getting mauled by harpies and Swiss cheesed by mechanoids, all while trying to shoot Kamikazes and avoid entire family reunion of Gnaars. 

Playing Serious Sam is like headbutting trees: Its fun, but you're going to get a traumatic brain injury if you do it too much. 

Take breaks and drink plenty of water. Give your mom a call and ask her about her day after you've died to the same area for the 30th time in the past hour. Take a walk and listen to the birds and take in some nature.

I rate it "Cock and Ball Torture: The Game"/10

An excellent adventure game that looks like a collection of vague, unrelated episodes… until it’s not. Very creative presentation, mixing approaches from different gaming eras (text-based, point and click, moving in 3D), an analogue devices’ aesthetic and strategically limited camera angles to create suspense and immersion. The core twist is very traditional, but it’s less about the twist itself and more about how smartly it ties seemingly disjointed elements into a tight experience where the puzzles don’t just align with the story, they [i]are[/i] the story.

Granted, it asks for at least some familiarity with or patience towards more old-school gameplay mechanics that can trip you up on technicalities (getting a text command’s wording slightly wrong, missing a tiny interactable object, this sort of stuff). However, even if you don’t have any, using a guide is a perfectly valid option too, since it’s all about the story, not solving puzzles (one might even say they aren’t really puzzles but simply instructions to follow, which is also fully justified on the narrative level).

Overall, this is probably among the most memorable 2-3-hour games I’ve played, and I would highly recommend it to anyone interested in the art of interactive storytelling. It even single-handedly reminded me why I like psychological horror, although it’s not aiming to be particularly unsettling or scary, but it does feature some really well-directed, atmospheric scenes.

Little Friends: Puppy Island is a wholesome and lighthearted experience that captures the simple joy of companionship, discovery, and care in a bright, tropical setting. Developed by Big Blue Bubble and published by Fireshine Games, it presents itself as a cheerful blend of pet simulator, exploration game, and resort management adventure. The premise is straightforward yet charming—you arrive on a sunny island paradise filled with puppies waiting to be cared for, trained, and loved. What follows is a gentle, feel-good journey through lush environments as you explore, build, and nurture your growing group of furry friends. It’s a game that values warmth over intensity, designed not to challenge the player but to soothe them, much like the relaxing presence of the puppies it celebrates.

The gameplay unfolds across a series of interconnected systems that revolve around exploring the island, adopting puppies, and building facilities to support your canine community. The island itself is large and inviting, featuring several distinct biomes such as sandy beaches, flower-filled meadows, snowy peaks, and even tranquil forests. Each area offers opportunities to discover new puppy breeds, hidden treasures, and activity zones. You spend your time walking your puppies through trails, teaching them tricks, feeding, bathing, and dressing them in a wide variety of accessories. The more you interact with them, the stronger your bond becomes, and that connection translates into in-game progression—well-trained and happy puppies unlock new locations and items. There’s a sense of steady, incremental growth that keeps the experience engaging without ever feeling demanding, perfectly suited to its casual tone.

What gives Little Friends: Puppy Island its heart is the attention to detail in its presentation. The puppies are expressive and endearing, each breed rendered with care and personality. Their animations—tail wags, playful hops, and sleepy stretches—help make them feel alive rather than just digital companions. With more than a hundred possible variations across different breeds and over three hundred accessories to collect, customization becomes a key part of the fun. You can mix and match outfits, collars, and toys, creating an experience that’s as much about creativity as it is about care. The environments are equally vibrant, bursting with color and texture, from shimmering water under the sun to cherry blossom groves that sway gently in the breeze. The game’s visual design radiates optimism and warmth, inviting players of all ages to step into its world and unwind.

Complementing the visuals is the game’s laid-back tone, supported by calming sound design and a soft, upbeat soundtrack. The ambient sounds of nature—the chirping of birds, the rustle of leaves, and the distant crash of waves—help create a soothing rhythm that defines the experience. It’s the kind of game that doesn’t rush you or punish mistakes. There are no timers, no failures, and no pressure to optimize performance. Instead, it encourages you to take your time and enjoy the process of caring for your puppies and expanding your resort. This focus on relaxation makes it particularly appealing as a comfort game, the sort you can play after a long day simply to unwind and smile at your adorable virtual pets.

However, for all its charm, Little Friends: Puppy Island does have limitations that come with its gentle design philosophy. Its simplicity, while appealing to a casual audience, may leave players seeking deeper mechanics feeling unsatisfied. The gameplay loop is repetitive by nature—explore, care, decorate, repeat—and while the addition of new areas and puppies adds variety, the core structure remains largely unchanged throughout. The minigames, such as agility training and jumping challenges, provide brief diversions but don’t evolve much beyond their initial introduction. Some of these mechanics, particularly the controls in certain activities, can feel awkward or imprecise, occasionally interrupting the flow of an otherwise smooth experience. For younger players or those looking for something purely cozy, these issues are minor, but for seasoned simulation fans, the game’s lack of depth might stand out.

Despite its simplicity, there’s an undeniable sincerity to Little Friends: Puppy Island that makes it easy to appreciate. Its sense of joy feels unforced, and its world is crafted with genuine affection for its subject matter. The progression system, while light, provides a satisfying loop of rewards as you unlock new toys, decorations, and areas to explore. Building your resort adds a layer of long-term satisfaction—watching it evolve from a small cluster of huts into a thriving puppy paradise mirrors the nurturing spirit that defines the entire experience. The developers clearly understand their target audience, creating a game that prioritizes emotional comfort and accessibility over complexity or challenge. It’s a digital retreat for animal lovers, one that offers smiles and tranquility instead of tension and stakes.

Ultimately, Little Friends: Puppy Island succeeds in being exactly what it sets out to be—a cozy, relaxing, and irresistibly cute simulation about spending time with dogs in an idyllic setting. It doesn’t attempt to push boundaries or redefine the genre; instead, it perfects a niche experience focused on companionship and care. While it may not hold the attention of players craving intricate systems or fast-paced gameplay, it more than satisfies those looking for something wholesome and therapeutic. It’s a game meant to be savored at a leisurely pace, a reminder that sometimes joy can be found not in conquest or challenge, but in simple moments—feeding, walking, and playing with a puppy as the sun sets over a beautiful island built just for them.

Rating: 9/10

Penumbra: Overture isn’t just the beginning of a series, it’s the moment Frictional Games found their identity. Long before Amnesia redefined horror, Overture laid the groundwork: a first person survival experience built on physics-driven puzzles, oppressive isolation and a constant sense of dread that seeps under your skin rather than jumping at your face.

The story begins with Philip, a man drawn by his late father’s mysterious letter to an abandoned mine in the arctic. What follows is less a rescue mission and more a descent into madness; a journey through dark tunnels, flickering lights and the heavy silence of something not quite human watching from the shadows. The sense of place is extraordinary: claustrophobic, cold and uncomfortably real.

Mechanically, Penumbra: Overture still feels ambitious for its time. The physics-based interaction (pulling drawers, turning valves, swinging melee weapons) gives everything a tactile authenticity. You don’t just see the world; you handle it. Yet, those same mechanics can be clumsy, especially during combat, which remains the weakest link. Fighting feels awkward and unnecessary, often breaking the tension instead of deepening it. Thankfully, later entries learned from this and leaned fully into helplessness.

The atmosphere, however, remains unmatched. The minimal soundtrack, immersive sound design and scattered notes of environmental storytelling create a horror that feels earned rather than manufactured. It’s the kind of fear that comes from anticipation, not shock.

While its age shows in the visuals and some janky controls, Penumbra: Overture still holds up as a masterclass in mood and restraint. It’s intelligent, immersive and unsettling in all the right ways; a crucial piece of horror gaming history that rewards patience with genuine unease.

Because of this, I think a lot of people got turned off from it (thinking it's just a cutesy simple platformer), or started playing it and were let down. 之所以开坑《血龙》也是想着补完3代的成就顺手把这个外传资料片也给做一下，超乎想象的简单！花了两天晚上的时间成功完结撒花

《血龙》在整体上将3代的很多系统都予以简化，玩起来节奏很快，将武器配件装备上手后更是直接成为爽游，升到30级血条更是长到敌人的攻击像是在挠痒痒

视觉风格有点像五代的外传《新曙光》，《血龙》是整体的暗红色调，《新曙光》则是整体的粉红色，视觉疲劳感严重，幸亏流程短。而世界设定则有点像《荒野大嫖客》的亡灵DLC，在整体内容基本照搬本作的同时，本体的动物也进行了亡灵化，还是挺有趣的

《血龙》的节奏快还有一个很重要的原因是主角REX的性能强的可怕，不论是奔跑还是游泳速度简直不比驾驶载具慢多少，这使得我在整个流程都没有开过几次车和船，做任务全凭腿。而且REX没有掉落伤害，在探索特别是收集收藏品时非常方便

《血龙》的风格应该算是历代最诙谐的一个，REX从教程开始就明显的很暴躁，直接巴拉巴拉的开始骂起教程别说了快让他去杀人，玩家操控去收集也是吐槽个不停说怎么让他干这种事，唯一开心的时候就是去杀人了，不过嘴巴也是很难安静

总体来说《血龙》算是相当有特色的资料片，特别是“远哭”在3代之后基本游戏体验换汤不换药，像《血龙》这样的异类在这个系列中显得更加难得，细细想来，自3代后也只有《血龙》和《原始杀戮》有些新意了

成就难度很低，只不过为了打的快点免得通关后还要到处找的折磨，建议在流程中就可以注意着遇到血龙就打，尽快完成杀死25只的成就。人类敌人则多多爆头，特别是在“杀星试炼”中的三种敌人一定要爆头，通关后找不到。同样的，打5个血龙的口罩最好在用火焰喷射器烧血龙蛋任务时完成，这个任务正好有5个戴口罩的血龙，这个时候不做在大地图很难找得到。钱要多存，平时多摸尸、多开箱子，尽量不在商店买除了地图、配件以外的东西，全武器配件需要用到的钱还是蛮紧张的

搞砸一個平庸的遊戲，比徹底的糞作還致命。這是我對「紙人」的最後感想。

一開始其實是有好感的，畫面跟氣氛都營造得不錯，懸念也有，偶爾的突臉驚嚇也挺有感覺，加上遊戲本身運作還算流暢，所以剛開始的半小時是有期待感的，然而之後問題就開始浮現出來。

在開始直播之前，我有先在steam看一些負評作為參考，大致有兩點：解謎過於散裝、主角跑兩步就會喘。

實際體驗之後，確實有這兩個缺點，但是如果把整個遊戲設計考慮進去，這兩點其實不算是缺點。

首先是謎題過於散裝導致難以推理。這個遊戲一開始能走的範圍就滿大的，解開前廳謎題之後基本上能走通三分之一的地圖，然後就是各種收集物品跟碰壁，不過實際解謎之後，會發現難歸難，但是邏輯都說得通，沒有硬凹的成份，所以與其說謎題太難，不如說是設計思路相當復古。

早期在PS1時代，甚至是WIN95時代的解謎冒險遊戲，通常是這樣的設計，一個謎題相當於一個關卡，現場幾乎沒有提示，而是經過收集資料跟道具來解謎，所以本作解謎的設計並沒有多糟糕，只是比較老派。

至於最多人負評的走路速度，這確實無話可說。我自己體驗了一下，主角的奔跑距離大概只有三公尺，持續時間大約一秒，奔跑後的CD時間超過十秒，這確實是很首創了，以前只看過跑得慢的，沒看過跑得短的，雖然一開始的劇情演出有暗示主角的右膝蓋受傷，但這其實沒什麼說服力，單純就是故意搞人而已。

但即使如此，實際遊玩下來也不算是非常大的缺陷，因為本作的怪物們走得一樣慢，而且完全不會跑步，所以還能快跑一秒的主角其實已經很有速度優勢了。

不過從這裡開始，就延伸出一些更糟糕的問題。上面也說過，主角的移動緩慢是刻意設計的缺陷，他的目的其實是希望玩家能躲藏而不是逃跑或是走位，讀取畫面的Tips也一直強調這點，但是我在遊玩的時候最常死掉的狀況，就是怪物會突然刷在你附近，然後那個地方沒有辦法躲藏，例如死巷，或是沒有藏匿處的房間，加上本作沒有生命值的設計，被巡邏怪抓到就是即死，突出一個倒楣。

遊戲本身沒有自動存檔，只能依靠全地圖唯一的安全屋兼存檔點手動存檔，因為地圖不大，所以也不算太麻煩，但是在遊戲尾聲的時候卻變成一個令人生厭的缺陷。

結尾的高潮有兩段：限時封印戰、最後的逃亡。

遊戲在中期會出現一個封印系統，玩家可以藉由收集情報跟道具，把怪物的本體封印起來，這樣怪物就會消失，這個設計其實很有趣，但是在最後的限時封印戰就變得糟糕透頂。

在這場封印戰中，該怪物的本體會出現三個分身（沒有說明為什麼，突然出現的設定），玩家必須把三個分身都封印之後才能封印本體，然而封印的途中怪物會出現並摧毀封印，所以玩家必須搶在怪物之前完成三個分身封印，然後再封印本體。

這個設計本身沒問題，別的遊戲也做過，問題是這個設計不適合本作的機制。

主角本身的移動就很有問題，而怪物的速度跟主角差不多，整個封印場地也不大，中間還有張桌子擋路，所以怪物走來走去的時候，玩家只能繞一大圈躲避，不可能用走位擦身而過，這樣也導致雙方的速度差距非常非常短。

除了移動速度緩慢，封印的機制也很繁瑣：要先點擊分身（而且要靠很近，這遊戲無論調查什麼都要靠很近，連開門都是臉撞的）， 選取道具欄中的封印道具並選擇使用，然後4次QTE才能算是完成封印。

這樣的機制在封印其他的怪物時並沒有問題，因為只要封印一次，而且沒有被摧毀的問題，然而在這裡突然就來了個封印3+1和趕時間的警察抓小偷，這玩下來不是刺激，只是煩。

最後的逃亡原本是沒什麼問題的，但是前面也說過，主角只能跑一秒，而怪物是全方位衝出來擋路的，所以逃脫容錯率極低，而讓整個體驗雪上加霜的，就是前面提到的存檔。

本遊戲沒有自動存檔功能，全部都要手動，而存檔點只有一個，也就是說，每次的逃亡失敗，都要從存檔點走回觸發最後劇情的地方，那段路有點距離不說，還會有一段演出跟最後一次封印儀式，每次重來大約要花將近兩分半鐘走路跟看演出，這一段完全沒有必要，因為最後的逃脫很難，玩家只會想要趕快重試，而不是重複看那段沒什麼意義的演出，因此沒有自動存檔這點就變得很糟糕。

不過存檔這點其實也很復古，但不是老遊戲的什麼要素都值得學，以前那樣的體驗就不好了，照搬有什麼意義呢？

故事方面的表現也不盡人意，整個遊戲完全沒有故事可言，糊里糊塗的就來到這裡，然後東西拿著就開始解謎，每個鬼出來就是要殺你，被封印之後就說幾句類似「我好恨呀」的台詞後就沒了，唯一算得上能說明劇情的，只有某人的日記，那日記還是碎成一段一段的，本作的調查功能又很不方便，我全破了也沒找齊那些日記。

但說真的，即使全找到了也不會提昇劇情體驗，一款講故事的遊戲如果全靠收集資料來推劇情，那至少在說故事這方面是絕對失敗的。

如果是個純粹的鬼屋型恐怖娛樂就算了，但是這遊戲確實想講一個懸疑故事，因為這個遊戲的背景是建立在一個錯綜複雜的宅鬥關係，而且還以章節的方式出續作，說明「故事」在遊戲內容的佔比是偏高的，其中也有些東西可以考據，例如服裝、資料、擺設等等。

「想知道故事的話就去玩續作吧！一切都會在那裡揭曉！」by某網站攻略。

抱歉啊，完全沒興趣。

很多以章節為名的系列遊戲，之所以會讓人期待後續劇情、考據彩蛋，是因為它的表劇情有精彩的演出，還有讓玩家當下就能理解的故事，要先有吸引人的現在，才會讓人期待未來、探索過去。而本作什麼都沒有，除了解謎走路找鑰匙之外，什麼故事都沒體驗到，遊戲製作方不能要求玩家自主當考據黨，我們買遊戲是來玩的，不是來考試的。

當逃亡結束，結尾畫面唐突出現的時候，失望的程度到達谷底，原本還能接受的地方全都無法接受了，這遊戲處處偷著一種「欸，咱們這設計是不是挺屌的啊w」的莫名自豪感，尤其結尾演出的節奏感，完全就是隨便弄，最後再來個讓人更搞不懂狀況的預告片，要你期待續作。

那瞬間我覺得這一切都毫無意義，完全在浪費時間。

它原本只是個普通的作品，有點缺點，但是優點也不錯，不好不壞，至少75分以上，然後在最後的最後變成了一個50分不到的電子垃圾。

把平庸的作品搞砸，比徹底的糞作還糟糕，因為你本來擁有期望，它卻背叛了你，還嘲笑你的愚蠢。

總評：50分以下，徒有外表的劣作，不推薦，但是可以送給仇人玩。

P.S：看了續作的評價，本作所有的缺點在續作都有，也就是說這不是技術問題，他們是真的覺得這樣設計很好玩。

Разрабы предлагают стать боссом мафии, торговать запрещенкой, увеличивать влияние и карать конкурентов. Я в свою очередь предлагаю разобраться, получилось ли у разработчиков воплотить свою идею в интересный геймплей.

Сама игра начинается с того, что вам дают клочок земли в городе, на котором расположен перевалочный пункт, склад и магазинчик, который вы крышуете. Открываем своё первое предприятие по варке алкоголя, налаживаем поставки сырья до самогонного аппарата и доставку готового продукта до ближайших ларьков, где его будут впаривать местным жителям, - и получаем свои нечестно заработанные копейки. Весь процесс пошаговый, у каждого вашего подручного есть какое-то количество действий на карте. Самих подручных мы берем в семью по своему выбору, их нам предлагает, например, тот самый продавец, которому мы продали самогонку (скорее всего, его сын или дочь). И чтобы не запариваться каждый ход над передвижением каждой шестерки, в игре присутствует автоматизация - так и получается расширение семьи: взял типа, назначил ему работу, и он спокойно сам возит, что тебе надо, и куда надо.

Ну, а босс в это время занимается более серьёзными делами - открывает новые кварталы с магазинами, зарабатывает уважение жителей, чтобы те его боялись и отдавали свои денежки за крышевание. Получается некий менеджмент ресурсов: ну построил ты своих предприятий, варишь запрещенку и зарабатываешь валюту, и что? А то, что параллельно всё то же самое делают несколько ваших конкурентов-боссов, раскиданных по карте (а она, скажем так, не маленькая), - неумело управляемых искусственным интеллектом.

Сам процесс борьбы с неприятелем выглядит очень непродуманно и неинтересно - отправляешь одного или группу своих ребят с оружием на клетку, где в данный момент находится онный и нажимаешь атаковать. Все. После просчета процентов кто-то получает урон — количество зависит от оружия в руках вашего или его бандита. Если убил - забираешь дроп и везешь домой. Не повезло в этот раз — ничего страшного, едешь в ближайший перевалочный пункт, хилишься и повторяешь. Таким образом можно уничтожить любую группировку на карте, использовав всего только одного прислужника.

Кроме врагов-боссов, тут есть препятствия - полиция, которая, чисто по-сопрано, подкупается: катаются по району, если сталкиваются с твоими ребятами, с определённым шансом устроят проверку и заберут всё запрещенное. Весь процесс, честное слово, становится скучным и однообразным, когда начинаешь понимать, что тратить деньги можно только на очередной ресторанчик, в котором варят уже не самогон, а, например, шнапс, - ну и что? Расширение территории - пустая трата времени, просто ради визуала, чтобы вся карта стала цвета твоей фракции. То бишь, сделать интересный геймплей не очень получилось, но очень хотелось. Откуда у меня 30+ часов в этой игре? Я вжился в роль и для поддержания интереса сам не брезговал запрещенкой.

И вот тут я перейду к главной претензии — к этому жадному разрабу, который поставил цену за игру в 1кР+, при этом нагружая её кучей платных DLC, которые, судя по всему, и должны как раз добавить геймплея. Почему ты так жаден? Сделай эти DLC как обновление! Пусть мы, геймеры, с кайфом поиграем в менеджмент ресурсов, оставим тебе положительные отзывы, позовём ещё больше игроков - и всё будет по-честному.

This is a super unique game that works as both a store management sim and a dating sim. While it can be difficult to efficiently generate profit and the highest quality potions without external tools and/or lots of notetaking, there are many positives that make the game super fun [i](and relatively simple)[/i] to 100%.

[h1]Positives[/h1]
[b]Story & VA:[/b] If there's one thing this game does better than anything on the market, its writing. Every character has their own unique and fun story, with awesome references and fun little events, and the voice acting for each character is incredible. Each chance you have to pull yourself out of the game and just learn more about each character and why they act the way they do is just so fun. The story alone makes this game worth it.

[b]Variety of Strategies:[/b] Success in this game could be anything if you can figure out a way to make it work. You can set up a strong deck and haggle your way up, you can rush to the next tier of potions and never haggle in your life. You can use advertising or enhancements or bonuses from shelves or ageing to squeeze all the value you can out of your potions. 

[h1]Negatives[/h1]
[b]Too Complex:[/b] While the story can be relaxing and enjoyed in small parts, it feels like to succeed in potion making to the best of your abilities you need to run a C++ algorithm in time O(n^3*m) or have 400 pages of notes. 

With no ability to create potions again with the same ingredients, it feels like you need to spend forever noting what potions are the best you can and/or using some program to optimize what you can make. Without some kind of way to track potions, progress feels exponentially slower and it feels much harder to keep track of different things in the game.

My own experience:
[spoiler]I barely got through week 2 before setting up the potionomics ingredient optimizer to just organize what I could make. While it took some of the creativity and experimentation out of the game, it made the game feel more casual and fit better with the story.[/spoiler]


[b]Balancing:[/b] I feel like the devs were so creative and added so many features but struggled to keep everything balanced in the end. [url=https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/%3Fid%3D2879007152&ved=2ahUKEwjRo-bE586QAxVuEjQIHYpCOIYQFnoECBkQAQ&usg=AOvVaw3dJV2lfsYoSm1aRgfLbBkI]Infinite decks[/url] are too overpowered, some shops are too expensive for little reward, sending heroes on missions is so expensive for the same gain that some money can get you from Babtiste. 


If you are willing and able to overlook some balancing/overcomplication, or really enjoy an in-depth potionmaking system that rewards experimentation and the creation of so so so many potions, this game has an unbelievably good story and was clearly developed with so much heart and care. Would recommend.

As a big fan of the first two games, I was really looking forward to Origins.
So far, the first three and a half chapters were rather disappointing. The game feels lifeless and doesn't recapture the atmosphere of the originals at all.
There are very few hotspots to inspect and NPCs to talk with and some screens are just empty filler with nothing going on. The puzzles were ok so far. Nothing outstanding, but also not completely awful. They have that thing going on where NPCs have to give you a hint, before you can advance a puzzle despite having all the necessary items and player knowledge already (similar to Pendulo Studios' Runaway from 2003). This is especially annoying since the solutions are extremely obvious and telegraphed from a mile away.

The music is very bland and forgettable and the "PONY" DLC, which let's you switch the music to Simon 1 tracks, just hammers this point home. 特别神奇，这或许不是一部关于遗产的游戏，而是一部关于遗产如何终将散去的游戏。它不讲第三世界的秩序，而是在讲秩序的无声失效，它们被自己的故事背叛，被自己曾试图解释和治理的土地温柔地拒绝。教授代表的科学、神父代表的宗教、军阀代表的世俗，这三种古老权力在游戏中都像被雨水泡软的木桩，松散、发霉，毫无立足之地。世界革命的试验最终还是遭遇了民族的边界。长镜头移得漂亮，偷藏着穷人的宝贝、赃物和所剩无几的秘密、偷藏着一场只说了一句“再见”的爱情、偷藏着没来由的抒情、偷藏着更多的轮回和无常。旅途的前进其实是文明的后退，是一种缓慢而持续的陷落，陷入荒诞、陷入他人未竟的记忆、陷入一个与你文明逻辑毫不相干的世界。而水翼船在沼泽地彻底毁灭，就像一个人把剩余的世界还回给了泥土，所有文明的象征被义无反顾的瓦解，那一刻，旅途结束。理解开始。在这样的语境下，我们有必要重提雨林的意义。无论是阿彼察邦还是探险家的记忆传承，他们塑造的雨林都不是单纯的风景，而是一个迟缓、湿润、几近停滞的自然空间，那种介于生命与腐朽之间的热带湿气，穿过森林、穿过肉身、穿过梦境，化作永恒的病症。所以我们仔细一看，发现这又是关于记忆的故事，谈论的是身体与心灵的问题。难怪这里同样没有悲伤，好像悲伤只属于自以为能逃离自然秩序的人。在这样的语境下，拉美成为一种精神上的远方，一个永远被殖民、被遗忘、被浪漫化的地方，又因为这种反复而成为最能承载记忆的场所。法国作家尤其明白这一点。让冒险发生在拉美，就是让故事进入某种关于幻觉、瘴气、神话和政治历史之间的灰色地带。当然也有遗憾。像是它从一个宏大、深邃、带着历史重量的入口进入，但它选择从美学化的赎罪幻想中浮出。它承袭了整个 20 世纪末的欧洲探险叙事传统，却并未触碰其中真正的阴影。但我也足够。不嫌长不嫌重复。话还可以再少一点，比如神庙的军阀和教堂的神父两段。记忆的传承。集体的散文。有没有这样注视过一位老人、一只鸟、一棵树、一块木炭？生命的起伏、沟坎和轮回，一切存在的美，才得以被看见。

Syberia has always held a special place in my heart — it’s the series that made me fall in love with puzzle adventures. Funny enough, I only realized Amerzone was a completely separate game from 1999 after trying this remake demo. I honestly thought it was just part of Syberia’s lore, but it’s actually its own story set in the same universe.
The story is simple and quite predictable if you’ve played other Benoît Sokal games. Puzzles are mostly item-based and straightforward, but I liked the mini investigative element — collecting objects that tie into articles and notes about the world and its characters. That part kept me engaged, as I enjoy uncovering lore through documents and letters. The atmosphere of exploration and discovery gave me real nostalgia, and the world details are as rich as ever.
It’s a slow and meditative experience — in a good way — and I’m glad the remake lets you skip the long travel scenes. Still, some interactions feel overly complicated (like having to zoom in, select the key, insert it, and turn it just to open a chest).
[b]For me, it’s around a 7.1/10. Recommended for fans of slow-paced adventures and everyone who loves Benoît Sokal’s worlds.[/b]

Probably one of the least frightening (I would say not at all) games I have ever played. First, the gameplay itself is slow and shallow, like, what do you mean this is a game about creatures that can only hear you and you can't throw something to get there attention? Only hold your breath with both hands like a toddler. Second, the atmosphere is generic lovecraftian; really the basic b of lovecraftian horror settings. Third, the story is meh. Everything is pretty much disseminated to you through the dull broken up monologues of the manual save points. Which brings me to my final point, this game is a shining example as to why manual saves were phased out a long time ago. It is bad form to have such long gaps between save points and traps that kill you if you haven't sequenced the zone in a certain way.

Repetition is the antithesis to horror, the more the player is forced to do the same action over and over, the less novelty in each experience and less uncertainty in every step. For instance, having about 4-5 of the same enemy in every zone does not add tension when they are brain dead easy to walk by while holding your breath. This game is a decent idea produced in poor form.

Firstly, this might be a "me" problem, but the settings misbehave all the time. Sprint toggling will set itself to whatever the game feels like, and mashing the settings button and restarting doesn't work. Motion blur, V-Sync and FPS cap also don't give a F about what you choose in the settings. Since the game is very dark and refuses to give you a lantern or such, the ghosting and blurring forced me to constantly stop and check for what i thought was movement (it was never enemies, tho, just graphics misbehaving).

Game-wise, unfortunately the game breaks immersion constantly. The primary enemies are blind and react to sound. Your communication with the questgiver, on the other hand, is done by an ancient telephone line, and the thing rings VERY LOUDLY, but enemies will ignore that in favor of minor gasps and laboured breathing from the protagonist. 

Bruh, really? You don't hear the loud telephone, but you hear me breathe from 10 meters away? C'mon.

Did I say those dudes were blind? Actually they're blind-ISH. They don't see you alright, but if you stumble upon one and they bonk you in the head, suddenly they lock onto you and will chase you like a normal, unblindfolded man, navigate doors and corridors and mazes of stairs, SPRINTING after you.

Unfortunately they're also not scary. Theyre just dudes patroling. They have a habit of standing idly blocking your path, so it all quickly becomes a borefest of counting how much time till thise 3 idiots slowly step out from the doorway you have to go into.

There's a very questionable design choice, where the save points are gramophones that act like audio files that advance the plot and lore. This is a period piece, so you can't feed the audio into your in ear comms. So you save the game then stand around doing nothing for 1 or 2 minutes while you wait for the audio to play out. It's not a cutscene, so I suppose you can say F it, and exit the save room while the audio slowly fades behind you.

This is a reluctant recommendation. It's a good city-builder, with a decent number of systems, but it also has some significant flaws.

The main thing that's different is that you're building your village on the back of a giant 6-legged beast, which is constantly moving forward if it's not sleeping or eating. This means the climate changes constantly, though you'll spend several days in any given biome.

There are various ruins and places of interest along the way, and once you unlock scavenger teams, you can send them out to pick up various items. This is a significant part of play, since you can't make a lot of the items you find until the late game, and the plot requires that you visit specific sites.

It has a morale system, which is mostly driven by housing quality, food quality, and food variety. This is mostly about recruitment, since you won't get periodic population bumps if your morale is too low. Drop below a lower threshold, and villagers start leaving. The higher your population, the higher the morale requirements.

It has some simple production chains, such as wood -> planks, stone -> stone slabs, and iron ore -> iron ingots -> tools.

The main negative is that it has a LOT of micromanagement. This is largely driven by the central mechanic of changing climate zones. Every time you change zones, you have to change what your farms are producing to match the climate, and change what food your kitchens are cooking.

In some zones, you have to enable or disable buildings, or some of your villagers will be doing nothing. Fisheries only work in the water, so  you enable those as you enter a water zone, and turn them off as you leave.

There's also a need to frequently fiddle with what some buildings are doing. Mostly this is about running short of one item or another, or wanting to reserve some items for other uses. You're also constantly moving your wood and stone gathering camps. Few aspects of your village are ever stable.

There's a lot of sitting around and waiting, which can be dull, even with the game set to 4x speed.

Building space on the back of the beast is very cramped by the end game, which is irritating. There are some end-game monuments which are impractical to build because you simply cannot spare the real estate.

It has a plot, and an ending. The gist of the plot is OK, but the details are sometimes pretty stupid. A major part of the plot is collecting special "seeds" (which aren't really seeds), and most of the people you encounter  when looking for the seeds are ridiculous in some way or another. Like the guy with birds nesting in his hat. That, and the frequently have silly demands before they'll help you save the world, like finding them a tomato.

It's pretty decent despite the flaws, and it took me about 26 hours to finish. If you're into city builders at all, you'll probably enjoy it.

Code Vein turned out to be a fun and interesting soulslike. I had my eye on it for a long time but never really got around to playing it. Now that I finally did, I had a good time with it.

[h3]What I liked[/h3]

[b]Character editor[/b]
My huge respect. So many options, details and ways to customize your character. You can easily spend hours in it, and that's what I did.

[b]Controls[/b]
Feel responsive and comfortable. They are a bit overloaded with functions, but everything works nicely once you get used to it. Keybinds are customizable, and comfortable for keyboard players. The only annoying thing is having to scroll through consumables manually.

[b]Locations[/b]
They are great both visually and in terms of structure. They feel well thought out and atmospheric.

[b]Bosses[/b]
I played through all bosses solo, without a partner, and it was fun. Learning their attacks and beating them fair and square was super satisfying.

[b]Music[/b]
Really nice. Some tracks are incredibly beautiful and fit the game perfectly.

[h3]What I did not like that much[/h3]

[b]Bugs and technical issues[/b]
Even years after release, the game feels underpolished. I ran into a lot of hitbox problems where attacks just pass through enemies. The target lock can break randomly and send your character swinging in the wrong direction. Also, I had some issues with elevators.

[b]Too many cutscenes[/b]
Some of them feel slow and boring. The characters often say really cliche things. If you have watched at least a couple of teen anime, you have definitely heard it all before.

[b]Enemy variety[/b]
Pretty limited. In the second half of the game they start repeating constantly, and the later areas don't introduce any new enemies at all.

[h3]Final thoughts[/h3]

Overall, the game is good. But it has its flaws. I would rate the game 7 out of 10. I hope the sequel will be even better!

This game alone comes with a lot of the expansions. If you are down to play this game by yourself OR you want to play on say a Steam deck/Tablet with another friend or two while you hang out. Then it is still a great buy. If you are playing on PC and want to play with a few friends. There are issues that are pretty glaring. 

Going to explain Offline mode first. Offline, you can set up how much honor you are playing for, how many AI bots there are, expansions used, and AI difficulty. In Offline mode you could just play solo and just play a good game against 1-3 other AI. This mode DOES allow you to play with 1-3 other humans. However this requires that everyone have access to the one screen. So as stated before you could hand around a tablet so each person can play their turn. On a PC this makes no sense and would be silly. THERE IS NO REMOTE PLAY just before you ask ;)

Multiplayer online is available. You make a quick account through I think Playdek, confirm through email. Good to go. When you go to set up the game in this mode. Instead of changing the Honor Pool amount. It gives you a "timer". This essentially makes it so the other players have 30 minutes - crazy amount of time to play their turns. It is like chess and when your turn is over, the timer stops. Very strange. But if you and your friends jump through the hoops and get into a game finally. The honor pool is VERY low. And you can't change it for some reason. I assume the original rules of the game is "Amount of players = Honor Pool Total" (2 player pool is less than 4 players). But the game gives you access to a LOT of expansions. The game is amazing and the expansions are a lot of fun. But say you play with OG game, +2 expansions, and 1 promo pack. You can go a whole game without seeing any event cards from the promo pack because the honor pool is so low. 

TLDR the game itself is a blast. $10 is a steal if you are down to play alone. Hanging out in the garage, smoking hookah, passing around the tablet? Great! Hanging out in discord and you want to play with 3 of your friends? I was pretty unhappy. Felt like I got my friends to spend money on something that wasn't great. But really that 4 player multiplayer needs some tweeks. OR let people play remote play (you would be able to see each others hands. Does anyone else remember the outrage campaign against this game, claiming it was so horrible and beyond redemption? Clearly, those people never played Postal or don’t even know what it is. This game feels like a spiritual successor to it especially considering it was marketed as a “genocide crusade,” where you play as a misanthropic character who murders civilians. Yeah, that definitely fits the bill. As for the gameplay, it’s surprisingly solid. The shooting mechanics are responsive and weighty, with a variety of weapons that make combat feel chaotic but satisfying. Levels are fairly open, allowing for different approaches whether you go in guns blazing or take your time exploring. Enemy AI can be inconsistent, but the sheer absurdity and dark humour carry the experience. It’s not particularly deep, but it nails that old school, over the top carnage that fans of Postal or Hatred would expect. While the shock value wears off quickly, the game manages to stay entertaining through its gritty art style, solid optimization, and surprisingly competent gunplay. Though the repetitive mission design show's and with a lack of narrative depth the unapologetic tone and dark satire make up for it. It’s definitely not for everyone but for those who appreciate raw, edgy, and chaotic shooters, it delivers exactly what it promises.

Если вы думаете, что старость — это про вязание, сериал «След» и чаёчек с вареньем, Just Die Already тут же опровергнет эту ложь. Здесь седые ветераны жизни вырываются из дома престарелых и устраивают такой анархический трэш, что даже GTA завидует.

Вы — не просто старик. Вы — старик, которому скучно жить и который решил уйти красиво. Игра щедро предоставляет для этого всё: бензопилы, катапульты, ракеты, акулы и, конечно, добрых прохожих, которых можно слегка “подтолкнуть”… ногой… в пропасть.

Физика персонажей — отдельное искусство. Когда вы теряете руку, голову и половину прочих деталей, игра не останавливается, наоборот — кажется, теперь она только началась. Кроваво, абсурдно, и почему-то смешно до слёз.

Сетевой режим превращает всё это в соревнование “кто первым оторвёт себе ногу ради очков”. Люди кричат, смеются, превращаются в торсы на колёсах — и никто не жалуется. Ведь это не страдание — это искусство вымирания с юмором.

Итог: Just Die Already — это симулятор старческого маразма на максималках. Весело, дико, и после пары часов чувствуешь, что старость — не страшна, если можно запускать себя из пушки в мусорный бак.

[i]Tem jogos que a gente joga. E tem outros que a gente sente. Record of Lodoss War -Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth- é desses segundos. Ele não quer reinventar o gênero  quer celebrar tudo o que fez os Metroidvanias serem mágicos, com o toque nostálgico e poético que só uma aventura estrelada por Deedlit, a elfa mais icônica de Lodoss, poderia oferecer.

 Gameplay: o equilíbrio entre leveza e letalidade

Sabe aquele tipo de jogo que parece uma sinfonia entre movimento e precisão? É isso aqui.
A Deedlit se move com uma fluidez que lembra os tempos de Castlevania: Symphony of the Night  e não é coincidência. O jogo abraça descaradamente essa inspiração, mas com o seu próprio charme.
O sistema de espíritos elementais (Sylph e Salamander) é um toque genial: alternar entre vento e fogo não é só estética, é mecânica de sobrevivência. Cada troca muda a dinâmica do combate e do movimento  flutuar, desviar, contra-atacar. É intuitivo, viciante e traz um ritmo quase musical às lutas.

A progressão é limpa e satisfatória: ganha-se novas armas, habilidades e magias num fluxo natural, sem te afogar em menus ou grind. É aquele tipo de jogo que te faz pensar: “só mais um mapa…”, e quando vê, já são 3 da manhã.

 Gráficos: pixel art feita com alma

Se pixel art é uma arte, Wonder Labyrinth é uma pintura viva.
Cada frame, cada sprite, cada reflexo de luz carrega um capricho absurdo. Os efeitos de magia são um espetáculo à parte especialmente quando o fogo e o vento se misturam em um balé visual que te faz esquecer que está jogando um título 2D.

A ambientação mistura melancolia e beleza. Há algo de solitário e encantado em cada sala  como se Deedlit estivesse andando entre memórias desbotadas, tentando lembrar quem ela era e por que tudo parece tão distante.

Trilha sonora: sussurros de uma lembrança antiga

A música é suave, elegante e cheia de alma. Ela não tenta dominar sua atenção  ela te acompanha, te embala, e quando você percebe, já está totalmente imerso naquele clima de sonho nostálgico.
Os efeitos sonoros são delicados, e cada golpe, passo e feitiço têm um som que parece pensado para transmitir leveza  algo raro num jogo de ação.

 Narrativa: entre memórias e reflexos

A história é mais simbólica do que direta. Não espere diálogos longos ou longas cutscenes  o jogo é mais sobre emoção e lembrança do que sobre enredo linear.
É como se Deedlit estivesse vagando num limbo de memórias, revivendo o que perdeu e tentando encontrar um sentido em meio à solidão. Para os fãs do anime ou das novels, há um peso extra  é quase uma despedida silenciosa dessa personagem lendária.

 Game Feel e experiência do jogador

Do ponto de vista de jogabilidade, o “feel” de Wonder Labyrinth é quase terapêutico. O controle é preciso, a resposta é instantânea, e o movimento de Deedlit é um dos mais suaves que já vi num jogo 2D.
Você sente o vento quando flutua. Sente o impacto da lâmina. E sente o silêncio quando tudo para.
É um jogo que te coloca em um estado de fluxo, onde cada ação parece natural  como se o controle fosse uma extensão da sua vontade.

 Comparação e legado

Se Symphony of the Night é o rei, Wonder Labyrinth é o príncipe que honra seu legado com graça.
Não tenta competir  homenageia.
E, no meio de tantas tentativas modernas de reinventar o gênero, é refrescante ver um jogo que simplesmente diz:

“Lembra por que você se apaixonou por isso tudo?”

Wer in den 90ern gelebt hat und damals schon ein Nerd war, erinnert sich vielleicht daran, wie schwer es war, an Animes zu kommen. Heute ist die deutsche Medienwelt damit überschwemmt, aber das war nicht immer so. 
Es gab Biene Maja und Wickie und Heidi, von denen die meisten nicht wussten, dass sie aus Japan kamen, sowie Akira für den damals spezielleren Geschmack. Aber das war es auch schon fast. Fast. 
Denn es gab auch die Anime-Nächte auf Vox. Die ganze Nacht lang liefen Anime-Serien wie Neon Genesis Evangelion, Gunsmith Cats und Blue Submarine No. 6 auf Japanisch mit deutschen Untertiteln. 

Und da lief auch [b]Record of Lodoss War[/b]. Dabei handelt es um eine ziemlich klassische Fantasy-Serie, die vor allem durch ihren Oldschool-Charme besticht. Drachen, böse Zauberer, Elfen, Zwerge, Diebe, Goblins und so. 
Im Mittelpunkt steht Parn, ein junger Held, mit seiner Gruppe aus klassischen Rollenspiel-Charakteren. 
Einer dieser Charaktere ist die Elfe Deedlit, im japanischen Original Deedolito oder einfach Deedo genannt. 
Sie spielen wir in Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth. 

Das Spiel ist ein solides Metroidvania. 2D-Platformer mit RPG-Elementen, einigen Waffen, Schwertern, Bögen, Tränken, Magie, einigen Bossen und genügend Speicherpunkten. Außerdem schöne Pixelart und passende Musikuntermalung. 
Eine Besonderheit gibt es:
Wir haben zwei Geister, die uns begleiten und zwischen denen wir wechseln können: Sylph (Luft) und Salamander (Feuer). 
Die Wahl des Geistes beeinflusst, wovon wir verletzt werden können und wie viel Schaden wir bestimmten Gegnern zufügen. Und sie geben uns ein paar Spezialfähigkeiten. 

Insgesamt ist das Spiel eine recht spaßige Angelegenheit. 
Wenn das Genre etwas für Dich ist und Du Record of Lodoss War vielleicht sogar noch von früher kennst, kannst Du hier bedenkenlos zugreifen. Du wirst nicht enttäuscht.

A game I played on a whim because I was going through my Backlog and Ended up Absolutely Loving it. Super Lone Survivor is a homage to classic Survival Horror Games such as Silent Hill as it originally was developed to be a project that would turn into a silent hill demake, playing the game you can very clearly see the inspiration.

The game makes you juggle different stats throughout your playthrough; Sanity, Hunger, and Exhaustion. You find items along the way and most necessities are very scarce. The atmosphere of the whole game is really what captivates you inside this universe as you traverse through an apartment building infested with horrid creatures with minimal ways to fight back. The other half of the game will have you explore the town you inhabit which are filled with more monsters and things you can find. Along your journey, you will be introduced to side characters that will give you optional quest and its up to you if you wish to help. While playing, you will need to make decisions that will impact your survivability rate. Whether it be to use your ammo in dire situations, use your limited Items to avoid combat or head back to the safe room and rest so you can keep your sanity and exhaustion in check. The game is packed full of details and does a tremendous jobs on keeping you immersed by giving you minimal HUD elements while you play, a map that gets updated by you scribbling on it when you discover new details and your character exclaiming that they are hungry or tired while you adventure. The soundtrack is also a huge contributor by being part of the ambiance and establishing the different moods and feelings in certain segments of the story or areas of the environment. It makes you feel Safe when you're resting in the safe room or uneasy while you walk the empty corridors of the apartment building or the desolated ruins of the isolated town. The story is well written and plays with the psychological aspect as it has you questioning on what is really going on and pushes you to keep going for answers.

Overall this is an incredibly well made game, one that is for true Survival Horror Fans and game enthusiast. The inspiration is very clear and it delivers it extremely well. It even does that thing that old games do where after you beat it, it shows you your overall score and neat little stats of all the different things you did throughout your journey, it tracks everything! Highly recommend this masterpiece for any Silent hill fans or Horror fans in general. Another Solo Dev Project that was done masterfully.

「ダンジョンに千時間潜った戦士」よりも、「農業して調理して、高ステータスの手に入る料理に百時間かけた農民」のほうが戦闘ステータスが上がる。
農民のほうが 遥 か に 圧 倒 的 に 戦闘ステータスが高くなる。なのでダンジョンに潜る戦士に存在価値は無い。
はっきり言って萎える。
ダンジョン探索とトレハンよりも農業と料理が好きな人には良いゲームだろう。

[h1]Why it's worth keeping an eye on[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fresh take on itemization/progression. Most meta progression is based on your weapon and is extraction looter-shooter adjacent. The catch is weapon is the only thing you focus on. There are stat upgrades, but various effects (such as heal when picking up materials) are the core.
[*] Action feels great. It's similar to Darktide/Vermintide 2 melee, but roughly 70% of depth/quality. There's a bigger focus on mobility and less of a focus on hitting weakspots.
[*] Each area has a core path to exit/next area and a bunch of side areas which have have fights, loot (meta-progression) and other stuff.
[*] Despite it's current state, it doesn't feel low effort.
[/list] 

[h1]Why it's not worth it now[/h1]
There are game design issues and technical issues, and playing now means burning out on a game that will probably be good.


[b]The worst ones[/b] (not all of them)
[list]
[*] Instant kills. Almost every death I had on my first run was an instant kill. Several of them were chain deaths on boss (death-->revive-->death-->revive-->dash-->Death about 20% through dash animation), not even by the boss, but by his summons that have a fast dash attack.
[*] Visibility. I mentioned instant kills. Well at least 4 (half, maybe less) of those were by things spawning outside of my field of vision by an attack that was not telegraphed (I had no way to know it was coming). Even among less threatening enemies, there are some projectiles that just blend in with environment.
[*] Shield enemies. They block all damage, seemingly from all sides. You can breakthrough blocks with charge attacks, dash attacks and maybe just barrage of attacks. They are also always armored, blocking damage even after you break through guard. They require a fair amount of time OR stamina to kill. You're a stitting duck without stamina, and even if you choose the slower route of charge attacks, you're still being attacked by other things.
[/list]

The "great" part of this game of this game is running through enemies, in fast pace actions, reacting to things on screen.
The absolute horsecrap part of this game, is that fast paced action grinds to a halt as youre forced to slog through shielded enemies, or run in circles waiting for mobs to spawn and avoiding one hit kills.

PS: This is just game design, there are lots of technical issues that will take them at least a couple of months to fix. Here's a few 
[list]
[*] Camera jitters up things like stairs. In other games "stairs" only look like stairs, but the camera glides up them as if you were gliding up a slope. In this game moving up a stair is an instant camera jump from Vertical position A to vertical position B.
[*] Grappling hook uses janky ground targeting which doesn't feel intuitive when you have to use it to climb up. Some sections of the game are jumping puzzles with lava going up and grapling hook is not optional. Speaking about that, on gameplay design side the hook is on cooldown, so if you don't know when to use it in those jumping puzzles, you might have it stuck on cooldown when you need it.
[*] Lacking multiple graphical options, such as removing head-bobbing and motion blur. Good luck with that if you get motion sickness from games.
[/list]

Also, I don't know if it's intentional, but the game has a bunch of mechanics and it doesn't do a great job of teaching.

X-Plane 12 is Lego, while MSFS (2020) is Playmobil - let me explain;

Both are - by now - excellent Simulator Platforms that excel in their own way. Both have their benefits and downsides, both are well supported by mods, tools, and utilities. And most importantly, both can be serious fun. But X-Plane is snappy, direct and honest, and much like the Lego Brick on the floor it can hurt and annoy you. MSFS on the other hand delivers a smooth surface, with excellent and bold visuals out of the box, and makes up for what it lacks in depth, even with 3rd party software already considered. 

I don't want to take sides, I can enjoy both and I was annoyed by both, and frankly - I spent way too much money on both. But I (again) feel more at home within X-Plane 12 than I do with MSFS or even MSFS 2024. Simply because behind the wall of firstly overwhelming functionality, everything is logical, structured, and functional to me. No lack of feature has to hide behind a fancy UI mask - it's unappologetic in good ways as much as in bad ways. And I respect that. 

Funnily enough, after the mess XP12 was in its early access to me, I've sworn to settle down with MSFS, then after a year of release I bought 2024 and was equally disappointed, which again drew me back to XP12, as my MSFS install was already deleted. And likelihood of going full circle once more is definitely given. 

So, if you're
* not afraid of basic UI's with high functionality,
* keen to mod your experience to your liking,
* accept longer development times in exchange for actual feedback driven improvements,
* and accept a little less graphical fidelity over a little more depth, 
I can recommend XP12 to you. 

If any one of the above seems odd to you, you'll most likely have more fun in MSFS - and that's said without any sort of elitist note, because it's completely fine.

There sometimes comes a game where I really struggle to put my thoughts in any coherent order. I don't know where to start at all. So, I suppose I'll start where Shadows of the Damned begins.

This game starts with main character's girlfriend being dragged into hell with tons of innuendo and sexual imagery. This is your tone setter, and this scene pretty much sums up the game for me. It's not that you see anything grotesque, it's that it's pointless. It's a good beginning for this game, because Shadows of the Damned feels pointless. It doesn't know what it wants, and when it tries for something, it only fails and leaves a bad taste in your mouth. It feels like multiple games stiched together and fails to be as entertaining as every single one of its inspirations.

If there's one thing this game strives to be, it's funny. There are sexual jokes from the first scene, and it never ceases to try and make you chuckle. As you travel with your demon companion, heroes have almost a Beavis and Butt-Head style conversations, only completely unironically written to be funny to the player. At one point main character, Garcia, refers to vines as demon pubes. On another, after a puzzle, he asks if he needs to fuck a horse to open the next door. Once, a hand appears to snatch a key and your character just says "Hand job". This is the type of thing you'll be dealing with every step of the way.

As you venture through hell, you sometimes see visions of your girlfriend. Now, quiz for everyone who haven't seen the game: imagine a sort of an echo of a person. How does she look like? A ghostly apparition with no legs? Maybe something abstract? Or perhaps just a human with wounds? Well, how about a half-naked lady whose pubic hair you can see through her lingerie, who is constantly tortured and dragged around when you see her? I know this game was tempered by EA but if all the weird shit is publisher's fault, how come no one said no, anyway? And don't worry, you can see her breasts in some scenes as she performs a striptease dance. Classy.

I'm one of those people who thinks comedy can deal with anything, on one condition: you need to be funny. Shadows of the Damned's weird mysogyny where, aside from aforementioned shit, nearly every tortured person you see is a woman, is not helped by its immature bullshit the game throws at you with the frequency of a firing tommy gun. The one time game talks about a badass woman character is followed by a sex joke. And you're saying I'm supposed to like those characters?

This game is a sorry sight. You know that it's a collaboration of Suda and Mikami, but it also features music by Yamaoka and enemy designs by Q Hayashida. And it does sometimes look and sound very good! The enemy desings don't reach the level of inventiveness you'd see in Dorohedoro, but they can be fun. The fairly poor transition to 3D didn't help, because the 2D art I could see on the Steam cards was absolutely gorgeous! Music isn't something I'd listen to on my own time, but lots of latin guitars and distorted rhythms (sometimes at the same time) are an interesting choice.

Now, you see how I mentioned look and sound, and not the gameplay, right? Well, this seems like one of those now recurring instances of people pressuring Mikami into another Resident Evil 4.

Shadows of the Damned is a basic third person shooter in the vein of RE4, only with very limited arsenal and really restrictive levels. Exploration of the game basically consists of you hoping that you chose the wrong path because every time you go through a door it can magically lock behind you. Even if you jump through a window into a building, sometimes the game will just refuse to let you go back.

While the shooting is good, and I particularly like weapon upgrades you get, the enemies are somewhat boring. A lot are too easy, and the only way to die is from insta-death or game spawning a horde of them. It doesn't help that the game has a darkness mechanic. And that mechanic, or rather a gimmick, is an annoyance. Sometimes you're dragged into a dark dimension where your health drains and you can't attack anyone. That's basically it, but the game uses this constantly. Why? It's not scary or tense, just annoying! While the game uses this gimmick to its full potential, it's a fairly lackluster mechanic from the very beginning. It's just restrictive and unfun, and it's never that interesting even when it does something new. It feels like a time-waster throughout. A bad idea with some bells and whistles towards the end, but a bad idea nonetheless.

I think I've enjoyed bosses the most, and they're fairly plentiful and unique. A lot remind me of Metroid Prime 2 bosses considering the dark world stuff. Lots of them are puzzles, and quite a few make the darkness appear as attacks. I think the last boss is trash, but beyond that I've enjoyed them quite a bit!

Some parts of the game are just awful. Act 4 has multiple levels that are mind-numbingly boring, and it's insane to me that the boss the game's been building up to is here, and the actual boss fight is a slow shmup section where she has one attack. Act 4 also features one joke that kinda works. Your skull companion acts as your weapons throughout the game, and he calls sex lines so the gun gets bigger. Sure, it's an erection joke but considering the quality of the humor, this is at least visually interesting. Except it happens, like, 3 times and leads to a very boring turret section every time. And since we're talking about a pseudo RE4 you better believe there are useless QTEs all over the game!

I also don't really get what was "Hella Remastered" here. The game features no options for graphics and can look fairly unpleasant in parts, with washed out textures and shoddy models. The controls at times feel almost random, sometimes asking you to hit Enter, others Space to confirm, and binding key for skipping cutscenes to V for some reason, so most of the game I went through thinking cutscenes that replay after you die were unskippable.

I'm not offended by this game, since overall comedy vibe at least means the game doesn't have any messages to relay and it never acts like it's doing something smart, but I hope whoever was responsible for the treatment of women here got better about it. Credits put most of the blame for writing on Suda, which really sours me on the guy. It comes off as a product made for and by 13-years-olds. It lacks any sort of style it's going for, it's often just boring, and it's never as funny as it thinks it is. You can start playing "guess the punchline" and you'd be correct because most of the time punchline is someone saying the word or mentioning the act of fucking.

This "dream team" project isn't as disasterous as something like NightCry, but it's far more greasy. There are some fun moments, some cool imagery, but those are lost in the sea of shallow unpleasant garbage.

Strange Antiquities is the long-awaited "sequel" to Strange Horticulture and it does not disappoint! If you enjoyed Strange Horticulture you will undoubtedly enjoy Strange Antiquities. So go on, stop reading the reviews and immerse yourself once again in the gloomy world of Undermere! Even if you liked the concept of Strange Horticulture but felt a few things were lacking, there's a good chance you will like Strange Antiquities, as it has improved upon the concept. But no worries if you haven't played Strange Horticulture as you can definitely play this masterful narrative-driven, puzzle-solving mystery on its own. 

Set in the gloomy town of Undermere, you work in a "shop" selling "strange antiquities". Customers will come to you with their troubles and ask for help in finding the correct object. Sometimes they know what they want and you just have to identify the correct object. Sometimes they don't know what object they are looking for and it's up to you to figure out what would be the right item for them. And sometimes they know what they want, but maybe you don't want to give it to them. Your actions do have consequences though, as the game also likes to remind you that the citizens of Undermere don't forget (and neither will you).

During the game you collect several books which will help you in identifying the objects. Don't forget to label them once you've done so, or you can turn on the auto-labelling feature. Not all objects are what they seem and the clues and identifying features vary, keeping the game exciting and fresh. You also get a new card every day which might lead you to more antiquities, if you manage to solve it. Aside from the day-to-day dealings of artifact collecting and helping customers, there is something brewing under that dark cloud that is Undermere. A story in which you play a big role in how it will end. Who do you trust? Which path will you take and where does it lead? Or will you try them all? And if you haven't had enough mysteries yet, there are even more mysteries lying in the store itself. 

This game is perfect if you're looking for something with that dark, gloomy atmosphere, without being too scary or horror. It manages to fit into the cozy category, without being cute. Perfectly fitting for the Fall season and Halloween, but I honestly would play it any time of the year. And when you feel like your sanity needs a little something, you can always pet your cat (or can you?). And don't forget to try placing some objects next to your furry friend and see if he'll react!

Cruelty Squad is what Dadaists might have made, had videogames existed at the time. It's satire and shitposting at the same time, the kind of thing that Nazis would've labelled "degenerate art." It's ugly, it's angry, and it breaks all of the rules. Of course the Nazis, being the real degenerates, proved that the Dadaists were right to mock society. Their twisted logic, hollow aesthetics, and fetishization of tradition masking some of the most evil acts in human history are exactly the sort of thing that the nonsense of Dada opposed. That movement took shape in the wake of the barbarity of WW1, and the Nazis outdid that barbarity several times over. Then most of them died in the fields, and those that remain are still mad about Marcel Duchamps' "Fountain."

It's honestly a huge artistic achievement. It's expressive in a way that I've never seen in a first-person shooter, and it's very exciting to me as a long-time fan of the genre. It's not just because of the satire, it's how every part of the game supports it. The experimental and unintuitive controls, garish visuals, hostile level design, and shrill music drench the satire with a sense of disgust. Do you remember when Coca-Cola hired goons to kill labour organizers in South America? Cruelty Squad remembers. 

It's a confrontational and unashamedly political sort of game, whose defiance of conventions reminds me of French New Wave cinema in addition to the aforementioned Dada movement. It's the scene in Godard's "Weekend" where a painfully long dolly shot showing every car in a traffic jam finally reveals the cause: a car accident leaving at least one person dead and a woman weeping over her damaged handbag. 

It's worth noting that some of the jank is also just... fun? There's something about the reload mechanic which is satisfying in a way that a simple push of the R key can't replicate. I can't help but wonder how this kind of experimentation might influence future games. Love them or hate them, it's undeniable that the rule-breaking of Dada and the Nouvelle Vague were a fertile ground for future art. Without the former we may have never had Monty Python. Without the latter, no Quentin Tarantino. The "degenerates" and radicals led the way. The Nazis on the other hand created nothing, they only destroyed. The "master race" did less for the world than a guy who wrote on a urinal and called it art.

[h1] El Génesis del Survival Horror Moderno [/h1]
Retrocediendo un poco en la historia de los videojuegos, allá por 1996 nacía el "Resident Evil", un juego que cambió por completo el presente y el futuro de la industria. No era solo un juego de zombis, era el nacimiento de un nuevo genero entero. Su influencia y legado todavía resuena. Sin este título, muchos de los juegos que vinieron despues quizás no hubiesen existido de la misma manera. Jugar hoy a la versión remasterizada en HD no es solo revivir una aventura y probar el inicio de una de las sagas más icónicas y famosas de los videojuegos, es rendir homenaje al punto de quiebre donde cambió para mejor la industria entera.

Los ángulos de la cámara fija, los fondos pre-renderizados, la cámara que cambia sin aviso; estas características siguen presentes, siendo parte del encanto y la esencia pura del original. La gestión del inventario, los recursos contados, y la icónica mansión... todo esto está presente, intacto y brillante. En esta versión HD las texturas, los efectos de luz, el formato opcional 16:9, los modelos nuevos de los personajes remasterizados, todo esto aporta un plus extra a la experiencia sin traicionar la esencia. Los puzzles tienen un ritmo pausado pero firme, como es costumbre en el género. Demandan atención, exploración, y prueba y error. Todo estoque comenté, está envuelto en una atmósfera que juega con las luces, los silencios, los sonidos y la sensación constante de miedo latente.

En cuanto al desafío y la dificultad, es menos desafiante y complicado que el "Resident Evil Zero". Sin embargo, siguen presentes esas sensaciones. Sigue exigiendo prudencia, exploración con calma, buena administración de recursos y puntos de guardado, etc.

Se nota mucho la mejoría respecto al apartado visual. Los fondos y los escenarios lucen más pulidos. La música y los efectos logran sumergirnos en esta experiencia espectacular. Las cinemáticas contribuyen gratamente a la sensación retro del videojuego.

Si no jugaste a la saga todavía o si estas dudando en hacerlo, está versión es una oportunidad de oro para que lo hagas. Es una chance increíble para disfrutar del título y la saga, sin padecer la experiencia en la versión original del 96. Porque más allá de su antigüedad, "Resident Evil" sigue siendo un recordatorio vivo de por qué amamos este medio. Nos puede hacer sentir miedo, curiosidad y asombro a la vez. Y porque, al final del día, hay algo mágico en visitar la mansión, donde todo comenzó.

EVE Online is probably the deepest and most complex game you'll ever play. Very broadly speaking you might enjoy this game if you enjoy any of the following genres:

[list]
[*]Economy/business/trade games (X4, Offworld Trading Company, Runescape)
[*]Factory/logistics games (Factorio, Transport Fever, Anno)
[*]Truck/cargo simulators (Euro Truck Simulator, Star Trucker)
[*]Space combat/piracy (Elite: Dangerous, Star Citizen)
[*]Space mining (Elite: Dangerous)
[*]Empire building/politics (Stellaris, sort of)
[*]Dystopian space capitalism in general
[/list]

Yes, the game really is this broad. And while it may be a cliché at this point, the only way to really know if EVE is your kind of game is to try it yourself. So if you’re willing to dive on in, let me provide you with some information to make sure you have the best experience.

[h3]Unlimited Free Trial[/h3]
EVE Online is free-to-play for as much as you want, and will let you try out more than enough activities to see what takes your fancy. The entire map is accessible to you, as well as a very generous selection of spaceships. Take your time, EVE is best enjoyed as a marathon, rather than a sprint.

[h3]Do the Tutorial. No really.[/h3]
EVE has earned its reputation as one of the hardest games to get to grips with, and there are many different game mechanics to learn. The tutorial will help you understand the core mechanics of the game and gives you some money and new ships along the way. After the introductory tutorial you’ll be given the chance to work for several career agents who’s missions will teach you more about specific activities in the game. Do them all. It will give you some starter capital and valuable information. As the final exam, consider doing The Blood-Stained Stars Epic Arc to wrap up your introduction to New Eden.

[h3]Ask For Help[/h3]
Did I mention EVE is bloody complicated? You [i]will[/i] have questions. As a new players you will automatically join the Rookie Help channel where you can ask anything you want and get (mostly) useful answers. EVE has a very newbie friendly community, we want to see you succeed, and will do anything in our power to help you out.

[h3]Join a Corporation[/h3]
EVE is, at its core, a social game. Everything you do interacts with other players in one way or another. Corporations are EVE’s guilds or clans, and joining one is a great way to find friends to fly with. Personally I would recommend all new players join up with EVE University. They are the oldest and best accredited new player corporation in the game and also maintain the game’s unofficial wiki. It is a good place to learn the game and ask questions.

[h3]Hit me up![/h3]
If this review has been helpful to you and you’re looking for more help to find your way, feel free to contact me either on Steam or in-game. I’m always happy to help eager newbies find their way in this amazingly unique game.
