Alright. [i]POOLS[/i] is done and dusted. This is my kind of liminal spaces game. No creatures chasing you. Just a distorted reality that you attempt to puzzle your way out of. This one, as the name implies, features pools and a lot of water in general. Which was pretty cool.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3595892697

There isn't really much of a story, such as things go. There are however implications. That things within these liminal spaces look into our world and try to replicate what they see, but without a functional knowledge of how our world's physics work, why certain things exist, and how life interacts with the world. Which is fairly compelling in concept. Because, while there is nothing chasing you per se, there are things living in these liminal spaces. Also, the special level does suggest that perhaps creatures such as [b]It[/b] originate in these liminal spaces. 

The main thing in this game is the combination of stunning graphics mixed with puzzles that mostly follow the (mostly) subconscious rules of exploration. Which are that when lost or exploring, always choose the same direction unless presented with an undeniable option. For example, always turn left. That way, you can also always find your way back out or back to where you started again. Only here, rather than having a need to backtrack out of a cave system or what have you, you are simply trying to find exits. Still, the basic rules of exploration do mostly hold true in each level. At least, that's how I approached things.

As mentioned, the graphics are fairly stunning. At times, they just outright look amazing. At other times, where they are trying to present a mimicry of real-life things not fully understood by their creators, they take on a bit of an almost alien appearance, represented by simplified graphics. Such as some houses and streets you will find later in the game.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3596500384

Physics are also important, and there was a lot of detail in simple things like moving through water, walking in dry spaces while still wet, and so on. The attention paid to the little things in this game was pretty impressive. The sound of water splashing, you slowing down while traversing pools, and so on really serve to provide quite a bit of atmosphere to a somewhat sterile environment.

The puzzle design itself, while as mentioned before, mostly adhering to certain principles, isn't afraid to shake things up just when you're getting comfortable, and paying attention to seemingly minor details will definitely pay dividends as you navigate the various levels. There are also a number of secrets available to the intrepid explorer that will take you off the beaten path a little bit. The addition of a straight-up MC Escher level and the IT (clown) level really serve to define where the developer's mind was at while thinking through the creation of these exploration puzzles.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3596018098

I thought it was a clever game that drives home the feeling of isolation that is part and parcel with liminal spaces games while finding a way to keep you engaged without relying on chasing you around the levels with liminal spaces creatures. And both endings will leave you with some questions that you will need to answer for yourself. I thought it was a cool way to handle things and enjoyed my time in this game. I bought this on sale during the 2025 Halloween sale, but it definitely earns its asking price, especially if you're gonna play it more than once to find all the secrets. Although it's worth noting that there is a level select, so the cheevo hunters out there can be more selective in how they go about chasing that 100%. Definitely worth a look.

I played this game a lot in my childhood, encapsulated in this game's overall atmosphere. Music is good, characters are lovable, and exploration was quite intriguing. When you're playing for the first time, you might get stuck on some puzzles or on how to acquire pearls needed for progression.

Despite the old version's charm, which needed some tweaking to work properly on a modern system (and it's a shame Ubisoft pulled it from the store), this one ([i][strike]surprisingly enough[/strike], well, not really[/i]) needs it too. If you want to play on a [b]16:10[/b] monitor ([i]like a [b]Steam Deck[/b]'s one[/i]) - behold, black bars from [b][url=store.steampowered.com/app/268050/The_Evil_Within/]The Evil Within[/url][/b]. If you want a frame rate higher than 60 - .ini file editing as usual ([i]but beware - it does break some in-game logic, and the pearl mini-game won't register a score without a button press and will be very fast or slow depending on the frame time[/i]).

But despite all that, I enjoyed replaying this old gem on a [b]Steam Deck[/b] with 90 fps high settings galore with no stutters at all. Achievements registered properly ([i]because I was online all the time - thanks, [b]UbiConnect[/b][/i]) and didn't have any major issues ([i]some at launch reported [b]AMD[/b] graphics won't play nicely with this title[/i]).

Additional content with Jade's past didn't click with me. Characters are out of place and [i]cringy[/i]. The pirate life backstory is not really fleshed out for me, due to the game's nonexistent explanation of WHO Jade really IS and why she has her powers.



[h3]But I would still recommend getting this cult classic on sale. RIP BGE 2.[/h3]

If you’ve played any LEGO game before, you probably know what to expect and honestly, that’s not a bad thing. The familiar gameplay is still here, but what really makes LEGO Marvel Super Heroes stand out is how much it packs in. Not only does it deliver a ton of Marvel fan service, but it also throws in a big open-world New York City for you to explore between missions. It kind of feels like a family-friendly LEGO version of GTA, in the best way possible. There are loads of characters to unlock, from Spider-Man and Iron Man to the X-Men and the Fantastic Four. While the main story focuses mostly on big names like The Avengers and some classic villains, there’s still plenty of love given to other characters too. The main story itself isn’t groundbreaking, but it gets the job done and keeps things moving with that classic LEGO humor. Plus, the bonus missions hosted by Deadpool are hilarious and add even more fun to the mix. Visually, the game is bright and colorful, exactly what you’d expect from a LEGO title. The voice acting is surprisingly good, and the soundtrack fits the Marvel vibe really well. That said, the flight controls can be a little clunky at times, and you might run into a few minor bugs here and there. But nothing game-breaking. All in all, LEGO Marvel Super Heroes is easily one of the best LEGO games out there. Whether you're a longtime Marvel fan or just looking for something lighthearted and fun, there’s a ton to enjoy here. And if you could only pick one LEGO game to play, this one would be a pretty safe (and super fun) bet.

More of the same, but better... WAY better, especially when it comes to shooting parts. While action sequences in original Rogue City were already good fun, they never reached the full potential of RoboCop power fantasy. But Unfinished Business? Damn, I did not have this much fun in the first person shooter since first F.E.A.R.

The amount of havok you wreak in this game is just insane. And when you start thinking it can't get any better, they give you a freeze gun. Basically a RoboCop version of BFG. BFG wich makes BFGs from other games feel boring AF. And devs knew this, as they start throwing so much ammo (and enemies) at you, you never get a "I must save this for later" feeling, and you can just shoot it as much as you want with a big grin on your face.... AND then they let you play as ED 209! Fan service is at maximum level in this game.

But while all of this seems too good, UB is unfortunately far from a perfect game. First of all, it is still running on UE5, in it's worst state possible. While framerate is mostly acceptable, the amount of traversal stutters is sometimes unbearable. One of the worst I ever experienced. Maybe even worse than Dead Space 2023.

Then there are still sequences with sidequests for civilians, mostly consisting of fetch questing, where you just "run" from one point to another, doing the most boring stuff possible. They surely could have avoided  these parts, even if it would make game like 2 hours shorter.

But still, even with these flaws, it is definitely worth experiencing just for the shooting parts alone. 
And again, I hope that after Terminator and RoboCop, their next game will be Judge Dredd. Setting of UB is basically one big teaser for a Dredd game :)

[b]Честно говоря, эта часть зашла даже больше предыдущей[/b] 

Скорее всего это связано с более щедящей кривой сложности. В Elex 1 первые часов 20 игрока рвали даже рядовые противники, расставленные и в начальных локациях. Здесь же всё идёт плавнее, и противники с квестами распределены более грамотно.
Кстати о квестах, они приятно удивили. Конечно, в Elex 2 есть задания принеси-подай-убей со слабым сценарным обоснованием. Но всё же, как мне показалось, интересных квестов гораздо больше, даже простые в геймплейном плане задания часто скрашиваются неплохой историей, раскрывающей мир или конкретного квестодателя. Особенно понравились многоэтапные миссии по вступлению в ряды берсерков и альбов (очень хорошая история, много нелинейности и геймплейно разнообразно). Да и в целом нелинейность в игре радует. Очень часто дается возможность впоследствии ощутить результат своих действий.
Считаю, что лучшая часть игры - это именно первая глава со вступлением во фракцию. Тут любимый набор Piranha Bytes, и именно на эту главу тратится чуть ли не половина всего прохождения Elex 2. Далее же, геймплейно, все идет на спад, а миссии с зачисткой локаций к четвертой главе уже вызывают боль.
А вот сюжет, напротив, к концу игры набирает обороты. Постоянно случаются неожиданные (и не притянутые за уши) повороты, история мира обрастает подробностями, а персонажи развиваются на протяжении прохождения. Основной сюжет скрашивается взаимоотношениями группировок, за которыми интересно следить. В общем, сюжетную составляющую серии Elex я считаю лучшей среди всех игр Piranha Bytes (при всем моем уважении к серии Gothic).
Боевую систему за воина описать я пока не могу, т.к. играл за берсерка по пути магии. И вот она... скажем так, не способна сохранять интерес к сражениям надолго. Вроде бы и есть ближние и дальние атаки, фаерболы и еще некоторые способности, но все равно язык не поворачивается назвать боевку магией увлекательной, часто просто включаешь огненный дождь, чтобы сражение быстрее закончилось, особенно к четвертой главе.
Перемещение по миру сделали гораздо лучше, дав возможность летать на джетпаке, и сам мувмент стал приятнее. Сам же мир практически не узнаваем со времен первой части. Да и в целом он какой-то... уютный, ламповый, даже несмотря на его враждебность. Это у Piranha Bytes всегда получается как-то сделать.
Графически игра очень непостоянна. Качественная растительность, освещение и текстуры окружения соседствуют с мыльными модельками персонажей и очень большим количеством графических багов, будь то исчезновение текстур или очень странные светотени местами. А вот в плане дизайна окружения все гораздо лучше. Очень хорошо сделаны базы группировок, леса и даже руины в заснеженной локации. Броня на персонажах и они сами задизайнены удачнее, чего только стоит внешняя эволюция Кайи со времен первой части.
Музыка здесь - это в основном ремиксы из первой части Elex. Но она все так же отлично вписывается в мир (чего только стоят отдельные треки для спутников гг).

В итоге же я бы посоветовал эту игру тем, кому зашел Elex 1 сюжетно, и хочется продолжения. Да и геймплейная формула бережно сохранена и местами доработана. Чего только стоит первая глава. Однако ради развития истории и концовки придется осиливать последние главы, наполненные выматывающими зачистками территорий и сопровождаемые не самым лучшим техническим исполнением.

Добро пожаловать в Pathologic 2 (или, как я предпочитаю его называть, «Симулятор Хронической Тревоги и Плохих Решений»). Если вы ищете игру, где можно расслабиться после рабочего дня, где вам подадут уютный квест с чёткими указаниями и благодарным NPC, то вам не сюда. Уходите. Немедленно. Иначе вы рискуете понять, что такое настоящий, экзистенциальный ужас, замешанный на невыплаченных счетах и запахе гниющей плоти.

▎Что Это Вообще Такое?

Pathologic 2 — это не игра. Это 12-дневный марафон по выживанию в городе, который решил, что его лучший способ самовыражения — это чума. Вы играете за хирурга, который вернулся домой, чтобы обнаружить, что его дом сгорел, его отец мёртв, а город Стены охвачен Мором.

Ваша цель? Спасти всех. Ха-ха. Это самая смешная часть игры.

▎Геймплей: Искусство Не Умереть (Или Почти)

Разработчики из Ice-Pick Lodge решили, что страдание — это весело. И они правы. Но это весело так же, как смотреть, как горит ваша машина, пока вы пытаетесь вспомнить, где оставили огнетушитель.

1. Менеджмент Ресурсов: Шопинг у Зомби

Вам постоянно нужно есть, пить, спать и лечиться. И всё это стоит денег, которых у вас нет. Ваш инвентарь — это коллекция подозрительных трав, грязной воды и, возможно, одной-двух спасённых от разбоя костей.

Вы находите редкий, ценный предмет, который может спасти чью-то жизнь. Вы несёте его через полгорода, уворачиваясь от местных бандитов. Наконец, вы добираетесь до нужного NPC. И тут вы понимаете, что *вам* срочно нужно поесть, и вы с отчаянием съедаете этот ценный предмет, потому что полоска голода мигает красным, а смерть от голода выглядит менее героической, чем смерть от чумы.

2. Диалоги: Философия с Привкусом Плесени

Диалоги здесь — это шедевры абсурда и глубины. Вы пытаетесь объяснить местным жителям, что они умирают, а они отвечают вам цитатами из Ницше или просят одолжить им пару монет на водку.

Вы пытаетесь провести сложную медицинскую процедуру, объясняя пациенту важность стерильности. Он смотрит на вас с видом «Ты что, с ума сошёл?» и начинает рассказывать о том, как его бабушка лечила всё подорожником и верой в доброго царя. И, чёрт возьми, иногда его метод работает лучше, чем ваши антибиотики!

▎Персонажи: Ваши Личные Мучители

Враги? Нет. Ваши соседи. Каждый NPC в этой игре — это ходячий моральный компас, который постоянно указывает вам, что вы выбрали неправильный путь.

▎Итог: Зачем Это Играть?

Pathologic 2 — это игра, которая заставляет вас чувствовать себя не героем, а просто очень уставшим человеком, который забыл выключить утюг. Вы не спасаете город. Вы просто оттягиваете неизбежное для себя и для 90% населения.

Если вы любите игры, где «победа» означает, что вы смогли прожить ещё один день, не сойдя с ума от голода или отчаяния, и где каждая спасённая жизнь ощущается как личное, кровавое достижение, то Pathologic 2 — это ваш новый кошмар.

Ganz im Allgemeinen würde ich das Spiel jedem empfehlen, dem Teamplay nicht sonderlich wichtig ist, der sich an der recht gut gelungenen Grafik (zudem noch VR Modus und 4K - Kompatibilität) erfreut, oder denen, die gerne in Open World rumfliegen, Piraten, Aliens und gelegentlich mal nen Spieler jagen möchte.

Zum Teamplay selbst: Natürlich wäre es wichtig, wie in den meisten Online-Games. Allerdings ist es einfach nicht vorhanden. Die Schiffsklassen waren früher vielfältiger ( vor etwa 2-3 Jahren ) und ausgeglichener. Mitlerweile bestehen die meisten Schiffe aus einer Art "leicht anpassungsfähigem Einheitsbrei". Leider. Die einzigen Schiffe die sich noch wirklich unterscheiden - sind Kauf-/ Bauschiffe und Zerstörer (Welche ebenfalls gebaut werden müssen)

Zum Farmen / Fortschritte erspielen: Man kann laut Entwickler die meisten Schiffsteile und Ressourcen ingame bekommen. Betonung liegt auf KANN. Als Beispiel: Schiff X benötigt für den Bau 600 Schiffsteile. Pro Schlacht KANN man 1 Teil finden. Diese Schlacht muss man allerdings gewinnen - und da gibt es gerade mal eine Chance.
Andere Prototypen die nicht als Premiumschiffe gedacht sind kosten etwa das Doppelte, gibts allerdings unterschiedliche Ressourcentypen. Im Schnitt braucht man 3 Monate  intensive Spielzeit um sich 1 zu bauen.

Open World: ein wirklich interessanter Spielmodus, verschiedenste Sektoren die über ein Sprungtor (Map und ggf. Serverwechsel) zu erreichen sind. In den Sektoren trifft man auf Piraten, Aliens, die eigene Fraktion als KI und gelegentlich andere Spieler. Einen PvP Modus in open world kann man zwar einstellen, jedoch sind nur die Spieler angreifbar, welche sich ebenfalls dafür entschieden haben.
Zudem ist das Lootsystem eher eingeschränkt. Ressourcen finden, in den Schiffsslot einfügen (Zwischen 2 und 12 Slots, je nach Schiffsgröße) und dann sicher nach hause bringen. Wird man zerstört, verliert man seine Ladung.
Leider zu wenig besucht - vorallem zu wenig Quests, die das Spielen in open world lohnen würden.

PvP/PvE und Matchmaking: Balance ist unvorhersehbar, Matchmaking meistens unausgereift - vorallem wenn man als Team in einem Squad fliegen möchte. Es gibt die Möglichkeit einer Corporation beizutreten, jedoch sehr wenig Kooperative Modi. SC-League geht nur mit 5 Leuten, PvE mit maximal 4,  Turnier mit bis zu 8 Leuten, welches jedoch nur Sonntags Abend ist. [...]

The latest example would have to be the transition from destroyers to alien ships. I am not a person who likes the idea of destroyers in the game as it has been put into practice. On paper great, but initially they were very strong. Yes they had events to get these ships easily, but now they are difficult to get and have a sort of air of exclusivity.

 On this basis you would think that at the very least, customers are rewarded with a strong ship for investing real money.  But now they've been nerfed into the ground. The starter kit for which costs 40$ USD if you want to "convenience" your way to them and they are quite powerful. Right now there is a broker mission and some grinding you can to do to get there for free, but I imagine by the time the general community finally gets to them they could be nerfed as the new ship is released, with a new 40$ starter kit.  I've seen this sort of game balance strategy before and it ruined the community of a game I cared very much about. MWO is now dead because of this sort of economic model. Maybe I'm wrong. 这款游戏作为独立游戏完成度相当之高，尤其是动作系统，但目前体验下来别的方面问题还是太多了。
1.  锁定问题。我有点搞不清楚这做的是硬锁还是软锁，锁定点长期处于转不过来与随便乱飘的叠加态，如果不锁定就要面对拳拳打空气的情况。
2.  敌人的攻击欲望。不知道是不是我太菜了，宗师难度游玩过程中经常会被一群人围在中间打，而且在连招过程中常会被背后的敌人打断，而且游戏好像没有倒地保护，敌人一连就是一套，主角的防御性能面对这种凶残的攻击欲望有点太孱弱了（有些架势还根本没法防御），而且还缺乏一些控场能力，一被围殴就难以脱身。
3.  恶心的霸体怪。boss之类的我就不说了，后期为什么会出现霸体小怪？而且数量不算少，伤害还高，想优先处理还要被高攻击欲望小怪骚扰，想逐个击破但主角机动性又不算高，就贼恶心。
4.  红黄光问题。红黄光提示做的不太明显，我不是指看不到，而是时机提示上有些问题，你但凡出手前加一个显眼点的闪光呢，现在的红黄光还是需要一点目押的，目前红黄光最大的作用就是提示敌人在旁边给你憋个大的。说到目押，游戏里敌人的部分攻击是不是有点诡异了，第一关boss会平移着飞过来砍你，小兵的一些红黄光攻击动作太慢了，反应快了反而接不上。
5.  boss设计。说实话我没打算要求独立游戏有什么特别惊艳的boss设计，但你这个人均霸体和疯狗连段是什么情况啊？从第一个boss就这样，打入二阶段后全程霸体追着你咬，还有那个最终boss，很多攻击甚至只能跳起来躲避，从开始就常驻霸体，攻击还很多都是aoe，而且主角完全没有受身恢复姿态的能力是不是有点不应该啊？在空中主角根本没办法防御，哪怕做成一些技能慢慢点呢。
6.  道具使用与回血，道具栏我建议移到一个手指不用跑那么远的键位上，再就是我强烈建议把超级冲击回血的设定移到所有难度上，或者做成一个道具或技能都行，哪怕高难度回复量少点呢。

Antes que nada hay que aclarar algo, si les gustó el primer project warlock y buscan más como lo que vivieron en ese juego, entonces olvídenlo, está secuela se desarrolla como un retro FPS por niveles con elementos rpg pero sin las caracteristicas roguelike del original .

Este no es un mal juego, de hecho puede llegar a ser muy divertido pero los grandes problemas que tiene es que es un caos total, hay un desbalance terrible, como por ejemplo a partir del segundo capítulo, con solo decirles que pude pasar 99% de este solo usando el arma de cuerpo a cuerpo y abusando de la estúpida habilidad que te hace invencible por un buen rato, pese a que estaba en la dificultad más alta aún así todo fue ridículamente fácil.

El juego en general no tiene una dirección específica, intenta ser muchas cosas a la vez, es una mezcla de DooM eternal, Quake, tiene habilidades como en borderlands e incluso en el episodio 3 meten la mecánica de recarga activa de gears of war. Si bien en el episodio 1 es donde todo se siente más coherente, a partir del dos la calidad en general baja muchísimo porque cuando usas tus  puntos de mejora casi puedes eliminar a la mayoría de los enemigos de un par de golpes aún en la dificultad más alta. Por otro lado el diseño de niveles es terrible, algunos de estos son innecesariamente grandes, otros absurdamente cortos, se nota en varias áreas que se les acabó el tiempo o los recursos y terminaron como pudieron.

Exceptuando el episodio 2 que lo odie en su totalidad, el capítulo 1 me agrado bastante porque el personaje no tiene habilidades tan exageradamente poderosas; la acción es muy frenética y gracias el contador de combos te motiva a matar como en DooM eternal, las armas son estúpidamente poderosas y es divertido experimentar con diversos builds. Le pongo calificación negativa porque es importante expresarle a los desarrolladores que para su próximo título deben de enfocarse en crear una experiencia más concisa y no intentar hacer de todo un poco; este equipo tiene talento y un buen futuro si aprenden de los errores de este título.

首先是对1905年华沙风貌的还原十分考究，街景捏得很漂亮，跑图的感觉想起了极乐迪斯科，应该也受到了迪的一些影响。设计了多处散落在大街小巷间，还原各种民俗和人们的生活细节且有趣的收集任务，搭配上维克多有些犀利又幽默的吐槽，非常生动。维克多可选的发型和服饰也一定程度还原了当时的时尚，明显能看出俄国（哥萨克胡须）和以巴黎为代表的西欧风尚（时尚杂志上的插画）对一位中上流阶层的华沙市民生活的影响。

如果论游戏呈现的时代风貌的话，本作的时间背景在[b] 1905年，一个新旧交替而风起云涌的年份，其中呈现的现代性也更像是某种真正的*新时代*来临前的曙光。而因为它不是1919年，也不是1989年；1905年和它展现一些时代将前进的方向和前卫的理念也是有限的，必然受到各种因素制约，甚至被掐灭在摇篮中 [/b]，游戏对这一部分也表现得很具体。

以城市建设为例，完善的排水系统被许多人看作是共济会和犹太人的阴谋，而一些观念更为开明的人也从中看到了华沙借此摆脱西欧眼中“穷乡僻壤”印象的机会，但是要公众转变整体的观念，恐怕还需要相当长的时间。“空中的马”这一支线也比较体现这座一切看起来都正在发展，欣欣向荣的城市的暗面：受够了苦难的底层年轻人试图到华沙寻求更好的生活，却不得不沦落到廉价地出卖肉体为生，被这座城市吃得干净，以至于成为连环杀手来发泄对于不公的社会的怨气，最后被迫自我了断。空中的马是马车碾过桥洞下的破旧住宅的声音，也是城市快速发展暴露的各种社会问题的一角。

在民族性的问题上，游戏里体现了希望波兰能够独立，摆脱沙俄统治是许多华沙人的诉求，在社会上刻画为各种秘密结社，换掉俄语招牌，沙俄在华沙日益严酷的统治，哥萨克破坏民族议会等等。[b] 在许多情况下，过分强调单一民族国家的叙事都有所偏颇，且一定程度上回避了许多独立后的单一民族国家仍然是微型多民族国家的事实。但本作在相当程度上仍然保留了华沙这座城市在文化和政治上的多元性。[/b]在游戏里可以听到各种语言，沙俄女官丝苇兰娜说话夹杂着法语，另外警察、士兵往往会说俄语，一些外来者也会说德语，还有地下拳击场的西班牙人和美国人等等。

一些剧情也体现了对民族主义这把双刃剑的反思。一个典型例子就是莱基特人的支线任务，要求纯粹而单一的民族性也象征着文化保守主义和对其他族裔的仇视，甚至是针对无辜民众的恐怖行动。而旺达所在的左翼团体虽然也会为波兰独立采取激进手段，却反对并清算前者。另一个例子是在流动大学里的俄裔学生，她长期生活在华沙，却因为俄裔身份受到不公正的敌视，这同时也是当时一些有分离主义倾向的东欧地区俄裔会面临的处境。

对沙俄阵营的塑造同样也不是刻板的邪恶势力，除了兵痞和经常站在民众对立面的维稳警察，有总是会帮助维克多，和蔼的沃罗宁舅舅; 也有科涅奇金这样的暗中操持，会采取强硬手腕镇压革命者，更贴近一般印象中的反派人物的角色；还会有那位被派来调查民族主义恐怖袭击事件，却能出于为受害者声张正义的动机，政治冷感而一定程度上跨越种族偏见，说“为‘国家’这一抽象概念付出或夺走生命不值得“的朱可夫侦探。对科涅奇金这一人物的塑造同样也很出色，总是在危机关头出现，难以琢磨，直到从城堡逃出时才得知他如何抽丝剥茧地抓住把柄控制了斯坦尼斯瓦夫和一众人，而最后也选择了一种比较刚硬的死法[spoiler] （把血留在维克多家大宅几十年） [/spoiler]。他和莉迪娅的关系还有那封请求联姻的书信究竟是纯粹的利益和控制考量，还是带有一些复杂的情感，这大概也不得而知了。

和阿保利茨重修于好的友谊展现了华沙地下世界的一角，也是故事里比较轻松的一部分。喝酒胡闹差点用枪把自己打死的几个哥萨克，朝圣者和诗人的三幕剧，还有一起喝醉后天旋地转，胡言乱语的cg（感觉此处也是一个rdr2neta）想起来总是会心一笑。与阿保利茨一起行动的支线也为故事添上一些游侠故事的传奇色彩，是在沉重的时代间隙的一段有趣的轶闻。

同时，本作也塑造了一些令人印象深刻，具有当时相当前卫的观念与行动的女性角色。首先是在阶级和性别观点上都持有激进态度，并具有领袖魅力和决断能力的革命党人旺达[spoiler] （在最后一章的晚宴上，会发现旺达带着枪打算刺杀总督，且早已做好赴死觉悟）[/spoiler] 。还有会用穿裤装和经营家族产业来表达对社会陈规反叛的莉迪娅[spoiler] （所以最后并没有选择拿走莉迪娅身上“野心”的缺陷，在我看来这也是支撑她一直在各种阻碍间得以开拓自己的道路的动力之一）[/spoiler]。

比起魔幻，这作涉及奇幻情节的部分却带有更多的现实主义色彩。战斗环节多是因为华沙街头本就充满各种理由甚至无厘头的小冲突[strike] （不得不说维克多傲慢缺陷驱使下的各种发言很多时候纯属自己找打）[/strike]，而打倒对面的人很多时候也并不能改变既有的现实。以“华沙反奇唤士协会”支线为例，就算阻止集会，打倒了组织者和几个叫嚷着荒诞无稽理论的受众，反而进一步加深了多方心中的偏见和仇视，而他们仍然会在后续的剧情中反复出现。

另一点就是“缺陷”这个设定，缺陷可以吸引异界种，被缺陷操控的人会做出各种反常的行动，但是拿走了缺陷，那些人在缺陷驱使下的罪行就不应计较，或者是靠此来摆脱应有的惩罚吗？这显然是一个更深层次的有关伦理的问题。而在游戏中，索菲亚诱导追求者死在异国他乡路上；贵族公子皮加在穷朋友的友谊中彼此各取所需，却最终因为荒谬的理由打赌让穷朋友送了命，即使取走他们身上的缺陷使其变成“更好的人”，[b] 但他们的罪行仍然存在，却总会出于各种理由被掩盖过去。 [/b]

而奇唤士的设定除了改编自斯拉夫文化和西欧神话和民俗之外，在游戏中出现的几位奇唤士的身份也值得琢磨：灵婆纱蜜拉是遭到追杀流亡的吉卜赛人，伏介士波纳科维奇是鞑靼人，洛甫是犹太人，他们都是某种程度上在当时拥有一定力量但也随时面临威胁的少数群体。花园晚宴上贵族们试图收缴奇唤士财产中饱私囊，甚至对奇唤士进行脑叶切除术的提案也象征着社会长期以来对少数群体的迫害。以一条线路的洛甫结局为例，[spoiler] 当维克多为了重建圈子去找洛甫时，却发现他直接被仇视奇唤士的愤怒民众打死。虽然洛甫为人阴险，但不仅（走的这条路线里）从他手里抢走魔像的维克多逃脱不了此事的责任，而且他的死也是东欧历史排犹传统的一个侧面[/spoiler]；总督仇视奇唤士的原因[spoiler] 也来源于嫉妒和恐惧天赋异禀的奇唤士妹妹，并最后残忍杀死了她，同样也是另一种对弱势群体的迫害[/spoiler]。游戏设定里代表主流宗教的神父对奇唤士群体的态度也很有趣：[i] 如果你的撒旦存在，那么制裁他们的上帝同样存在。[/i]

出于个人的厌恶并不是很想走拉斯普京线就选了圈子，所以最后选择了让奇唤士的“圈子”继续存在[spoiler] （也没有取走那个奇唤士男孩身上缺陷）[/spoiler]的路线，在我看来这也代表了某种[b] 少数族群/异见者能够相对独立于主流却不是完全合理的政治和宗教外，继续生存和抗争的可能，并用他们的方式推动社会的进步。 [/b]

对自己打出来的结局并不能说完全满意，但必须承认这种处理仍然具有一定的现实主义色彩。[spoiler] 最后在脑内与沙皇谈判解决问题的方式也算某种开皇恩——奇唤士们希望自己的处境能够得到最高统治者的怜悯而得以改善。但沙皇的最终开恩很大程度上也是因为波纳科维奇以供出社会主义分子的名单和据点为代价达成谈判，尾声里圈子的三人仍然聚在一起——但是是在失败的革命后，社会主义者们的坟墓之前。奇唤士的力量得以保存，而工运又被更严酷的暴政扑灭，在剧烈的动荡间，为女性提供高等教育机会的流动大学也不久后被迫关停， [/spoiler] [b] 每种选择都必须付出一定的代价，也不存在不付出任何牺牲的道路。[/b]

在许多议题上，制作组虽然有时会流露明显倾向，但维克多的对话选项总是留有一定的自由度，且维克多那种总是不免戏谑和嘲讽一切的态度还是把很多评判剧情的空间交给了玩家。维克多对父亲斯坦尼斯瓦夫的评价可以认为他不负责任就是个混账，也可以宽容他曾经的无奈之举，以至于继承他的理想走下去却不被其代表的陈规束缚，但无论如何，和死者的对话始终是出自自身的幻想而不是和奇唤术一样*超现实*的。可以加入拉斯普京试图用神秘主义拯救大俄罗斯的计划，也可以在最后和他切割，同时也背叛他曾经在奇唤术上为维克多提供的各种帮助。对这些复杂角色的态度和理解同样存在多样性。[b] 有*最好*的选择吗？这是个难以一言概之的问题，也取决于玩家如何看待这些取舍。[/b]

作为一个历史游戏而言，拉斯普京看到的无数人伤亡，帝国解体和王侯将相惨烈丧生的幻象更像是某种ww1的预演，这可能也改编于otl里拉斯普京对沙俄参加一战流露的明显的消极态度；而让死在逃亡维也纳路上的丝苇兰娜恐惧不已的断头台短短十几年后就用来砍下罗曼诺夫王朝贵族们的头颅。

[h2] [i] 在华沙全城戒严和为最终下场凄惨此时却一无所知，尚在襁褓之中的阿列克谢太子举办的庆生宴里度过夏日最后一天；在酝酿中的真正撕裂沙俄的风暴来临之前趁此刻瞥一眼这座旧俗和革新交替而充满魅力，同时各个阵营暗流涌动的城市。 [/i] [/h2]

非常喜爱此作呈现的时代感和历史风味，能玩到这样用心的游戏很满足。

（笔者对波兰史和相关文化背景的了解很肤浅，先为可能的剧情疏漏、不严谨和明显错误道歉）

**Rating: 8/10**

Holy crap, I freaking love this game! Space Flight Simulator is an incredible experience that captures the thrill and challenge of space exploration in a way that's surprisingly accessible. The graphics are decent—I'd rate them around a 7/10—they're simple but effective, creating a clean and realistic space environment that immerses you without demanding high-end hardware. The game’s visual style is minimalist but functional, which actually helps keep the focus on building and flying your rockets.

The gameplay is where this game really shines—it's a solid 9/10. The controls are surprisingly intuitive, making it easy for newcomers to start designing rockets, launching, and navigating through space. You can experiment with different rocket designs, orbital maneuvers, and planetary landings, which adds a lot of depth for those willing to learn. It’s straightforward enough to pick up quickly, but mastering complex orbits, achieving stable landings, or designing efficient rockets takes time and effort—giving it that perfect "easy to learn, hard to master" vibe.

One of the best aspects is the open-ended sandbox nature of the game. You're free to set your own goals, whether it's reaching orbit, landing on moons or planets, or just experimenting with different rocket configurations. The game also does a great job of teaching basic physics and orbital mechanics in a fun, interactive way, making it a fantastic educational tool.

However, the game could benefit from more content—such as astronauts, space stations, or more complex mission objectives—to make the experience even richer. Currently, it focuses mainly on rocket design and flight, which is great, but adding crew management or interplanetary missions could really elevate it.

Another thing I love is how accessible it is—it's easy to get started, yet there’s enough depth for serious enthusiasts to explore advanced concepts. I could definitely see this being used in schools or educational programs to introduce students to space science and engineering concepts in a hands-on way.

Overall, Space Flight Simulator is a fantastic indie game that delivers an engaging, educational, and fun space exploration experience. It’s not perfect—some more content and features would make it even better—but it’s definitely worth your time, especially if you're a space nerd or curious about rocket science.

Ratshaker is an oddity, because it's both an exploration of the darkness in a person's addiction but also something that doesn't try too hard to take itself seriously. I think the subtext in this game is so blaringly obvious that it's oddly something... strangely missable? 

You begin as a person holding a rat in a field, and as you shake it, things begin to form around you as the rat comments on your grasp of reality (and to a greater extent - of itself), and the game takes a morbid turn as soon as you begin to step foot into the house. Ratshaker does a great job of both rewarding and punishing curiosity, as certain things can be done, and they don't tell you that it can kill you until you figure it out yourself. 

In a horror setting, environments can feel oppressive, claustrophobic and almost cruel. In Ratshaker, there're a lot of these things with the additional subtext that you have something to feel guilty about, and have something that's gone very, very wrong - and it's likely your fault. Without spoiling anything, the game rewards you with ambiguity at almost every turn, but I think that's what makes it quite unsettling the further you go and you uncover the secrets the house is holding. 

Ratshaker's overall premise is interesting, and while it's a pretty short game, it offers enough breadcrumbs to feel... uniquely intriguing. It's humorous, it's bold, it illustrates addiction in a pretty grotesque way, but there's something to that. If you get a chance, I'd easily recommend Ratshaker as a standout, especially for the low price. 7.8/10

Jogo que precisa ser anunciado com CGI em vez de trailer in-game já entrega o fracasso que continua sendo – maquiagem digital para esconder o vazio.

Eu jogo essa b*osta, mas sinceramente, não é com o mesmo apreço que jogo outros. O sentimento é de que, além da Giants Software nunca entregar o que deveria, o único objetivo é arrecadar dinheiro. Já estabeleci pra mim mesmo: qualquer jogo ou pacote adicional dessa empresa, antigo ou novo, é automaticamente não recomendado. Cansei dessa sacanagem disfarçada de franquia.

Não há evolução plausível pra justificar lançar um “novo” Farming Simulator a cada um ou dois anos. É sempre o mesmo jogo remendado, a mesma estrutura capenga, o mesmo motor gráfico engessado. E eu realmente não sei quem é pior: a Giants, que finge estar inovando, ou os jogadores que continuam dando palco pra esses malucos há pelo menos uns cinco anos.

Percebo que o FS25 é o retrato da estagnação. Falta otimização – o jogo engasga até em hardware moderno, não faz sentido! Tem bug de textura no solo (bastante notório e ridículo), iluminação incoerente e uma física realmente porca. Os veículos, que deveriam passar sensação de peso e tração, parecem feitos de papelão, quicando pelo mapa – impossível não comparar com o SnowRunner.

E, agora, resolveram “inovar” com pesca (risos). Só que pescar um peixe nesse jogo é como pescar um PNG na tela – não tem peso, não tem movimento, não tem graça nenhuma. É só mais um recurso vazio pra enfeitar o marketing.

A Giants vive de adicionar culturas novas e chamar isso de “evolução”, mas é tudo cosmético. As mecânicas são as mesmas, a IA continua burra, o som é reciclado, e os menus carecem de atenção. Eles empurram essas melhorias injustificáveis só pra sustentar um jogo que não tem acabamento.

No fim das contas, o FS25 só existe porque a comunidade segura o jogo nos ombros com mods – são os modders que corrigem, melhoram e até reinventam o que a Giants não tem competência ou vontade de fazer. Sem eles, o jogo desmoronava.

É a mesma velha m*erda embrulhada num marketing bonito. A empresa perdeu completamente o senso de autocrítica — e enquanto tiver gente comprando, eles vão continuar vendendo. Veremos a "mesma" bomba ser lançada em 2027.

[b] Nota: 6/10 [/b]

I've enjoyed hundreds of hours of Giant's FS games over the years and they keep improving, and FS25 is no different. The latest update introduces a gorgeous new map and fishing mechanics but even without that optional DLC the core game is excellent, add on some free maps like Silverrun Forest and there are alot of options for different gameplay styles available

Do you like large projects that require huge amounts of resources to complete, that changes as you contribute to it, and is visually updated - then FS's "contruction projects", an optional feature (that can be ignored if you just want to "farm") add that aspect, and boy it's so much fun

If you enjoy the process of building a "business" from the ground up that is here too - start small (even give yourself some debt to clear from the get go) and build up over in-game years until you own factories, production lines, land and bigger machines as you aim for that "$10,000,000 in the bank" achievement

Want to jump straight to a big farm with everything and just plow the fields? Go ahead, start off with tons of cash and go big off the bat, even add on the optional "Precision Farming" mod for extra realism if that's your thing - or if you like the realism on the lower end there are options to turn it all off, so no weeds, lime, plowing etc. Everyone is catered for

Speaking of mods - well this has plenty, to put it mildly. Are they essential / required? Nope. Do they enhance the game? For sure! Mod support is even part of the main menu, no external software required, and they don't break achievements. There are websites dedicated to them and Giants even supply the software on their website so you can start making your own

What's missing? Hmm, maybe some of the repairing & restoration gameplay in Farmer's Dynasty? But one could argue even that is kinda there with it's construction projects...

Overall it's a very polished high quality game (is "game" the right word?) and I've enjoyed every moment of it - never had any issues with performance, nor has it crashed, nor have I experienced any bugs. If that doesn't qualify as an overall positive experience, I don't know what does

Kurze Rezension: Ich kann mich den anderen Anschließen, die sagen, das das Spiel Potenzial hat aber noch ausbaufähig ist.

Lange Rezension:

Performance:
Ich spiele seit ungefähr zwei Monaten das Spiel. Ich finde auch, das sich das Spiel deutlich verbessert hat. Die Performance hat sich zum Beispiel in den zwei Monaten merklich verbessert. Ich habe nicht mehr FPS Drops in die 20ziger bis 30ziger, zumindest wenn nicht eine Monsterherde einen Jagd. 
Später im Spiel gibt es die Auftraggeberin Valeria, die eine Quest hat, wo man drei verschiedene Funkmasten auslöst. Sobald ich diese ausgelöst habe, musste ich und mein Mitspieler (ich bin der Host) die Beine in die Hand nehmen, weil sonst binnen weniger Sekunden meine FPS von ungefähr 50 FPS auf 5 FPS. Mein Mitspieler hat ein etwas leistungsschwächeren PC, zumindest bei der CPU (Ryzen 7 3.Gen) und er hat genauso FPS Einbrüche wie ich mit meinem i5 13600K. Es liegt nicht daran, das meine oder seine CPU auf 100% springen, sondern eher an der Engine, die auf diese Zombiemassen nicht klar kommt. 
Aber auch generell bei der Performance ist wirklich noch Luft nach oben. Ich spiele in WQHD (2560x1440) mit mittleren Einstellungen, ohne Hardware Raytracing und dem Potato Mode auf Niedrig mit 50-65 FPS (Einzelspieler) und 38-55 FPS (Coop, Host). 
(Update zum folgenden Baum FPS Problem, heute wurde das Problem mit der v1.5.6 bei mir behoben,  das ist ein gutes Beispiel dafür, das die Updates auch wirklich was verändern)
Auch ein großes Problem ist der Hunger nach VRAM. Das bemerke ich vor allem wenn ich Bäume fälle, weil mein VRAM permanent voll ist (im Schnitt 10700/11000MB VRAM) und beim abholzen von Bäumen kommt es leider des öfteren für ca. 25 Sekunden zu sehr starken Lags (bis jetzt nur im Einzelspieler Modus), laut MSI Afterburner braucht in dem Fall meine RTX 2080 Ti, die manuell übertaktet ist ca. 3-6 Sekunden pro Frame. Aber das Spiel fängt sich immer und ist nie bei mir gecrashed. Diese starken Lags können aber natürlich auch an meinem OC liegen, auch wenn ich dies nicht denke, weil das Spiel und andere Spiele sonst flüssig und ohne Probleme funktionieren. 
Für die, die sich fragen, welche Hardware man benötigt um auf höchsten Einstellungen in WQHD mit 60 FPS oder mehr zu spielen, man benötigt die Hardware von Geforce Now Ultimate. Ich habe es ausgetestet und habe mit den Zen 5 (16 Threads) und der RTX 4080 im Coop (1 Mitspieler und ich als Host) und im Einzelspieler diese Werte erreicht. Und wow sieht das Spiel schön aus wenn man die passende Hardware hat... Aber WICHTIG, es gibt momentan keine Steam Cloud für das Spiel, was ich als sehr problematisch ansehe. Weil man kann daher nicht mit Geforce Now mit seiner alten Welt spielen und wenn das Speichermedium, auf dem das Spiel ist kaputt geht, steht man vermutlich ohne Speicherungen seiner Spielstände da. Ich und mein Mitspieler konnten auch nicht einen Ordner oder Savegame Dateien vom Spiel finden, die man als Backup nutzen könnte, was z.B.  bei Satisfactory (was aber auch eine Steam Cloud hat) funktioniert. 

Gameplay:
An sich finde ich das Spiel vom Gameplay wirklich gut, die Waffen klingen gut, sehen gut aus und der Quest und Survivalaspekt reizt mich so sehr, das ich über die technischen Schwächen hinweg sehe. 
Man bemerkt natürlich, das das Spiel nicht vom Umfang an ein vollwertiges Spiel (Vollversion) heran kommt, aber es gibt genug Umfang finde ich. Ich spiele parallel auf einem Save im Einzelspieler und in einem anderen Save im Coop (2 Spieler) und habe noch reichlich Quests so wie es momentan aussieht vor mir, zum Kontext bis jetzt habe ich ungefähr 9 Stunden im Einzelspieler gespielt und den Rest (stand jetzt ungefähr 13 oder 14 Stunden) im Coop.  
Klar ist auch Bugs gibt es. Sei es, das getötete Tiere manchmal ein paar Meter mit mehreren Umdrehungen wegfliegen nach dem Erschießen oder das es Barriere bzw. Platzprobleme gibt. Ich meine damit, das man z.B. nicht ohne ducken wirklich gut beim schrägen Dach vom großen Haus, was die Veranda teils überdeckt lang laufen kann, weil der Spieler zu groß oder die Barriere um den Spieler zu groß ist. 
Sonst noch ein eher größerer Kritikpunkt ist, das Inventar. Mir passiert es sehr oft, das ich Items suche, aber diese erst nach mehrfachen hoch und runter scrollen entdecke. Auch ein Punkt wo man bemerkt, das es ein EA ist, ist das man z.B. keinen Rucksack hat (zumindest habe ich keinen bis jetzt gefunden oder habe bei anderen gesehen, das es diesen gibt). Am Anfang habe ich mir gedacht "wow, die sind mal wirklich großzügig mit dem Inventarplatz (100 Slots) und dem Zulässigem Gewicht (300 Kilo), aber mit Waffen, Ausrüstung, Proviant usw. wird der Platz wenn man ein bisschen dabei hat zunehmend sehr knapp. 
Auch muss ich im Punkt Inventar bemängeln, das wenn man z.B. nur noch 3 Kilo frei hat (297/300 Kilo) und dann z.B. ein Haus oder was anderes, was das Gewichtslimit durch die Itemgewichte übersteigen würden, im Nichts verschwinden. Ich meine damit, das ich als ich mein Haus abgerissen hatte, deutlich weniger Planken hatte, als ich eigentlich haben sollte, weil mein Gewichtslimit voll war (299,7/300 Kilo)
Das letzte was ich im Gameplay Bereich bemängeln muss, ist das im Einzelspieler es manchmal bei mir vorgekommen ist, das die Questmarkierungen nicht angezeigt wurden, wenn die Quest aktiv war. Meistens hat es geholfen, wenn ich das Spiel neugestartet habe. Manchmal musste ich aber eine andere Quest als aktiv setzen und mein Spiel neustarten und dann die vorherige Quest wieder auswählen, um die Markierung zu erhalten, 
Es fehlen auch Animationen bei anderen Spieler im Coop, z.B. wird das nachladen nicht animiert. Aber auch Waffenaufsätze oder das Nachtsichtgerät sind im Coop bei anderen Spieler nicht zu sehen
Positiv muss ich aber anmerken, das das Spiel über 4 Schwierigkeitsgrade verfügt und die Spielwelt stimmig und atmosphärisch ist.  

Thema KI und "Asset Flip"
Ich finde es nicht schlimm, das KI verwendet wurde. Die Sachen die mit KIs generiert wurden fügen sich, wie ich finde gut in die Spielwelt ein. 
Man bemerkt, das manche Sachen Assets sind, aber ich finde genauso wie die KI Inhalte, das die ausgewählten Assets sich gut ins Spiel einfügen und nicht störend sind.  

Zusammengefasst, kann ich nur sagen, das das Spiel leider zu früh in den Early Access gestartet ist und daher jetzt nur noch (laut SteamDB) mit ungefähr 15 aktiven Spieler, von Peak ungefähr 1500 Spielern auskommen muss. Aber das Konzept mit dem Survival und dem Quest Aspekt und dem optionalen PVP (man kann auch auf PVE umstellen) finde ich perfekt und auch bis auf die genannten Schwächen sehr gut umgesetzt. 
Abschließend kann ich euch nur empfehlen das Spiel jetzt oder in ein bis zwei Monaten auszutesten und euch ein eigenes Bild zu machen und wenn es euch nicht gefällt es zurückzugeben.

So I'd give this game a solid 7.5 out of 10 for where it's at....especially compared to most survival early access games. 

However...I think it's $10 over priced, right now anyways. There's definitely a lot you can do so idk what people are talking about who are saying there isn't much to do. BUT...people are right about the graphics. The graphics are GOOD, but definitely do not match the game play graphics in the videos. I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Every aspect of the game was fun and well executed. The exploration, paired with the great music and fantastic dialogue and characters, was super satisfying. I love open world investigation games like these, and this game nailed it. The vibes were just immaculate.

The most important part of an investigation game though: the story. It was convoluted just enough that it made me second guess myself all the time, I had to keep rethinking what I thought about the characters, their motivations... But at the same time, it was still coherent enough for me to form a good theory that fit most of the puzzle pieces, and was very close to the "truth". I was really satisfied with the ending. I also love that even with all clues collected, I wasn't 100% sure what happened until the trial. The best part is that it wasn't frustrating, it was engaging - which I feel is a thin line to tread. I also appreciate the game's setting. It's unfamiliar, which adds to the mystery and also helps to make exploration more fun.

What I enjoyed the most was the package as a whole - the fact that the game managed to combine a thrilling original story with everything else. Truly a hidden gem.

Je ne sais pas quel est mon problème avec les suites de FF XIII. 

Le fait qu'elles soient bugguées ? Un lore sous-exploité ? L'habitude un peu trop ancrée que les Final Fantasy offrent une happy end ? Un dernier opus particulièrement moche (hormis les cinématiques et les protagonistes) ?

En tout cas, le calvaire est enfin terminé.

Honnêtement, ils auraient pu sortir un jeu d'habillement de Lightning et ils n'auraient pas raté leur coup.  Au lieu de quoi, on a le droit à un ersatz d'histoire à grands renforts de Deus Ex. Ce monde en train de s'effondrer n'est pas franchement crédible : trop peu de gens qui se sont laissés allés au désespoir ou à la folie, y compris nos héros… ils ont eu cinq siècles pour, quand même. Ils n'ont littéralement aucune substance, émotionnellement c'est le point mort pour eux comme pour le joueur. Zéro budget pour écrire des dialogues ?

Je n'ai pas du tout aimé le gameplay, c'est mou. Alors on a le droit à des animations stylées quand on utilise certains pouvoirs, je dis pas.

Je n'ai aucun souci avec le death and retry quand il s'agit de diablolike ou roguelike, mais ici ? C'est juste une façon de rallonger artificiellement le temps de jeu. Pourtant, c'était pas bête cette histoire de pression sur le joueur à cause du temps limité dont on dispose.

La fin m'a également laissée plutôt indifférente. 

En bref, abstenez-vous si vous n'êtes pas masochiste.

I've played my share of VR brawlers, but my experience with GORN 2 on PC VR has been one of the most disheartening I've had in recent memory. It's immediately clear where this game’s priorities lie: it was designed and optimized almost exclusively for the standalone Meta Quest headsets, and the PC version suffers for it in almost every measurable way.

The Graphics: A Sacrificial Lamb
I never thought I'd say this about a PC game, but the graphics are, frankly, terrible. They scream "Quest port." The visual compression and low-resolution textures are so aggressively noticeable that they actively detract from the experience. This isn't a stylistic choice; it's a consequence of over-optimization, stripping the world of any detail or fidelity that a modern PC VR setup should be able to handle effortlessly. It makes the arenas feel cheap, hollow, and utterly uninspired.

The Gameplay: Clunky, Floaty, and Unrewarding
The heart of any combat game is the feel of the fight, and this is where GORN 2 truly falls apart.

Weightless Combat: Everything feels clunky and floaty. Swords, maces, and even enemies have no satisfying sense of weight or impact. Every swing is a non-committal flail, making the violence feel cartoonishly light rather than brutally visceral.

Unchallenging & Repetitive: The combat is far too easy and becomes monotonous almost instantly. There’s no genuine challenge, and as a result, no real reward. I wasn't fighting for survival; I was merely going through the motions.

Replay Value is Non-Existent: Once the initial novelty of the goofy physics wears off (which happens fast), there's nothing compelling to bring you back. Without satisfying combat or visual appeal, the game is little more than a short-lived husk—a product with no real soul.

Ship, Inc. is one of those “just a bit more” games that sneaks up on you: simple, colorful, and oddly satisfying… until you realize Day 50 feels exactly like the Day 1 tutorial. I played entirely in hardcore mode, unlocked every upgrade, and snagged all the non-grindy achievements (43/48 total). So trust me, I’ve spent enough time in the warehouse to earn my packing license, even though I didn't reach that shiny 100% yet.

The game looks great. It's bright, clean visuals with a fun art style and smooth mouse controls. The upgrade system adds a nice sense of progression, and I appreciated the little bits of humor (some of those bills made me giggle way more than they should’ve). I didn’t encounter any of the bugs others mentioned, likely thanks to the devs being very responsive. The good news is, Ship, Inc. tells you right away if it’s for you since the loop doesn’t really evolve, so you’ll know within the first hour whether to keep going or refund it.

That’s also the main issue, though: there’s no real evolution. Once you’ve upgraded everything, the gameplay becomes pure repetition. No story, no consequences for choices (like selling stolen goods), and achievements that border on grindy nightmares. On hardcore, it’s stressful; on normal, it’s borderline sleepy. Great as a background task or podcast game, but not something you’ll get lost in. The cat is cute but more of a nuisance unless you buy its pillow, and the physics occasionally go haywire (looking at you, spasm-truck of boxes).

Ship, Inc. is a solid little time-waster. It’s fun for a few hours, scratches that idle-sim itch, and works perfectly as a cozy “between big games” break. Just don’t expect it to keep you hooked for long or to evolve beyond its humble cardboard roots. Definitely only worth grabbing on sale.

C. Kane is an... interesting game to review.

From a gameplay standpoint, the game stands. The RPG mechanics are clear, present, your party is small and every character has a decent amount of strengths and weaknesses (except Leland, who has no weakness), and the bosses have some interesting gimmicks at times. It's challenging, but never too insanely difficult -- I think I died once in the entire game while fighting the hidden end game boss. The game is only about two to three hours long if you choose to explore the world, less if you just run through.

When it comes to writing and story, C. Kane is a love it or hate it. One thing that would DEFINITELY increase your enjoyment of the game is seeing the film Citizen Kane, as there are a few amazing references to the film and world. However, the writing occassionally gets a little flat, and just starts seeming weird for the sake of being weird. I wish there was a little more substance to the story, as I felt like it had potential that it didn't use.

The soundtrack is actually my biggest gripe in the game. It's very limited, and all the loops are very short. The songs are hilarious at first, but quickly become repetitive -- especially during some of the longer fights.

Overall, if you like the trailer and love puns and Citizen Kane, you'll likely enjoy the game. If you don't find the trailer funny, don't bother. It's a good game, but not one that I'd recommend to everyone I know.

This game is amazing, you already know that, everybody told you that. I have two minor qualms, only because I love the design so much:

1. Because of how the class is designed around specific gimmicks, there are certain classes where you really do not want to add more cards to your deck. This is so common in many roguelike deckbuilders out there but not present in something like Slay the Spire because in StS your core deck is ass. In Diceomancer, your core deck is sometimes "good enough" and you really only want a handful of other very specific cards. This makes runs feel very samey for some classes (mostly red ones).

2. The balancing can be a bit all over the place, but it's understandable due to the dice mechanic. Runs are usually more on the easy side.

3 (extra I guess). The game has a very cool mechanic which is this corruption that follows you, which means unlike most roguelikes of its kind, you can actually backtrack in the map! However, there is little incentive to BE in corruption. I can't be the first one who tried it. If you really love a game, you will wonder what happens if you do this thing, and a good developer will usually reward you, "hey, thanks for wondering around! Here's a bit of content for your trouble". Here, the coolest answer would be "cool new cards" or "cool new secrets" or "cool hidden enemies". However, the game just gets harder and harder and you get nothing major from corruption. I understand you can't backtrack forever, but this is lost potential.

Незважаючи на те, що до свого релізу проєкт дійшов аж в 2022, особисто ознайомитися з цим твором цифрового мистецтва видалось лише зараз, три роки опісля.

Розпочинав гру в очікуванні естетичного задоволення від аудіо-візуального наповнення та імерсивного сприйняття, а закінчував із інтелектуальним оргазмом. Перше занурення в цей всесвіт буде відчуватися саме таким як він виглядає: чужорідним, ворожим, небезпечним, незрозумілим. Але його магнетизм, цілісність і естетика, не випустять зі своїх липких обіймів, ні на мить. 

Сюжет, мотивація, лор всесвіту, абсолютно все в цьому творі буде оповідатися лише через візуальну складову. Не буде жодних записок, текстів і поводирів, які введуть в суть перепетій. Тому увага до дрібниць та просторове мислення неабияк допоможуть, адже найголовніші відповіді будуть на самому видному місці і "великим шрифтом". Але ніякого закладеного розробниками порогу занурення не буде, все залежатиме лише від вас особисто. Головний персонаж(і), як і власне ви, розпочинаєте на одному рівні світосприйняття, і так само разом поступово починаєте його розуміти. Бо він як і ви, щойно з'явилися в цьому місці, в цьому світі. 

Розробники протягом всієї хронології будуть переслідувати одну ідею, думку, яка мейнстрімом в'ючного мотка, розкручуватиметься, аж до фінальної сцени. Але і це не все! Рівень метафоричного символізму, підводного рифу, вразить вас своєю невимовною глибиною і комплексністю. Він буде присутній скрізь, пронизаний в кожному клаптику органіки на кератинових стінах, в маленьких кімнатах та механізмах. Це ще одна комплексна історія, таємне подвійне дно, приховане під багатьма мазками іншої. Але це осяяння прийде згодом, за філіжанкою чаю, коли ви переварюватимете отриманий закінчений досвід та завершений на останній сторінці артбук.

Артбук в цій історії є обов'язковою складовою, тим пазликом який з'єднає дві половинки картини в єдине полотно та заповнить всі відсутні елементи. Все через вирізані дві локації, одна з яких є сюжетно і лорно важливою, без якої сприйняття сегментується. Саме її опис довершить ваш умовивід основної повісті.

Це як раз той випадок, коли говоримо про ігри як мистецтво. Сучасне цифрове мистецтво, з усіма атрибутами споглядання, осмислення та інтерпретації. Автор(и) сюжетного і смислового наповнення, не побоюсь цього слова, справжні генії. А дизайнери візуальної складової взагалі надлюди, ті самі біороботи з далекої технологічної цивілізації. Якщо вам гра здаватиметься важкою для розуміння, то не спішить її закидати, не здавайтеся, даруйте їй другий і всі послідуючі шанси. Це одна із тих історій, яка варта бути розказаною. Окрема подяка розробникам за українську локалізацію.

The atmosphere is outstanding. It could have been a great horror walking simulator with puzzle aspects. I want to recommend with a thumbs up, but I can't.

Here is what kills it:
- The combat is frustratingly cumbersome. Everything is slow. That includes stashing ammo, reloading, switching weapons. Everything has an animation that prevents you from running. Fighting more than 1 enemy is challenging in an unrewarding way. I feel like given the setting and atmosphere, I would have preferred having no weapon and playing hide and avoid the monsters. You can skip most of the encounters, but when it is unavoidable, you'll wish you were playing any other game.
- The story's pace is slow and bucket shaped, meaning the high points are at the beginning and at the end. It has a very long middle part filled with linear puzzles, redundant environment and out of place combat. It's a linear game where areas become inaccessible the more you progress, so wandering and exploring is not on the menu. Nothing is said about the setting and the story. You have to imagine it yourself. I personally like that, but you may not.
- The game is ridiculously short for the price. Just check my play record. at least 2 hours is me getting lost in the beginning and dying to enemies. Don't get unless it drops to 5$.

That being said, I would keep an eye out for another game set in this universe.

Вторая попытка разработчика сделать Х1.   
Поэтому разрабы наступают на одни и те же грабли.   
1.  В игре НЕТ случайных событий.  Т.е. Пришелец никогда случайно не выстрелит в АЗС, которая взорвавшись может уничтожить как твоих солдат, так и других пришельцев.   
2.  Крайне замкнутый интеллект.   Если в Х1  пришельцы шарились по всей карте.  Входили или выходили из разбитого корабля.  Даже на шум выходил кто-то типа посмотреть - кто там бродит рядом?  Тут, они тупо сидят.  И вся твоя логистика сводится к одному!   Зачищаешь карту и тупо выстраиваешь перед дверьми корабля весь свой отряд.  Хоть УСРИСЬ, хоть топай, хоть в бубен бей,  никто из корабля не высунется. 
3.  Ваншоты.  Просто ваншоты.   Твои бойцы постоянно мажут, а пришельцы, даже тупые, просто ваншотят.   
4.  Корабли пришельцев при катастрофе не разрушаются.  В Х1,  после долгого боя или в зависимости от того, каким оружием НЛО сбивали,  оно могло упасть либо с минимальным повреждениями,  либо анигилироваться до состояния 20 трупов и 1 пришелец, раненый спрятался в сарае и ты его ищешь по всей карте.  Зато потом, в следующий раз, ты используешь не убойные ракеты, а пару пушек, чтобы от корабля что-то осталось для сбора крафта.   
5.  Укрытий НЕТ.   Встать за угол, это всё равно, что встать в открытом поле.   Всякие мешки, поддоны, стоги сена - НЕ РАБОТАЮТ как укрытие.  Тебе надо реально на 2 клетки заходить за стену.  Это бред полный.  
6.  Нельзя изучить оружие пришельцев и затем его использовать.  
Вобщем погонять можно,  но многое жутко бесит.   И это часть 2.

Consume Me starts off pretty easy to get a grasp of. The gameplay is pretty much repetitive tasks centred around the protagonist's attempt at being an "all-rounder child of immigrant Asian parents that is smart, hot, and thin". Obviously no matter how hard you try to get everything right, something has to give because it's impossible to do it all. The game however does not go in this direction as after about 8 hours of playing, it suddenly pivots towards finding Jesus and allowing him in your life....THAT is the key to doing it all. Some reviews say this is just a small part of the game and does not affect the overall story or gameplay, but you actually get to progress quicker and easier if you choose the religious activities such as reading the bible or saying a prayer instead of reading a fitness magazine or calling your boyfriend (which are all very normal things for a college kid to want to do). The only content warning in the beginning of the game is for eating disorders and diet-related trauma, but nothing about religious trauma,   so I was very disappointed to see how it isn't being treated as a serious matter by the game makers but also that its Christian ties were not mentioned ANYWHERE in the game's synopsis. Unless you read the reviews, you would be going into this game blind. I've stopped playing because it was really irking me, but Steam would't do anything about it because I've played for too long.

A really charming and creative autobiographical strategy game! My one criticism is that I wish the marketing would've made it more clear that there is a religious aspect to the later part of the game - due to the nature of it coming in near the end, I feel like it wasn't really explored in full, and I'm not expecting the game to avoid Christianity emtirely what with it being important to the creators life but it does come in quite suddenly and is presented as a saving force for the character, which caught me off guard. It is mentioned in the epilogue offhandedly but I feel like going from nothing to a fully voiced sermon was quite a ramp up, and I would've appreciated knowing that would be an aspect of the game going into it. Still, a very enjoyable game, and one that handles the rest of its themes very well imo!

It's a good game that isn't receiving nearly enough attention.

It's a factory game, but it's significantly different from other factory games. Your factory is run by robotic ants, and you dictate what they'll do by drawing trails. It's even different from factory games centered on robotic workers, like Autonauts or OddSparks.

While it contains no actual programming, it's very programming-adjacent. You need to think not just about the "normal" case for a production building, but all the ways it can fail. What happens when it runs out of one of the input materials? What happens when the output is full? What if an ant gets old? This is the kind of defensive mind-set you need to be a good programmer.

Unfortunately, a lot of players making YouTube videos for the game do *not* think about these things, and design trails that will lock up if things go wrong, sometimes catastrophically.

An important mechanic is that ants get old and die. Basic small workers only last 5 minutes, but some advanced ants last 10, 15, 30 or 45 minutes. You can either recycle an aging ant into raw materials, or upgrade it to a more advanced ant. Newly upgraded ants start with a full lifespan. A big part of the game is creating a necropolis, where you can appropriately process all ants near the end of their life.

While most ants die of old age, some don't. You start with 4 immortal ants. There's a mid-game ant called the Pod Worker that can live forever, provided you recharge it periodically with Energy Orbs. In the very, very late game you can manufacture more of the immortal ants.

At the start of the game all you have is Small Workers. It takes a while to unlock things like the recycler and trails that can detect that an ant is old.

Small Workers and Workers require no resources to make.  Your Queen continuously lays Larva provided you feed her with Energy Orbs, which are a renewable resource. More advanced ants require materials to make. You get the full cost of an ant back when you recycle it, but not if it dies of old age first. It's thus very important to reliably recycle more advanced ants.

It's remarkably easy to screw up and have a mass die-off, even if you're careful. The simplest version of this is if your recycler gets full. That can create a long line of ants waiting and dying of old age because the recycler isn't working.

It has a lot less logistics in it that most factory games. Mainly because Storage buildings have Dispensers with a near-infinite range. A Storage can send its output anywhere  on the same island instantly. The major aspect of logistics in the game isn't moving materials, it's routing ants where they need to go.

It has *some* logistics. You unlock additional islands as you progress, and a Storage can't put a Dispenser on another island. Initially ants must carry materials between islands, but later in the game there are catapults that can launch materials to a Storage on another island, provided it's within the Catapult's range.

It's much higher maintenance than most factory games. Ants going out and harvesting materials tend to exhaust the deposits they're collecting quite quickly in the early game. A harvest loop can end up with a full storage if you haven't taken precautions, and you generally need to transfer the results somewhere by hand eventually. It's also important to inspect new constructions periodically in case you made a mistake that didn't show up right away.

I ended up re-designing my factory frequently. This biggest thing driving this was the discovery of new ant types, which meant I had to enlarge my necropolis on a regular basis. Re-designing to handle the immature queens (called Gynes) was a huge headache, since that requires combining 6 different kinds of ants.

One complaint I have is that the game doesn't really have a proper ending. There's a "Instinct" dialog that progresses as the game goes along, giving you a series of goals. Eventually it just says "Welp, that's it, no more instincts, thanks for playing." That's the whole end of the game.

While it's no Factorio or Satisfactory, it's still one of the better factory games out there.

[h1]Mein persönliches Ubisoft-Comeback…[/h1]

… auch wenn es sich eventuell nur auf dieses eine, großartige Spiel beschränkt.
Mit Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag kam ich 2013 in den „Genuss“ der damaligen Uplay-Beta, die nicht nur meinen Spielstand bei 80% zerschossen hat, sondern gleichzeitig keine Cloud-Saves funktionierten.

Aus purer Frustration habe ich damals Spiel und Launcher deinstalliert – und mir geschworen, nie wieder etwas von diesem Laden zu kaufen.

Der fehleranfällige Client und die sich ständig wiederholende Ubisoft-Formel gingen mir ohnehin derart auf die Nerven, dass ich dem Publisher über zehn Jahre lang den Rücken kehrte – und ganz ehrlich: Ich habe nichts vermisst.


[h2]14 Jahre später …[/h2]

Ja, so viele Jahre sind seit "The Forgotten Sands" vergangen – eine verdammt lange Zeit für einen PoP-Fan wie mich, der seit 1989 jeden Teil gespielt und selbst den schwächeren noch etwas Gutes abgewinnen konnte.

Zum Release von The Lost Crown häuften sich die positiven Reviews, und langsam kam Vorfreude auf. Trotzdem saß der alte Ubi-Frust tief – ich konnte mich einfach nicht dazu durchringen, wieder Geld in Ubisofts Hände zu legen.

Doch dieses Jahr war es so weit: 17,49 € für die Complete Edition.
Also dachte ich mir: „Scheiß drauf, ich probier’s einfach.“

Und was soll ich sagen? Ja, der Client startet mit – aber einmal richtig eingestellt, läuft er still und leise im Hintergrund. Keine Abstürze, kein Drama. Einziger Wermutstropfen: Man muss zwingend die Ubi-Cloud nutzen – Steam-Cloud-Saves wären mir lieber gewesen.


[h2]Die Rückkehr des Prinzen[/h2]

Das Spiel entführt dich in ein mystisches, zeitverzerrtes Persien, wo nichts so ist, wie es scheint. Du spielst Sargon, ein junger Krieger der legendären Unsterblichen, der in einen uralten Konflikt hineingezogen wird, als der Prinz des Reiches entführt wird.

Auf der Suche nach ihm betrittst du den heiligen Berg Qaf – einen Ort, an dem Zeit und Raum ihre Bedeutung verlieren. Jede Stufe tiefer ins Labyrinth enthüllt neue Geheimnisse, vergessene Götter und eine Geschichte, die weit mehr mit Sargon selbst zu tun hat, als er ahnt.

Was als Rettungsmission beginnt, wird schnell zu einer Reise durch Zeit, Identität und Schicksal – erzählt in einer Welt, die mit jeder neuen Fähigkeit ein Stück größer, gefährlicher und faszinierender wird.

„Wie es im Spiel so schön heißt: ‚Niemand ist je herausgekommen… Vielleicht, weil nie jemand wirklich hineingegangen ist.‘ – ein Satz, der perfekt beschreibt, wie sich der heilige Berg Qaf anfühlt: geheimnisvoll, verführerisch und gefährlich zugleich.“

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3585690496

[h2]Gameplay & Steuerung[/h2]

The Lost Crown ist ein 2,5D-Metroidvania, das klassisches Plattforming mit modernen Action-Elementen verbindet. Du steuerst Sargon, einen agilen Krieger, der sich mit präziser, butterweicher Steuerung durch labyrinthartige Areale bewegt.

Das Spiel lebt vom Trial-&-Error-Prinzip – gerade die Plattform-Passagen fordern gnadenloses Timing und fühlen sich oft wie die eigentlichen Endgegner an. Die Bosskämpfe stehen dem aber kaum nach: selbst auf niedrigeren Schwierigkeitsgraden verlangen sie Konzentration, Mustererkennung und Geduld.

Die Welt von Qaf ist riesig, voller Geheimnisse und clever miteinander verknüpft. Neue Kräfte öffnen Wege zu zuvor unerreichbaren Orten – klassisches Backtracking, aber motivierend umgesetzt.

Zur Ausstattung gehören Amulette, Athra-Kräfte, Ausrüstungs-Upgrades, Nebenquests und jede Menge Sammlerstücke, die Entdeckergeist belohnen. Knapp an der Grenze zur Überdosierung ;)

• Präzise Steuerung, flüssige Animationen
• Anspruchsvolles Plattforming & faire, aber harte Bosse
• Tiefes Erkundungssystem mit motivierendem Fortschritt
• Viele Anpassungsmöglichkeiten durch Amulette & Kräfte
• Starker Wiederspielwert für Perfektionisten

https://youtu.be/46vlMczyXxA

Das Spiel belohnt Geduld, Neugier und Beherrschung der Mechanik – und zeigt, dass ein paar Leute bei Ubisoft doch noch wissen, wie sich echtes Gameplay-Handwerk anfühlen kann.

Du kannst sowohl mit Controller als auch Maus und Tastatur spielen. Für mich persönlich ist das Xbox Gamepad die erste Wahl.


[h2]Grafik & Sound[/h2]

Das Spiel geht optisch einen ganz neuen Weg in der Reihe – bunt, stilisiert und deutlich weniger düster als frühere Teile. Ehrlich gesagt war mir das anfangs fast zu farbenfroh, aber je länger ich spielte, desto stimmiger wirkte der Stil. Heute bin ich überzeugt: Gerade diese Mischung macht es zu einem der besten Teile der Reihe.

Die Animationen sind flüssig, das Art-Design durchdacht und technisch läuft alles sauber und stabil.

Beim Sound wird abgeliefert: persische Klänge treffen auf orchestrale Power, der Soundtrack trägt das Spiel und schafft echte Atmosphäre. Die englische Version wirkt teils etwas blass und unbeteiligt, während die deutsche Vertonung überraschend solide gelungen ist – nicht perfekt, aber stimmiger und emotionaler.

For years I avoided playing Dead Rising 4 due to the negative reviews and word of mouth.
 
I finally decided to give it a try and found that while much of the criticism is valid it’s still a Dead Rising game and one that I had a lot of fun with.
 
To address the negatives first, yes it’s true that DR4 is lacking the heart and soul of the previous games.
 
Many staples of the series like the game loop & timer, psychopaths, survivor escort missions and multiple endings have been removed and replaced with more generic gameplay.
 
Frank West also has a new voice actor and the writing for his character felt out of place. Frank is now an arrogant a-hole who quips one-liners nonstop and will screw over anybody and everybody to get the scoop, contrasting the previous games.
 
There is a new “investigate the clues” mechanic that I see people complain about but honestly didn’t mind it, I felt it helped to connect to the story better and flesh out the details.
 
As for the story, it was pretty weak and uninspired. No spoilers but there is a lead into a big reveal that ended up being underwhelming. The final boss fight was the worst in the entire series by far.
 
The ending itself was just OK, it felt a bit anti-climactic. I found out later there is only 1 ending instead of multiple like the previous games. If you want the “better” ending you need to buy the Frank Rising DLC. Weak.
 
For the positives, it’s still a Dead Rising game, so you have an unlimited amount of zombies to kill in a myriad of different ways along with an impressive list of weapons.
 
Also present are the crazy weapon and vehicle combinations, a detailed map to explore with lots of collect-a-thon type gameplay, hundreds of different outfits to try on.
 
There are survivors to rescue, the catch being the survivors always spawn in the same spots which felt weak. You don’t escort them back to the safehouse either, it’s no escorting at all or only a short distance until they are “safe”.  
 
For a game of this size the load times are impressive, from first boot to playing the open map its quick and seamless.
 
While Dead Rising 4 is without a doubt the weakest entry in the series its still a lot of fun, especially if you go into the game with tempered expectations.
 
Go into this knowing its Dead Rising lite and you’ll have a good time.

This game is a lot like old school Heros of Might and Magic, but the combat is auto-battler style, which for me is a huge bonus. 

When I used to play HOMM, I would micro-manage my combat early on. This would make me agonize over losing just a few units and sometimes I would reload and try to replay the fight. In this game the auto-battler takes all but the big picture decisions out of your hand and THIS IS HOW A REAL GENERAL WOULD FEEL IN BATTLE. You train your units and position them and hope for the best. 

The auto-battling also makes the late game a breeze. In HOMM and games like Age of Wonders, late game battles can be a slog, especially if they aren't the most important battles but you have to make sure you don't lose too many units. In Songs of Silence, the battle just happens. Your general can change the tide through the use of "spell-like" cards but a big chunk of your performance is up to your units. Again, this is what it would be like in real life for a general trying to direct an army.

Aside from the auto-battling, the artwork is gorgeous. It's bold and colorful and the character design is weird and feels actually magical. It's It feels truly original its not just "dwarves, orcs and fairies'. They have created a strange and vibrant world in Songs of Silence.

It feels like it SHOULD make things weird if you dog on someone over videochat (The MC gets really worked up about teasing the Grim Reaper/Casper, you do not have the choice to act chill and lean into the narrative of imminent death) and then call them a babygirl to their face. I think this type of thing is fine and pretty funny as part of the fan community, but when the game itself indulges it feels like you spoil the joke. 

While there are a fair bit of dialogue options, which I do appreciate, the MC occasionally gets locked into dialogue choices that feel very immature. Considering the amount of character customization the game offers, which I greatly enjoyed, those moments when options are taken away from you feel very frustrating. 

I've read other reviews where people seem to understand the MC as being edgy, which I suppose makes sense, but considering the story is about you own looming death you have very little opportunity to lament the fact or have much of a genuine conversation about it.

Without spoiling too much for those who still feel drawn to play it for themselves, there is quite a huge tone shift between the characters at some point. For me the romance didn't land at all, but for you it might. 

The game was not boring, I felt compelled to see the story through and I took care to solve the mystery to get what I assume is the good ending, but yeah. If you're looking at the chatroom format and thinking the game will be closer in maturity to the level of Mystic Messenger (Which I wouldn't call an overly mature game anyway, but at least it's serviceable) then this is not it. If you're looking for your next anime boy crush and some backstory for your self insert, then this game is probably for you! The art is very nice throughout, systems worked fine and without any bugs, and there's a level of customization that should make the MC at least visually appealing to any player

I hope to see more from this developer, as they've proven themselves capable of creating a nicely functioning game with some very neat assets. This time it just wasn't for me.

So, this is a weird review to write. I played this game a lot, and... it's my kind of game in many ways. I love StS, I love deck building, and adventures. 

But unless you're a die hard card game player for a game like this, and even then, I can't recommend this game.

The basic gameplay loop isn't terrible... but the game system is terribly convoluted, and many of the fine detail mechanics aren't obvious. I played it through the first time on Roguelite mode on the Hard difficulty setting, and had a few close calls as I got to know the game, but then hit a point where my decks got good and just kinda soared through the last half of act 3 and all of act 4.

And, the main problem with the game is that it's all balancing on a knife's edge with difficult to track mechanics. Both you and the AI are usually playing an all or nothing game. You either trounce their whole team, or find yourself killed in one hit. If you're playing on Roguelike mode, that means that character is dead forever. If not... the game is incredibly easy.

Simply put, the game balance is off. Either the game is too easy with a very convoluted progression system, or it's too hard to understand to play at the highest level and isn't fun.

Many mechanics in game aren't described at all, and there's no way to know the order of operations of different effects. You've no idea how your cards and abilities interact sometimes until you play them, and some are so poorly worded that I've no idea what they really do. 

Games like this live and die by their mechanical precision, and this one doesn't cut it.

But, if you don't feel the need to push yourself that hard, and just want to kill some monsters... I guess if you've finished StS and want something a little different? Nah, just get StS

I love every Agatha Christie game, and I'm happy to see Microids Studio bringing those novels to life with a fun twist by adding additional characters to their games. Death on the Nile is one of Agatha Christie's famous novels, where you follow the famous Hercule Poirot as he solves the mysterious death; however, this time, he is paired with detective Jane Royce, who has her own mission to find the people who murdered her friend. The two detectives cross paths and join forces to solve the mystery. Even if you know the original story, the game still has additional mysteries on the plate and two different endings.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3584699278

The dual protagonist and the switching between them is something I've been enjoying recently, as I see the events from different points of view and how each character analyzes them. The game has nine chapters, alternating between playing as Jane and Poirot, with a couple of chapters allowing you to play with both characters, switching between them as you investigate the scene. There are two epilogues, depending on your actions and relationships with the other characters. The good part is that once you beat the game once, you'll have access to choose which chapter you want to replay. You'll also unlock the collectables room, where all the golden mustaches you collected will unlock a beautiful artwork, and the rewards are worth it. The soundtracks will be unlocked as you collect the golden records throughout the game.  
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3584699188

The puzzles were not extremely difficult, but some of them were unique, what I didn't like is the controls, sometimes it is very cluncky, I tried both keyboard+mouse, and a controller, I had to alternate between both, but the controller is a little bit more toleratable when it comes to solving the puzzles as you have to slide and push items most of the time. The dicing menu and connecting the evidence are the same as the previous games; however, the additional section is discovering each character's background and connection to the other characters. It was fun trying to find everything. The character's style wasn't bad, but I enjoyed the scenery more; the music is good as well, fitting the 700's atmosphere.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3584699161

Pros:
+Interesting story with a new twist.
+Dual protagonist. 
+Choices and consequences.
+Beautliful soundtracks.
+Filling character profiles by speaking to them and discovering their secrets.
+Fully voiced and amazing Voice-overs.
+Good game length. (Total of nine chapters and two epilogues)
+Two endings.
+Collectables (Two types. Will unlock artwork as well as soundtracks)
+Mind-map
+Chapter select.
+Steam achievements.

Cons:
-No manual save.

Although the significant consequences were all based on Jane's chapters, the game is still a good tribute to Hercule Poirot. I enjoyed it, and it took me around 28 hours to beat it once. However, keep in mind that I was exploring everything and taking my time to enjoy every part of the game. I always recommend Agatha Christie games to everyone, especially those who enjoy detective games.

险胜的及格分，断断续续耗时一个月才通关，非常不尊重玩家时间的一次改编。现版本存在两大弊病不容忽视，第一个是烂到令人发指的引导系统。游戏并非没有引导，点开脑图会指出需要继续找证人谈话或找线索等。但是，这个证人和线索到底在哪里呢？比如，第七章需要为鹦鹉找一碟花生，但花生在哪完全未知，也就是说你得在豪华游轮上下四层的巨大空间内里去大海捞针！（这里我直接报答案在酒吧里潘宁顿坐的旁边）实在难以想象这是2025年能出现的游戏设计，除了恶心玩家经常不知道干嘛没有任何作用。特别是我同期正在打KCD2DLC，即使找个小物件人家的指引也是给你领到位的，对比惨烈。这不是3A和独游的制作问题，而是你有没有去考虑玩家体验的问题。

第二个是作为一个推理游戏，解谜和推理部分的占比竟达到惊人的7:3，还要狂塞一堆构思小游戏。解谜和小游戏难度颇高、耗时巨大的同时，已经完全和时代脱轨，像在玩20年前的赛伯利亚之谜。另一方面，谜题又与主线案情毫无关联，简直就是外包出去做的益智小游戏，产生一种你短剧正刷得起劲突然强插一段广告才能解锁下文的既视感，把你想体验剧情的热忱给冲得稀巴烂。你是真不明白冲着波洛和案件名号来的玩家在期待什么吗？还是揣着制作经费装糊涂？难道不是推理，不是原著深邃的人性分析和波澜壮阔的剧情？（为了迎合政确毁掉前作埋下的伏笔，再度软重启将女主改成了同性恋黑人大妈。同样的创作人员会亲手糟蹋自己的成果吗？我好像突然明白了什么……）建议至少学恶魔之女给小游戏加个可跳过选项，不排除有少数老派解谜玩家好这口“沉浸感”，反正我是受不了。这两大问题加不能跳的墨迹对话把水时长做到了极致，差不多越过10h这个节点琳内特险被砸才开始热起来，玩家更可能早在撑到这前就卸载逃跑了吧。唯一值得表扬的小游戏在第六章，又是逛遍开罗街道的风景又玩起跟踪和密室逃脱，给了我一点Hitman的感觉。

当然本作肯定不是一无是处，就只论这3/10的推理部分还是到位了，颅内推理的连线和选择题很清晰，新增的心理复现还原犯罪也还不错。（偷听系统只能说复刻了波洛无视他人隐私之作风）制作确实增大了投入，夜店、旅馆、轮船、神庙、开罗等开阔场景轮番上阵，视觉体感上比前作列车狭窄空间丰富许多（但这点对引导起到副作用），bgm70s迪斯科和爵士乐明显花了心思。倒二章的原著结局全篇最佳，刻画出犯人不为人知的脆弱面，基本符合了我个人期待。最后的改编结局玩了个平行宇宙，走私仇路线能扮演波洛展示其感性光辉，走理智线能对Spire集团有更完备的结构分析（尽管这个线索墙的引导再次烂到令人发指）。最后两章的收尾营造出某种莫名悲壮的宿命感，还算漂亮，一定程度上挽回了前期颓势。

关于剧情本身的不满：我不知道为什么要把原著里“全动机”这个设定给削了。我记得贝斯纳医生的嗓子是被琳内特毁的，而莎乐美写的书也遭到了她的恶评。[spoiler]肆无忌惮的富家千金栽在爱上更令人怜惜[/spoiler]女主线的剧情很平庸，首先是将首富家族和邪恶组织联系的阴谋论太俗套，然后是案情和手法都很敷衍，全程都只能“浮”在原著剧情之外，让路易斯去敲诈职业杀手更是画蛇添足。游戏质量本身并不低，而是制作重心发生了偏移，钱没有花在刀刃上，衬得前作的成功沦为一次无心插柳。不管是制作组乐意再出几个补丁（跳解谜、跳对话、强引导），还是后续有出比较详尽的攻略，都能预测到评价是有回暖趋势的，所以先打个差评放在这里吧。（作为童年阴影读物，sad）最后，无论读过原著与否，都推荐去看看78版的电影，你不会后悔的。

Este videojuego se basa en una leyenda urbana de Taiwán donde tomaremos el control de un grupo de jóvenes universitarios que se enfrentan al implacable espíritu de una mujer que fue asesinada dentro del campus de la universidad.

Le recomiendo el juego a aquellas personas que disfrutan del terror asiático, siempre y cuando lo consigan a un buen precio porque es un producto entretenido, pero dura aproximadamente unas 4-6 horas.
