Honest review by me, a man who dropped out of high school and has absolutely no book smarts whatsoever or any knowledge in Aerospace, Engineering, etc… 

TLDR; The game is amazing, 10/10. Lot’s to learn to be able to keep playing. Be prepared to fail and learn a lot. The tutorial is semi helpful, but consider yourself to be on your own and do your own research to survive. Loads of content that can get you to be very creative.

I’ll start off by saying this game requires a passion to want to learn more about how everything works within the game. As someone who knows nothing about science and such, I have no idea what I’m doing and have perished many, many times… With each failure, I learned how to survive a little longer. Being just over 50 hours into this, I finally have a pressurized habitat balanced with Nitrogen and Oxygen so I don’t suffocate and fall unconscious! It only took 50 hours! Tutorials are hard to come by and guides are outdated since this new update. The learning curve is intense and requires lots of trial and error.

I do have a lot of passion when it comes to space and science, but never could get myself to actually do the school to pursue a career(s) in such a vast field of knowledge and learning. I have never played a game where I have done so much reading and note taking. I literally have a notebook next to me when I play to keep track of what has worked and what has failed. For example, pressurizing pipes and filtration of gasses, air locks inputting and outputting specific gasses, and logic on how to automatically angle solar panels to follow the sun! The list goes on! I still have yet to grow a single potato. I’m struggling there.

This is not an easy survival crafter. Dedication is required. I am not sure what’s fueling me to keep playing, but it is certainly scratching an itch in my semi smooth brain. I have no idea how realistic this is compared to what real life science people do, but I feel smarter playing this! Unbelievable amount of content as well. I feel I have only scratched the surface to the content that awaits in my playthrough.

Absolutely recommend this game. Quite the challenge and something I’ve really wanted in a survival crafter.

Tested on Steam Deck OLED

The original Splinter Cell still defines stealth 23 later - and it runs beautifully on the Steam Deck OLED.
No Ubisoft Connect, no online check-ins - it just launches instantly.

There is no native controller support, however community controller layouts handle movement well, though you’ll need Steam + X a few times for the on-screen keyboard. Mouse sensitivity settings affect analog control, so lowering it smooths out aiming and movement perfectly.

Visually, the Deck’s OLED display gives this old Unreal Engine build new life - shadows, reflections, and night vision all look great.
At 60 FPS, battery life averages around 7:30 hours, or 6:45 hours at 90 FPS.

It’s simple, quiet, stealthy and still one of the most atmospheric stealth experiences ever made.

Verdict: Timeless classic. Perfect performance on Deck and no technical issues.

Ok where do I start. This game is good but, could be great.
Its very addicting and a true step up from the first game. I really liked alot of the changes that were made but not all, and i will go into detail in a bit. First let me just make it simple. If you like tycoon games, the first game, then get this one. Its a no brainer. That being said I have to ideas and thoughts if ever they make a third game. This will be a bit long but Ive thought about this for a while and came up with ideas that would work in the games already existing systems and way of doing things.

1. Bring back the starter garage and buying land. Its a much more satisfying thing to feel you've worked hard enough and made enough money to buy a new office area/land area then just expanding to the next plot over. 

2. No more structured tech releases. Tech should be in the form of a tech tree that the player can research. That way if a person wants to focus on things like console development or a certain genre of game, they could do that and not have to wait for some arbitrary time period for it to be released. 

3. No more genre research. Everyone from day one of game development knew what a role playing game was. What an adventure game was. We had them as soon as the idea of games was invented. You shouldn't stifle game development by genre unless its tech related. Like mmos. But something like that could be unlocked in the tech tree. 

4. Early game depth/contract system rework. Some people that play may want an alternative way to play the game besides just making their own games. First, throw out the current contract system. Its annoying and frustrating. Alternatively offer a free agent system. Depending on your specialization, designer, programmer, graphics artist etc, you can put yourself up as a free agent to receive contracts based on that specialization. No more contracts showing up that you don't want. That gives the player a way to make money early without having to jump right into making games. Then if you do want to start making games later, you take yourself off the free agent list and do your own thing. Conversely, if you want to specialize in contracts you can earn rep with companies you work for. Get enough rep and you can be offered an exclusive contractor partnership with that company. Then you work only for them. The advantages could be that you only get the really high paying contracts from an exclusive deal. So you could be a free agent working for anyone, an exclusive agent working for one company, or work for yourself making games as normal. This would offer different paths of making money that could be done from the start and would work in about same way a contractual publishing deals would.

5. Designer and programmer specific rooms. I like how you can have specific rooms for graphic design and sound etc, but why limit that to just those? Then you have your designers and programmers still frustratingly trying to work on sound and graphics even when they have their own departments. So again I propose a rework here. The main development room would still be a thing, but that would be more of an all purpose room. (Ill get into this more later). In the same way as the graphics room or sound, designers and programmers should have their own rooms. So they can focus on just the things they specialize in and don't have to worry about everything else.

6. The all purpose development room. The main development room could be still used by as an all purpose room. That would provide players with the ability to not have to specialize with a bunch of other specific rooms. They could get jack of all trades type employees (see next point) and still make great games. You would just need top rated employees in all areas and more of them to achieve the same numbers of each stat, graphics sound etc. 

7. Jack of all trades employees vs specialty. Put the stat system back to a full 100 percent for all stats, but allow for specialization that gives an employee or your own created character an extra, say 20 points in a specific expertise area. So you could specialize and have people who just work in their respective areas of expertise, but also play an all around style as well. With employees set up like this, tied in with the all purpose room, you could play in a way where you never have to have specialized rooms.

8. Developing your own pc. Just in the same way that you would a console, allow players to make their own pc. You could research tech on the tech tree that allows for you to get into building your own pc. But a pc is not just parts, its an operating system as well. When it comes to that you could buy a licence for an operating system...windows, linux, or mac just as you would for dev kits or movie tie ins. Or you could develop your own operating system even without the pc that you could then license out to others in the same way you now do with engines. You could use sliders in the same way you now do with games for things like, ease of use...style...ease of programming for, etc.

9. A cleaner more intuitive UI. Yes the UI is workable in the game but its a bit bare bones basic and ugly to be honest with alot of unneeded things. The first games UI was a bit kiddy but it worked and had its own style. The UI here just...gets the job done and thats about it.

10. I wish i had a 10 here but thats about it.

Overall its a great game. If a bit limited. I think with a few tweaks and inclusions, the game could be amazing. Im going thru my first deep dive into it and I already feel like ive seen and done everything there is to see gameplay wise. I hope the developer takes the time to read things like this and makes a third game. I would love to see at least some of the things mentioned in a third game.

And if anyone reads this, let me know what you think of the ideas.

I've been playing Panther Games - from Highway to the Reich, to Conquest of the Aegean, to Command Ops 1 and Command Ops 2, for at least the last 10 years. Great to finally see them on Steam.

There are literally hundreds of WW2 video games. So why should you care about another one? Well Command Ops 2 does what no other game does - puts you in the shoes of a real commander in highly detailed scenarios set in different theatres of the war. From the German invasion of Greece, to North Africa, Malta, Operation Market Garden, the Battle of the Bulge and on to the Westwall.

[b]The Good:[/b]

[list]

[*]Unlike traditional wargames (and Civ 6), this game gets rid of hexes and turns and models everything in pausable real time on an open map, making the gameplay more dynamic.

[*]The AI. If you're sick of dumb units who couldn't pathfind themselves down the Yellow Brick Road, this game has no such issues. You can order units to take the quickest route or safest route to a goal. They will probe, attack, fall back, bunker down, rout, regroup and defend as the battles ebb and flow. The game also models pretty much everything about each company, from morale and cohesion down to the number of bullets they have for each gun. The upshot of this detail is it gives your units a personality in how they behave. Weaker units (or poorly thought out attacks) will fail. Stronger units and organised planning will result in the enemy going away with a bloody nose or worse; 

[*]Although you can micromanage every unit, Command Ops uses automation to let you delegate tasks to subordinate brigade and company commanders who will attempt to carry out your plans (and do a reasonable job). A neat twist to this is the game also models the delay that would occur for your orders to travel from HQ down to the front line. So the game rewards careful planning and anticipation of events, rather than twitch based responses to new threats. In other words, it is a strategy game with real strategy.[/list]

[b]The Not So Good.[/b]

[list]
[*]Yes, this is a wargame. That means your units are just small squares with numbers on them. Two dimensional wargames are a definite niche that most people (justifiably) pass over. The graphics are functional, but dated. Same with the game sounds.

[*]The game makes few concessions for newcomers to the genre. There is one tutorial mission (which is in the demo), but after that, you're left with a series of complicated scenarios and a 200 page manual. There is no grand campaign that gradually introduces you to units and strategies. You're sent straight into battle where you're expected to know the difference between a Sherman Tank and a Panzer Mk IV. [/list]

Summing Up: Funnily enough, the game that Command Ops most reminds me of is Dark Souls. They're both games that focus on providing a certain 'old school' type of gameplay and unapologetically ask the player to make an investment to discover the solid gameplay mechanics at their core. That's an investment that has repaid me many times over.

5 Stars.

你说二氧化碳登陆STEAM我滋不滋瓷，我肯定是滋瓷的。

作为屈指可数的超拟真度二战军级建制推演游戏，本作在硬核向模拟圈子里一直有着自己的一席之地，毕竟是黑豹社出品、打磨多年的游戏，其对二战军团级战略、营连级战术参考价值可以说是今世顶峰。

每场剧本经过了详尽的时代考究，开战前都有当时战役大背景的介绍。战斗中从当时的地形地貌、天气情况、补给线路，再到士兵的士气、武器装备、建制内残存战斗人员的多寡，都确保尽可能精确地还原当时各部队的状态。

连级（+特种排）部队一级一级交错构成了CO2里庞大的作战建制模拟，让玩家可以仔细操作每个连的详细动向。但连级单位基数的巨大并不会影响到整体态势的判别，如果你想，只需给营、团乃至军级指挥部直接下达指令，AI会自动帮你排兵布阵，尽可能以当时部队作战标准的战术流程替你的执行任务，让你能将更多的时间停留在战略对抗的思考当中。
战斗中的命令需要层层下达，真实的反映了指令的传导时间，再加上传达错误、单位士气/体力低下/缺乏补给、指挥链断开等导致的无法执行命令的复杂的战场状况，让玩家不得不对自己的战术命令推敲再三，一步小小的战术失误轻则让部队丧失先机，重则直接会断送几百人的性命。当然，这也令最终胜利所带来的满足感更胜一层。

灵活的剧本难度调整也是本作的亮点，如果你想要休闲一下，完全可以关闭指令下达延迟，将自己的补给、援军抵达速度提高，体验一把虐菜的快感。不过，那样不就失去了这个游戏最核心的乐趣了么。

多说无益，只有将全身心沉浸下来细品其中细节才能享受本作。本作注定绝非像那些休闲游戏一样能有大批簇拥，毕竟，硬核终究小众，更何况这种硬到骨子里的推演呢。但我希望愿意体验真实战术、战略指挥推演的玩家绝对不要错过这款佳作，虽然它很难上手，但一旦入门，便又是新的世界。

刚出的时候就买了，一直没有机会和时间打开，前两天有朋友聊天的时候力荐这部作品我就选择试试。两个多小时忍着晕3D体验下来,游戏给我的感觉确实像是一部文艺片，看到有些朋友说太短，我倒觉得这样的长度刚好，一是再长我就晕的玩不下去了，二是我觉得它很像一部电影，这样的长度注定无法将故事讲的多完整和深刻，但它给了我们从中解读的空间。
  我个人不喜欢看文艺片，因为看的时候我总是会看睡着，我喜欢那种实在且直给的东西。游戏也是一样，这部作品给我的感觉也是很复杂的，一方面它有着充沛的情感表达，一方面在游玩上我会觉得它不是一部好玩的作品，有太多不足和可以提升的角度和空间了，玩的时候有些烦躁。(全成就稍微有点难）但同时我也承认它确实是一部优秀的作品。正如创作者所言这是一部“苦乐参半却时而如梦想般的半自传式的青春故事。”
    游戏充满了生命力，用足球为线索串联起一段亦真亦假的回忆，2001年经济危机的阴霾与世界杯晋级的狂欢看似矛盾实则共存。在这里足球成为了普通人对抗困境的精神支柱，厄瓜多尔从不回避苦难，也从不粉饰狂欢，在球迷的呐喊声里，一直都混着失业者的沉默。
     通过一个游戏去了解一个国家，这个游戏确实做到了这一点，游戏中掺杂着对童年和时代的追忆，所以虽然是足球游戏，它的重点还是在讲人，人的情感、记忆、成长和自由。
    游戏的探索和互动做的其实不差，可互动内容也很多，想探索的点也很多，可是时间是有限的，就像是对一个时代对一个事件对一个还可以抓住的确定的时间告别一样。当我们匆匆赶回家，手表指针划过黄昏的仓促，那是我们童年的易逝，更是一个民族在混乱里抓紧“片刻希望”的状态，就像苦难从不缺席，而我们追球的脚步，永远比阴影更响亮。
     从个人的角度去划开时代的裂痕，那些日子一去不复返，但成长从不是告别过去，而是把童年的印记揉进后来的人生里，就像记忆碎片一般，没有消失，只是变成了成年后的生活细节，我对于童年的感受和作者一样，其实是很朦胧的，我不想主动去回忆，它可能也不是什么美好的记忆，但当我回忆起来我会觉得那个时代对我来说是美好的，就像“我们或许会问为什么我们喜欢梦核”有一句很经典的评论是“你可以回到过去，但那里已经没有人了。”
    我们会回忆，我们会感受到这种惆怅下的温暖。对于失去的记忆和过去，那不是悲伤的告别，而是温柔的确认，感谢那段让自由住进身体的时光，它可能对我们来说是最完美的一天，一个让你想起就会开心的夜晚，哪怕它以结束的姿态出现，却早已成为生命里最柔软的支撑。
   正如朴树在1999年发行的«我去2000年»给我的感受，当新一世代的我们听到«New boy»中那种向上那种希望，我们或许是偶尔悲伤的，那种悲伤是来自未知的迷惘。其实我们有时对于过去，越来越不知道自己为什么要追忆，甚至我们为什么要为了痛苦哭泣，所以当足球滚过2001年的街巷，当朴树的歌声飘过2000年的空气，我们会收获到那种感动，来自心里的感动。我们知道好的艺术形式从来都不需要刻意用力，在这些远离宏大叙事的体验中我们痛苦我们释怀我们获得力量，就像足球会自然落地，朴树的歌声会自然入心，那些藏在岁月里的温柔与自由，总会在某个瞬间，我们都能懂。
   在这里，游戏与现实的边界早被磨平，就像我们从未真正离开过绿茵，也不过是那个被妈妈拉出公园的孩童，终于长成了能把自由弧度藏进心里的大人。
   我喜欢最后一幕。

From a game design perspective this is the best tower defense game I have played so far.

You get a variety of towers to pick from - some are really basic and can be found in any TD game while others are unique to Rogue Tower only. You have to unlock them one after another though, so the game doesn't overwhelm you with too much at once which is good I think.

It my not look like it at first but the mechanics offer A LOT of depth and possibilities. You get elevations with range and attack bonuses, Mana which can be gained and spent in different ways, three different "health" types in enemies, several ways to gain gold which is your only resource to buy and upgrade towers and more including random and progressive map generation, random enemy units, bosses, etc. So its not like other TD games where you can basically follow one simple strategy per map which will work every single time but you have to adapt to the always changing situations.

The achievements are exceptionally hard but personally this is what I look for in games. The hardest achievement (not rarest though) which I recently got after trying for many many hours involves a lot of luck. I don't know if this is a good thing or not since it can get frustrating. But if you want to go after that you have to invest a ton of hours and bring plenty of patience.

The only things which really bugged me (not counting the luck factor) are two things. 1) You can't rotate the map. Some tiles are inaccessible sometimes to build on because they are blocked by other taller tiles. 2) The graphics could really use some more love. I guess the current state is fine considering one person developed the game (I think) but a well designed game like this deserves better graphics.

Initially I thought the pricing was a bit high after watching the videos showcasing the poor graphics but as of now my money was totally worth it and there is always a sale around the corner ;)

I can only highly recommend playing this if you like Tower Defense.

My other Atelier reviews:

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Synikx/recommended/936180?snr=1_5_9__402]Totori[/url] 
[i]Note: Being that this is the 3rd in the Arland series, you should not be starting here. I’m writing this review with the players in mind who have played/completed Rorona and Totori[/i]

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world is very similar to Rorona and Totori - you have city and exploration areas. I would say the only thing I noticed that was different is how some of the zones change as you complete quests. For example, you build out an area that is able to farm goats, you can now visit that area to get goat milk. Most of these changes are visual and provide new paths, and gathering points. I did the small changes of the areas, but it's nothing significant. 

The plot is a bit simple. You play as Princess Meruru who is trying to become an alchemist under the tutelage of Totori, yes that Totori. Many of the characters from Rorona and Totori make appearances here. Anyways, like the other games, you have a strict timeline to meet criteria to prove to your father, the king, that you are adept at becoming an alchemist. 
The vast majority of the plot occurs through random cutscenes as you enter an area from time passing. Unfortunately, while these cutscenes do add some flavor to the characters, the main plot does little to entice the player. This is not a story-driven game, it's a time management and mechanical game. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
So how are the mechanics, since that seems to be the focus? Well, I found the alchemy and crafting part to be the same as Rorona, which I really enjoyed. But the time management part left me overwhelmed and frustrated. Meruru implements parts from Totori that were a bit harsher on the time side - things like gathering and battles both use up time, whereas I don’t believe they did in Rorona. This creates a somewhat odd gameplay feeling of whimsical teenage girls having fun while also being chased relentlessly by the clock. 

I found the difficulty to ebb and flow. It starts off easy, then skyrockets when you get some level 20 boss quests, then is easy again until you get closer to year 3. Towards the end, I was inundated with quests and exceptionally hard areas that made traveling back and forth a massive endeavor. It’s annoying to travel a month to unlock 3 areas, only to find out the 3rd area is impossible with your level/gear. So do you load a past save (if you have one) and try again, knowing you can’t really grind too much because of time restrictions? Or do you take the extra time penalty in walking there and back, and then back again later after trying other quests? It’s really rough at times. 

[h1] [b] Graphics (Quality/Technical) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
The quality is the same as Rorona, but a bit better than Totori. Totori was a mess as it apparently wasn’t a full remaster, but Meruru is very comparable to Rorona in that regard - it's a decent remaster. Looks very much like a PS3 game. 

On the technical side is where things start to go downhill. I experienced multiple crashes to desktop. The game has no resolution option over 1080p. When I experienced no issues, it generally ran fine, which it seems to be locked to 60 FPS. 
i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | Windows 11 installed on SSD 

[h1] [b] Audio – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
The music is fine, not as good as Rorona’s energetic music, but still decent. 

Same with voice acting, it’s fine. 

[h1] [b] Replay Factor (Longevity) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
There is an option to have an ending save file and you can replay the game using that file from the beginning. I think it has some decent replay value as you can attempt to try new paths or ways of getting things done, but still not much should drastically change, it would be more about optimization instead of enough changes to warrant a replay. 

[h1] [b] Final Verdict – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Oh Meruru, how I wanted to like you. I want to start off by being very clear about my frustrating experience with the time management aspect -  After 32 hours of playtime, I got the failure ending. I did not follow a guide, but I did my best to only do travel and crafts explicitly for the quest(s) I had. This obviously wasn’t enough. I wish there was an option to be gentler on the time aspect, maybe cut off gathering and battles from using time, but unfortunately this doesn’t seem to be the case. 

I liked everything about Meruru but the time part. It has addicting crafting and gathering. The facilities building up the city was a nice feature. The characters were nice and each have their own abilities, which makes forming a party a tough decision. There’s a lot to like here, and I can definitely see why Meruru is touted as the best of the Arland series. 

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend Meruru because of my experience on the restrictive time management aspects. I cannot stress enough how terrible it feels to play 30 hours into an RPG only to fail. Imagine you play a Final Fantasy game and after 30 hours it just ends because you weren’t high enough level or something. Your only option now is to restart the game at the beginning. I can’t recommend that. If you don’t allow me to have fun grinding in a rather enjoyable game with enjoyable features, then this is something I can’t get behind, which is a shame because Meruru was a good experience that I [i]wished[/i] I could spend more time in, but the game apparently doesn’t want you to.

[h1]BRUTAL JOHN 2 — is one of those rare moments when you launch a game “just for a couple of minutes,” and suddenly it’s deep into the night, you’re grinning like an idiot, thinking: “Alright, just one more level... and that’s it.”[/h1]

[b] [i]I stumbled upon this project in my Steam feed — someone from my friends list was playing it. I figured: why not try it too? Honestly, I expected “just another gory shooter.” But no… I bought it — and I didn’t regret it for a second. This game is a treasure trove of references to references. There are so many Easter eggs that you start wondering: is this really a game, or some kind of pop-culture museum disguised as a shooter?

And yeah, the first impression hit instantly: “this is Duke Nukem, no doubt!”
You look in the mirror, press the action button — and Brutal Johnny throws out those classic lines. 🥰😆
It’s not just nostalgia bait. It’s a respectful nod to the old legends — done with style, taste, and zero cringe.

Gameplay is fast, punchy, and never drags. Everything crashes, explodes, screams, and blasts the way only true old-school madness can. But it doesn’t feel outdated — you can tell the devs know exactly when to speed things up, when to give you a breather, and when to hit you with something wild.

The best part is that feeling of constant winks from the developers. Little details, little jokes — you can’t help but smile and think: “Oh you clever bastards, I see what you did there.”

BRUTAL JOHN 2 is loud, bold, absurd, and stylish as hell.
It doesn’t try to please everyone — it just does its own thing, and it does it damn well.

If you love old-school shooters, enjoy Easter eggs, appreciate classic anti-heroes, and want a game that gives you not just entertainment but a full-on stream of fun — grab it. No hesitation.

I’m not just satisfied — I’m genuinely glad I stumbled onto it by accident. Steam rarely gives surprises this good.

P.S. The game is in early access, but it's still gorgeous. I'm quite surprised that there are only three people making this game. You know, big studios make games as a crowd, and it comes out muddled. And then 3 people gathered and made a masterpiece! Thank you so much for letting me shed tears again, reminding me of the old time.[/i] [/b]

A very underrated retro shooter.
I don't know how games half its quality are seeing success while this one is going unnoticed.

First of all the game is extremely polished. Everything works beautifully and the usual clunkiness of an EA title is nonexistent. It's impressive how the developers were managed to fill the levels with new and fun content again and again. Speaking of levels, they are pretty varied and I especially liked the urban settings. Shooting feels fun, weapons are punchy, gibs are flying. Basically everything you would expect from a game like this is here and works nicely. There are well done cutscenes, driving sections, many arcade games and much more. Long story short, the game is pretty good gameplay-wise.

Next, it's pretty funny. The tone, story, and cutscenes combined with the cherry on top that is the cast's accents make everything hilarious, and I very rarely laugh at any media. I wouldn't even mention the humor as a point if it weren't one of the main draws for me.

Finally, the references are very smart. With these games we usually see what, a nod to Doom or a hidden dopefish somewhere in the level right? While Brutal John also has dopefishes sprinkled everywhere (seriously, he's everywhere) there are also very smart and sometimes biting commentary. Finding Duke's corpse crushed by gears and later getting a call from Duke whose apparently looking for his lost balls are just two examples. I would give more examples, but half the fun comes from discovering these on your own. I really hope the developers will continue adding more of these as more levels get released. And I know the devs are real FPS fans, because not many would add Gus the Miner to their game as an easter egg. I doubt many will even know who that is.

Overall I enjoyed the game very much.
I wish the developers good luck with the project.

[h1] Better Upgrade and 2nd Attempt from Previous Game [/h1] 

Granblue Fantasy Versus Rising is the perfect game for me, and I think it’s great for anyone who wants to play an anime fighter (or fighting game in general) without being overwhelmed by long combos or high execution requirements.

It plays fast without sacrificing clarity. Even though it uses modern fighting game features like auto-combos and special move shortcuts, it’s not dumbed down at all — there’s still plenty of depth.

[h2] Character Roster [/h2] 
Right now there are 38 playable characters, with one more on the way. (Season 3 hasn’t been announced yet, so we’ll see.) Every character feels distinct, so you can easily find an archetype that fits your playstyle. Some characters even come with extra gimmicks that make them stand out more.

[h2] Online Experience [/h2] 
Matchmaking has been fine for me so far. I’m playing from Indonesia (SEA) with a so-so internet provider, and I can still get stable matches against players from Japan and China. Disclaimer: I use a cable connection — and you should too.

The playerbase is still active enough that you can find online matches without long queue times. And since the game has crossplay, the actual number of players is bigger than what SteamDB shows.

[h2] Single Player Content [/h2]
There's Story Mode, Arcade Mode, and Survival Mode (where you get random power-up bonuses every 5 rounds). That’s already enough for a proper single-player experience.

Is the story only for Granblue Fantasy fans? Not really. Newcomers can still enjoy it because the game includes glossaries and character bios. The cast is lovable enough that you won’t feel alienated or lost.

[h2] Art Style & Soundtrack [/h2]
The art direction is chef’s kiss 🤌 and the soundtrack goes hard. Every character has a theme that fits their personality and vibe, and almost all of them are bangers.

[h2] Price & Monetization [/h2]
I suggest to grab the Deluxe Edition when it’s on sale (usually around 60% off). You’ll get the base game plus Deluxe Character Pass 1, which already unlocks about 87% of the roster. Most of the other DLC aside from Character Pass 2 — are cosmetics only and is purely optional.

There is also seasonal Battle Pass, which also unlocks more cosmetics contents. [b] Do note that with recent updates, some battle pass exclusives item (costumes, weapon skins, exclusive colors) will be sold as separate DLC at later date. [/b] So less FOMO contents I guess?

If you’re still unsure, there’s also a free-to-play version. It limits you to 4 rotating characters and locks most modes outside of online lobbies, but it’s enough to test the waters.

[h2] Overall [/h2]
This game is fun for both casual players and competitive ones. Like I said earlier, every character is charming in their own way, so you’ll definitely find someone to love — whether that’s for their design, gameplay, personality, or the whole package.

[b] Now go give Cygames your money so we can get Season 3! [/b]

Welch tolles Spiel!

Selbst im EA ist Enshrouded schon nahezu perfekt. Keine halbleere Welten/Biome, guter und spannender Geschichtsverlauf, ausgewogenes Kampfsystem und ein super tolles Bausystem.

Ich bin 71 Jahre alt und zocke Enshrouded mit sehr viel Freude und Herzblut. Über 1'800 Spielstunden habe ich bereits in dieses Spiel versenkt. Dazu gehören u.a. der Aufbau von zwei Basen, welche viel Zeit in Anspruch nahmen.
E hat einige Aspekte bzw. Inspirationen von Valheim, Zelda und Subnautica. Und das kommt sehr gut an.

Die Fortbewegungsmöglichkeiten sind vielfältig und optimal: Fussmarsch um möglichst viel zu entdecken, Reisen zwischen Flammenaltaren, Greifhaken und Gleiter. Gleiten war anfangs alles andere als meine Paradedisziplin. Inzwischen hab ich es jedoch gut im Griff. Es lässt sich gut und zielgerichtet navigieren. Abstürze mit Fallschaden oder das verfehlen von Zielen kommen immer noch vor, aber viel seltener und durch mein Fehlverhalten. Hin und wieder zu sterben gehört auch zum Spiel.

Was ich auch ausserordentlich schätze sind die individuellen Einstellungen beim Schwierigkeitsmodus. Ich spiele im Normalmodus und habe z.B. bei Todesfall die Einstellung "alles behalten" drinn. Das ist für mich eine grosse Erleichterung weil ich nicht mehr zum Todespunkt zurück reisen muss um mein Inventar auszulösen. Spart auch viel Zeit. Eine weitere Einstellung, dass sich meine Waffen (ausser der Fackel) nicht mehr abnutzen. So spare ich Platz im Inventar, weil ich Waffen nicht zwei- oder dreifach mitnehmen muss. Hingegen stelle ich bei den Feindbegegnungen häufig auf "viele Feinde". Zum einen, weil es mir Spass macht, die "Kampfsau" raus zu lassen, zum anderen, um mehr Loot zu bekommen. Und noch eine grössere Anzahl an Wildtieren, um mehr Fleisch zu ergattern. Das Futter meiner Haustiere (Hunde + Katzen) besteht hauptsächlich aus Fleisch und wird schnell mal zur Mangelware.

Das Spiel läuft schön flüssig und die Grafik ist sehr gut. Besonders die Lichteffekte sind nahezu realistisch und auch wunderschön. Und egal wo man gerade steht oder geht: Die Aussicht oder Weitsicht ist schon fast atemberaubend schön.

Bei Enshrouded spürt man förmlich die Liebe der Entwickler zu ihrem Spiel und das macht es auch so einzigartig.
Meine Empfehlung zu diesem Spiel ist daher sonnenklar:)


Mehr als gut gemacht, Keen Games und ein grosses Dankeschön für dieses Spiel:)

Honestly, when I first launched NFS 2015, I was blown away by the atmosphere — the night city, the rain, the reflections, the roar of the engine — it all looks amazing, especially when you’re drifting through the narrow streets of Ventura Bay. The car customization is awesome too; you can tweak every little part, from bumpers to decals, and it really feels like your ride.
But then comes the infamous Prestige mode — and holy hell, who thought this was a good idea? It’s like the game says, “Oh, you finished everything? Cool. Now do it all again, but harder, more annoying, and with zero fun.” The cars handle like soap, the traffic appears out of nowhere, the cops spawn from thin air, and if you screw up even once — boom, restart. It’s not challenging in a good way; it’s just frustrating as hell.
And don’t even get me started on the always-online thing. Why do I need a constant connection just to cruise around alone? Lag, disconnects, and the fact you can’t even pause the game — seriously, who thought that was acceptable?
Still, I can’t lie — the game does have soul. When you’re flying through the rain-soaked streets at night with the turbo whistling and the soundtrack blasting, it feels damn good.

[h3]My rating: 7/10.[/h3]
[h3]Could’ve easily been a 9 if it weren’t for that f***ing Prestige mode and the always-online nonsense.[/h3]

Итак, я стою перед выбором, определяющим мою жизнь, разрываясь между двумя мирами, одинаково требовательными и одинаково погруженными в тайну человеческого существования. С одной стороны – темная часовня, где тишина нарушается лишь шепотом молитв и звуком заколачиваемых гвоздей. Здесь, в царстве мертвых, я гробовщик, чьи руки готовят усопших к последнему путешествию. Сглаживаю их лица, омываю тела, облачаю в погребальные одежды, пытаясь найти в их застывших чертах отблеск былой жизни.


Но с другой стороны – залитая светом церковь, где я священник, голос надежды и утешения для скорбящих. Здесь я веду паству сквозь мрак утраты к свету веры, читаю заупокойные молитвы и совершаю обряды, дарующие покой усопшим и надежду живым. Это служение, требующее сострадания, мудрости и непоколебимой веры.


И вот, передо мной встает новая задача – изгнание бесов, осквернивших тела усопших. Зло, которое я должен изгнать, это не просто болезнь или несчастный случай, а тьма, поселившаяся в душе и проникшая в плоть. Ритуал сложен и опасен, требующий не только знания, но и духовной силы. Крест и молитва – мое оружие в этой борьбе, вера – щит, ограждающий от зла. Я чувствую ответственность, лежащую на моих плечах, ведь от меня зависит не только упокоение души, но и освобождение тела от скверны. Мои руки, привыкшие к погребальным инструментам, теперь держат святой крест. Мой голос, привыкший к заупокойным молитвам, теперь произносит слова изгнания. Я гробовщик и священник, поставленный между жизнью и смертью, долгом и верой, тьмой и светом. И я должен делать свою работу.

This is, quite possibly, one of the worst things ever released onto the Steam platform. Not because the combat is bad (it’s actually fantastic), but because the entire structure is a masterclass in psychological predation. I actually didn't write a negative review like 2 years ago when I stopped playing because I was just so impressed by how impressive the psychological tactics were that it honestly should be a positive review. 
This game is a brilliantly toxic product that targets its audience who are pretty much all basement-dwelling rats with non existent awareness, tricking them into believing that running the same meaningless chore on twelve alt-characters is a valuable life contribution to their imaginary community. It makes you feel valuable surviving on welfare checks by convincing you that maintaining your roster level just to find a group for a raid is some sort of a noble calling of you leading some sort of heroes that give you the imaginary perception of being better than other people when in reality you’ve just built a sweatshop for yourself. Every day you feed them Chaos Dungeon rations, send them to do your busywork, and somehow convinced yourself that funneling mats into your main is real life progress.
The monetization is the final humiliation: your 400 hours of grinding for an upgrade, thinking it was all worth it for that +1 honing success only to instantly fail and having all your gold evaporate when one bored banker by swiping his Amex on a lunch break gets his cartoon sword shinier than you. And the worst part? You know this, but you still log in the next day and whisper to yourself "one more try". That’s the level of psychological brilliance of exploiting FOMO we're dealing with, disguised as fantasy. You’re chasing timers like they owe you rent. You log in out of guilt, collect your daily “rewards,” and tell yourself it’s self-care. It’s the first game where burnout is an official feature, and logging off feels like quitting your job without notice.
It’s addictive and fundamentally rotten. The perfect mix of dopamine, despair, and denial is a monument to how far humanity will go to feel “productive” while achieving absolutely nothing.

Final Verdict: 10/10 - escaping this self-torture and hitting uninstall felt like rolling the credits on my life, giving me a newfound clarity even two year later, but I guess it seems like I’m still recovering...

Honestly, this game is truly underrated. That 2009–2016 era of FPS games was something special, and coming back to Titanfall 2 just reminds me how unmatched it really was. The combat is slick and incredibly fluid, movement just feels great even if a little floaty. I’m still not the biggest fan of some of the guns (a few lean a bit too hard into sci fi gimmick territory for me with a few interesting ones I wont lie), but the moment to moment gameplay more than makes up for it. The story isn’t the most original premise you’ll ever see, but it never tries to be anything it isn’t. It’s confident, tight, and surprisingly heartfelt. The banter with BT hits that perfect balance of dry humour, warmth, and weight a nice emotional break from the game’s overall darker tone. It's genuinely one of the better buddy dynamic narratives in shooters. And the level design? Honestly incredible. There are moments here that feel like master class set pieces taking advantage of unique mechanics in ways that are memorable without feeling like gimmicks. Levels like that one (you know the one) are still talked about for a reason, and even outside the standout moments, the campaign’s pacing and creativity keep things constantly engaging. It's got some decent performances by its voice actors which is always appreciated. It’s short, punchy, and doesn’t waste your time a rare thing now. Titanfall 2 really deserved better support and recognition at launch, because even today it stands toe to toe with the best shooters ever made.

I wanted to like it so badly. I'm a HUGE Rocky Horror fan. It's like a generic "spooky" retro platformer got some Rocky Horror elements. The soundtrack is so fun, and some of the sprites are great! I was so genuinely disappointed by this game in so many ways.

There is a funny story about how I first discovered The Rocky Horror Show. I can’t remember the exact year anymore but it must have been in the early 90s, and the night before I had secretly watched the first adaptation of Stephen King’s IT. 
The next day, which I clearly remember was a Saturday, I visited a friend I knew from a nearby playground. She lived with her two mothers in a lovely house a bit further up a hill, and I had agreed to help out in their garden again because it was always a lot of fun, and a great change from all the nonsense I usually got up to. Once we were done with the work in the garden, the family invited me to have dinner with them and they asked if I would like to stay overnight and join their little Rocky Horror Picture Show party, which would also be the first time for this friend to see it. They explained to me that after dinner a few friends of theirs would come over and we would all watch the movie together, and afterwards sit around and play a board game. I had already stayed over at their place a few times before and the two mothers were very kind and interesting people whom I liked a lot after only a short time, so it was a total no brainer because whenever they did something, it was always a lot of fun. Curious as I already was back then, I wanted to know what the movie was about, and they told me that it was a kind of comedy horror film that originally came from a musical and besides its rather crazy story it featured lots of music. That all sounded great to me and I thought it would probably just be a cozy evening with a movie I would forget again soon, and wow was I wrong about that.

What I would give to be able to contact that family today and tell them that there is now a Rocky Horror Show video game, and how nice it would be to play it with them, kind of like in the good old days. Although with this game, we probably would not have cheered as much as we did back then during the movie. Calling it a party really was accurate, because it was a party with singing along, dancing and shouting at the screen. I even once yelled, “Hey, that’s Pennywise” and everyone burst out laughing. The retro music in the game is mostly a nice rework of the original material and fits this pixel art 2D platformer very well. The level balance and the mix of the other sounds feel uneven in some places, but luckily it doesn’t drag things down too much.

A week before this year’s Halloween a friend came over to play some games. While he was trying out this NES-like version of The Rocky Horror Show, a few of the points I had already noted down as cons really solidified. For example, you have to replay the same levels multiple times. Sure, you switch characters and the difficulty ramps up, but they could have done more with that idea. In my playthrough I died 216 times and cursed the game in two specific spots. My friend died 463 times and said he only had fun during the first twenty minutes. After that it became frustrating for him as a casual gamer, his final words: I love the movie but I hate this game. So I’d definitely recommend it to people who enjoy games like Ghosts ’n Goblins, Rick Dangerous or Castlevania, and at the same time have a soft spot for The Rocky Horror Show.

It's good but not great.

The graphics are impressive for a pixel-art game, gorgeous even. That's really all I have to say about that, we all know graphics don't make or break a game.

The music is really good, but not great. I found myself humming and whistling a few of the tunes while not playing the game. But the bar for music in Square RPG's has been set so high that I can't call it great -- it's not Final Fantasy tier.

The combat can be fun, but it can also get old. It kept me engaged enough to keep coming back to the game, but I was usually getting sick of it by the end of a session. The battle is pretty strategic for a turn-based JRPG -- mindlessly attacking or just casting your strongest spells is not the way to go here. Enemies have weaknesses to certain weapons or elements, and you'll want to plan your actions accordingly to maximize damage and disrupt their turns. 

You might have to grind a little, but nothing too bad. I did very little grinding and got through pretty easily. There were a few battles toward the end that bordered on frustrating.

I'll echo my usual RPG complaint about unclear systems. It's not clear what all the stats do, how they interact, and how holding multiple weapons with different stats works. Searching up the mechanics reveals a lot of hidden info that should have been explained in the game.

For me, story is the most important element of an RPG. This is where the game kind of falls down for me. You have 8 characters, each with their own story. The stories don't really intertwine at all, and even the individual stories feel disjointed. Character A's story will be: you go to town 1 and do a thing, go to town 2 and do a different thing, etc. etc. In the last town you fulfill that character's main goal. All 8 stories are like that and there's very little "connective tissue". Some of the characters were better than others, but overall I didn't really care about any of the stories or characters.

The game gets a little repetitive. You go to a new town, use your character abilities on the people there to get items and quests, then wander a dungeon and fight a boss. Over and over and over and over. The dungeons are all pretty small and linear -- any small deviation from the path leads to a dead end with a treasure chest. 

Overall I spent around 80 hours on it and it was mostly fun, but I probably won't play it again for a very long time, if at all.

不容错过的经典rts作品，也是童年回忆之一。记得最早还是父亲推荐给自己的，可惜的是当时自己觉得难度过大，没坚持多久就跑回去打红警了。后来自己在steam上补了票，在游玩几次独立战役复健后断断续续地打完了所有战役并获得了全勋章，算是弥补了童年时错过的东西。
严格来讲，与自己接触的其他传统rts相比，《英雄连》的设计有较大不同之处。最显著的便是对局中玩家资源获取方式的差异：传统rts的资源获取往往建立在玩家基地/分基地扩张的基础上，通过建造获取资源的相关建筑/单位进行资源提取的操作，整体上遵循基地扩张-资源开发-军队建设-局部作战优势-基地扩张的基本思路，也是传统rts的显著标志。而《英雄连》的不同之处在于，玩家的资源获取基于对资源点的占领，而这些资源点——尤其是交火前线附近的——的巩固往往需要依靠局部区域的优势，而这一部分需要依靠大量的战术操作。虽然在红警等传统rts内也有诸如油井之类的、依靠占领获取的资源点，但整体来看这部分资源更多的属于锦上添花，与本作相比差别较大。再加上生产建筑不能超出原始基地附近的限定范围（除英军外），以及后文会提到的人口上限机制，本作的产能扩张收到了极大限制，因此盲目增加生产建筑（即所谓的多开）、扩张生产基地在《英雄连》中并没有太大意义。本作整体对局思路大致可归纳为局部作战优势-资源开发-军队建设-局部作战优势这一循环，这样的设计对于那些习惯于传统rts操作的玩家而言需要一定时间适应，不过在适应期过后回头来看，此种设计也不失为某种程度上的创意之举。
游戏内的资源有三类：人力、弹药与油料，其中人力是玩家扩张的基本资源，基地建造、防御建筑的建设、军队扩张、班组增援、部分战术支援升级等绝大部分操作都需要人力，而人力增长会随着玩家兵员的增多而逐渐递减，除了美军补给场科技升级能够减少维护费外，该递减趋势无法抑制；油料被用于载具的建设与小部分针对载具整体的升级科技；弹药则决定了玩家的一切战术行动：班组的大部分战术技能（手雷、炸药包、爆破、自动步枪火力压制、重机枪/at炮穿甲弹等）、针对单个班组或载具的升级（探雷器、喷火器、火箭筒、无后坐力炮、坦克的大口径车载机枪等）。可以看到，游戏内存在大量即时战术要素，再加上游戏刻意弱化了基地扩张这个rts的重要操作，导致《英雄连》至今仍然被部分玩家归类于rtt。这里不得不提及一个令我深恶痛绝的机制——人口上限。玩家拥有的每一个班组、每一辆载具、建造的每一个防御塔（指机枪碉堡、防空炮、榴弹炮等需要人手操作的防御设施，不包括观测所、铁丝网、壕沟、地雷等），而人口上限仅能通过占领特殊的人力资源点来增加，并且有最大上限限制。此种设计彻底断绝了TR（tower rush，可简要理解为建造大量防御塔来达到压制敌军、推进战线的特殊进攻手段）在本作实施的可能性，玩家也因生产建筑无法于初始区域之外建造而无法扩张分基地。这也是本作玩法设计上自己最不喜欢的一点。
然而，尽管游戏设计层面存在一些另自己不是很满意的内容，《英雄连》仍然是我迄今为止游玩过的最优秀rts作品之一。究其原因在于，2006年发售的《英雄连》用那个时代的游戏引擎与简陋的实体建模，构建了一个无比真实、代入感极佳的二战战场。本作创造了极度拟真的掩体系统与武器系统，将整个战场环境细分为完全、部分、无掩体三类状态，作为掩体的除了手动建造的防御设施外，载具本身或残骸、农场栅栏、树桩、石块，甚至是炮弹命中地面产生的弹坑，都可以成为掩蔽等级不同的掩体。而武器的命中率会随着武器类型而变化，士兵面对不同的武器攻击、身处不同的状态，也都拥有相应的受击反馈：被小口径冲锋枪击倒后的痛苦挣扎、遭到喷火器袭击后全身着火疯狂奔跑、被重机枪压制在掩体后动弹不得、坦克炮命中士兵所在的房屋后砖石与躯体一同滑落......确实，以今天的眼光看，每一处场景细节单独提炼出来仔细端详，其建模都是粗糙的贴图，然而游戏在当时的技术力限制下，用无数粗糙的细节组合在一起，共同构建了一个极度真实而又残酷无比的二战战场。
正如《英雄连》这一游戏名，游戏的战役部分抛弃了写实战争题材策略游戏惯于使用的宏大场面描写，转而聚焦于一个个身处不同阵营的基层作战单位。美军A、F连，英军第三营，德军教导战斗群，游戏中的士兵不再是一串冰冷的战力数字，从无缝衔接的过场cg、任务开始前的简报再到作战中的互动语音，玩家仿佛真的成为了身处战地指挥所中的指挥官，这也是包括我在内的很多《英雄连》新手玩家都会陷入追求伤亡最小化而束手束脚的原因——当真正身临其境那片战场时，没人能轻易下令让自己的袍泽去送死。有人可能会认为这种设计是西方一贯的个人英雄主义写照，但我更愿意将其称为牺牲精神的代言。游戏没有政治偏向性，没有刻意抹黑对手历史的战绩，奥马哈滩头、卡灵顿、莫尔坦、沃梅兹、奥斯特比克、卡比奎、卡昂......绞肉机一般的战场用枪炮的轰鸣与士兵的惨嚎，共同谱写了一曲血与火的交响乐。
最后是steam上的游戏版本说明。目前，steam上的《英雄连》1代共有四个版本：《英雄连》、《英雄连-遗产版》、《英雄连：抵抗前线》、《英雄连：勇气传说》。其中遗产版为最早的英雄连游戏原版，而非sega发行的最新般，无中文无法兼容steam售卖的抵抗前线与勇气传说两个dlc，且无法单独购买，不推荐游玩。而无任何后缀的《英雄连》为最新版不包括dlc的游戏本体，自带繁中，只有“诺曼底登陆”这一条美军战役线。《抵抗前线》与《勇气传说》为游戏的dlc扩展，且均可以单独游玩，其中《抵抗前线》包括德军战役线“市场花园作战”与英军战役线“解放卡昂”，《勇气传说》则包括三个迷你战役线“虎式精英”“公路”“法莱斯包围战”。需要注意的是，当单独游玩dlc时则游戏内指挥解锁相应dlc的战役线，若要一次性体验完整六个战役线，则直接购买捆绑包并启动游戏本体即可。

[h1]Introduction[/h1]
Bug Fables: The Everlasting Sapling is a sprawling 2019 Turn-based RPG with Realtime mechanics developed by Moonsprout Games and published by DANGEN Entertainment. The game follows Kabbu, Vi and (eventually) Leif, as they go on an epic adventure to uncover the Everlasting Sapling, a powerful, ancient artifact, thought to give eternal life to those who use it.

[h1]Main Review[/h1]
The game is beautiful, with fantastic art, and great music. The story is deep and genuinely tugs at your heart strings. The characters and worldbuilding are fascinating the entirety of the way through and most of the areas and boss encounters are fantastic. It’s not quite Sea of Stars, nor does it hold a candle to this year’s Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, especially gameplay-wise, but it’s still an incredibly lovingly crafted experience.
The bad parts of the game are chiefly found in two aspects: The grinding and the cooking. Both of these things are interlinked. Money (in the form of berries) is annoyingly sparse, when compared to its many (often expensive) uses. The cooking, a really important mechanic of the game, particularly on the Hard Mode, which is what I first played this game on, is cumbersome. Unskippable, long cooking animations (that you can only slightly fast-forward, after an update back in 2020, but still not skip), no batch cooking (cooking more of the same food at once) and no batch purchasing of ingredients in shops, as well as no item stacking, make the game a hell of inventory management and money-farming. Sometimes enemy farming for the occasional, non-purchasable ingredient compounds alongside the former two issues to kill the game’s replay value, needlessly pad the playtime and make needlessly laborious a game I would otherwise be replaying often and recommending without any caveat.

[h1]Closing Statement[/h1]
If you’re not an achievement freak like me, just play the game on Normal, to circumvent some of the more glaring quality of life issues listed above, and you’ll have a beautiful time.

作为从《刺客信条 2》一路追过来的老玩家，能够明显感觉到从《大革命》带来的创新和变化真的不少。

它试图为刺客信条系列开启一个次世代的新方向，在画面、世界规模和玩法构思上展现了巨大的野心。技术力打造的巴黎至今仍是旅游模拟器的天花板之一，其艺术成就无可否认。

剧情是真的让我又爱又恨。亚诺和艾莉丝的感情线写得太戳人了 —— 热气球上的晨光吻、雨夜里的争吵、结局那封没送出去的信，尤其是艾莉丝死后（DLC列王陵墓），亚诺追着相似背影狂奔的场景，我当时对着屏幕愣了好久。

但主线节奏简直灾难，三级会议、路易十六被处决这些大事件全成了背景板，反而花了太多笔墨在神棍组织上，到最后我都没搞懂反派的动机。

不过支线里的 "谋杀之谜" 必须夸，跟着线索找真凶的过程像在玩推理游戏。

玩法上的革新和坑几乎对半开。跑酷系统在当年绝对是跨时代的，亚诺翻窗、蹬墙、跳屋顶的动作流畅得不像话，配合巴黎高低错落的建筑，有种飞檐走壁的真刺客感。

但这系统也有脾气，窄巷里经常卡墙，人群中容易 "手滑" 摔下屋顶。

战斗系统就更迷了，防反被削弱就算了，连砍三刀还会硬直，遇到多个敌人只能绕着跑，说好的刺客大师怎么成了 "脆皮法师"？。

现在回头看，《大革命》更像育碧的一次技术狂欢：首发的全局光照、无缝地图、千人同屏的群众系统，这些放在2014年都是跨时代的。

但急于展示技术导致优化拉胯，剧情深度配不上画面表现，成了它最大的遗憾。

不过如果你能接受它的缺点，愿意花时间探索巴黎的每个角落，这款游戏依然能给你一场独一无二的革命史诗体验——毕竟，哪里还能找到第二款能让你在刺客信条里当福尔摩斯、和拿破仑并肩作战、还能顺便谈场轰轰烈烈恋爱的游戏呢？

最后：
建议大家按照《刺客信条》游戏的现代故事情节顺序（也是游戏的发售时间顺序）开始游玩。

因为《刺客信条》每代作品的现代剧情是按照发售顺序连贯，而古代线却不一定是连贯的。

这也是体验该系列游戏画面、操作、玩法、刺杀、开放世界等方面演变的最佳方式。

不然一下从刺客新作跳到刺客旧作，那个画质和操作，大部分玩家真的接受不了。

《刺客信条》（Assassin's Creed）（2007年发售）

平心而论，游戏是个好游戏。无论是由装备决定卡组使得组卡组时要综合考虑不至于每张牌都是烂强卡导致卡组千篇一律，还是多种类型的卡片的组合导致战术的多样化，PVE模式的趣味性和PVP模式的斗智斗勇（特别说一下PVP，这个游戏的PVP是真正的根据每期地图和其他对手决定的，比如对面全法师就能采用三战士六豹打，或者两战一牧，对面带五甲的战士多你的战士就多带破甲和穿甲，总之相对复杂的卡组构建，不断变化的地图和多种多样的战术选择使这个游戏的PVP充满了乐趣），还有趣味联赛中的娱乐性更强的对战，丰富多彩的收集元素，以及良心的日商周商使得不氪金也能轻松成为大佬，种种因素使得这个游戏是不错的游戏，即使没有汉化也不影响它本身的趣味性，看到这里大家就应该明白我对这个游戏的喜爱和推荐了吧。
然而，问题不仅仅这么简单，这么优秀的游戏却有着一群跟我们思维构造不同的GM和MOD，他们在没有事先通知的情况下封了几乎所有参加过PVP的人，而且时间有的多达30天甚至是365天，经常玩这个游戏热爱这个游戏每天游戏时间足够长的所有国人无一幸免，而且申诉机制异常奇怪，真正该封禁的人被解封了，无辜群众反而被关在了里面，据一些因为玩游戏频率不高而侥幸逃过一劫的国人反应，本来偏小众的游戏的在线人数进一步减少，本来一场联赛平时1分钟以内就一定能排到对手现在却排了四五分钟都无法匹配成功，游玩人数大量减少，玩家纷纷弃坑，然而面对这种结果，GM和MOD却仍然表示满意，绝对自己做得很是正确。另外，由于这个游戏是人治，所以管理上有明显的偏袒，和mod关系好的人不会被封禁然而其余人很容易被封禁，据少数国人反应，游戏内可能有一定反华倾向，在世界打字中文会收获到举报，总之你一定要做好随时被封禁的心理准备即使你只是正常的老老实实的玩游戏。一次封禁很有可能直接抹消掉你之前的时间和金钱投入，所以，即使这个游戏很有趣，但大家入坑前还是要慎重，即使决定了入坑，购买付费内容的时候还是要慎重，毕竟，他们封禁你的时候不会在乎你花了几百几千人民币的。

[h1] Genre [/h1] Ein Third Person Sandbox Ziegen Simulator

[h1] Gameplay [/h1] Es spielst sich genauso wie das Original. Wir haben hier lediglich eine verbesserte Grafik und ein paar QoL Verbesserungen. Man kann jetzt z.B. jederzeit direkt im Level die Ziegen Mutatoren wechseln bzw. an oder ausschalten. Es sind hier natürlich auch alle DLCs mit inbegriffen + ein Brandneues Level, welches sich "Buck To School" nennt. Es ist eine recht Überschauliche, kleine High School Map aber auch hier gibt es einiges zu Entdecken und auch Ziegen Trophäen zu sammeln. Achievement Mäßig hat man hier ordentlich runter reduziert. Beim Original mit allen DLCs kam man auf 127 Erfolge, hier sind es jetzt nur 42. Das Spiel macht nach wie vor gewohnt Spaß und ist absolutes Chaos

[h1] Achievement Schwierigkeit 4/10 [/h1] Es gibt insgesamt 42 Erfolge. Die Erfolge sind die selben wie im Original. Man muss in allen Leveln alle Ziegen Trophäen sammeln und in jedem Level etwas spezifisches machen. Für einige sollte man einen Guide zur Hand nehmen weil man auf einiges gar nicht kommen würde

[h1] Pro/Contra [/h1]
+ Genau wie das Original, immer noch sehr Witzig für Zwischendurch
+ Man kann jetzt jederzeit im Level die Ziegen Modifikatoren ein & ausschalten
+ Verbesserte Grafik
+ Alle DLCs sind inbegriffen + ein Brandneues Level namens "Buck To School", welches gut gemacht ist
+ Man kann auch hier Couch Co-Op spielen
+ Achievements
+ XBox 360 Controller Support

[h1] Fazit [/h1] Ein sehr nettes Remaster, welches genau wie auch das Original Spiel, sehr spaßig ist. Das Neue Level ist eine Nette Neuerung und macht viel Laune. Zudem sieht die Grafik deutlich Hübscher aus und man jederzeit die Ziegen Modifikatoren im Level wechseln, was ebenfalls eine gute Neuerung ist. Ich kann es jedem Fan vom Original Spiel sehr Empfehlen. ich hatte damals viel Spaß mit dem Original und auch das Remaster hier, hat mir sehr viel Spaß gemacht

I was hoping this would be a lot closer to being a 1.0 release than it currently is. I know the team pushed back the deadline and I do appreciate them doing their best to make a quality game. I can see the potential for the game, but I can't really recommend it as is. Hopefully the future updates improve the game and I can update my review.

[h1]Positives:[/h1]
+ Character designs, movement, abilities all feel really good.
+ Game's art style is polished and distinct. Not a whole lot of games that look like this so its a nice change of pace.
+ Harvesting mechanics are fun, picking up trees and throwing them into sawmills (or vice-versa) is a unique aspect of the game and I would love to see more.

[h1]Negatives:[/h1]
[h2]Lack of System Feedback[/h2]
There are a lot of systems in the game, but they either aren't transparent enough to let you know what is going on or they don't do anything noticeable. It doesn't matter if your villagers hate your guts or that a biome is full of pollution. Things seem to keep on going the same. I can see the developer not wanting to add full on fail states, but I feel like these systems should have some reasonable outcomes and difficulty could set the severity of the issues:
Low citizen happiness: They riot and defect into bandits.
High pollution: Lower happiness, stronger enemies with worse drops.
Hunger: If a villager is at 0% food for long enough they die.
and so on.

Having an advisor character/panel that could let you know when something isn't right would be a good way to let the player know what to fix.

Increased visibility to metrics of a region, building, or villager would also maybe give you a better idea of what is going wrong.

[h2]Lack of Depth/Control[/h2]
It feels like being the ruler should involve more ruling. Filling out the tech tree is decent progression, but it would be nice to have things like royal decrees that have trade-offs.
ex:
Being able to increase money earned at the cost of happiness.
Generate 200% more metal at the cost of more coal and even more pollution.
Loggers plant new trees at the cost of fertilizer.

These of course only work if the systems above do enough to get the player's interest.

Being able to tell villagers to run from threats or not, letting builders clear obstacles for buildings set via the map would all be good quality of life changes.

[h2]Lack of Stress/Goals[/h2]
The bandit raid with the ability to diminish the raid by destroying their camps is great, but it's the only real pressure felt by the player. More varied events like this one could keep things fun.

Paying off a difficult opponent could be another fun way to play. Imagine the bandits demand coin instead, you can pay them off and focus more on resource generation until you think you can beat them. Alternatively give the player a couple of in-game weeks to stockpile a resource to trade for a bigger reward. ex: Collect tomatoes for a visiting kingdom to get a new ability or a ton of coins.

[h2]Bugs and Performance[/h2]
I found after playing for a few hours the game became very choppy especially while looking at most of the world. I'm betting with some clever optimization and adjusting texture/animation/simulation quality at a distance could improve things quite a bit. No reason to calculate the physics of a tree falling on the other-side of the map, even if it is pretty cool.

The game becomes laggy as the world generates. I feel like spacing re-generation out more and having a hard stop with a stats screen might work better. The screen could tell you how you did compared to the last in-game week and if you have a problem or goal appearing in so much time. Pausing all the AI and interactions in the world would let the regeneration occur faster as well so it might be over in a few seconds as opposed to a few minutes of sluggish game play.

I also ran into bugs where my population couldn't find homes, despite having more than enough unused housing for everyone. Villagers also couldn't find jobs despite there being plenty.

Me and my fiance have been playing Borderlands together through our entire relationship, going on fifteen years at this point. We've played the entire series all the way through multiple times. We've both played nearly every character to max level, and have always enjoyed playing the game together. When Borderlands 4 came out, people kept saying it wasn't good, but we were skeptical- we heard people ask the question: if it's just another borderlands game, is that enough? Our answer was yes. 

Our answer is still yes. 

But there's no easy way to say this: this doesn't meet that standard. And I'll take the time to go into depth for why.

First, expectations. Most assessments we saw before getting the game were negative. We didn't expect this to rival Borderlands 2. We expected, at best, something more on par with 3. We heard there was a darker tone to this game, and that was actually a welcome idea. Taking the series in a new direction could be a good thing, leaning a little away from the cornball humor might be good for things. So while we weren't expecting anything amazing, there was optimism. 

Then, the tone- the prologue shows you a villain who takes people's free will and does some pretty horrible things. You see, for instance, a man forced to murder all his friends with his bare hands before snapping his own neck, and another man forced to stab himself to death. This villain comes off as very serious, very dangerous. It'd be like if they actually showed you Handsome Jack gouging a man's eyes out with a spoon instead of just mentioning it. But literally the next scene is Claptrap singing some nonsense song about collecting beach trash for change, and we spend time palling around with him as he's his wacky self. What happened to the darker tone? It's a jarring shift. Even the scenery shifts suddenly- the prologue is dark and dreary, fitting with the dark tone, but it suddenly shifts to a vibrant coastal mountain range that almost looks like something out of fortnite. In game, it hardly even looks like Borderlands. The comic book aesthetic is downplayed compared to previous entries.

Next, the gameplay. There are three issues- the guns, the enemies and the player characters. 
Compared to other entries in the series, the guns are HORRIBLY bland and boring. The "boring" manufacturers- that is, the ones that just make "ordinary" weapons- seem to be the best for the chunk of the game i played. Gone are the chargeable Maliwan weapons, the Tediores that sprout legs and chase enemies down when reloaded, the Atlas smart bullets. An assault rifle or a pistol from a given manufacturer will behave pretty much the same as another one- you don't see the variety of effects. Borderlands 3, by comparison, had the guns down. Every manufacturer felt different- a Jakobs felt like a cannon, Tediore felt like something someone 3D printed, Dahl like you were playing CoD... Of all the things to screw up, making the guns feel samey in a Borderlands game is unfathomable, but they did it. 

The enemies lack variety and don't do interesting things. In BL3, Maliwan soldiers moved from cover to cover and fought tactically, COV fought with abandon. It feels like enemies all fight the same in this game- and beyond that, you run into the same kinds over and over. You have Rippers, Timekeeper Minions, and animals- and none of them seem to have unique AI, when they even HAVE functioning AI. The amount of times an enemy will just lock in place and let you shoot them to death is staggering. Beyond that, they're SUCH bullet sponges- a normal enemy of your level should not require you to empty several magazines to take out.

Finally, the characters- this is a weird complaint to have to say, but... you get your toys too fast. In Borderlands, by the end of the game, things get silly- you have a Fire Kreig in BL2 shooting homing exploding fireballs at anyone that hits him, and healing for all the elemental damage he does... but you get this at the end of the game. Similarly, my maxed out Ice Zane in BL3 has permanent action skills because the durations reset every time I freeze something. Things GET silly... but here, my gravitar can delete an entire camp of enemies  with one shot of her action skill by level 10. Without depth, and with guns being so weak in comparison, this gets very boring very fast. 

Finally, the world and characters... they don't fit with this villain at all. You have a villain literally enslaving a planet and forcing people to kill themselves in brutal and horrifying ways, and the first chunk of the game is a sun drenched beachfront paradise brimming with color and characters acting silly. What happened here? Was there some kind of rift in the writing team? The first town is populated by a pack of what I can only call goofy goobers, not a single one of which looks like they're having anything other than the time of their lives. Sure, they SAY they're oppressed, but when you have your alleged resistance leader literally always wearing a huge grin, "anxiety baking" and busting out the star shaped cookie cutters... and the civilians sitting around eating TV dinners in the open while commenting offhandedly that they're not even hungry, they're just eating because they're bored... the town not having a single armed guard, wall or even lookout tower...

Well, I just can't believe that these people are the resistance fighting against the villain you showed me earlier. No.  These people have an overabundance of food, and are apparently so secure that they live in an open town on the road with no means to defend themselves. Were there soft civilians in borderlands 2? Yes, they lived in a walled town full of guards. Were there quirky weirdos hanging around in borderlands 3? Yes, but they were armed and would fight when prompted. 

You might think, some of these reasons to not like it are kinda petty. Well, unfortunately, when your gameplay loop isn't fun, these things really stick out. And this gameplay loop isnt fun. The world is big and empty- like a dead server on an MMO, the enemies are samey, the guns are boring and ineffective, the action skills are cartoonishly imbalanced, the tone is all over the place, and the NPCs don't fit the villain. 

Bottom Line? We both paid over $100 for this game, and it's pretty bad. I don't know if my fiance feels the same, but I feel like I got suckered. In it's current state, HEAVILY not recommended.

[h1]Ōkami is a truly unique experience...[/h1]

a game where art, myth, and heart coexist in harmony. Its art style, the vibrant music, and the playful comedy all blend together beautifully. What held it back for me, was its overly episodic first half, a long stretch of random quests that made it feel unfocused. But once the story begins to tighten, everything changes. The narrative takes off into something deeply emotional and powerful, and all that early buildup finally makes sense.

What makes Ōkami special isn’t just its gameplay or even its visual artistry — it’s the quiet spirituality behind it. You don’t just play as Amaterasu, the sun goddess in the form of a wolf; you become the witness of divine compassion itself. There are few games that make you feel what it might be like to be a god — not through power, but through empathy, patience, and love for all living things. The game lets you experience creation, care, and faith from a perspective both cosmic and deeply human. It’s subtle, wordless, and absolutely profound.

Ōkami feels like a quiet masterpiece that reveals its depth only to those who stay with it. Beneath its colorful humor and cartoon charm lies something ancient and true — a reflection on the meaning of prayers and how it connects everything.
It’s not just about restoring the world, but about remembering why we do. For me, it became one of those rare games on which I shed tears for.

以下日本語の攻略情報が少なかったので参考までに
-------
## ストーリー攻略
最初のマップから次は砂漠か火山に向かうメインクエストになるのだが、
対空攻撃が解禁されてから敵が密集して配置されてたり、引き寄せ攻撃、凍結攻撃、高火力気球など出てきて「え？」ってくらい難易度が上がる。
序盤でクソゲーとならないためには、

＊すべてのクエストクリアまでは都市を大きくしすぎず～40人程度小型都市で運用する
　機動力やヒットボックスを単純に小さくするため
　大きくしすぎても恐らくリカバリが間に合わずに資産欠乏状態になってしまう
＊メインクエストの砂漠or火山は砂漠を最初に進める
　火山メインクエストのボスがクソ、育ってから進めたほうがいい
＊サブクエスト、マップの未開地探索は優先して行う
　設計図の解放や遺物が重要なため
＊研究の優先順位は基本をメインに戦闘、貯蔵、揚力or推進
＊バラージキャンのは早めに解放、建設する
　集的対策
＊テスラ・コイルは早めに解放、建設する
　範囲対空みたいな説明だが、それプラス範囲の砲弾も防いでくれるシールドの役割がある
＊航空機を出してくる塔みたいな敵拠点を優先的に破壊する
　航空機が無限に湧いてくるので
＊炎上砲台も優先して破壊する。燃え続けてすぐに建築物が壊れる
＊光塔は早めに解放し、遺物が手に入ったら建設する
　ダメージカットや資源消費コストといった強い遺物がメイン、サイドストーリーで手に入り戦闘がかなり楽になる
＊速度は50％以上をできれば保つ
　砲撃をよけれたり、敵の同速度に追いつけず一方的に攻撃されないようにするため
＊一つのメインクエストをクリアすると、一部空賊はリポップする？感じがあるのでマップの空賊を殲滅してから次のクエスト～とやると二度手間になるかも

上記を意識すれば比較的なんとか進められた。メインクエストで敵が強くて倒せなかったら他メインやサイドを進めて自軍を強化しよう。
また戦闘中に手が回らなくなったらちゃんと一時停止して状況を整理して対応しましょう。

## 他トロコン攻略
場所が明記されないクエストの情報についてはSteamのコミュニティページに書いてある。
そこで手に入る設計図はかなり強力だがストーリー攻略で使うにはリスク高いためクリア後のやりこみ要素感覚で。

空賊船団はリヴァイアサンみたいな生物がいる島の周辺を回遊していることが多い気がする。

設計図は基本メイン、サイドクエストでほぼ揃うが、揚力２つの設計図は空を飛んでる商人から買う。
だいたい「ウォッチフォート」と「リタロス」周辺を周回してる。

設計図の研究についてはどんなに研究施設を増やして減らすことができるが、それでも結構時間かかるため早めに進めたほうが放置の時間が少なくて済む。

王国人口250人達成に向けては50人単位くらいで雇用金額が上がっていくのでそれなりにお金がかかる。
市場でガンガン買い物している攻略だとマップで手に入る金額だけでは足りなくなるかも。
膨大な資源と、雇用の関係ですべての集落や都市を巡回するためクリア後、すべてのクエストをクリアして空賊がマップから大幅に減った後にやると効率がいい。

Fatal Frame / Project Zero: Mask of the Lunar Eclipse, developed and published by KOEI TECMO GAMES CO., LTD., is a haunting resurrection of one of the series’ most elusive entries. Originally released exclusively in Japan in 2008 for the Nintendo Wii, this remastered version finally brings the mysterious Rogetsu Island to a global audience with enhanced visuals, refined presentation, and the same chilling spirit that defined the franchise’s legacy. It’s a game that blends psychological horror, tragic storytelling, and methodical exploration into an experience that feels distinctly old-fashioned in its pacing, yet timeless in atmosphere. Though the gameplay retains many of its early design quirks, it stands as both a love letter to the series’ roots and a reminder of how effective Fatal Frame’s brand of slow-burn terror can be.

The story begins with a group of girls who were once kidnapped on Rogetsu Isle during a festival years earlier. Rescued but left with their memories erased, they return as young women to uncover the truth behind what happened to them and the mysterious illness that seems to follow in the aftermath. The narrative unfolds through multiple perspectives, shifting between characters such as Ruka, Misaki, and Madoka, each with their own psychological scars and personal connections to the island’s haunting secrets. As they explore the decaying remains of hospitals, shrines, and mansions, the boundaries between the living and the dead blur, and the players must piece together the truth through journals, photographs, and spectral encounters. What makes the story engaging is its melancholy tone—the horror here isn’t just in the ghosts but in the weight of forgotten memories and lingering guilt. Every specter tells a fragment of a tragedy, and uncovering those fragments becomes as compelling as surviving the island itself.

At the core of Mask of the Lunar Eclipse’s gameplay lies the iconic Camera Obscura—a weapon and storytelling device rolled into one. Players use the antique camera to fend off hostile spirits by photographing them, capturing their energy and revealing their tortured pasts. The mechanic remains one of the most creative in horror gaming: combat feels intimate and terrifying, forcing you to look directly at your enemy instead of running away. Each battle becomes a tense test of timing and courage, as ghosts lunge toward you and you wait for the precise moment—known as the “Fatal Frame”—to take the shot and deal maximum damage. The remaster improves the responsiveness of aiming and adds modern conveniences, but the essence of the combat remains faithful to its origins: methodical, nerve-wracking, and deeply atmospheric. The combination of combat and exploration ensures that moments of safety are fleeting, as every dark corridor or flickering light could hide a phantom waiting to be revealed through your lens.

Visually, the remaster breathes new life into the game without sacrificing its eerie charm. The environments—dilapidated sanatoriums, fog-drenched courtyards, and ceremonial halls—are rendered with impressive lighting and texture work that highlight the game’s focus on shadow and contrast. The new character models and animations are more lifelike, yet they retain a certain dreamlike quality that enhances the supernatural tone. The lighting engine, in particular, plays a crucial role in maintaining tension; the faint glow of a flashlight cutting through the dark hallways often reveals just enough to fuel the imagination but not enough to provide comfort. The sound design complements this perfectly. Creaking wood, distant whispers, and mournful melodies evoke constant unease, while the faint shutter clicks of the Camera Obscura punctuate the experience like the beating of a terrified heart. It’s a sensory experience that rewards headphones and patience, relying less on jump scares and more on slow, creeping dread.

Despite its strengths in atmosphere and storytelling, Mask of the Lunar Eclipse still bears the marks of its original design era. The character movement feels sluggish, and navigating tight corridors can sometimes be cumbersome due to limited camera angles and deliberate animation pacing. While this slow rhythm contributes to the sense of vulnerability and realism, it may frustrate players accustomed to the fluid controls of contemporary horror titles. The backtracking—a hallmark of classic survival horror—is abundant here, and though it adds to the tension, it can occasionally feel repetitive. Combat, while engaging, can also lack variety, as most encounters follow a predictable rhythm of photographing ghosts at key moments. Still, for fans of the genre, these elements add to the nostalgic authenticity of the experience, recalling a time when horror games relied more on atmosphere and restraint than on spectacle or speed.

Narratively, the remaster preserves the complex, layered storytelling that defines the Fatal Frame series. Each character’s journey explores themes of identity, memory, and ritual sacrifice, gradually tying together through documents and flashbacks scattered across the island. The game’s central mystery—the ritual surrounding the lunar eclipse and the masks used in the island’s ceremonies—offers both cultural intrigue and emotional weight. The pacing of the revelations is deliberate, sometimes even glacial, but it allows the tension to build organically. The result is a story that feels more sorrowful than purely terrifying, a meditation on the ghosts of human emotion as much as supernatural ones. This blend of tragedy and horror has always been Fatal Frame’s signature, and Mask of the Lunar Eclipse exemplifies it beautifully.

In the end, Fatal Frame / Project Zero: Mask of the Lunar Eclipse is a hauntingly elegant revival of a lost classic. It’s a game that thrives on mood, patience, and empathy, offering an experience that is as much about uncovering personal pain as it is about surviving the supernatural. While its gameplay may feel dated to newcomers and its pacing occasionally meanders, its atmosphere, storytelling, and artistic direction remain among the finest in the genre. For longtime fans, this release is both a long-awaited reunion and a preservation of a key piece of horror gaming history. For new players, it’s an opportunity to experience a slower, more introspective kind of terror—one that lingers long after the final ghost has been exorcised.

《祭囃篇》：8.4 / 10 （优秀）

单周目流程时长：15 - 30 小时

——————

“孩子们，我的外挂到账了，我们有救了”

本篇的游玩模式非常特殊，不同于其他篇章，它并不是纯粹的单线，而是走着碎片叙事的路子。在剧情的中途，玩家需要收集并解锁51块碎片，也就是阅读51篇关于雏见泽过往的故事后，才能够进入主线。

说实话，在本篇之前我本来以为自己已经对这些角色足够了解。结果这些碎片真的是一条比一条关键，几乎把所有空白都补齐了——这一点属实是超乎我的预期。

是时候，整理一下目前为止的真相了。

一切的开端，起源于一名研究者的梦想。“一定是存在的，那种寄宿在人类大脑中，可以影响情绪的寄生虫”、“只要能够发现这一点，就会在人类的历史上留下重重的一笔”。所以研究者孤注一掷，倾尽一生，渴望建立自己的伟业。

“我的研究总有一天会得到大家的认可，到那个时候，我就可以成为神了。所以没有在有生之年就急着得到世人认可的必要”

“嗯，我为了让爷爷可以得到全世界人类的赞美，也会更加更加努力的帮忙！”

“祖父会成为神”
“我也会成为神”
“所以，可以永远的”
“一直，在一起”

这是，田无美代子的梦想。她的父母瞒着她去百货公司买东西，却因为一次火车脱轨的意外，抛下了年幼的她独自一人。在这之后，她被扔进了如监狱一般的孤儿院。

好在，她父母的恩师，高野一二三爷爷，把她救出了绝望的地狱。尽管两人没有血缘的联系，甚至未曾谋面，但爷爷，仅仅因为几句话还是义无反顾的前来救她。

对于高野三四（美代子和三四同音）来说，这之后的生活，无比的幸福。

她将会成为和爷爷一起数到三，然后能够数到四的人。

但这一切都突然结束了，她爷爷研究一辈子的“雏见泽综合症”，被别人当成废纸。而高野一二三，则成为了众人的笑柄。

高野三四很清楚，神明最喜欢的，就是这样玩弄人类的命运。

在爷爷落泪的那一刻起，高野三四知道了，自己诞生的意义。

坦白讲，本系列真正吸引我的地方，不是什么惊天阴谋，也不是什么过往故事。比起这些，我更在意伙伴们的日常与人情。而本篇开头这段超长的前传，也是再次让我感受到了第一部前期那又无聊又困的体验。

但抱怨归抱怨，不得不承认，鹰野的故事确实写的很出色。

在《皆杀篇》的结局之后，我对鹰野唯一的感想就是快点把她“剁成臊子”，唯一需要考虑的就是“剁的有多碎”。

但是本篇实在是把鹰野的过往描绘的太惨了，把爷爷的梦想描述的太有代入感了，把鹰野的决心诠释的太热血了。

以至我能够理解她对爷爷的爱，以至于我能理解她对于爷爷留下来的研究的执着，以至于我在不知不觉中就原谅了她。


鹰野与“神”的对抗，可以说是贯穿了整篇故事。

她幼年的不幸，让她在与“神”的对峙中获得了胜利，“神”给予了她10元铜板的救赎，将她从泥潭中拉出，返还给了她同等的幸福。但随后，“神”又无情的夺走了她的一切。

为了向神明复仇，她造下无数的孽果，她将10元的铜板还给了“神”，向“神”发出了挑衅的战书。

当鹰野三四真心为了爷爷的学说去行事时，一切好运都仿佛站在她的身边，没有任何的阻碍，所有人都在支持她，仿佛她的爷爷就在身边保佑着她。

可是，正当她以为自己已经战胜了神，凭借着努力超越了命运的时候，“神”却又给她开了一个残酷的玩笑。她所谓的成就，无人在意。一切，不过是因为另一个“爷爷”的庇护。当保护伞消失时，她再次孤独一人，如同一只丧家之犬。

讽刺的是，就当鹰野三佐逐渐忘记了初心，忘记了，爷爷为什么要研究“雏见泽综合征”；当她泯灭人性，背叛了爷爷的研究，摧毁了爷爷建造的“高塔”，只记住“成神”的那一刻起。

她的确成为了击败神的存在。

然而，她以强烈意志编织而成的命运，最终却被更强烈的意志汇聚而成的“奇迹”击碎。残酷，却也是人类这个物种的法则。

而她不经意间保留的最后一丝善意与人性，最终又成为了她唯一的救赎。

说到底，她口中的“神”，究竟是什么呢？


然后是，古手梨花。

本质上，过往篇章里那些伙伴们的心结——梨花都有。她不信任伙伴，自以为坚强，其实是一种软弱。这也是为什么，她一直无法突破自己的命运。

但随着伙伴们的努力，她也终于不再是那个软弱的梨花了。此刻的她，拥有的信念，丝毫不输给鹰野。

本作的暗线很多。园崎魉的转变、大石的决心、圭一的转学、羽入的人生观、沙都子的过去、赤坂的成长、悟史的行踪、蕾娜的黑历史、入江的真面目等等等等。

看起来杂乱且互不关联，但当你梳理完本作的剧情后，就会震惊的发现，这些暗线本质上都是同一条线，环环相扣。所谓的“巧合与奇迹”，全都是来自于个人的情感与努力叠加出的那股永不服输的信念，从而打破那封锁命运的xyz法则，最终战胜鹰野那悲惨且牢固的信念。

其实关于本篇的结局真的没有什么好说的。它的结构就是教科书级别的王道公式，经典大结局伙伴聚集，每人发挥一点高光，然后热血中二发言，反派垂死挣扎。其实在《皆杀篇》，我就已经预料到了这样的结局，所以也没有报多少期待。

不过最后，除了几位成年人的故事之外，它实打实的没有带来多余的惊喜，多少还是让我有点失望的。

不对，不是失望，而是不舍吧。

I never expected the Mystery Dungeon formula to work in a survival horror setting, but somehow it just does. The atmosphere here is just a treat, especially with such a timely October release, and the gameplay is solid too. TL;DR: it's a pretty easy recommendation if you like this particular brand of roguelikes.

While the gameplay is, like I said, solid, it is perhaps a little simplistic, comparatively speaking. The consumables are varied enough, but the equipment leaves something to be desired. Basically there's just 3 types of melee weapons (essentially light, medium, heavy), 3 types of ranged weapons (same here) and armor. Most equipment seals don't really feel as impactful either. Enemy variety is fine, with some of them having somewhat interesting mechanical interactions, every zone of the main dungeon is also capped off with a unique boss. At the end of the day, it is a rather small indie game, I understand that. Still, the developer clearly knew what they were doing and put in a lot of effort, which in my opinion totally paid off.

While retaining items between runs is somewhat common in Mystery Dungeon games, House of Necrosis puts a very big emphasis on retreating, gearing up and trying again, with the items that are necessary for returning to the safe spot being rather abundant - cheap to purchase and having a much higher drop rate if you don't already have one in your inventory or on the floor. You also permanently retain any inventory upgrades and spells you learn, building up power across runs even if you die and lose all your items. Some of the spells are also hilariously overpowered, which is somewhat balanced (but not really) by the fact that you can only use each spell once per run.

That said, you probably won't be dying too much, with the only things really capable of doing you in being a powered up enemy or a monster house. Enemies can powered up for up to two times, gaining HP and damage as they do. The first tier is not too rare and can be seen in the wild, but you probably won't be encountering the second often until you get to the ranged enemies that are able to kill other enemies and power up that way, or unless you use a certain item if you know what you're doing. Monster houses also don't seem to occur naturally in the main dungeon and can only be triggered via a trap. Traps, however, are always marked on the minimap when you're adjacent to them and can be revealed by striking the tile ahead as usual, so they rarely are a problem.

Overall the game is rather easy and short, even if you count the extra dungeons that feature their own unique challenges and some extra postgame stuff. There also doesn't seem to be any kind of time limit nor a hunger mechanic, so you can take your time and play as carefully as you like. There isn't, however, any kind of passive health regen either, healing can only be done via items, spells or traps. On one hand, this keeps the pacing pretty breezy and the game doesn't overstay its welcome. On the other hand, it can absolutely leave you wanting more. Trying to get full completion can be rather grindy and blatantly unfun however, even having the item that is supposed to help with that. The dev is apparently very active in the community and is currently working hard on fixes/changes/additions though, so that might be changing in the foreseeable future.

In conclusion, if any of it sounds even remotely interesting to you, do at least give the demo a shot. It gives a pretty good feel for the game at large, despite being based on an older version. For me personally it was worth picking up at full price after that.
