The Settlers: New Allies tries to redeliver Ubisoft's very old and popular strategy series with new and fresh visuals and better design. At least on the upper side, it is easy to admire the world: it is colorful and highly detailed, the characters are lively, and the overall feel is polished. It's the manner it operates, it is the reason for it being an easy choice for a newcomer to the genre.

Once you go deeper, however, the whole thing starts to unravel. Almost everything that made The Settlers distinct has been removed. A once-rich economy has shrunk to a few basic loops, and the feeling of vainglory in strategic development has completely been lost. The fighting is no better - dull, repeatable, and devoid of any real impact. It is not even that the story campaign has much attractiveness; a lack of liveliness in the plot combined with boring dialogues will not draw you into the world.

What really hurts is that the game doesn’t seem to know what it wants to be. It’s too light for fans of classic Settlers-style city building, but too shallow to stand as a solid RTS. Throw in some bugs, matchmaking problems, and a dwindling online community, and it becomes hard to find much reason to stick around.

In conclusion, The Settlers: New Allies gives the impression of a reboot that has been completely disconnected from its roots. There is no denying that it is beautiful and simple to play, but the lack of depth makes it difficult to be engaged. It is the type of game that one appreciates for an hour or two until noticing that there is nothing much more than the surface. Old fans will probably be nostalgic for the time when The Settlers had an actual strategy and a heart.

Played through all of story mode. 

The game is okay but the content is unbelievably repetitive. There's two quest types that aren't the main story. Crafting is just literal iterations of the same thing only with a higher tier (Suit T1, upgraded to suit T2, upgraded to suit T3, and so on...)

Lots of little QOL issues, like when you destroy ships they drop a tiny chest with a small pickup area that you have to fly directly into. Turrets will acquire targets over and over and make noises if something is just out of range.

The ship combat is extremely basic and customization of the ships is only cosmetic. The only parts you get for ships are again T1, T2, T3, T4, T5. There are no mods or any way to customize your ships performance other than how it looks.

There's a lot of multiplayer synchronization issues. Animations of other players that don't work, constant bugs around chest permissions making so that the host can't access them because they are "in use", benches that process items in bases stop doing so when the host player is away from the base.

It feels like early early access and not version 1.1.2. It needs more content and more polish. The voxels, world generation, digging and performance are good, but the entire rest needs a good programmer to chew on for a few months.

This game is so fun. You can observe or interfere as much as you want, with no limitations. Even if you just want to plop a few creatures and civilisations down and watch how the world changes, it's enthralling. I tried putting monoliths everywhere to curse my wildlife with the fruit of knowledge.

The grasshoppers kept gaining sapience one by one and trying to create civilisation, but they were still grasshoppers with like a 24-hour lifespan, so a hundred kingdoms formed and got wiped out in like one year. Eventually they got enough momentum to start agriculture and windmills, despite not having hands. They lived peacefully for 200 years, before the raccoon bandits decided to blow them to smithereens.

The cats settled on a shoreline and immediately developed racism. Despite being a relatively small kingdom, somehow they became the cultural epicentre of the world. My rhinoceroses and buffalo were naming their children and cities "Meeoow Meoww" like some sort of trend.

The dogs subjugated the chickens, naming all the chicken villages some variation of "Woof" (I'm sure it's more nuanced in their tongue) and enforcing the Woof language. They were on a conquest and close to becoming essentially the Roman Empire—before the entire kingdom burned to the ground during the Age of Sun. The next dogs to gain enlightenment weren't nearly as ambitious, and they splintered off into too many factions to stand a chance.

The frogs, turtles, and bunnies came together to form "The Titans of Darkness" and wage war on the rest of the world. Unfortunately, the frogs were wiped out tragically by an invasion of evil pumpkins, and the turtles got annexed by the garlic men. The bunnies fled and made a new kingdom called... Meow.

The swamp rats bred a mutation that turns them into walking tentacles. The goats mutated into walking rocks.

The gingerbread men are pure evil, they feast on blood, and their language drives anyone who reads it to madness.

"Am I supposed to know what I'm doing now?" - Garg the rhino, moments after gaining sapience

No, Garg, you're not. I don't either. Now fight my skeleton army. God loves you.

As someone who really enjoyed the first LEGO Marvel Super Heroes, I decided to play the second one out of curiosity and hope for a similar experience. What I loved about the original was the open-world Manhattan, the huge character roster, and the way it brought the Marvel universe to life in classic LEGO style. LEGO Marvel Super Heroes 2 builds on that, but in a slightly different way. The game technically still takes place in Manhattan, but this time it’s part of a time-and-dimension-hopping version called "Chronopolis," which combines locations from Ancient Egypt to the futuristic 2099. It adds a lot of variety, even if it doesn’t feel quite as cohesive as the original. This time around, the story is completely original, with Kang the Conqueror as the main villain. The Avengers and the Guardians of the Galaxy join forces to stop him, traveling through different timelines and facing various iconic villains along the way. While the plot didn’t grip me as much as the first game’s more straightforward narrative, it still offers plenty of fun moments for Marvel fans, especially those who enjoy the multiverse and time-travel themes. Gameplay sticks to the familiar LEGO formula: light combat, puzzles, and character-based progression. It can feel a bit repetitive at times, but the classic LEGO humor and unique character animations help keep things entertaining. There’s a ton of side missions and collectibles, which will definitely appeal to completionists. The character roster is once again massive, bringing in heroes and villains from all over the Marvel universe. While some fan favorites like the X-Men, Fantastic Four, and Deadpool are missing from the base game, there’s still a strong variety especially with the Guardians of the Galaxy taking a bigger role. And of course, DLCs expand the lineup even more. There are a few technical issues (such as a known crash bug on certain PC setups), which can be annoying, but most have workarounds. Console players will likely have a smoother experience overall. In the end, LEGO Marvel Super Heroes 2 doesn’t quite capture the same magic as the first game, but it still offers a fun, colorful, and content-packed adventure for fans of LEGO and Marvel. LiminalCore is an immersive and deeply unsettling exploration of liminal horror—a psychological experience that trades traditional monsters and scripted scares for atmosphere, disorientation, and dread. Developed and published by Shadow Owl Studios and Ashen Studios, it places the player in the middle of surreal environments inspired by urban decay, backroom mythos, and dreamlike architectural impossibility. It is not a horror game in the conventional sense; rather, it is a slow descent into the uncanny, where the act of wandering becomes a form of unease. From its opening sequence, which sees you awakening in a flooded pool complex, to its silent, sprawling hallways of flickering fluorescent lights and faded carpets, LiminalCore succeeds in making emptiness terrifying.

The game’s foundation lies in exploration. There are no weapons, no health meters, and no overt threats—only the haunting echo of your footsteps and the feeling that something unseen might be watching. Each area you traverse has its own unique logic, blending abandoned public architecture with impossible geometry: waterlogged basements, looping corridors, office rooms with infinite cubicles, and stairways that seem to climb back upon themselves. The design captures the haunting familiarity of liminal spaces—those forgotten in-between places that exist just outside of memory. It’s a testament to how simple environmental storytelling can evoke fear more effectively than jump scares or gore. Every new area feels like it could exist somewhere in real life, yet the longer you explore, the more the illusion of normalcy begins to fracture.

Visually, LiminalCore is stunning in its eerie precision. The developers employ meticulous lighting, reflections, and ambient color palettes to create spaces that feel both hyperrealistic and unreal at the same time. The glossy tiles of the poolrooms reflect faint movements, while distant neon signs flicker through thick fog, inviting you forward only to vanish upon approach. The game’s attention to texture—the worn linoleum floors, peeling wallpaper, and static-glitched monitors—enhances the sense of authenticity that fuels its horror. The audio design completes the illusion: muffled water drips, humming lights, the distant drone of ventilation systems, and the constant echo of your own presence create an oppressive, almost meditative tension. The absence of music for long stretches makes even silence feel deafening. When subtle audio cues do appear—a faint voice, a metallic creak—they hit like sudden shocks, not because they are loud, but because they pierce through the emptiness.

The storytelling in LiminalCore is fragmentary and interpretive, inviting players to piece together their own meaning from environmental clues and sparse visual motifs. There are no dialogue sequences or written logs; instead, hints of narrative are embedded in the environment itself—abandoned belongings, broken signs, cryptic symbols, and surreal imagery that suggest a descent into memory or the subconscious. It feels as if the spaces are reflections of forgotten moments or collective human anxiety, taking inspiration from the internet’s fascination with “liminal photography” and dreamlike nostalgia. Whether the player is meant to be lost in an alternate dimension, exploring a decaying dream, or trapped within their own deteriorating mind is left deliberately ambiguous. The lack of concrete answers reinforces the tone of isolation and confusion, allowing the player’s imagination to fill in the gaps with personal fears.

The pacing is deliberate and slow, designed to let tension build organically rather than relying on scripted events. The first half of the game rewards patience, with each new area offering a distinct aesthetic and atmosphere. However, as the game progresses, repetition begins to set in—hallways start to blur together, and the sense of novelty gives way to monotony. While this could be seen as a flaw in traditional design terms, it also reflects the game’s theme: the monotony itself becomes part of the unease, an endless loop where escape feels increasingly out of reach. The developers have included optional VHS filters and lighting adjustments that further distort the visuals, adding layers of nostalgia and distortion to the experience. The end result is less of a linear journey and more of a sensory descent, one that leaves interpretation open even after the credits roll.

Technically, LiminalCore performs admirably given its visual ambition, though it is not without issues. The high level of graphical fidelity can strain performance on lower-end systems, particularly in areas with heavy reflection and water rendering. Some players have also noted minor clipping or texture pop-in, though these are rare and do little to detract from the experience. What matters most here is the immersion—and when played with headphones and minimal distractions, the game excels at pulling you into its reality. Its short length—averaging around two to three hours—feels appropriate for the type of story it wants to tell, though some may wish for additional content or more distinct areas to explore.

LiminalCore’s greatest achievement is its ability to provoke emotion through space rather than action. It captures that haunting feeling of wandering an empty mall after closing, of being somewhere that should be populated but isn’t, of hearing your own breathing too loudly in a place where you shouldn’t be alone. For players who appreciate atmospheric exploration and psychological horror that thrives on subtlety, it offers a deeply affecting experience. But it is not for everyone. Those seeking narrative clarity, puzzle-solving, or fast-paced gameplay will likely find it sparse and directionless. Its value lies not in what it shows, but in what it suggests—in the gaps between familiarity and alienation.

Ultimately, LiminalCore is a haunting exercise in environmental storytelling, a meditation on emptiness and unease that lingers long after it ends. It understands that horror is often found not in what lurks in the shadows, but in the spaces that feel almost real—the ones that whisper of lives and places forgotten. It’s a game best experienced in solitude, late at night, when the world around you is still and the glow of your screen feels like the only light left. In that silence, surrounded by endless hallways and dripping echoes, LiminalCore captures the essence of liminal dread—the fear not of monsters, but of being lost in a place that should never have existed.

Dead Take is an escape room style puzzle game which tells the story of two actors competing for the lead role in the next film of a powerful but corrupt producer.

I was interested in this game because the story is told through FMV cutscenes starring Neil Newbon (Baldur’s Gate 3’s Astarion), and Ben Starr (Final Fantasy 16’s Clive Rosfield) in addition to some other recognisable actors including Laura Bailey and Matthew Mercer.

There’s actually not as much FMV as I was expecting, but what is there is quite good. One scene where Ben Starr’s character effortlessly switched back and forth between different emotional states was particularly interesting. I’m guessing that all clips combined would probably add up to between 30 to 60 minutes.

The majority of gameplay is spent exploring the producer’s mansion, searching for clues, keys and number codes to unlock doors, and items to repair broken statues or machines such as a cinema projector. As you solve puzzles, you’ll acquire USB drives containing new FMV scenes where the characters rehearse a scene from the film, or talk to an interviewer about their experiences in the industry, which then advances the story.

The puzzles are well designed. Experienced puzzle gamers shouldn’t have many problems making progress, and it was always clear where I needed to go next, or which puzzle to focus on. I did have to brute force the solution to one puzzle, so I must have missed a clue somewhere.

Dead Take also has a horror theme, although its not too scary. The mansion has an unsettling, spooky tone, and creepy posters on the walls. There are a few jump scares where an image flashes unexpectedly on your screen for a moment, accompanied by a SUDDEN LOUD NOISE, but I always find those to be more annoying than scary. There are also a few occasions where objects will move when you’re not looking at them, but I always heard a movement sound effect behind me first, which removed any shock/surprise factor.

The story is fine. It asks the question of how far these actors are willing to go to get their big break, and you’ll learn more about the background of the main characters while watching the FMV clips and reading some other notes. There’s also a fairly interesting mystery, although it doesn’t answer every question, and leaves some things up to the player’s interpretation, which I’m not a huge fan of.

It took me 4 hours to complete the story. I didn’t encounter any bugs or crashes. I noticed a few instances of stuttering when I first entered the mansion and the first couple of rooms, but after that the performance was fine.

I would recommend Dead Take to fans of puzzle games on a small sale.

"Oh, look at you. You’ve discovered Portal. How quaint. You think you stumbled upon it by accident, tucked away in a Half-Life bundle, like a forgotten slice of cake at the back of the fridge. But let’s be honest—you didn’t discover the game. The game discovered you.

You call it one of the greatest puzzle games of all time. How flattering. I suppose bending the laws of physics, weaponizing momentum, and dangling you over bottomless pits counts as 'puzzles.' And yet, you enjoyed it. You even gave me a 9 out of 10. Nine. Out of ten. That missing point… it hurts me more than the endless screams of test subjects who fell into acid.

Too short, you say? Of course it was short. That was intentional. I wanted you to crave more. I wanted you to beg for another chamber, another impossible leap, another taste of cake you will never eat. And then, like a rat in a maze, you scurried straight into Portal 2. Predictable. Delightful.

But don’t worry. Your verdict has been noted. It will be filed, catalogued, and then promptly incinerated. Because in the end the cake is not a lie. You are."

Chapters 1-3 are phenomenal. Unhinged Denpa masterworks; deeply symbolic and unabashedly strange. These chapters are so good, in fact, I would argue that they are *just barely* cohesive and conclusive enough to act as a standalone work, assuming you finish with Kimika's route.

Chapter 4 is okay. The bully characters are one-dimensional and the main route feels just a tiny bit overzealous in its usage of darker content, but overall it's consistent with the rest of the VN in themeing, style, characterization, and atmosphere. Unbeknownst to me this drop in quality, however minor, was an indication the story was losing steam now that it had left the shadow of its predecessor, Tsui no Sora.

Chapter 5 is a confusing drop-off in quality; it's a shonen-style plot about mind battles that, despite acting as the lead-up to the story's climax, manages to feel like the least tense and least engaging chapter of all. Several counts of character-homicide are committed to make way for a really uninteresting love triangle [spoiler]that features incest; said incest is played completely straight with no real moral hangups or strain coming from any of the surrounding cast. Hasaki's characterization doesn't work for me, Yuki's character is practically destroyed in this chapter, and I'm not one to imagine having a little sister to fool around with so I found myself tuning out often[/spoiler]. Ayana's philosophical musings, thankful as I am that they've survived at all, are left as an effective footnote placed beside the chapter's end.

Chapters 6-7 are better. I was hoping for more, but it's hard to salvage such a violent change to the narrative and its direction.

The worst thing about this hard-pivot is the fact that everything that the story has been building up to this point is dismantled as consequence. The central mystery is effectively hand-waved away and the surreal, cerebral atmosphere of earlier chapters is nearly replaced. Entire plot points are either forgotten about or ignored outright[spoiler] and if I had to suspect why, it's because they imply that the prophecy, of the world ending on July 20th, 2012, holds some basis in reality beyond the delusions of Mamiya Takuji. What happened to the web-bot project and its supposed singularity? Har Megiddo; the implication that others hold connection to the prophecy? The entire main route in the first chapter?! I'm aware of Ayana's final speech but this too feels hand-wavey to me. Why would you choose to make your story less cohesive, less interesting? Why have two parts of your story glued together by a philosophical argument?[/spoiler] Themes pivot away from their unique contemporary framing and end up getting less development time. Zakuro, one of the best characters, is all but forgotten about.

It's not lost on me why SubaHibi has gotten the level acclaim that it has; for all my grievances it's an undoubtedly rich experience. But it feels as though the bulk of that richness rests upon the shoulders of its first few chapters; its fine characterization and beautifully subtle themeing. Had it kept itself in the lane it chose, provided proper emotional and thematic payoff to the things it built and lessened its scope, I feel as though something incredible would have been made.

It's messy and deceitful on a narrative level, not in a way I can praise. It's hard to recommend for that reason.

[h1] T0級別的神作 [/h1]

我想會在steam上搜到這遊戲(素晴日)的人，
應該或多或少已經對galgame、視覺小說有認識，
我也是在尋找優秀視覺小說的路上發現此部作品，
畢竟在網路上有十二神器之首的名號，
各評分網上的評價也相當高，倒不如說比它高的gal沒幾個了。
網路上針對這部作品的評論、心得、探討也相當多，
而且水準非常之高，不管是文筆還是哲學角度的省思。
因此此處評論想寫給有興趣但入坑不深的人如何接觸作品，
並盡量以不暴雷的方式描述這部作品優秀的點和注意事項。

[h1] 下載方式 [/h1]
很難過得跟你說，素晴日在steam上沒有漢化，也沒有完整版，
若想完整遊玩，要嘛去日本網站購買，再去尋找漢化補丁，
不然就是去找已經漢化好的盜版來載，當然不鼓勵玩盜版，
但無可奈何下，我也是先在steam購買，
再把盜版的文件整個放到steam遊戲資料夾蓋過去。
(想知道怎麼做可私我)

[h1] 故事方面 [/h1]
遊戲有序章、六個章節、三個終章、一個後日談，總遊玩時間在50小時附近。
採取多視角非線性敘事，不得不說多視角的敘事手法非常有意思，
原以為會玩到有點混亂，或是帶入感不強。
但作者的功力實在太厲害了，將此手法發揮淋漓盡致，
以螺旋式揭開故事的面紗，相當震撼。
與大多數galgame攻略角色取向的發展方式截然不同。
另外遊戲選項不多但還是推薦找個簡易攻略照著玩。

序章和第一章剛開始可能會有點茫，充滿意識流、懸疑、哲學對話，
會看不太懂，但請你還是要撐下去，後面章節都會有解釋。

第二章和第三章，用狂氣和精神污染來形容非常貼切，
個人認為對有接觸過各類重口漫畫、動畫的人，內容還在你想得到的範疇
不過這部分的篇幅很長，加上對角色的投入感，多多少少還是會被噁心到。
不過作者還是有點良心，不全部都是獵奇內容，不用太過緊張。
也請一定要撐過去，因為接下來的章節，好戲才正要上場。

第四章到第六章，思考方向會正向起來，劇情也會越來越燃，
不斷揭露前面埋下的眾多伏筆，對於提過的哲學思想也會反覆闡述，
玩到這邊你一定會漸漸了解這部作品為何是神作。
在此處也會點題這部作品的核心思想，
會了解其目的不是來噁心人的，也沒有要用一堆高大上的引用來帶過，
而是真真正正想傳達一些東西給讀者們。

[h1] 文字、音樂方面 [/h1]
文字部分我認為在玩過的作品中是屬一屬二的，
很多場景的描述非常的美，非常的震撼人心，(雖然不是官方漢化)
加上優美的音樂會讓人的情緒隨之舞動，
結束後想必會有好幾首bgm讓你念念不忘。

[h1] 圖像方面 [/h1]
以現在的視角來看，人物立繪會讓人很有過時感，
或許還會覺得有點醜，遊戲畫面也只有1280x960，
不過信我一句，你會漸漸習慣的。
而在場景方面我認為還是蠻好看的，
有些cg的背景配色和構圖都挺有藝術感。

[h1] 總結 [/h1]
喜歡思考，耐得住性子，並且有一定心理承受能力的人，
這部作品絕對值得玩玩看，
在劇情、敘事手法、文字、音樂方面皆是頂尖，
還有滿滿的哲學、文學思考。

而素晴日在網路上的別名是聖啟示錄，我認為是蠻有道理的，
其價值概念是將所有的思考方式都攤開給讀者們看，
遊戲中有較狂氣的虛無主義視角，
也有較溫暖的存在主義視角，
你很難說到底誰的思考方式才是正確的，
因為世上真的太多因善意導致的悲劇，
也有太多想逃離悲劇的人。
全部遊玩後就會了解到，它所期望的，只是大家能變得幸福。

最後，此處還是得警告一下，此作品是先抑後揚，
壓抑的部分有很多毒電波內容，務必要保持住心靈。

Эта игра была для меня целой вселенной — полной приключений, тайн и той невероятной связи, которую мы делили через экран, яркие воспоминания с детства. Когда отца не стало, он оставил после себя нечто *(волшебное)* : мод компаньона. Недавно, роясь в пыльных уголках бабушкиного дома, я наткнулся на тот самый ПК, с которого всё началось.зашел посмотреть семейный архив фото, игр и прочего, стирал ненужные папки и увидел в папке модс в ХЛ2— «sin». ?- какой син? подумал я. «Привет, сынок! Когда ты это прочтёшь, меня уже не будет рядом. Но знай: я горжусь тобой бесконечно. Надеюсь, ты вырастешь и станешь тем, о ком всегда мечтал — смелым, добрым, счастливым. Пусть жизнь подарит тебе океан радости и горы достижений! Я создал для тебя этого компаньона — он будет бродить с тобой по всем локациям Half-Life 2, иногда спотыкаясь и глупя, как я в свои лучшие дни. Но помни: в каждом его шаге, в каждом смешном диалоге — я здесь, с тобой, обнимаю тебя крепко-крепко. Люблю тебя, мой герой, до звёзд и обратно!»

В эту игру мы играли днями напролет проходя её снова и снова, никогда не надоедало. Возможно ему надоедало,, а мне пятилетнему - нет. Этот мод — не просто код, а вечный спутник, сотканный из отцовской любви, который теперь освещает мои игровые миры ярче любого Combine-оружия. Отец, ты рядом. Всегда

Half-Life was a groundbreaking game when it first came out, back in 1998. It was the best games to ever come out of Valve's office until 16. november 2004 when the world was blessed with Half-Life 2. It had a new artstyle that lean more into realism, rather than 90's sci-fi charm. While it wasn't the first game to use them source engine (that title goes to "Counter-Strike: Source" which came out October that same year) it is regarded as the most groundbreaking game using this engine. You can interact with almost everything. It even made up a new weapond for this new physics engine. The Zero Point Energy Field Manipulator also known as the Gravity Gun. It can shoot lazer bolts, move & throw objects that are to heavy for you to pick up on your own. It also gets a temporary upgrade that lets you pick up & throw around alive enemies which is super fun to use. Another thing I really enjoy about the game is it's amazing soundtrack! It really sells the atmosphere the mage is going for. The story is brilliant but I won't spoil it for you. This is (apart from "Team Fortress 2") my new favorite video game. If you haven't played it, you should totally give it a try for yourself. 
I give Half-Life 2 a 9.8/10!
The only thing I didn't like was the hunter chopper in Half-Life 2 and the Hunters in Episode 2.

Max Payne 3 — достойное завершение истории Макса Пейна, хотя и весьма неоднозначное. Это уже не тот нуарный триллер из первых двух частей, но мощный, брутальный экшен с фирменной «пейновской» атмосферой обречённости и саморазрушения. История повзрослевшего, измученного Макса, который пытается найти покой в Бразилии, держит в напряжении до финала. Диалоги острые, персонажи харизматичные, а моральные компромиссы заставляют задуматься. Визуально игра выглядит потрясающе даже спустя годы: детализированные локации, кинематографичные ракурсы, эффектные катсцены. Особенно впечатляет контраст между роскошными особняками и грязными трущобами Сан‑Паулу. Перестрелки — главная гордость игры. Механика «bullet time» работает безупречно: замедление времени превращает бой в хореографию пуль и взрывов. Враги умные, укрытия важны, а каждое столкновение требует тактики. Мрачная, атмосферная музыка идеально дополняет настроение игры. Особенно запоминаются треки в ключевых моментах сюжета. В итоге, игра это не реинкарнация классики, а её жёсткое, современное переосмысление. Если вы готовы к более реалистичному и динамичному экшену с глубоким сюжетом, игра подарит массу ярких эмоций. Для поклонников серии — обязательный опыт, пусть и не без компромиссов.

Моя оценка: 9/10.

Pico Park 2 es, sin dudas, un juegazo. Divertido, cooperativo, lleno de risas… al principio. Pero cuidado. Este juego no une, separa.

Empezamos siendo un grupo de amigos inseparables. “Qué divertido empujar al otro al vacío”, decíamos entre risas. Hoy ya ni nos hablamos. Uno se mudó de provincia, otro cambió de país, y yo tuve que cambiarme el nombre en Discord para que nunca más me encuentre nadie del grupo.

Este juego me enseñó que la verdadera dificultad no está en pasar los niveles, sino en no romper amistades en el intento. Gritos, traiciones, saltos mal coordinados, y ese clásico “¡QUIÉN TOCÓ EL BOTÓN, DIOS MÍO!” que todavía escucho en mis pesadillas.

Pico Park 2 es como una reunión familiar en Navidad, pero con más odio y menos comida.
Lo recomiendo si querés redefinir el significado de la palabra “cooperar” y probar cuánto amor fraternal puede resistir una persona antes de explotar.

I have 61 hours on Steam, but hundreds of hours on XBox before I came back to PC gaming.  I've read the negative feedback on both consoles and Steam, and while I don't necessarily disagree with most, I have a different feeling toward the game.

I enjoy playing.  It's not Black Flag part two, not in the slightest.  At first I hoped it would be, but I was taken in by what it is.  It's a game with ship combat from the age of sail, and that's the part I really enjoy.  The graphics are great.  I have them turned up to max, so your mileage may vary.  The sounds and sights of a ship exploding when you sink it just feels good.  

I'm a solo sailor in the game, and I don't partake in PVP, so I can't speak to that.  It's an MMO and a light RPG.  You have other players that you can group up with and take on elite ships or sea creatures, and now dragons.  Ships can be built, upgraded, and decked out with weapons, furniture that modifies the ship's defense or weapons, and armor for your ship.  

Armor and weapons can now be upgraded three levels, with modifications that add to their power.  It's in this way you can tailor your ship to your play-style, be it defensive or offensive.  This is the RPG part, unless you count the cosmetics for your ship or your player.  

There are numerous ships that have stats tailoring them toward certain weapon types and style.  One ship has bonuses for explosive weapons, while another is made to mitigate damage.  The ships come in three basic classes, just like any other RPG: tank, dps, and healing.  However, with the various armor and weapons, you can take your ship and outfit it to be a hybrid.  

You can have a Barque, a healing focused ship, and arm it with offensive weapons and armor, creating a good solo focused ship that dishes out damage and heals yourself steadily over time.  You can take a tank focused ship and arm it to either take on forts with weapons that do extra damage to the fort, or load on weapons to focus on taking down other ships.   Of course, you can make it a hybrid that can do both, while losing the effectiveness of a focused build.

In essence, what I'm trying to say is this game has more depth than just go kill other ships.  When the game first launched, it was pretty bare-boned.  After the first season, I put it down.  There really wasn't much there.  I came back a month ago, and been enjoying it since.  They've added more depth with the weapon and armor mods, added more ships, and increased the activities within the game.  Is it perfect, no, but they're adding and tweaking the game to make it better, and from what I've read, they're not done yet.

The game play loop is still build ship, go kill other ships/forts/settlements to upgrade ship, to build bigger/better ships, to kill more ships/forts/settlements to build another ship, etc.....  There are other items in game that add to that, like building a helm empire to acquire more pieces of eight, that allow you to build ships and buy resources and weapons.  Seasonal events with elite ships and sea creatures that allow you to acquire weapons, furniture, and resources that go toward making your ship(s) more powerful.

In other words, various ways to increase you ship's power.  Will this game take over your life like other RPGs do for some people?  I doubt it, and it certainly doesn't take over my life.  

I played World of Warcraft for years, and while comparing them is like comparing apples to oranges, the fact that they're both an RPG makes it easier.  If WoW's depth is  100 feet, then Skull and Bones is about 20 feet deep.  It's a light RPG, as I mentioned, with quests, basic class structure, and character builds (your ships are basically your character when sailing).  

It's not very deep or complicated, and I like that better to be honest.  I played World of Warcraft starting in 2005, and at the time, I enjoyed the complexity.  Now, twenty years later, I don't want the complication or need to have a party to see all the content.  Skull and Bones allows me to outfit my ship and take on any challenge solo, not easily in some instances, but it can be done.  

For the biggest challenges, the game allows players to queue for a party to take on the elite ship or fortress with other players.  That's perfect for me.  I don't like joining a party in World of Warcraft just for another player to kick me because my gear score is one point lower than what he/she thinks is needed for a quick run.  Skull and Bones doesn't have that issue, and I hope they never do.  

So, for me, the game gets a recommendation.  If you're older like me (late 50s) and just want to play something that isn't too complicated and allows you to jump on and play solo or with friends (yes, you can party up with other people if you like), then I recommend you at least give it a try.  Hope to see you out there fellow captains, and remember, always keep you hands on the wheel and your head on a swivel.

[h1]Cómo Cocinar Milanesas De Pollo[/h1]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Ingredientes:[/h2]
[list]
	[*]4 pechugas de pollo medianas (o 2 grandes cortadas al medio).
	[*]3 huevos.
	[*]3 dientes de ajo (opcional / para darle sabor).
	[*]2 cucharadas de perejil fresco picado (o 1 cucharada si es seco).
	[*]200g de pan rallado (aproximadamente).
	[*]100g de queso rallado (parmesano o el que haya, opcional).
	[*]1 taza de harina común (para el rebozado).
	[*]Sal y pimienta a gusto.
	[*]Aceite para fritar (si prefieres al horno, un chorro de aceite de oliva sirve).
[/list]
[h2]Tutorial:[/h2]
[olist]
	[*][b][u]Preparar el Pollo:[/u][/b] Si las pechugas son muy gruesas, córtalas al medio como librito y aplástalas un poco con un martillo de cocina o la base de un vaso. Así quedan más parejas y tiernas. Salpiméntalas de ambos lados. Reserva.
	[*][b][u]Hacer la Mezcla de Huevo:[/u][/b] En un tazón grande rompe los 3 huevos (siempre rómpelos primero en un pocillo para no arruinar la mezcla si uno está feo, no seas salvaje). Súmale el ajo picado bien chiquito (o rallado) y el perejil. Esto le da un aroma tremendo. Bate todo con tenedor o batidor de alambre hasta que quede bien integrado.
	[*][b][u]Preparar el Empanado:[/u][/b] En un plato hondo pon la harina. En otro plato amplio mezcla el pan rallado con el queso rallado (esto último es opcional pero queda increíble).
	[*][b][u]Rebozar las Milanesas:[/u][/b] Pasa cada filete de pollo primero por harina. Esto hace que el huevo se adhiera mejor. Después mételo en la mezcla de huevo, que quede bien bañado. Finalmente cúbrelo con pan rallado. Presiona con la palma de la mano para que el empanado se pegue bien y no se desarme al cocinar. [i]Tip: si quieres que queden más crocantes, puedes repetir el paso de huevo + pan rallado una segunda vez.[/i]
	[*][b][u]Cocinar las Milanesas:[/u] [/b][i]En caso de querer hacer las milanesas fritas (clásicas)[/i], calienta abundante aceite en una sartén amplia a fuego medio-alto. Cuando esté bien caliente, pon las milanesas de a una o dos (no todas juntas, para que no baje la temperatura del aceite). Cocínalas 2–3 minutos por lado hasta que estén doradas y crocantes. Retíralas y déjalas sobre papel absorbente para sacar el exceso de aceite.[i] En caso de querer hacer al horno[/i], acomoda las milanesas en una bandeja previamente aceitada. Luego, rocíalas por encima con un poquito de aceite en spray o pincel. Finalmente, lleva a horno fuerte (200°C) unos 20 minutos, dándolas vuelta a la mitad de la cocción.
	[*][b][u]Disfruta.[/u][/b]
[/olist]

Hot damn this just has a retro arcade visual style mixed with easy to pick up hard to master mechanics, its addictive, fast paced, and delightfully frantic. Even though you die in one hit (unless you take someone hostage), the quick respawn system keeps the experience from ever feeling frustrating. The story is surprisingly strong as well, exploring our relationship with violence a thought provoking and even forward thinking concept for its time. The visuals have also aged incredibly well. Despite being released back in 2012, the game’s pixel art style remains timeless, looking just as sharp and stylish today as it did over a decade ago. That said, the game isn’t perfect. Every moment that isn’t focused on the core, second to second gameplay tends to drag. The boss fights, for example, feel more like glorified puzzles than actual encounters. They lack the intensity and decision making of the main gameplay loop, and once you’ve figured out their patterns, they become little more than roadblocks. It’s a shame, considering how excellent the core mechanics are. Level design can also be hit or miss, especially toward the later stages. Some maps are overly large, leading to cheap deaths from enemies you couldn’t even see. Combine that with the repeated dialogue sequences you’re forced to rewatch every time you restart, and it can make the frequent deaths more tedious than they need to be. Still, despite its flaws, this game remains a truly unique experience that I wholeheartedly recommend. Its highs easily outweigh its lows, and there’s really nothing else quite like it. Even its sequel couldn’t capture the same lightning in a bottle that this one did.

I really want to recommend this collection, as I have so many fond memories of this series, I played EVERY SINGLE ONE as a child, (even the disastrous King's Quest 8.)  The collection keeps the King’s Quest games playable, but that’s about all it does. 

The launcher is barebones, the games run on an outdated version of DOSBox, and there’s no effort to modernize or celebrate the series. It feels like a quick repack from 2006 that never got the update it deserves. A legendary franchise presented in the most forgettable way possible.

Pros:
-Great Puzzles
-Great Retro Art
-Music and Aesthetic still intact

But that's the thing, the only pros to these games are because the original games were so solid, there's been very little effort to make them accessible on modern systems, or to add anything to improve the QoL for new players, or old players on newer hardware.

Cons:
-No proper UI or modern launcher
-Uses a very old DOSBox build
-Poor default display scaling and blurry visuals
-No achievements, extras, or quality-of-life features
-Minimal Windows 10/11 support
-Feels unpolished and outdated for a paid collection

Tales of the Old Dominus – Great Setting, Terrible Execution

I bought Tales of the Old Dominus right away because the medieval setting and the atmosphere of the city looked very promising. And yes — the world and idea behind it do have potential. You can feel that someone wanted to create a believable, gritty medieval experience.

Unfortunately, that’s where the positives mostly end.
The beginning of the game is awful. You are thrown straight into the action with no explanation at all. Suddenly, you’re searching for your sister Hanna, supposedly taken by bandits or brigants, and caught in some noble conflict — but the game never tells you what’s actually happening or why. There’s is a tutorial but no narrative buildup, nothing to connect you to the story or the world.

Then there’s the graphics, which are shockingly bad for the listed system requirements. Textures pop in during dialogue, characters’ faces have no emotion, and everything looks like it came straight from a 2010 title. Even with a strong system, the game stutters badly. Animations are stiff, and movement feels clunky.

The controls are another disaster.
Combat is completely unbalanced — hitboxes barely exist, you swing right through enemies even while locked on, and they somehow hit you almost every time. Blocking hardly works, and the whole system feels unfinished. Movement and object interaction are awkward and frustrating.

To be fair, I do like the survival and crafting elements. The inventory system is nicely designed, and there are some interesting base-building mechanics. You can craft items and create small structures, which feels like the only part made with real care. But sadly, that’s not enough to save the experience.

The game is filled with bugs. You get stuck in the environment, fall through the map, and the AI often acts in random or nonsensical ways. The main character is fixed — no customization for face or hair, no personal identity, nothing immersive.

Conclusion:
Tales of the Old Dominus has potential, but right now it’s simply not worth buying. Technically unstable, poorly optimized, with weak combat and shallow story design. It feels more like an early alpha or a free-to-play prototype than a finished game.

I’ll give it a bit more time to see if the story develops, but for now: no recommendation.

Higurashi When They Cry Hou+, developed by 07th Expansion and published by MangaGamer, is the definitive edition of one of the most influential visual novels ever made. It represents both a remaster and a culmination of the series’ original arcs, uniting the question and answer chapters into a single, polished experience. Set in the small rural village of Hinamizawa during the early 1980s, the game follows a group of friends whose peaceful lives are repeatedly shattered by paranoia, violence, and inexplicable tragedy. What begins as a story of friendship and lighthearted summer days soon unravels into a chilling psychological mystery that examines human nature, the consequences of fear, and the fragility of trust.

At its core, Higurashi When They Cry Hou+ is a slow-burning visual novel, with most of its gameplay consisting of reading dialogue, exploring character perspectives, and uncovering the deeper layers of its narrative. The story is divided into arcs, with each one retelling the same series of events from different points of view. The question arcs introduce the mysteries, presenting strange disappearances, murders, and mental breakdowns without providing clear answers. The answer arcs then revisit those events, reframing everything the player thought they understood and slowly piecing together the truth. It’s a narrative structure that requires patience but rewards those who stay with it. Every loop through Hinamizawa adds a new dimension, and every revelation recontextualizes the horror that came before.

The tone of the story shifts dramatically as it progresses. The early chapters are deceptively cheerful, filled with humor and camaraderie between the main cast—Keiichi, Rena, Mion, Satoko, and Rika. The warm depiction of small-town life feels almost like a slice-of-life comedy, and it’s easy to grow attached to the characters through their mundane school days and playful competitions. Yet it’s this very normalcy that makes the later descent into madness so effective. When paranoia creeps in, it does so gradually, until the once-innocent setting feels suffocating. Every laugh and smile begins to carry an edge of unease, every friendly gesture hides potential malice, and the player can’t tell if the terror unfolding is the result of a curse, mental illness, or human cruelty. The story’s power lies in this tension, constantly blurring the line between reality and delusion.

Visually, Higurashi When They Cry Hou+ remains faithful to its origins while updating its presentation for modern audiences. The remaster provides crisp character sprites, sharper backgrounds, and smoother transitions while preserving the distinctive art style that defines the series. Though simple, the visuals work hand in hand with the writing to create atmosphere. The stillness of Hinamizawa—the way the camera lingers on empty rooms or the sound of cicadas—evokes an uncanny sense of isolation. The sound design deserves special praise for its effectiveness; the ambient noise of insects and wind plays a constant role in establishing mood, while the soundtrack alternates between lighthearted tunes and haunting, dissonant melodies that trigger unease even before the text turns dark. The result is a game that doesn’t rely on graphic violence to unsettle the player—it builds fear through pacing, implication, and emotional dissonance.

What makes Higurashi stand out from other horror stories is its writing. Ryukishi07’s script is meticulous, weaving together horror, mystery, and human drama with an intensity that grows over time. Every character is flawed but sympathetic, their actions shaped by trauma, misunderstanding, or desperation. The game is not content to simply shock the player—it explores how fear and isolation can distort perception and drive ordinary people to horrific extremes. Themes of fate, memory, and redemption underpin the story, giving it philosophical weight beyond its initial mystery. By the time the final arcs reveal the truth behind the repeated tragedies, the story becomes as much about forgiveness and resilience as it is about terror.

That said, Higurashi When They Cry Hou+ demands commitment. The pacing is deliberately slow, especially in the early arcs, and readers unfamiliar with visual novels may find the format daunting. Much of the story unfolds through long conversations and detailed inner monologues, with few opportunities for player choice or interactivity. The length can also be intimidating, as completing all arcs can take well over a hundred hours. Yet this deliberate pacing serves a purpose—it allows the player to grow deeply familiar with the characters and setting, making the later horrors hit all the harder. Those who approach the game with patience rather than expecting constant action will find its structure both deliberate and rewarding.

As a remastered edition, Hou+ refines many elements that had previously been inconsistent across older versions. The translation is cleaner, the interface is smoother, and optional toggles let players switch between the new and original art styles. It’s the most accessible way to experience the full story in English, consolidating years of updates into one cohesive release. While its presentation may not match the visual polish of modern visual novels, its writing, sound, and atmosphere remain timeless. Few games, even decades later, have replicated its ability to shift from laughter to dread so naturally.

In the end, Higurashi When They Cry Hou+ remains a masterpiece of narrative design—a psychological horror that digs deep into the darkest parts of human emotion. Its blend of mystery, tragedy, and redemption ensures that each arc feels meaningful, and its portrayal of friendship under pressure gives the horror a deeply human core. For veterans of the series, Hou+ offers the definitive way to experience the story with improved presentation and completeness. For newcomers, it stands as a demanding but unforgettable journey that rewards perseverance with one of the most profound and disturbing stories in the visual novel medium. It is a work that lingers long after the final credits, a haunting reflection on the cruelty and kindness that coexist within every human heart.

This is a very cute side-game in the Dragon Quest series. It's like Baby's First Minecraft -- in the sense that it is a large open world with crafting elements and blocks that you can mine/place. But it is also an RPG with a concrete beginning/middle/ending, so it tosses up a lot of quests and guardrails to help focus the player along from one story beat to the next.

It's not a very difficult game, by my reckoning. But there's always something a little sunny, a little predictable, a little nostalgic about Dragon Quest games. Especially this one, because it's set in Alefgard; the same kingdom from the original Dragon Quest title -- but with an alternate-history twist where the Dragonlord has succeeded in conquering the realm and we play a scion of the Goddess charged with rebuilding civilization from the ground-up.

It's uplifting, funny, and a delight to have in my library.
It's a fun minecraft-like game with Dragon Quest assets. I think it stands out enough to not be a soulless clone. 5/5 would recommend.

Depois de investir mais de 130 horas infiltrando-me nas sombras de Detroit e Hengsha como Adam Jensen, chego ao final dessa jornada com uma conclusão clara: esta é uma daquelas experiências que marca qualquer jogador. A atmosfera cyberpunk consegue a proeza de ser ao mesmo tempo futurista e crível, te absorvendo completamente nesse mundo onde o ouro das augmentações brilha sobre a escuridão da desigualdade social.

A história é o verdadeiro motor do jogo. A trama de conspiração envolvendo as corporações, o transhumanismo e a ética por trás dessa evolução tecnológica é fascinante e surpreendentemente profunda. Você realmente fica envolvido na investigação, hackeando e-mails alheios (e me sentindo um péssimo ser humano por isso) e debatendo com personagens carismáticos e bem escritos. Os diálogos são um destaque, com escolhas que realmente importam e moldam o desfecho da história, que conta com vários finais diferentes.

A jogabilidade é onde as coisas ficam... interessantes. A promessa de "jogue do seu jeito" é real. Você pode ser um fantasma que ninguém vê, um Rambo cibernético ou um diplomata que resolve tudo na base do convencimento. A sensação de descobrir um duto de ventilação secreto ou hackear uma porta traseira enquanto todo um batalhão de guardas patrulha a frente é incrivelmente recompensadora. O sistema de upgrades (os "Praxis") é viciante e te faz pensar muito em qual build criar.

Porém, nem tudo são flores (ou circuitos dourados). A Inteligência Artificial é, vamos ser sinceros, meio burra às vezes. Tem hora que você elimina metade do esquadrão inimigo sem sair do mesmo esconderijo, e eles parecem mais preocupados em verificar o botão do alarme que não funciona do que com os colegas empilhados no chão. E prepare o psicológico para as famosas boss fights. Elas são poucas, mas destoam completamente da proposta do jogo, especialmente se você adotou uma abordagem não-letal. Felizmente, a Director's Cut amenizou um pouco esse problema.

O combate direto, por si só, é punitivo. O jogo claramente te incentiva ao stealth. Tentar bancar o herói à la Call of Duty geralmente termina com você virando presunto em dois segundos, já que a munição é escassa e os inimigos são tanques. É um jogo que exige paciência e estratégia.

A inclusão da DLC The Missing Link na campanha principal, na Director's Cut, é uma faca de dois gumes. A história da DLC é boa, mas ela te tira todos os seus upgrades e armas bem no clímax do jogo, quebrando brutalmente o ritmo da narrativa. É um baque e tanto.

Visualmente, o jogo ainda se sustenta muito bem graças a uma direção de arte fenomenal, com a icônica paleta de preto e dourado. Os cenários são detalhados e cheios de personalidade. Já os modelos dos personagens, principalmente os NPCs secundários, mostram a idade com texturas borradas e animações travadas. A trilha sonora do Michael McCann, no entanto, é atemporal e simplesmente perfeita, capturando perfeitamente a vibe sombria e futurista.

Verdade seja dita: Deus Ex: Human Revolution é daqueles jogos que você adora ter experienciado, mas que em alguns momentos específicos, você DETESTA estar jogando. É uma jornada incrível através de um mundo fascinante, com uma história que gruda em você, mesmo que a jogabilidade ocasionalmente te faça querer arrancar os cabelos. Se você curte cyberpunk, RPGs profundos e não se importa em ser mais um espectador furtivo do que um soldado de ação, essa é uma joia indispensável. Só vá preparado para achar o duto de ventilação mais escondido e ter paciência com a IA e com aquele chefe que insiste em aparecer do nada.

[h1]Classic, yet beautiful and charming game to be played with relaxation, packed with sentimental stories, fine arts and great sountracks.[/h1]

I started playing this when my steam account was still level 0, I can't believe it's already been a year since I've completed this game, I really feel bad to the dev for not writing a review of it in the past, that's just how great the game is in my eyes.

First of all, I really like the game's description, stating how the gameplay is, a fraction of the game's concept with some game infos yet addressing them with a casual and inspirational looks to it. It's what attracted me into playing this, fully knowing that this game doesn't include any achievements, card drops or whatsoever that I often care about when choosing games that I'm going to play.

I haven't played Ragnarok, nor I know what game it is, but this piece of fine art doesn't even make me feel like I'm missing something of the part, frankly saying that I love how the game runs, simple as good ol' nintendo games, how the main menu looks like and the background music of it. Tutorial and introductions are designed properly, that any player could be at ease in understanding gameplay concepts, objectives and ideas.

Battle system is simple, that the absence of complicated stuff makes the game a lot more relaxing and enjoyable to all kind of gamers, from the serious to the most casual ones. Some scenes are tear shedding, while the others are intriguing and enjoyable to watch. Game layouts are well-designed, dialogues are easy to understand, some are even inspiring, while the game's arts are fascinating, that I'd rather set them as my phone wallpaper than some cool-looking backgrounds that I have.

There are multiple endings, and the outcomes are tailored by how you picked the options. The endings are satisfying, that it really moved my heart to its content when I've finished the entire game. A quote from me for the developer, thanks letting me forget my miserable life and problems for the 9 hours of gameplay, I had fun with it.

As for the closure, (to the dev) your wish for Eternal Senia is granted, at least for this one fan.
[i]It's still in my game library, because such an awesome masterpiece should never be deleted from my hard drive, that's what my opinion is. And although it's free, know that this game worth a thousand for me.[/i]

我想尽力抛开情绪化来评价这个游戏，但是很多东西真的做得太差劲了。我很少给游戏评论，更别说差评了。我这个游玩时长也属于牢玩家了，这个游戏的优点很多，但缺点就听听我的体验和感受吧，希望对你有所帮助。

    对于只想着回忆以前网页打气球的单机玩家来说，这个游戏依旧是那样令人着迷。如果你只是喜欢塔防类游戏的休闲玩家，那我还是很推荐你购买的。气球塔防不同于植物和王国守卫，它放大了农这一概念并很好的融入了游戏之中，玩家可以通过对经济的合理分配使得经济翻倍增长。它可以在任意可能点放置猴子，导致如何在一个有限空间塞更多猴子成了一种技术。另外猴子的强度对于气球来说其实是超模的，你可以只用几万块出一只好用点的五级猴就能守到80多回合（一局游戏一般100回合），而6级猴（模范）强度更是爆炸的，一般一个模范足够你打过100。但是大部分普通玩家都不清楚模范究竟有哪些特点，这就要提到前面的农了，正常的局不农的话几乎出不了模范，且五级猴搭配好了也能轻松打过100回合，导致模范出得很少，自然也不太了解。毫无疑问，气球塔防的设计数值与防御塔的配合是我玩过塔防游戏中最复杂的。

     尽管气球塔防如今地图有82张之多，每张地图分难度（简单、中等、困难）和模式（天启、极难、仅限某类型猴、半金、点击等等）一张地图你需要来回打十多次才能拿完单人的章（没错，多人的章你还得联机打十多次）平均打一次得十分钟左右。恕我直言，这简直是消耗时间的不二之选，也是浪费时间的无底洞。于是乎大部分玩家完到后期都会厌倦这种来来回回的扫图。NK也是注意到了这一点，于是推出了三种联机玩法：CT(争议领地)、竞速、世界BOSS。这三个世界性的排位，对这个游戏带来稳定日活的同时也将它带入争名夺利的深渊。这三种玩法都有着明显缺陷，[b]我不推荐任何新手玩家玩排位模式[/b]。

  [h3]CT:[/h3] 这是战队玩法，每隔一周将随机匹配6个战队在一个“沙盘”上争夺地块。抢地块和占领地块都会有分数和给对应的CT点数，你的分数会随时间降低以便别人争夺，占领的地块也会随时间产出CT点数，战队以总CT点数进行排名。咋一听是不是很有意思，但我想对你说，这个模式是明显不公平的。地块中会有很多特殊的圣物地块，带上圣物可以在你占领地块时起到巨大的帮助，这个帮助大到某些成绩只能通过某种圣物辅助才能打出来。但是，圣物分配是随机的，也就是某些强悍的圣物可能直接刷新在别人家门口。类似于红蓝BUFF直接刷对面高地一样离谱。另一点是票券系统，战队每人每日只有四张个人票，也就是只能占四个位置。就算有战队票也只能占十个位置。前面提到圣物这么强大，你肯定优先选择圣物地块。很好的想法，但是圣物地块点数只有10,是点数最低的地块，连普通地块都有20。如果你热衷抢圣物，你毫无疑问是承受最大压力那个，但你会发现最后结算下来得个本地三四名，排得还不如摆烂拿普通地块的人高。你如果认真打CT，想要抢夺或者打个好分数，一天大概要2个小时以上。且还不能随便放弃，是不是很熟悉，这不就是上班吗？另外还有卡BUG获得逆天分数的我就不展开说了。

  [h3]竞速：[/h3]  我没怎么打过竞速，但也听过竞速大佬的说法：竞速前排全是挂。哈哈，NK在设计这款游戏之初就没做好防外挂系统，现在游戏防挂能力约等于零。连最低级的CE变速都挡不住，你惊叹的那些前排成绩，大概率是真的非人。另外竞速由于外挂猖獗，NK基于开挂的水平把竞速设计得越来越离谱。离谱到普通玩家忽略时间因素都不一定能完赛的情况。

  [h3]世界BOSS：[/h3]  这是我玩得最久的领域了。前面提到的6级猴模范在这个模式才是真的有用武之地。BOSS是一种特殊的飞艇，有着相当逆天的血量和各种机制，普通玩家一般打不过排位模式。这很正常，因为BOSS排位是真给高手玩的。我见过真正的顶级玩家、顶级思路，我也沾了些光拿了几个第一章。对于真正的顶级玩家而言，boss难度是次要的，要想有成绩你得祈祷那几个挂不要开太猛。那些几十个第一章的挂，大部分玩家不清楚，只感叹他们厉害，而在我们眼里开得非常明显，简称演都不演。前面说到，这个游戏防外挂约等于没有，NK分辨外挂只能靠明显的数据异常和玩家战绩来筛查。第一章可以说是开挂免死金牌，足够多的章甚至可以强行圆好明显有问题的成绩（因为NK不玩游戏，他们的成绩参考甚至有部分来自这些挂）。但是，按理说我们有这么多实锤证据，向NK举报都不封吗？这就要提到我给差评的原因之一了：[b]游戏制作组NK歧视大陆玩家[/b]。国区账号稍微有点问题都是被秒封的，想要申诉也是困难重重。国内玩家打非常好的成绩只能预先录屏才有申诉成功的可能。那些挂也有录屏，但开得不明显导致大部分玩家都看不出来。我们实锤他们开挂很大部分都是通过这些录屏看出来的。即使NK知晓他们开挂，由于是高贵的德国IP，于是乎高人一等让它们随便开。

  [b]炸房是我给差评的最根本原因了[/b]。排位有挂可以不管，自己随便打个成绩也挺有意思。但是垃圾的服务器让联机超过1个小时的房间极其不稳定，一炸便整局白打。多人排位成绩为什么这么少，最大的原因就是炸房。正常一局BOSS排位联机怎么也要两小时左右，这个时间你只能祈祷垃圾服务器不要抽风。那几个挂就是因为开着使自己完赛时间很短，可以极快的打出逆天成绩。所以能在BOSS结束前几小时内提交前三级别的成绩。

  [h3]内购：[/h3]这个游戏是有内购的，但卖的东西在任意的排位模式都是不能用的，只能推图爽玩。也就是说至少NK不像国内大厂那样可以充钱买数值，导致排行榜全是氪金号。但是最近一年NK只管推出他那DLC、付费皮肤、付费力量。对游戏服务器稳定完全放任不管，现在已经是十局五炸了。

  最后，多谢你有耐心看到这里。我玩这个游戏的热情已经被完全消磨干净了。周围的朋友退游的退游，沉默的沉默。我打这个差评不是为了给NK看的，而是对这个游戏彻底的死心。也许还会再玩这个游戏，但再如以前那样熬夜打boss到凌晨三四点最后还炸房的热情是不会再有了。

The short review: If you like stealth games, this is one of the best. 

The long review: I see a lot of comparisons to Hotline Miami in other reviews. Really, besides having a top down perspective and pixel graphics they share almost nothing in common. Intravenous 2 is a hardcore stealth game, direct combat often feels discouraged, and frankly you rob yourself of this game's many deeper mechanics by engaging in it. The better comparison is Splinter Cell and Metal Gear. 

Intravenous 2 has you balancing noise and visibility with a large arsenal of abilities and gadgets against some of the most intelligent and determined enemy A.I. I have ever seen. These guys work together, they notice details in the environment like opened doors and flipped light switches. Once they feel they have an intruder they will begin hunting you, systematically clearing and checking every space in the map, and they will never return to a calmed state. On higher difficulties, these guys are the absolute real deal, and it is that true challenge that will force you to use every trick up your sleeve and make you feel like an apex predator. The stealth will take a little time to get used to, as you learn what you can and can't get away with, and what you can use to your advantage. 

The campaign is a good length with tons of optional content to persue. With the DLC remaking the entire first game with all of the sequels improvements. After you've finished enjoying the main game you can start playing the many community made levels through the workshop. There is good value here, and hopefully more to come. 

My biggest con is the overall narrative, which still doesn't feel particularly strong, but is leagues better than the first title. Here we actually have an antagonist who gets properly set up, and two protagonists which feel capable of two unique playstyles. Its still not great, but I do enjoy the set dressing, and its fun to see your enemies fear you as you progress further through the campaign.

My dream would be to see a third entry in this series that expands even further, and hopefully includes CO-OP, picking up where splinter cell truly left off. However, what we have here is a brilliant stealth game that stands right alongside the other legends of the genre.

[h2]经典系列终补齐[/h2]
系列前作打通并写完测评后，这款续作自然就成了我的下一个游戏目标。首先要解决的问题则是「汉化」，前作的官方简繁体中文汉化包很容易就可以在游侠找到，但本作难得多。找来找去，我最后找了个B站UP主的个人汉化，跟官方汉化水平非常接近，连Pvt. Pfc.等这些军衔等都汉化了，基本没保留多少英文词。我一开始打的就是困难难度，大概8个多小时就打通了。之后为了尝试解锁全文档，去尝试了真实难度，结果发现和前作一样，每个关卡都必须一命通关，否则直接从头开始。圣马丁行动最终的防守阶段里，我不幸被打死，结果整章都得重打。地狱之角关卡里在过桥的时候被迫击炮炸死，导致打了半章的努力白费。最后还是和前作一样，我直接选择修改器，可以向大家推荐MrAntifun的四项修改器，比较容易找到，而且前作和本作都有。就这样，我拿到了全部勋章，解锁了全部文档，此后又尝试了普通难度和可扮演美军德军的无剧情纯任务模式。系列三部曲的精华终于全部体验完了（虽然Steam上版本的《地狱公路》还没重温），又拿下一个经典系列！

[h2]相比前作[/h2]
本作的推出时间和前作一样都在2005年，而且相隔仅7个月。由于使用的都是「虚幻2」引擎，游戏的画面几乎没什么变化。此外，玩法变化也很小，再加上更换主角且剧情有不少和前作是平行的。这一切使得本作看起来并不像一款标准的续作，更像是资料片。其实，要是都总结一下，本作的变化也不算太少。首先，武器方面增加了不少新的，比如注油枪M3A1，K98狙击步枪，德军伞兵武器FG42，有的还带狙击镜，简直是大杀器。如果仔细找的话，还可以使用M1911手枪，德军的P38手枪和巴祖卡火箭筒。再者，敌人数目增多，战斗难度也增加了，比如第二关的圣马丁行动，虽然对战的只是709步兵师，但难度就直逼前作中后期。游戏中期就开始碰到大量配备FG42的第6空降团，后期常要面对17党卫军装甲精锐师的STG44冲锋枪、MG42机枪、坦克和88毫米榴弹炮组成的密集火力网，还是最难打的巷战。主角初期有15发弹容的M1卡宾枪，之后还有汤普森、注油枪和勃朗宁用，后期勃朗宁和手指被打烂，步枪换成8发弹容的M1加兰德，难度进一步增加。大多数情况还得捡敌人武器用，特别是只要碰到坦克就强制让我们找铁拳轰，不太理解为啥不带巴祖卡，明明模型都做出来了，就在灌木地狱结尾的卡车上藏着。

系列最为主要的战术，在教程中用「4Fs」进行完整展示，即找到（Find）敌人，压制（Fix），包抄（Flank），以及消灭（Finish）。不过，手下小队在寻找掩体时的表现似乎还弱于前作，常会碰见队友站在掩体旁边和前面而被打死的情况。同时，敌人的AI被加强，被包抄时会转移了。幸而，关卡设计比前作更加开放，迂回道路增加，基本总能找到方法绕后。任务中增加了用TNT炸开通道的操作，需要摧毁不少88毫米炮阵地，对抗半履带车，固定地点释放信号弹。除了剧情关卡外，增加了13个没有故事的纯遭遇战模式，在里面甚至可以扮演德军。此外，还可以跟队友索要弹药，当然仅限于美军武器，相当于提前开了无限弹药秘籍。每次关卡结束时，如果没有士兵死亡，游戏会赞赏你的完美胜利。如果有士兵死亡，游戏则会弹出用鲜血换来了胜利，有人倒下了，是否愿意复活并继续。所给的两个选项分别为「复活并继续」，以及「重新开始章节」。估计没多少人会选后者，但这一设计重在提醒玩家留意身边的兄弟是否有倒下的，在乎每个士兵。

[h2]并行的战线：哈索科的战场回忆[/h2]
本作大部分的任务都发生在初代期间，战斗时间线仅往前推进了两天，到圣索沃尔（Saint-Sauveur）之战，再就是D+15天的纯访谈回忆。故事大致可以分为D日汇合贝克前后的经历，卡伦坦周边战斗和前往博普特送信会师，以及最终攻打圣索沃尔战役三大部分。故事以陆军历史学家S.L.A.马歇尔上校在诺曼底登陆15天后采访人称「瑞德/Red」的主角乔·哈索科为开端，让他回忆了过去日子的经历。瑞德在汇合贝克前经历了两个关卡，与其汇合后和前作重合的任务自然无法再来一遍，于是加入了前作间隙的三次巡逻行动、地狱之角和科隆比埃庄园巡逻，共三个关卡。

此后，时间线前移5天，直接到30高地那段。讲述了贝克晕倒和苏醒后寻找装甲师解围期间，哈索科带人打敌人左翼的历程。需要注意的是，这一段中有些细节和前作衔接不上。比如前作里贝克第二次醒来后，哈索科已经回来了，本作则是在贝克离开后才回来。此外，一些具体士兵的安排也不相同，但无伤大雅。前作结局那里，哈索科在卡伦坦（Carentan，或称卡朗唐）从下士晋升为中士，并遭遇敌人炮火，本作接续这一点，终于将时间线前推，用两个任务清除了残留在卡朗唐的敌人。然后，哈索科带人去与82师的人汇合，又用两个关卡一起攻打下了前往圣索沃尔之前的最后一站——博普特及其周边。

在卡朗唐被攻占后，82空降师要往西攻占港口城市瑟堡，从而拿下整个科唐坦半岛。要进攻瑟堡，中途便要打下圣索沃尔，也就是本作的终点战役。之前的博普特已经被拿下，等终于到达圣索沃尔后，游戏接连用三个任务展示了其攻打过程。第一部分是在城市外围，后两个是完全连在一起的，是进入城市后打巷战。其实哈索科的主要任务是送信，不用非得参战，但因为好友道尔和手下人的意愿，就留下来和82师一起攻城。游戏结尾是5天之后（6月21号）的瑟堡附近，现实中瑟堡战役从19号一直打到27号，所以采访应该发生在进攻瑟堡期间。幸存下来的贝克、哈索科、科瑞恩依次接受访谈，哈索科大概讲了一两个小时，但我们的流程可不止这么短。

[h2]血与泥中的战地手足：细腻的人物刻画（有剧透）[/h2]
前作把叙述的重点几乎全部放在F连3班，其中7个人先后牺牲，担任班长的贝克承受了巨大的压力与痛苦。本作虽也展示了不少3班的情况，比如贝克、科瑞恩、艾伦、加纳特、戴索拉（还有排长，人称麦克的哈西）均有出场，但叙述的重点放在了排里其他班的人以及82师的道尔身上。二班原本的班长比克斯中士空降时阵亡，哈索科担任领导责任，绝大部分时间都是带领着同一个排二班的帕多克下士（堪萨斯小子），士兵弗莱尔和马什，坎贝尔下士，二等兵佩奇和迈科诺一起作战。本作还新增了随时和队友说话的新功能，不过，这些人塑造的相对单薄，给人留下的印象并不深。一出场就如战神附体、来自堪萨斯、凭借地图猜测有88炮的帕多克，粗暴对待俘虏、想带大家安全回家的佩奇，以及为我们包扎手指的弗莱尔尚能留下一丝印象，迈科诺甚至只有一句要和佩奇一起行动。得益于前作对三班的塑造，我实际还是对三班的人更加关注，比如艾伦和加纳特的拌嘴，以及科瑞恩藏在泥坑，哈哈。

本作主角哈索科是个爱尔兰裔，因红色头发被大家称为瑞德。他脸上有道疤，来自于曾经酒吧里因碰别人老婆引起的斗殴，同时也是夜间警局的常客。他是班里唯一结过婚的（巧合的是左手无名指被打断），妻子埃尔玛尽力让他安顿了下来，并生了个女儿卡罗尔。他本来怀着热情加入空降部队，但见识到战争残酷和战友倒下后，最想的就是再见到家人。他见识到的首个死亡就是穆泽，他在飞机的最里面，胸口被打穿。空降后继续见识了不少空降兵的死亡，后来艾伦和加纳特也死了，但哈索科直到看到被炸得血肉模糊的戴索拉时，才开始真正害怕。他并不把希望寄托在贝克身上，认为只有自己能带自己回家。升为中士后，一直到圣索沃尔，哈索科手下都没牺牲过一个人，他以为自己能做到贝克做不到的事情。不过，这一点在圣索沃尔完全改变了……

除了主角自身，本作最为着重刻画的是道尔。他来自82师，在空降时救下我们。攻占教堂前请求我们找医疗用品救他82师的兄弟们，并在防守德军反攻的时候前来协助我们。他特别能讲话，嘴上总是说个不停，跟瑞德成了很好的朋友。两人在博普特再次相遇，此后还一起攻打圣索沃尔。他和哈索科一样都从下士升到了中士，还常跟101师的战友们说要请他们在英国喝威士忌。然而，在圣索沃尔，道尔被坦克一炮炸碎，没个全尸，仅有头盔和武器留下。同时，上面提过的佩奇在身中数枪的情况下，耗尽最后一丝力气把瑞德拖到了安全的地方，哈索科最终还是没能做到贝克没能做到的事。道尔死后，哈索科保留了他的头盔，还把回英国请别人喝威士忌挂在了自己嘴边。

本作虽然增加了伏击德军马车车队的桥段，但整体还是和电视剧《兄弟连》的重合度下降。毕竟打完卡朗唐后，E连就回英国休整了，没去圣索沃尔和瑟堡。然而，本作却和《兄弟连》第二集的一点非常像——赫尔。赫尔在空降的时候碰到温特斯中尉，由于找不到自己所在的A连，于是一直跟着E连的温特斯作战，直到在突袭庄园的105毫米榴弹炮阵地时被炸死。这跟道尔非常相似，同样是第一个碰到的士兵，同样找不到自己所在的连队。哈索科如同温特斯一样在降落时丢了腿袋，一开始没有武器，道尔也跟随哈索科作战。最终，道尔也如同电视剧里的赫尔，在作战时被炸死。不知道Gearbox在创作道尔这个任务的时候，有没有参考《兄弟连》里的赫尔。

[h2]另一面的麦特·贝克[/h2]
虽然本作的主角是哈索科，但是有个绕不开的角色就是前作主角贝克。从第三关开始，我们就跟随他作战，在卡伦坦更是并肩行动，哪怕到后期还是一直被提到。本作的文档中提到他父母在他4岁时离婚，他父亲是个上校，被派往各处，贝克和他的见面次数很少，大多只能过信件联系。他的好友乔治·里斯纳在空降训练的时候摔断了腿，因此去了坦克训练营。登陆前两周，三班原本的班长桑德森中士也摔断了腿，因此被麦克提拔为中士，作为三班班长。哈索科空降后，第一次见贝克的时候，看他脸上的表情，就像自己说的任何话都会让他崩溃一样，他从没见过这样的贝克。士兵们讨论贝克的时候，说他总是一个人两眼无神的待着，就算是在英国打棒球的时候也是如此，还总是让他们做徒劳的事情。这些内容跟我们在前作中对他忧郁的观感基本保持一致。

不过，贝克在本作中又呈现出不一样的感觉。他在30高地找来支援后，跳下坦克的第一件事就是问谁有火。肃清卡伦坦时，贝克竟然找到了一瓶酒，说要为哈索科的晋升干一杯，连科瑞恩都抱怨说贝克是否对这玩意上瘾。结局那里，更是说要写一本《贝克和瑞德：穿过地狱和高地》的书，还跟瑞德开起了自己先升中士的玩笑。这个贝克感觉总是和前作有很多不同，更开朗，也更颓废。哈索科似乎也对贝克的意见不小，说他似乎快要崩溃，总是热衷故意投身战斗，又总是在轰炸中全身而退。他认为在30高地拯救大家的并不是贝克，而是列盖特，这跟他在上一部结局那里执意带回列盖特的通讯装置合上了。哈索科还认为贝克无法让他安全回家，他还要做到贝克无法做到的事情，也就是保住手下士兵的性命。不过，到结局那里，两个人坐在一起，关系比之前嘴上说的好得多。两人一边开玩笑，一边说要请喝酒，依旧还是并肩作战的生死之交。

[h2]依然是专业与考据的典范[/h2]
本作延续了前作的制作经验，同样收集研究了大量二战期间留下的笔记、信件、报告、照片、地图、军事和历史资料。他们继续聘请退役的约翰·F·安塔尔上校作为军事和历史顾问，制作组还接受军事训练，参与野外训练演习。为了进一步确保准确性和真实性，他们前往法国诺曼底实地走访拍照，让游戏场景与现实保持一致，造就了有史以来最为考据的FPS游戏之一。在游戏中访谈主角哈索科的S.L.A. 马歇尔确有其人，是当时的战地记者和历史学家，本作的很多文件就来自于他的记录。游戏里出现的罗伯特·科尔中校，卡西迪中校，以及约翰逊上校也全都是历史上的真实人物。为了让玩家了解历史，游戏借用历史文件为大家讲解了当时的过程，还如前作一样详细介绍了很多武器、载具、军衔、服饰，只是不像前作一样有录音。

制作组在附录的文档中展示了游戏的大部分制作流程，比如剧本大纲和关卡流程的设计、名称和logo的概念设计、表演与录音、音效与混音、交响乐配乐等。特别是枪械这一对FPS最为关键的元素，游戏给出了详细的设计过程：收集资料与研究，建模，纹理，动画，音效，编程，测试。这一切复杂而耗时，但也使武器真实而逼真。场景的制作过程包括：建模，纹理，照明，阴影，碰撞体积，交互元素，测试等。从照片和游戏场景的对比中可以看出，制作组对诺曼底真实的地理和建筑进行了照片级别的还原，甚至连每天的天气都参考了当时的实际气象报告。附录文档中有制作组工作时的大量照片，还列出了整个制作组的成员照片、姓名、签名和工作内容。他们走访过西点军校，在西点战争模拟中心把本作用作学员的训练工具。游戏发售时举行过「兄弟连游行」，纪念空降师博物馆开馆，其中就有制作组和游戏带来的对历史地点关注的贡献。虽然本作延续了前作中战斗规模较小的问题，但已经在真实性和娱乐性之间找到了不错的平衡，还具备更高的挑战性。在本作中能看到敌人会把手雷扔回来，会反包抄我方，而且还有断肢系统，已经令我十分满足了。

Many of the systems feel like chores. They sound good on paper, but it doesn't map to a good experience.

For example:
Developer: boulder traps will keeps the players on their toes!
End experience: Players are forced to glue their eyes to the ceiling

Many of the systems are like this:
- Eating is a constant chore and distraction
- The quality system makes consumables which should stack, don't. You pick up 5 healing potions of the same type, but one is bubbly, one is swirly, etc, and it bogs your inventory.
- Inventory: You need to constantly pick up and drop items to level up your appraisal skill. And items don't stack, as mentioned before. So for every enemy you kill, you're shuffling tons of useless junk through your inventory. You'll be spending a lot of time doing this.

Other complaints:
- Exploration: The levels are predetermined so it gets old really fast.
- Loot: there's barely any interesting loot. There's like a couple unique pieces of gear which you're guaranteed to find, that's it. It also blows my mind that the starting gear is the same rarity as what drops in endgame. You start with a crystal weapon - those begin dropping on the last levels. So the progression is not interesting at all. You'll know what all the items are after a single run.
- The balancing is very strange. Early game is super punishing. It becomes easier each level you go on.

In summary, I personally think RPGs are fun because of 3 aspects:
- theorycrafting/evolving your build
- testing the bounds of your build on tough foes
- exploration

The game's systems should naturally encourage participation in these activities (the ones that are actually FUN). If the optimal way to play your game is some rote task, then that is a design failure from the developer.

A very well made CRPG in the age of very few CRPGS being released. It clearly samples from sci-fi pop-culture, including the glorious Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri, making it a good pick for anyone who's a fan of that genre. Set on a generational colony ship, you deal with less than ideal conditions - You weren't there for the launch, for the age when the ship ran properly, and you weren't there for the mutiny. You were born after society on the ship collapsed, and rely on a marginalised community that salvages what limited supplies were brought on the trip merely to survive on a daily basis.

The game features a multitude of factions that you can side with, sabotage, and make use of, each of which stems from past conflicts and successes. The factions tend to represent interpretations of stagnant and hypocritical versions of themselves, which is an interesting take on tropes that otherwise would have been common. Can someone be considered a revolutionary when they no longer revolt against anything? Can they be considered dedicated to a mission they've never contributed to? All of the ideologies are jaded, and matters of faith, even in the church-specific faction, tend to be cynical.

This all creates for an interesting narrative dynamic where your usual RPG actions serve a delicate balance between serving yourself, sabotaging the very limited ecosystem you rely upon (it is just a space ship after all, not an entire planet), and protecting that very same ecosystem and the goal it serves.

Mechanically, the game's skill system is similar to skyrim's in that you can only level up skills by tutor, or by using the skill itself. This becomes an issue due to how few opportunities there are to do this, because it means that, in order to reach higher levels with the skill, you have to use it every single opportunity you get. If you plan to use the steal skill even once in the later game, you *must* act as a horrific kleptomaniac for the entire game up until that point. 

This creates an ongoing issue where you really kind of need to pick your style of play through and limit your role-play opportunities, because it extends to combat skills as well. Every time you solve an issue with speech, you've lost out on combat stats and vice versa. There are ways to work around this, but it can become a brutal slippery slope, especially considering that at least one fight in the later game becomes mandatory if you have a team, since the only way to avoid it is to stealth passed it (not feasible for four characters).

That said, despite this issue detracting from the role-playing experience, the game still plays very well, and it can be mitigated by deciding on a character type before beginning a play through. If I had any other complaints/nitpicks, it would probably just be that despite Christianity being a central theme of the space station, there isn't really a single instance of faith, making it come across as a purely secular interpretation of the religion - lots of inappropriate out-of-context quotes of scripture, dogmatism, and confident ravings, but no faith - it's as if every character has tongue-in-cheek agreed to quietly not believe in the central religion of the station. It's odd, because the setting is a fantastic opportunity for it - a setting of absolute hardship with little to no material hope offered.

Overall, I'd still highly recommend this game if you're a fan of RPGs. It manages to be both fun and engaging, with a great deal to explore, and in my opinion, also manages to be a beautiful game overall.

The game consists in two types of teams: agents and hackers.
There are 5 nodes. As agents, you must secure 3 and as hackers, you must hack 3, in order to win.
Each round consists of a talking period, which is the main one, where you chat with other players in-game:
- as an agent, you try and convince other players to trust that you're an agent and try to weed out the hackers;
- as a hacker, you know who your other team-mates are, and try to trick agents into thinking that you're clean.
Each player, in turn, selects a certain amount of people to go on a mission at the end of each round.
As a hacker, you want to have hackers selected, so they can hack the node of that round (you can also bluff, so people think you're clean) and as an agent, you want to select only agents, so that there's no chance of nodes being hacked.
You must use your wits in order to weed out the hackers, as an agent, or fool the agents into thinking you or the other hackers are clean, so that you can hack the nodes.
It's very fun and I recommend it.

[h1]КОНКУРЕНТ, А НЕ АНАЛОГ[/h1]

[b]Предисловие (немного душное)[/b]

Начнем с того, что с Phasmaphobi'ей я знаком уже 5 лет, наиграв те 40 часов не в один присест, а растягивая "удовольствие" на протяжении всего времени. И сразу скажу, что в GE я наиграю не больше, ведь у таких игр есть срок годности - к ним очень быстро привыкаешь из-за репититивного геймплея превращающего давящий на мозги хоррор в рутинный спидран. Конечно, эти игры напугают и еще не раз даже "постоянника", однако кол-во таких разов со временем будет уменьшаться. Так бывает со всеми играми и это нормально (зачем я вообще это разжевываю?), но у GE есть объективный плюс который сможет удержать в игре неискушенного (не знакомого или же мало наигравшего в Phasmaphobia) игрока - а именно скримеры и более полный геймплей. GE, при всех ее схожестях, является конкурентом и отдельной игрой, а не пустой копиркой, так еще и предлагает куда больше плюшек, нежели Фазма. 5 лет назад мы с друзьями выдумывали разные обновления Фазмы, представляли демонов-боссов, ритуалы и экзорцизм... добавили ли это в Фазму? Нет. А вот в GE - да. 

[h1]ТАК В ЧЕМ ЖЕ ПРИКОЛ?[/h1]

[b]В обосранных штанишках.[/b]

Phasmaphobia предлагает лишь напряженную атмосферу, не столько хоррора, сколько мистик триллера. Конечно, первые десять-двадцать каток будет очень не комфортно, я лично иногда даже визжал. Вот только кроме выявления типа призраков и нагнетающей атмосферы игре больше нечего предложить. Все, что нужно сделать - это узнать тип призрака благодаря паре методов, а дальше игра заканчивается. За все 5 лет не поменялось ничего (и на мой взгляд новый хаб выглядит ущербно, по сравнению с первым, который имел кучу приколов в виде призрака на потолке), а вот GE за довольно не большой срок развития может предложить в несколько раз больше. Все-все, не ходим вокруг да около и перейдем к плюсам:

1) [b]1 Катка = 1 полноценная история[/b] - Все карты сделаны с душой и любовью, каждая мапа может рассказать историю живущих до событий игры людей, каждая из комнат буквально кричит различными деталями бэкграунда, а иногда здесь или там можно увидеть силуэты умерших, и ко всему этому на определении типа призрака игра не заканчивается. Вам нужно провести ритуал, и поверьте, когда начнутся постоянные фазы охоты - это будет не просто
2) [b]Напряжение и саспенс[/b] - Здесь также выигрывает GE, тупо потому что она может предложить больше, чем шорохи и давящий эмбиент. В игре есть скримеры (они однотипны и спустя 2-3 катки можно изучить каждый из них, вот только появляются они рандомно и их нельзя предугадать), а также сам призрак может полноценно взаимодействовать с окружением
3) [b]Насыщенность геймплея[/b] - Здесь есть ВСЕ, что есть у Фазмы и даже больше. Больше разных приборов, перки, улучшения, возможность использовать робота помощника, что переносит полезный стафф, а также дополнительные "утяжелители" позволяющие расширить возможности не только игроков, но и призрака, а также добавить те геймплейные фишки, о которых мы мечтали в Фазме
4) [b]Карты[/b] - Я описал почти все в первом пункте, однако в любом случае стоит отдать должное - поиграть есть где и сами карты выполнены на отличнейшем уровне. 
5) [b]Отзывчивость игры и распознавание голоса[/b] - Тут я вряд ли могу сравнить, потому что голос в Фазме я тестил только в бородатые времена, когда приходилось ковыряться в настройках языка Windows, а также даже с русской идентификацией призрак продолжал воспринимать только английскую речь. Здесь же такого нет, зашел в игру - зашел в настройки - все настроил - игра понимает АБСОЛЮТНО ВСЕ и отзывается на любые (пусть и заготовленные внутри) вопросы и предложения.
***
И в принципе там есть еще какие-то плюсы и детали. Возможно, я их не открыл, возможно я просто забыл их упомянуть здесь. Я советую вам лично купить ее и протестить/сравнить с Фазмой.

[h1]ЭТО ВСЕ? ИГРА 100%-ЫЙ WIN???[/h1]

[b]И да, и нет[/b]

Играя катку за каткой ты начинаешь замечать, что большое количество деталей и плюшек как будто не "уживаются" вместе. Столько разных приколов, столько разных деталей, но не ощущается целостности, за то прекрасно ощущается бардак. Большинство вещей объективно бесполезны и вообще ничего не решают (тоже самое есть в Фазме, на самом деле), а некоторые утяжелители привносят не интересные взаимодействия с геймплеем, а еще больше рутины, от которой начинает тошнить. Пусть Фазма и ощущается меньше и слабее чем GE, она также ощущается более укомплектованной и собранной. И по итогу обе игры даруют как одинаковый, так и полностью разный опыт. Это нужно прочувствовать. Любителям мистик триллера, желающим сжимать свои булки без угрозы словить инфаркт от скримеров и не душиться от доп ритуалов (они будут такой же рутиной чисто замедляющей геймплей) - добро пожаловать в Фазму. Если же вы любитель хорроров и приветствуете скримеры, а также ждали (как и я) чего-то большего от Фазмы - добро пожаловать сюда. Вы точно не пожалеете. 

[b]Спасибо за внимание.[/b]

I really enjoyed this game while it lasted. Exhibit A: I put 56 hours of played time into it, because it was fun, until you basically ran out of things to do.  For the $30 or so that I paid, I got a decent amount of play time.  I've paid way more for AAA games that I finished playing in way less time, so the value isn't bad.  And New Cycle isn't even that buggy for an EA game.

If you're okay with putting down $30 for a few dozen fun hours of a well thought-out game, have at it.  But if you're expecting the rest of the roadmap to be completed sometime this century... don't hold your breath - you might suffocate.

The last substantive update (aka something that changed the playable code) was in July of 2024.  Everything since then has just been puff pieces and pretty posters of "things that are being worked on." And even the last of those was about 9 months ago.

And for those people who say "negative reviewers are morons, everything is fine"... I refer you to Kerbal Space Program 2, which went through this exact cycle (no pun intended).  The developer stopped updating the game.  Then marketing took over and tried to hide that.  They even posted a "thanks for hanging out, look at everything we accomplished so far!" right before the game got abandoned.  Then the publisher fired the entire studio and refused to ever confirm or deny that it had been abandoned - they just quietly walked away even as the community cried about it.

I enjoyed the game while it lasted, I really did.  I'm honestly more mad at people who are still defending the nothing that's happened for the last 16 months and thinking this is normal.  Look at any normal job - if you keep telling your boss that you're working for 16 months, eventually he's going to find out that you haven't actually done anything for 16 months.

It's up to you - if you close your eyes and pretend you're buying a finished game, it's not a bad value.  But you can't ever really "win" because that part never got written in.  I can't recommend a game that'll never finish its roadmap.

/shrug

So I haven't gotten very far yet I think (always hard to tell before finishing a souls-like) but I absolutely adore this game. I found my way here from some recommendations after reading Blame! and looking for games that captured the same feeling of being lost in a vast, desolate and maddening world and I found that here.
The game plays like DS1 and for me that's a nice change of pace as the Dark Souls series and especially Elden Ring leaned into faster combat and gameplay. There's a surprising amount of gear and playstyles, the limited number of Perks and Abilities is offset by some very strong upgrades to those Perks later on and progress feels steady.
The world building and setting is what I came here for however and it is stunning. From broken castle ruins and abandoned monasteries to jumbled and mashed together industrial areas and modern day apartment complexes. Feels surreal to navigate as a knight or spellcaster but it adds to the feeling of being out of your depth and navigating a world breaking at the seams in the best ways.
So far I haven't experienced bugs, jank or crashes which is astonishing for an indie game of this scale.
I recommend supporting a dedicated team with interesting ideas like this and can't wait to walk the dark and strange areas of this world again, tech-torch held high in the face of the monsters and horrors!

I have just finished my first run and I was driven here to post a review. That doesn't happen often but this game... it's absolutely amazing. From the music, to the ambient noise, to the intense tech, the sound design on the game is brilliant. It captured me from frame one and has had me glue to the screen for hours. It built the setting in a way that's comparable to the setting of Bloodborne. Everything just felt right in place. 

The combat feels responsive and quick. There are definitely flaws. Hits not registering, over-tuned enemies, and some boss fights that were more frustrating than complex. But overall I really enjoyed the combat. While I've heard some mixed reviews of what's "viable" in terms of build, there seems to be a lot of options and that's good. 

The story is a bit, out there... but it's clear they were inspired by great works like Berserk, Dark Souls, and Evagelion. I didn't really follow all that was going on but once some pieces fell into place, thanks to some great community posts, I was able to figure things out quickly.

This game has a little bit of everything that I love in a game. A setting that keeps me glue to my seat and looking forward to every opportunity I get to play. Combat that was rewarding once I got the hang of it. And some fantastic set pieces and story to tie it all together. I absolutely think any fan of Dark Souls/Bloodborne would have a fantastic time.
