Grim Dawn is often spoken of as though it were merely a distant echo of Diablo, born in its shadow and destined never to escape it. Yet this is a misconception. Yes, its lineage is impossible to deny — the isometric perspective, the relentless combat, the endless hunt for loot, the dank caverns and infernal beasts — all these remind one of Blizzard’s legacy. But here the similarity ends. Grim Dawn is not a tale of a world fighting against damnation. It is a tale set long after damnation has already won. Humanity is not resisting the end — it is sifting through its ashes. What remains of the world is cracked, rusted, quiet. Here, magic is no divine gift, but a disease that clings to the flesh of the dying. The gods are silent. Salvation is no longer on offer. And it is this silence that gives the game its unmistakable presence.

The world of Grim Dawn does not tell its story with pompous cutscenes or heroic proclamations. It whispers it through scorched journals found in abandoned farms, through the final scribbles of dying soldiers, through broken machinery and crumbling village walls. The narrative is not handed down like scripture, but unearthed like bones. And upon these bones grows one of the most intricate role-playing systems the genre has seen. The dual-class mechanic, at first glance familiar, reveals itself to be a marvel of creative freedom: arcanist-soldiers, occultist-shamans, necromancer-demolitionists — combinations that should not make sense, and yet they do. Add to this the Devotion system — constellations of ancient powers drawn across a darkened sky, each gifting subtle strength — and building a character becomes less like ticking boxes, and more like practising alchemy: deliberate, risky, and strangely beautiful.

Combat in Grim Dawn does not dazzle the eye — it weighs upon the hand. Every swing, every explosion feels tangible, as though steel genuinely meets bone, and fire truly burns through oil and cloth. The music does not soar to angelic heights, as in Diablo II; rather, it seeps into the world like mist over moorland — quiet, mournful, ever-present. It belongs not to heroes, but to survivors. It is not a hymn of hope, but the low hum of a forge still burning in a ruined town because to stop would mean admitting defeat. And in this weariness lies a peculiar comfort.

One cannot, in fairness, compare Grim Dawn to Diablo IV in terms of production spectacle. Crate Entertainment does not possess Blizzard’s coffers, nor its orchestras, actors, or cinematic bombast. But what they do possess is rarer: craftsmanship, resolve, and a kind of honest reverence for the genre. Grim Dawn does not flatter the player, nor beg for applause — it simply exists, solid and unpretentious, like an old stone bridge built to endure storms rather than impress passers-by. It expects you to learn, to fail, to rise, and try again — and in return, it offers a world that respects your time and intelligence.

Thus, Grim Dawn is not a “Diablo clone,” but rather a parallel branch of ARPG evolution. If Diablo is myth — glorious, biblical — then Grim Dawn is chronicle. If Diablo sings of saving the world, Grim Dawn quietly asks what one does when the world is already lost. And in that simple, solemn question lies its strength. It stands, firmly and humbly, somewhere between Diablo II and Diablo III — not to surpass them, but to walk its own road, through fog, mud and broken steel.

This is a great game; it scratches the itch for a space, RPG, loot game and does it surprisingly well. You start off pretty basic, picking a specialization (has minor impact) and working through some missions along side a story quest. Start grinding credits to upgrade that ship, or maybe get a new ship..maybe you want to start mining instead! Once you get the hang of the missions, reputation, inventory you reach the end...of the prologue! The game opens up vastly, more ships, more equipment, more systems ect. 

Great job with the progression! You feel stronger as you gain skills, level up and get new ships and crew. A big function is the ability to use your Echo or AI. This nifty companion can run missions for you, mine, do all sorts of things that are customizable to an extent. It's nice to let the AI take control for a bit while you get a beer refill or do some work. 

Some things that could use improvement: 
1. Sound (there are a lot of lacking sound effects, like mining lasers, thrusters, ect.) there are alot of sound elements that need some love.
2. Fuel costs - No fuel costs in the game, and I think having to refuel your ship from time to time would add a more realistic element to it.
3. Some RPG elements with different ships or captains. Missions like working together or even recruiting other ships would be fun.

Overall this is a gem! I love where it is now and very hopeful for future content and improvements. It's one of those games where you start playing and it's suddenly 2am in the morning with work in 3 hours.

Borderlands 1 was an incredible game when it first came out. It offered a delightful change from the monotonous and repetitive games of its time. The addition of cartoony graphics to the realistic Mad Max-esque atmosphere created a truly captivating atmosphere. Andalso the lore details they presented throughout the game created a unique atmosphere.

With each new game, new mechanics and features were introduced to the Borderlands series. Because Borderlands 1 lacked none of these, we play it in its rawest form. If you're a new Borderlands player, you might not notice these. But when you look back at the first game after all these years, you feel like certain things were missing, leaving you feeling a sense of emptiness. For example, not being able to use a fill ammo key at vending machines or being unable to move freely for a second wind.

I think it has some positive aspects compared to later games (especially Borderlands 4). First of all, I think the game's art style is quite noticeable. I think this style has been toned down and dumbed down considerably over the years. Perhaps it's because the development team has changed a lot, breaking away from its original style, or perhaps it's because of the advancements in graphic technologies. But the most important aspect of the game style is its atmosphere. The bold lines around objects and the deep blue sky immerse you in an interesting environment.

I loved the map designs. You can almost imagine yourself traversing "living" areas. There are no civilians around, only enemies. However, these maps are included with details that reflect the possible civilians' lives and work. Garbage dumps, massive tractors, and visible factories make the game feel like you're navigating a real world.

Of course, there are some issues stemming from the inexperience of the first game. First among these are the enemy types and the unbalanced nature of the elements. When you enter an area where there seem to be no enemies at first, suddenly enemies start spawning from all sides. You're caught in the middle of a sea of ​​enemies unprepared. You lose the opportunity to approach from afar or use tactical approaches, and you find yourself trying to escape the enemies that suddenly gather around you.

Skag, Spiderant, and Scythid all have fundamentally similar attack methods. They run at you when they see you, and they leap at you from a certain distance. This makes things even more challenging. Imagine 10 Spiderants jumping at you from different directions at once. Considering that enemies like Rakk, Psycho, Crabworm, and Guardian can also get right up to you and attack, the game becomes more of a "constantly dodging back" game than a "serious gunfight."

One reason for this may be that the game is designed for co-op with friends rather than solo play. Kiting enemies with multiple players can make the game much easier. But of course, since you can't do this solo, it makes progressing alone much more difficult. On the other hand, I think the bosses in the game die too easily. I don't even have as much trouble against the important bosses as I do with the  radom mobs I encounter. This makes me think the game's balance hasn't been adjusted properly.

The game itself was released in 2009, and the "Game of the Year Edition" in 2010. In 2019, they released a remastered version called "Borderlands Game of the Year Enhanced." They adapted Borderlands' graphics to the 4K era and introduced the minimap and character customization from Borderlands 2. However, they didn't seem to make any other improvements. You'll encounter a lot of bugs in the game, and I'd expect them to be fixed. Some are obvious, like getting stuck on the edge of objects. The mouse sensitivity settings in the game are also very poor, requiring you to modify the game files. While this would be somewhat understandable if the game were released in 2009, we're talking about a "modernized" update in 2019.

I wrote a negative review, erased it and decided to give it another chance, and now I've got to go back and stick with my original opinion. I just can't with these mechanics. I'm leaving this as much to tell myself not to play this and do this to myself again, as I am to inform others. 

So future me... don't do it! Whatever you hope to find by installing this and opening it up again, it's JUST NOT WORTH IT.

Anyway, to break down the issues:

Stores don't sell things in Soulash 2. What you do is bring raw material to a store and then you pay a price and they make it for you. Which is actually realistic for a frontier medieval town but doesn't work well in a game like this. Because in practice of course, it's a lot easier to kill a villager and take his pants than it is to find 5 snakes and take their skins and pay a dude to make pants. 

It's kind of like that with a lot of things. There's all these carefully laid out mechanics that you're better off ignoring or playing around. So there's a way to build a settlement and invest a bunch of time into it, but why would I do that? It takes a while and when you're done, assuming you've done it properly, you can earn income. But since the stores don't sell anything, what do you spend that income on? All I do is hire companions and sometimes make trading runs between villages, but I get more than enough money to do that from the little random quests I do. I don't need to build a safe place to rest like in Minecraft. What do I need to build a settlement for other than just to do it?

Abilities are capped at a very low level, and to increase potential, you have to find a guy to train you and pay him. Well, this being randomly generated, there might be like 2 people in the entire world who have the skill you want to train and you have to track them down, which is just as exciting as it sounds. This makes spell abilities kind of a noob trap, since if there are people who can train you in those skills, it's not been apparent to me in the 2 worlds I've played. It's like spells are sort of tacked on as an afterthought. There's very little magic in the game overall, which is alright if that's what you're going for. But if that's the case then why have these spellcasting abilities at all?

There's icons for different creatures and they don't look bad, but they're hard to tell apart. So this last run, I was being attacked by bobcats a lot. One of them was right in the middle of a store in town, which was kind of annoying. Anyway, later on I'm walking along in the forest, and hear the combat music break out and I look behind me and there was a bobcat, so I shot him. Actually it wasn't a bobcat. It was a dude with a cat head and now I'm wanted in the town or would be if the dude hadn't killed me.

That brings me to another thing. There's no unpredictability that you can generate. What I mean is, in a normal roguelike you might be confronted with a monster who will obviously kill you, or maybe your health is 4/70 and it's about over. What you do is sort through your inventory and try and find some clever use of an item, or you try and use the terrain, or you use a spell you hardly ever use to try and get away with your life. Those encounters bring a lot of the life into a roguelike run. But here, there's nothing like that. It's like... I see such and such enemy... the maps are gigantic and wide open, so I can't run if the enemy is faster than me. I have no way to temporarily boost my ability or utilize some aspect of a deep magical system to try and get away. I can't whip out some funky item and try it out. It's just over.

No, I'm done with it. I know it's EA but these aren't EA type issues. The mechanics just are never going to work for me.

The story itself is also surprisingly good- in the main story mode of the game it’s nothing to write home about, but is fun and doesn’t take itself seriously, with the dlc (which are both free in the HD Renovation) expanding upon the story more. The twist in Dollhouse especially is probably one of the saddest twists I’ve actually seen in a horror game. So, for all intents and purposes, this game is phenomenal and much more than just a silly walking simulator- I highly recommend anyone play through it.

Freddi Fish 2: The Case of the Haunted Schoolhouse, developed and published by Humongous Entertainment and later re-released by Nightdive Studios, remains one of the most beloved examples of 1990s children’s adventure games. Originally released in 1996, it builds upon the foundation laid by the first Freddi Fish title, offering a more polished, narratively engaging, and humor-filled underwater mystery. The game stars Freddi, the intelligent and compassionate yellow fish, and her excitable best friend Luther as they set out to solve the case of the mysterious “ghost” haunting their school. When the ghost steals the students’ toys—including Luther’s prized Codfish Commando action figure—the two young detectives take it upon themselves to uncover the truth and bring the culprit to light. What unfolds is an endearing blend of mystery, comedy, and light puzzle-solving that captures the essence of Humongous Entertainment’s creative philosophy: games designed for children that never talk down to them.

From the very beginning, the game sets a charming tone that balances humor with a touch of intrigue. The underwater schoolhouse is lively and filled with personality, setting the stage for an adventure that feels both cozy and mysterious. The story unfolds at a gentle pace as Freddi and Luther explore colorful aquatic environments, speak with quirky sea creatures, and gather clues about the so-called ghost that’s been terrorizing their classmates. While the word “haunted” might sound ominous, the game’s atmosphere remains lighthearted and playful, ensuring that younger players experience excitement without fear. Freddi’s calm intelligence and Luther’s enthusiastic curiosity make for a delightful dynamic—Freddi often acts as the voice of reason, while Luther’s impulsive actions bring humor and warmth. This relationship anchors the narrative, giving the game a sense of friendship and teamwork that is both relatable and reassuring.

Gameplay in Freddi Fish 2 follows the traditional point-and-click adventure format, but it is carefully designed for accessibility. The interface is intuitive and encourages exploration: players move through various scenes by clicking on exits, interact with objects and characters, and collect items that can later be used to solve puzzles. The puzzles themselves are straightforward but cleverly integrated into the world’s logic, requiring observation and reasoning rather than abstract guessing. One of the standout features of the game is its replayability. Each time the player starts a new game, the necessary items and pathways to solve the mystery are randomized, which means no two playthroughs are exactly the same. This simple but effective mechanic encourages curiosity and replay, something rare in children’s adventure titles of the time. It also subtly teaches problem-solving adaptability, since players must adjust their thinking to the slightly different conditions presented in each playthrough.

The visuals remain one of Freddi Fish 2’s greatest strengths. Humongous Entertainment’s signature hand-drawn animation gives the underwater world a rich, storybook quality. The bright, saturated colors, smooth character animations, and expressive designs make every frame feel alive. The world teems with tiny, interactive elements—plants that dance when clicked, shells that reveal surprises, and small sea creatures that perform amusing animations. These moments of interactivity, while not always related to the main plot, enhance immersion and reward players for exploring every corner. Even decades later, the art direction holds up remarkably well, especially in the remastered version handled by Nightdive Studios, which smooths out edges and improves compatibility for modern systems while maintaining the original’s nostalgic charm.

Sound design and voice acting add even more life to the experience. Each character has a distinct and memorable voice, performed with enthusiasm that perfectly suits the game’s tone. The dialogue is simple enough for children to understand but peppered with enough humor and personality to entertain adults as well. The background music is upbeat and melodic, with a gentle aquatic flair that reinforces the setting without becoming repetitive. Sound effects are crisp and plentiful, with nearly every object producing a unique response when clicked. These playful touches—combined with the lively soundtrack—create a world that feels cheerful and organic, keeping players engaged even during slower-paced moments.

Thematically, the game encourages positive values through its storytelling. Freddi and Luther demonstrate teamwork, courage, and problem-solving in a way that feels natural rather than forced. The mystery itself turns out to have an innocent explanation, teaching young players that fear often arises from misunderstanding rather than malice. This moral is subtle but effective, woven naturally into the narrative’s resolution. The ending reinforces the idea that intelligence, kindness, and curiosity can overcome fear and deception—a timeless message that has helped the Freddi Fish series maintain its educational and emotional resonance across generations.

As with most titles in the Humongous Entertainment catalog, Freddi Fish 2’s biggest limitation is its brevity. A single playthrough typically lasts under an hour, and experienced players may complete it even faster. However, the randomized elements and charming details make it a game worth revisiting. While it lacks the complex puzzles and intricate storytelling of traditional adventure games, its simplicity is part of its strength. It provides a welcoming introduction to the genre for children and a comforting, nostalgia-filled experience for adults who grew up with it. The remastered Steam version preserves everything that made the original special while ensuring smooth performance on modern systems, making it easy for new players to experience a piece of adventure gaming history.

Freddi Fish 2: The Case of the Haunted Schoolhouse stands as a wonderful example of how a game can be educational, entertaining, and emotionally satisfying all at once. Its vibrant world, lovable characters, and smart design make it just as enjoyable today as it was in the 1990s. Beneath its simple puzzles and child-friendly presentation lies a masterclass in intuitive design and storytelling. Whether played by new audiences or returning fans seeking a wave of nostalgia, Freddi Fish 2 remains a shining gem in the ocean of classic adventure games—a lighthearted, imaginative mystery that continues to delight across generations.

Решаем ситуацию в пользу одного, получаем другие новые истории, а также ещё новые возможности повлиять, постепенно эти самые руты усложняя. В ходе чтива даже получается потихоньку проникнуться каждым из героев, и в конце искренне стараешься найти найти лучшую концовку для каждого. 

Проходится всё на одном дыхании, а в конце остаётся желание ещё во что-нибудь подобное сыграть.
[spoiler]WILL: A Wonderful World[/spoiler]

Lovely game, super wholesome cast. I found it easy to get invested in exploring every ending. Art style is very cute too. It's very fun to try out different combinations and experience how every person is a participant in their own tragedy, no matter how virtuous or vitriolic they were. I can highly recommend this type of game to anyone who loves timeline-divergence really, but I'd especially recommend this game to over-thinkers and 'could I have done something differently?' people. 

The game does a great job of hammering in that your choices are more meaningful than the outcome. [spoiler]Trying to be a good person doesn't lead to a happy ending. Trying to be bad person doesn't lead to a happy ending. Between those, though, you can be the person that you want to be, regardless of whether or not it's good or bad to anyone else. I think it's fascinating that no matter what, you'll always end in a tragedy; but the true ending where everyone acts as fully their own beliefs leads to a bittersweet reunion. I would have loved to hear that last conversation between everyone in the burning room. What did they think about themselves? Do they regret their own choices? and, if so, did they wish to be more self-fulfilling or more team-oriented? Even when it can look like from any one perspective, 'I had nothing to do with this. They're burning me because of their own issues,' it's all interwoven. Even when we try to be our best selves, we all participate in the cause of our misery, some way, some how. I think it's pretty neat that this game explored that.[/spoiler] 

[spoiler]Also, I was very moved by the powerful post-credits scene. I feel as if that moment of humanity from the author really tied together the themes that the tragedy theatre had been replaying over and over, because it's like how a grieving person might replay alternate endings in their own mind, over and over. They're all tragic, because if everything had been perfect the first time, the author wouldn't have imagined this game at all. It's a story that proves its case by existing.[/spoiler]

[h2]遥想当年[/h2]
游戏发布于2010年，正好是我上了大学以后，配上台式电脑自由玩游戏的那几年。当时游戏的CG预告片十分震撼，开场CG也是顶级，很是惹人关注。游戏刚出后不久我就下载玩了，虽然不带中文，但游侠的天邈汉化组和3DM的潜龙汉化组都对本作进行了汉化。经过几轮的更新，汉化质量已经非常高了，字体也很好看。我故意用的繁体中文，配上汉化组文邹邹的字句，看着很带感觉。游戏画面风格偏向于卡通化，或者说漫画化，可能跟主创之一的漫画家身份有关。本作主体为战斗加解谜，比较对我的胃口。其实我当时也没玩过多少大型游戏，几乎对每年发行的所有知名游戏照单全收。

游戏另一个吸引我的主要因素就是其剧情和世界观。因为刚开始有信仰，我对圣经相关的游戏和电影大作都很关注。《但丁的地狱》（2010）是主机独占，我当时玩不到。本作则有PC版，且有汉化组助力。其故事取材自新约的《启示录》，这种把圣经文字具象化的设计很是吸引我。当然，实际玩过之后就知道，游戏内容跟圣经关系并不大。最主要的四骑士本应是瘟疫、战争、饥荒和死亡，该系列则把瘟疫和饥荒改成了怒神/狂怒和祸乱/纷争。与其说更像圣经，还不如说更像《暗黑破坏神》，都只是借用了天使和恶魔战争这一设定。

[h2]震撼的开场和结局[/h2]
整个故事开始于人类现代生活中突如其来的恶魔入侵，随后就是四骑士之一的战争和天使的现身。本以为他是来战胜恶魔并拯救人类的，没想到人类在天使恶魔大战中处于微不足道的地位，仅存在于开场CG和序幕之中。没过多久，全部人类就灭亡了。在启示录的记载中，未来会出现七印（末世的预兆）、七号（患难和试炼）和七碗（震怒和审判）。四骑士伴随着前四印而出现，第五印是殉道者，第六印是超级地震，第七印则是寂静和之后的七号。恶魔的结局是注定的，包括撒旦/龙、敌基督、假先知和大淫妇等。人类在其中的角色是很重要的，不悔改的人将遭遇震怒和审判，所以要接受警示，成为得胜之人，得以进入千年王国和新天新地。

本作故事最大的悬念就是四骑士之一的「战争」为何会在第七封印（显然和启示录记载内容不符）被打破之前现身，是个典型的悬疑故事。扮演审判角色的焦灼议会将一切归罪于战争，并派其消灭名为「毁灭者」的头号恶魔。与此同时，有的天使堕落了，有的天使被封印，有的天使仍在奋战。恶魔内部也发生分裂，毁灭者囚禁了萨麦尔，也驱逐了一些恶魔。战争凭一己之力，先后干掉四大守护恶魔，与萨麦尔合作，将其释放并恢复了力量，从而得以进入高塔。从里面封印力量的死亡天使亚兹拉尔得知部分真相，原来是阿巴顿找他一起谋划破坏六个封印，引诱恶魔进攻人类世界，然后将其歼灭后恢复六封印。这样的话，就能不被发现的组织黑暗势力滋生，让人类在光明力量下成长发展，锁定最终三方决战的胜局。然而，他显然高估了天堂的力量，根本无力对地狱产生压制性力量，自己还被反杀。此后，借助伊甸园智慧树的指引，战争得知了毁灭者就是阿巴顿死后堕落而成，背后还有未知的女性干预一切。重铸末日之剑后，战争消灭了毁灭者，也得知了焦灼议会明明知道一切，从一开始就在装糊涂，让自己背锅的事实。

借助于和女天使乌列尔的誓约，战争自愿被杀，并由乌列尔打破第七封印复活。此时的他摆脱了议会控制，恢复了力量，准备复仇。乌列尔说，白城和议会都会追杀战争，他一人对抗不了。战争说，不，我并非一人！伴随着第七封印的打破，另外三位骑士化作流星降临地球！这简直是最燃的结局之一了！故事并没有完结，很多事情也没说清楚，造物主和白城等仅在口头被提到，未知邪恶力量也没现身，焦灼议会动机仍然存疑。铸造者乌塞因种族，堵门的石巨人一族也没有更多解释。不过，之后所有的续作都是前传或并列时间线，故事线再未推进。这一局面终于在今年夏天打破，下一作要来了！

[h2]四位一体：战斗、解谜、收集、升级[/h2]
IGN将本作评价为「鬼泣」+「战神」+「塞尔达传说」合体的游戏，说明了其本身并非单纯的动作游戏，解谜也占很大部分。彼时，我从未玩过「塞尔达传说」，「战神」只打过一点PSP上的流程，「鬼泣」虽玩过，但从未通关。没有那些优秀作品的成见，我对《暗黑血统》评价颇高。除了推进流程，战斗可以升级武器，收集灵魂；解谜可以收集生命、怒气和盔甲碎片，还可额外增加灵魂。专门去做收集，过程中解开所有支线谜题的话，能拿到深渊铠甲大幅增加防御，生命和怒气全都达到惊人的十个，轻松拿捏最高难度。此外，还有四种传奇装备，能买各种招式，升级四种怒气技能。总之，角色在战斗、解谜、收集、升级四位一体的过程中不断获得正反馈，让角色越来越强，也有清图的快感。

游戏的战斗略显单调，简单和一般难度中的大部分战斗都可以用挑起+旋转下劈，以及有间隔的按攻击键来水平旋转攻击莽过去。只有到最高难度中，技巧才显得重要，需要不断适时猛冲躲避，并注意切换目标才能顺利战胜，否则那点血量很快就会耗尽。游戏的BOSS战都很有设计感，不是单纯的战斗，都搭配有专门的解谜，必须摸清敌人的套路，然后重复至少三四个回合才能胜利。所有BOSS中，沙虫的那个最为震撼，面对体型上的绝对差距，仍然可以靠走位躲避与不间断射击取胜。其余BOSS的出场和终结技也都很不错，各有特色。只是有些过于简单了，比如面对黑暗面的自己，我在最高难度中走上前发动了七次地刺技能（其余三种技能使用频率极低），然后双方开混沌模式对砍就无伤通过了，全程不到两分钟。

地图中心是萨麦尔所在的灼热绞架，通向一开始的十字路口、三大BOSS区域以及高塔。沙虫所在之地又通向第四BOSS和伊甸园，除了彼此之间的连接，还有传送通道和骑马帮助快速抵达。所有收集品散落全图各处，但取得方式各不相同，得随流程推进拿到对应道具才行。这使得地图具备重复探索性，后期拿全装备一个个破解并集齐时，让人很有清扫一空、没有遗憾的满足感。只是有些收集品藏得过于隐蔽了，推荐看看指南，要知道连传送通道里都有三个收集品！我也是好不容易才集齐的，中间有段时间不知漏下哪个，重复跑图的滋味可不好受。

[h2]被关闭的Vigil催生出了Gunfire和Airship Syndicate[/h2]
Vigil Games由漫画家乔·马杜雷拉和游戏设计师大卫·亚当斯于2005年成立于美国，次年就被THQ收购。他们的作品稀少，除了参与《国土防线》（2011）的制作，就只有2010年和2012年的两部《暗黑血统》。2012年12月，母公司THQ申请破产保护，旗下的所有工作室和资产均被出售，但唯独只有Vigil未被收购。没办法，找不到人接手，Vigil Games只能被迫关闭。关闭前，他们一直开发的网游《战锤40000：黑暗千年》项目不顺，后被取消。此外，他们还有个代号为《Crawler》的未公开项目也被取消了。不过，《暗黑血统》系列的质量和名声（百万级别销量）有目共睹，这个IP和员工注定不会就此沉寂，比如白金工作室的制作人稻叶敦志就曾表示有意收购《暗黑血统》这个IP。

2013年，Crytek处于扩张期，看中了Vigil的联合创始人大卫·亚当斯及其工作室成员，于是成立了新工作室Crytek USA。这使其成为Vigil的精神延续，但并不拥有《暗黑血统》的IP。次年，Crytek USA规模缩减，大卫·亚当斯辞职并带领一批前Vigil的核心开发人员成立了独立工作室Gunfire Games。他们仍对《暗黑血统》念念不忘，于2015年与THQ Nordic合作推出《暗黑血统2：死亡终极版》，2018年又推出正统续作《暗黑血统3》。2019年，Gunfire Games工作室被THQ Nordic所收购，真是兜兜转转一大圈，又回来了！

Vigil的另一名联合创始人乔·马杜雷拉在工作室关闭后回归了漫画行业，但2014年，他又连同另一位前Vigil成员一起成立了独立开发组Airship Syndicate。该工作室专注于俯视角游戏，在首款游戏取得不错的成绩后，他们又转向《暗黑血统》IP的持有者THQ Nordic寻求合作机会。这一合作最终成为了广受好评的系列外传《暗黑血统：创世纪》（2019），可见只要是Vigil的人就对这个IP念念不忘。今年夏天，《暗黑血统4》公布了CG预告片，由Gunfire Games工作室负责制作。里面的语音就是初代结局里女天使「乌列尔」的话，然后另外三位天启骑士骑着马一同走出，四骑士齐聚！如今每位骑士都有各自的单独作品，终于能续写初代的故事了！

A deckbuilder whose cute and simple-looking exterior belies a more intricate and deeply interesting game.
Appears to be inspired by FTL and Deckbuilding genres, with some extra twists and tweaks. The game has you selecting a ship and various crew members at the start of a run. Your crew members, such as pilots and weapons officers, will determine what kinds of upgrade cards you get. Meanwhile, on the battlefield, positioning matters as your cannons and launchers will point at one segment of the opponent's vessel while theirs does the same to you. This leads to some pretty interesting choices before the game (which crew do you select), in battle (do you need to move now or should you fire and risk return damage), and deckbuilding selections (if you add this attack card, for example, will your movement cards now come up too infrequently?).
Soundtrack is pretty nice.
There is a story and some humour inside, though you can ignore that and focus solely on gameplay and still have a good time.

I like it a lot, and I would like to play more often.

It doesn't have as much replayability or depth as other roguelike deckbuilders, but it still has more than necesarry to be worth buying and playing. It is so good looking and still super fun! It is definitely a game that I would recommend to anyone who enjoys the genre and people learning the genre.

카이로 소프트 게임 느낌이 살짝 나는 데스크톱 방치형 게임.
 
 게임의 진행구조는
용사 후보생 모집->몹 소환 건물에서 소환한 몹을 사냥해서 경험치+골드 획득->성장한 용사를 졸업&승급->얻은 재화로 본진 및 기술 업그레이드->더 나은 용사후보생 모집->반복
이라는 구조를 가지고 있고 유저가 신경쓸 부분은 건물짓기, 용사 졸업&승급 결정, 기술연구, 버프&소모성 아이템 만들기&주기, 명성 레벨 올리기(일종의 간이 레이드)정도지만 초반에는 은근히 할 게 많다.

 하다보면 초반만큼 바쁘진 않지만, 나름 용사들 키우는 맛도 있고 승급하면 스킬도 달라지는등 보는맛도 있는편이다. 조금 템포가 느린 타이쿤 게임 하는 느낌도 없지않아 있는듯.

 플레이하면서 느낀 단점으로는 화면 이동이 땅, 건물, 나무등을 우클릭&휠클릭 상태로만 이동이 된다는 점인데 건물 사이사이의 배경 부분을 클릭하면 이동이 안되는 게 은근히 신경쓰인다. 차라리 휠 움직임으로 화면이동이 되게 해주던가 키를 할당해서 키보드로 움직일 수 있게 해줬다면 좋았을 것 같다.

 그리고 번역 부분에 있어서도 기본적으로 AI 번역은 아닌 것 같고 나름대로 번역 퀄리티도 좋은 게 티가 나긴 하는데 부분적으로 번역이 안되어 있는 곳이 조금씩 보인다. 99% 한글번역 이라고 해야할지. 번역 퀄리티도 좋은데 이런 부분에서 미흡한게 조금 아쉽게 느껴진다.

[strike] 이런 단점이 있긴 해도 이 가격대에 이정도 퀄리티의 게임이라면, 개인적으로는 방치형 게임중에서 상위권의 게임이라고 평가해도 될 것 같다는 생각이 든다.[/strike] 

생각보다 게임 볼륨이 작다. 용사 최대치 12명에 메인건물 풀업글이 6레벨이 끝. 데스크탑 방치형 게임들이 추구하는 캐주얼함이라고 포장 할 수도 있지만, 좀 재미있을려는 찰나에 성장이 강제적으로 멈추는 느낌이 크다. 게임 가격대를 보면 이정도가 적당한가 싶기도 하면서도 만들다 만 것 같은 느낌도 든다. 차라리 DLC라도 내서 분량을 키우는 편이 좋을 것 같다는 생각이 든다.


+엔딩&올업적까지 12시간 걸렸다. 방치한 시간을 생각하면 플레이 시간이 정말 짧다. 그리고 퀄리티 좋던 번역은 후반부 건물&유닛에 갈수록 애매한 번역이나 미번역이 늘어난다. 플레이에 지장은 딱히 없지만 조금은 거슬리긴 하다.

또한 비싼 값을 들여 업그레이드하는 식당, 도서관, 연금술 건물중에 식당, 도서관은 업그레이드 한 의미가 거의 없는데다 도서관은 종종 캐릭터가 사용을 마쳤음에도 계속해서 자리를 차지하는 버그가 있다.

물론 이런 부분들을 감안해도 충분히 재미있는 게임은 맞다고 생각하지만, 전처럼 강력히 추천한다고 하기에는 애매한 게임인 듯하다.

[h1]Между двух огней[/h1]
[b]В тоталитарном государстве люди делятся на два типа: те, кто работает на него, и те, кто являются его жертвами. Очевидно, что в таких условиях всегда находятся люди, поддерживавших тиранию ради своей выгоды. Об этом и расскажет Beholder.[/b]
[h2]Теперь это ваша обязанность[/h2]
[b]следить, расспрашивать, писать рапорты и характеристики тех, кто живет в доме в неизвестной стране за Железным занавесом.[/b] В общем, всячески быть нехорошим человеком и помогать тоталитарному режиму. Впрочем, этому имеется оправдание — у вас есть семья, которой нужно как-то выживать в условиях тотального дефицита всего. Но даже несмотря на это у вас все еще остается выбор.
[quote=kai]В игре есть отсылки и на Papers, Please. Достаточно только всмотреться в концовку.[/quote]
[b]Перед тем как привезти вас в новый дом, вам дали экспериментальное лекарство, подарившее вам способность не спать, чтобы круглосуточно следить за соседями.[/b] Распорядок дня жильцов, впрочем, больше похож на обычный. Каждое утро они спускаются вниз позавтракать тем, что есть, и поехать на работу, куда их распределили. В этот момент вы, обладая всеми ключами в доме, можете обыскивать квартиры и устанавливать камеры, купленные во внутреннем магазине за очки влияния. Которые, в свою очередь, можно получить за выполнение заданий от правительства, своей семьи и, конечно же, местной повстанческой группировки.
[b]Практически каждое задание имеет таймер. И если оно не будет выполнено в срок, являясь указанием правительства, то вас оштрафуют на деньги — основной ресурс в игре.[/b]
[quote=kai]Beholder хоть и не блещет технологичностью, обладает атмосферным дизайном, где все персонажи изображены в виде черных фигур, а вокруг — мрак войны и запустения. Как в This War of Mine, которой, вероятно, создатели игры тоже вдохновлялись.[/quote]
[h3]стоит откладывать[/h3]
[b]Зарабатывать деньги, конечно же, можно доносами.[/b] И если от желания купить шоколадку семье еще можно отказаться, то когда дочка заболеет пневмонией, а лекарства будут стоить двадцать тысяч, вы поймете: или вы работаете на правительство, или ваши родные умрут.
[b]С первым рапортом в игре все очевидно[/b] человек изготавливает наркотики и сам по себе довольно неприятен — такого и сдать не жалко. Но дальше вам придется идти на сделку со своей совестью. Как можно написать донос на профессора литературы, который дал нужные книги вашему сыну и, в целом, довольно мил? Конечно, некоторые ситуации можно будет решить в обход необходимости отправлять кого-то на расстрел, но далеко не все.
[h3]К сожалению[/h3]
[b]даже когда можно выбрать относительно хороший вариант решения проблемы, иногда приходится звонить «кому нужно». Все из-за странной сложности.[/b] Суммы денег нужны непомерные, и даже в случае, если вы не заплатите их, часть все равно отберут. Так, если вы не найдете пятнадцать тысяч на обучение сына в университете, вам придется самому заплатить за его отчисление. И если у вас не будет достаточной суммы — то все, конец. Главная причина конца игры в Beholder — это уход в минус, после чего вас обвинят в растрате и уничтожат вас и всю вашу семью.
[quote=kai]Угроза исходит не только от тоталитарного аппарата, но и от ваших жильцов, которые тоже могут донести на вас или сделать другую подлянку.[/quote]
[b]За выполнение даже самых прибыльных заданий можно получить до пяти тысяч, а за шантаж ваших жильцов — и того меньше. При этом тратами вас забрасывают с первой же минуты. Оплатить счета, купить продукты, подкупить чиновника, купить предметы на задание. Не совсем понятно, как в этом мире выживают другие, у которых нет таких возможностей, как у вас. Поэтому выглядит это как минимум странно.[/b]
[h2][b]Кроме того, ваш выбор часто совершенно непредсказуемо влияет на игру.[/b][/h2]
 Так, неудачная афера с местным моряком не позволит вам спустя какое-то время решить другой вопрос. Это несколько расстраивает. В игре довольно большое количество заданий, но она полностью линейна. Уже после второго-третьего прохождения вы будете знать, как максимально эффективно решать те или иные задачи. В целом, у игры есть несколько вариантов прохождения, но какую концовку вы получите, будет решаться преимущественно в конце.
[u]Если вдумчиво заниматься прохождением, то добраться до финала можно за десять часов, учитывая, что первые несколько раз вас будут расстреливать еще в самом начале из-за тех самых непредсказуемых результатов выбора.[/u]
[b]Оценка:8.8/10[/b]

[b]10 hours in — I called it quits.[/b]
I stopped having consistent fun several hours ago. The short version: there’s a lot of wasted potential here. What starts off promising becomes increasingly repetitive. I recognize that backtracking is part of the Metroidvania genre, but this feels like Backtracking: The Game. Venturing into the “wrong” areas doesn’t just waste time—it often results in getting one-shot by overpowered enemies you weren’t meant to fight yet. Wishing the dev the best, but this one’s a miss for me.

[h2]Pros[/h2]
[list]
[*]I like the pixel art and gothic aesthetic. The blend of European towns, swamps, and cathedral-like architecture nails the dark fantasy atmosphere.
[*]You can skip most cutscenes, which I always appreciate.
[*]The gameplay initially feels great—like a love letter to DS-era Castlevania.
[*]The first half of the bosses were fun and fair, offering challenge without feeling cheap.
[*]Enemy placement feels deliberate early on, adding tension without being unfair (unless you’re in an overleveled area). This quality drops off later in the game.
[*]Leveling up provides a noticeable power boost early on. That immediate sense of growth helps pacing—for a while.
[/list]
[h2]Cons[/h2]
[*]Leveling gives huge stat jumps, which creates a binary difficulty curve. You either melt enemies or get deleted in seconds. A smoother progression with ability gating would have worked better.
[*]Only one weapon type—the whip. If you don’t enjoy its moveset, that’s it. Equipment variety is too grindy and spread out to help early on.
[*]Controls are intentionally rigid, just like classic Castlevania. I personally like it, but it won’t be for everyone. You have to be very deliberate with movement and attacks.
[*]The game wants you to go in a specific direction, blocking other paths with overpowered enemies or missing traversal powers. Getting punished with instant death for exploring feels awful.
[*]Navigation lacks intuition. It’s easy to get lost with little guidance on where to find new traversal abilities. It almost feels like the game is designed to halt your progress repeatedly just to send you elsewhere.
[*]The forced story segment where the main character loses their weapon and must sneak past enemies is miserable. It doesn’t fit the game’s core design and single-handedly ruins replay value.
[*]Crafting (Transmutation) is clunky and grindy. The resource demands are high, and the menus are frustrating to use.
[*]Menus in general are poorly designed. Items are sorted by acquisition time with no filters, and the map must be closed using the same button that opens it—pressing your reflexive “cancel” button just zooms the map instead.
[*]“Puzzles” that require selecting items from your inventory to destroy objects add pointless tedium.
[*]Status effects are punishing without depth. Poison drains your health rapidly, Curse disables mana regeneration, and Injury halves your stats. They’re just annoyances that waste time.
[*]A few cutscenes cannot be skipped.
[*]Later bosses feel overtuned—designed around abusing heals or near-perfect runs. They’re frustrating, not fun.
[/list]
[h2]“Do I Want to Keep Playing?”[/h2]

[b]1 Hour In:[/b] Absolutely.
The game feels great, looks beautiful, and sounds excellent. A strong first impression.

[b]5 Hours In:[/b] Yes.
Still engaged, but the forced stealth section and occasional direction confusion are starting to bother me.

[b]8 Hours In:[/b] Barely.
The pacing keeps breaking, and finding new content feels more like a chore than progress.

[b]10 Hours In:[/b] No.
I’m done. The repetition, backtracking, and recycled content killed my interest. It’s a beautiful, atmospheric game that forgets to respect the player’s time.

[h1] Short and Focused: The Perfect Franchise Spin-off [/h1] 
Assassin's Creed Rogue is often described as "Black Flag in the Arctic," and that's both its greatest strength and its core identity. It takes the fantastic naval mechanics of its predecessor and packages them into a tighter, more focused experience with a narrative premise that remains one of the series' most intriguing.
https://youtu.be/19GE57IUjfk
This game is essentially a compact version of Black Flag, but with a far more centralized and personal story. You play as Shay Patrick Cormac, an Assassin who witnesses the dark side of the Brotherhood and defects to the Templars. This "from the other side" perspective is executed brilliantly, making the Templars feel surprisingly human and justified. The story is sharp, focused, and mercifully free of the bloat that affected other entries, delivering a compelling arc without unnecessary stretching.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3490712374
The core gameplay sailing the Morrigan, exploring icy waters, and engaging in thrilling naval battles is as satisfying as ever, now enhanced with new tools like an oil slick and Puckle guns. The North Atlantic is a beautiful and dangerous playground.

However, this compact nature has a downside: the world, while visually stunning, can feel smaller and less "lived-in" compared to the vibrant Caribbean. The core formula, while polished, offers very little that is truly new.

This is a difficult review to write. As someone who owns the last four versions of FHM, I've witnessed a passionate community and dedicated developers working with limited resources to build something special. Unfortunately, this latest edition falls short of expectations.

Let me provide some context. I played EHM for years and even contributed to roster updates for two years with Blue Line. When that shut down, I switched to FHM. Despite the learning curve, I recognized the potential and the genuine care the developers invested. For hockey management fans, it offers incredible depth—perhaps overwhelming for newcomers, but rewarding for those who invest the time.

However, persistent issues have eroded my enthusiasm over the past four years:

The trading system remains fundamentally broken. Unless you actively place players on your trade block, you receive zero trade offers. The computer simply cherry-picks from your trade block rather than behaving like an actual GM would. This isn't AI—it's a simplistic algorithm that undermines the entire trading experience. Four years, and this core mechanic remains unchanged.

The UI desperately needs attention. It feels like the developers either don't play their own game or have become blind to its usability issues. Adding players to shortlists or watchlists is needlessly tedious—there's no bulk selection feature, something I've repeatedly suggested on their forums. Want to scout 20 prospects? Click each one individually. Additionally, viewing a player profile and returning to your previous screen? Your filters and page position are gone. These aren't minor inconveniences; they're fundamental UX failures that drain the joy from gameplay.

I won't leave a negative review because, honestly, if you're new to hockey management games, FHM remains a solid choice. The depth is there, the simulation works (but still damn slow whatever you CPU), and you'll likely enjoy discovering its systems. But for veterans like me who've been playing for years, buying this version feels pointless. The same frustrations persist, the same workarounds are required, and the same promises of improvements remain unfulfilled. Save your money until they demonstrate real commitment to fixing these longstanding issues.

I won't request a refund—I respect the effort involved. But I won't be purchasing future versions unless these core issues are addressed. 

To the OOTP team: If you need help with UI/UX design, reach out. This is literally my profession, and I'd genuinely like to see this game succeed. You have something special here, but it's being held back by fixable problems that have persisted far too long.

First of all, I'm biased to the setting, as at the age of 10-13, I was enthralled by the Greek mythology.
On the other hand, in this case, I would demand more from the setting converted to TW franchise, right? ;) Anyway, when I first launched the game, I got a feeling that the Bulgarian CA team had the same attitude to the Greek mythology.

So, contrary to what you may have watched/read before about TWS: TROY, at the release, the developers [b]perfectly[/b] captured the spirit and the style of Iliad, Odyssey, etc. 
Cuckold Odyssey who can pierce 20 cuckers with one arrow, invincible Achilles easily soloing stacks of Troyans, warrior [b]woman[/b] Penthesilea with her Amazons, fast centaurs pictured as horseriders, medusa Gorgon turns people into "stone-dead" by poisoning a water source in a settlement… So many explanations of and allusions to myths, but not to the extent of 'historical' vibe.
And I mean before the main CA office forced to add fantasy crap via the Mythic DLCs later.

What actually killed the TWS:TROY franchise were the fiasco with the free release on Epic Games and then a year of unavailability on Steam. Oh, well, Chinese Communist money never give good in the long run. :(

Even the problems with the battle mechanics (killer-chariots--we had them in TW multiple times), or general warfare gameplay (neverending settlement defence--introduced by TW:WH), or diplomacy (trade system exploits--don't even remind me of TW:ME2 2-turn win), or overpromised correction of key problems (missile units stronk--as usually in TW) ----- all these could be mitigated with proper support of already existing TW fanbase on Steam. And eventually, the major flaws were corrected to some extent, but the TW fans remembered the gaslighting from CA, and turned their hate to Troy for this reason at the first place.

So, to the point, [u][b]why the game is bad:[/b][/u]

1. Very little replayability. Enemies are preset to the greater extent: you pick either the West coast or the East coast. You can, of course, go against the tide and betray your supposed partners, but it won't make your preset enemies love you.
2. Unlike in TW:WH1-2-3, the unit models have generally little distinction at the bird view. BUT this is literally the same for most historical TW.
3. Settlement battles. Constant. Neverending. The AI overestimates itself predicting a win in autoresolve, but loosing if you fight an easy battle manually. I think I've never ever played that many settlement defence battles in any other TW franchise.
4. Sieges. Generally OK (except for butt-ladders and siege attackers). Are filled with chokepoints but the controls are awful, especially if playing with unit size of large+. You just can't place your stack of harpies in the desired position.
5. Capturing settlements with the crap TW:WH mechanics, when you capture a settlement, it drops -1 level. Combined with constant settlement battles, it's just tiresome.
6. Mythology mode. Changed the vibe from the epic mythology to a Warhammer poor clone. The good thing that you are allowed NOT to play in this mode.
7. At higher difficulties, the AI is not smarter, but receives gazilions of bonuses. It's applicable to most TW franchises, but on the other hand, the bonuses can be easily exploited with barter mechanics.
8. Only Troyan hordes.

[u][b]Why the game is good:[/b][/u]

-1. The whole idea that the mythic creatures and epic heroes are not just another fantasy crap, but actually people who pretend to be such creatures, and everyone surrounding believe in it -- is just wow!
0. OPTIMISATION!!!!!1111oneoneone The game runs perfectly even on old machines, provided that these machines had challenges with both, TW:WH1-2 and TW:3K at the time.
1. Each faction has its unique mechanics. You can, of course, play without them (except for the Hordes), but those differences [i]somewhat[/i] allow replayability.
2. Another addition to replayability is that each faction has its own roster, with advantages and disadvantages, ranging from minor to gamebreaking.
3. Historical mode for old-school TW fans, where gods are almost non-existent and your hero is just a regular TW general with a squad of bodyguards.
4. [b]You can break your opponents[/b], by flanking or attacking in the rear, unlike in TW WH1-2-3.
5. Choke points do matter, especially if you line up enough unit models to close the gap.
6. Barter system with food, wood, bronze, stone and coins -- FINALLY, something else than blatant TW gold mana.
7. Decent visuals and aesthetics, although some are anachronistic (Helen's makeup). Pleasant music, although with only a little of the Greek vibes, if any at all.
8. THIS IS SPARTA!!! (although, without any Persians).

PVのような派手な採掘をする前にゲームクリアしてしまうというレビューがあったため、補足。
一部ネタバレがあるのでみたくない人はご注意ください。








ゲームには２段階のクリア設定があります。
1日ごとに集めなければならない石炭の量のノルマがあります。
この量が日が経つごとに増えていきます。
そして１段階目が15日をクリアできるかどうか、そして２段階目が25日をクリアできるかどうかです。
25日の方はTrue endingと設定されており、新しいゲームモードの解放の条件にもなっています。
「PVのような派手な採掘をする前にゲームクリアしてしまう」というのはおそらく15日でのゲームクリアを指していると思います。
ゲームモードによりますが、最高の装備は大体20日前後に購入できるようになるので、25日まで遊ぶことを前提にするなら、ド派手採掘は十分可能です。
ちなみに、25日を超えてもエンドレスモードで遊ぶこともできます。
が、22日くらい以降は同じことの繰り返しなので、個人的には25日で十分です。

ゲーム内容についても少し書いておきます。
ノルマクリアで一定額のお金がもらえ、余剰分の鉱石を売ることで追加のお金がもらえます。
そのお金を装備の購入やカバンの拡張、労働者の雇用などに使っていきます。

ゲームモードにはボムの値段が半分だったり、カバンの容量が無限だったり、破壊された瞬間に家に格納されるなどがあります。
一番基本のゲームモードでは、カバンに掘った鉱石を詰めて、地上にある家の横の箱に格納しなければなりません。
そのため、掘る能力を高めて、たくさんの鉱石を掘れるようになっても、カバンの容量が少なければ、何回も箱に格納しに帰らなければならず、結果あまり成果が得られないというようなことが起きます。
そこで、カバンの容量を増やすアップグレードを活用して、掘る能力と運搬能力のバランスを取っていくのがこのゲームの肝です。

しかし、上記に書いた「カバンの容量が無限だったり、破壊された瞬間に家に格納される」モードは掘る能力のみを強化するだけでいいので、稼ぎを伸ばしやすいです。
なので、25日のクリアがかなり簡単なので、25日クリアが難しい人はおすすめです。

ゲームモードは10個くらいあり、そこに5つの鉱石の配置パターンの変化があります。
「深くなるほど硬く中身の多い鉱石配置」が基本のパターンで、「横に行くほど硬い」や「鉱石が空にある(上下反転)」などの配置パターンがあります。
その組み合わせなので50通りくらいのゲームモードがあります。
現在40時間プレイしてますが、また解放してないゲームモードが１つあり、鉱石の配置は基本パターンでしか遊んでいません。
なので、40時間プレイして全体の20%弱くらいしか遊べていません。
まぁ全部のパターンをやるまで楽しめるかは分かりませんが、概算で全クリするまで200時間遊べると考えれば、別に1700円はむしろ安いと思います。

I bought Hot Wheels Unleashed 2: Turbocharged because I really enjoyed the first game. Overall, the second game is much easier compared to the first one (including achievements). This time, they've added jumping, ramming (pushing other cars), and a skill system. I really liked the new skills for example, you can turn a grippy car into a drifty one, increase your nitro capacity, or make your car more stable. These features didn’t exist in the first game, where you could only upgrade your vehicles. The jump mechanic makes it easier to avoid track obstacles and leap over blocks, unlike in the first game where you’d often crash into them. Also, if someone tries to push you, you can now ram them back to the sides. The main story includes some short but nice cutscenes. They're not too long, but they add a bit of atmosphere. On top of that, several new game modes have been introduced I found them pretty fun and refreshing. In general, this second game l offers a very different and much easier experience than the first game. I was hoping to see a Toyota Supra in the Fast & Furious pack, but even without it, it’s not bad.The online experience in the first game was pretty unstable, but they really improved it in second game. It's way more stable now and you can see your opponents. If you're looking for a more challenging and competitive game, I’d recommend the first one. But if you want something more chill and casual, the second game is a better fit. I’d recommend picking this game up during a sale. And if you’re planning to 100% the achievements, definitely go for the third bundle that includes all DLCs, it’s worth it.

YouTubers Life 2 é uma agradável surpresa dentro do gênero de simulação de vida moderna. Desenvolvido pela UPLAY Online, o título expande com competência as ideias do primeiro jogo, oferecendo uma experiência mais rica, imersiva e envolvente para quem sonha em entender — ou viver — a rotina de um criador de conteúdo digital.

Logo nos primeiros minutos, o jogador é apresentado a NewTube City, uma cidade vibrante e cheia de personalidade, onde cada bairro tem seu próprio ritmo, estética e oportunidades. A ambientação é um dos pontos altos do jogo: tudo é colorido, animado e transmite uma energia positiva que combina perfeitamente com o tema de ascensão e popularidade na internet.

O sistema de progressão é bem estruturado. Criar vídeos, editar, analisar tendências e interagir com o público se tornam mecânicas cíclicas e recompensadoras. Há uma boa sensação de progresso — cada novo equipamento, assinatura ou upgrade de estúdio traz aquela satisfação de estar evoluindo como um verdadeiro influenciador. Mesmo com uma jogabilidade acessível, o game consegue manter uma camada estratégica interessante, exigindo atenção ao timing, à relevância das tendências e ao equilíbrio entre produtividade e vida social.

Outro mérito é o nível de personalização: o jogador pode definir seu estilo de conteúdo, aparência, estilo de vida e até suas relações com outros personagens. Essa liberdade permite que cada jornada seja única, incentivando a criatividade e a experimentação.

A trilha sonora é leve e contagiante, complementando o clima descontraído do jogo. E, embora o visual adote um estilo cartunesco, a direção de arte é competente e consistente — tudo parece feito para entregar uma experiência agradável e acessível, tanto para o público casual quanto para quem busca relaxar entre jogos mais exigentes.

Em termos de narrativa, o jogo mantém um tom leve e motivador. Ele mostra que o sucesso digital não vem apenas de números, mas também de autenticidade e dedicação — uma mensagem positiva que reflete a realidade de muitos criadores de conteúdo atuais.

Conclusão

YouTubers Life 2 acerta ao equilibrar diversão, leveza e estratégia, entregando um simulador que vai além do simples ato de “gravar vídeos”. Ele recria, de forma lúdica e carismática, os bastidores da vida de um influencer moderno — com todos os desafios, recompensas e momentos de descontração que esse universo proporciona.

Para quem busca um jogo criativo, acolhedor e cheio de personalidade, YouTubers Life 2 é uma escolha certeira.

⭐ Nota: 8.5/10 — Um simulador envolvente, divertido e cheio de boas vibrações.

Add in Friend Pass, which lets you play with your friends across different platforms, and the fact that there’s no Denuvo or annoying third party launchers that alone is a huge sign of respect toward gamers.

Story wise, I think it’s a bit weaker compared to It Takes Two and A Way Out, but that ending… absolutely mind blowing, creative, and emotional. I was honestly stunned.

Despite being made with Unreal Engine 5, the optimization is fantastic I didn’t run into a single issue.

My only real complaint is the lack of mini games. Unlike It Takes Two, which was full of fun little side activities, this one doesn’t have them but the amazing side missions make up for it pretty well.

With all the positives and the clear respect the devs have shown toward players, there’s no way I could give it anything less than a perfect score.

Когда что-то шумит в подсобке - тебе страшно. Когда в пустом магазине за тобой вдруг запирается дверь - тебе очень страшно. Ведь это значит, что кто-то всё это время в эту самую подсобку тебя заманивал, и притаился рядом, чтобы тебя там запереть.  Но когда всё это объясняется призраками - ломается всяческий интерес к опасению. Потому что теперь размах того, что может произойти совершенно огромен. Всё становится похоже на проходной ужастик про очень злых духов. Мы не экзорцист и не Антоха Городецкий, призраки для нас это штука неостановимая, а потому и бояться её не очень-то хочется. 

И, к сожалению, в своей концовке игра окончательно переходит в жанр фантастики, подобно тому как это делает Night Security, другая игра автора. Ей богу, когда из интересного сеттинга мрачного захолустья или же тихого многоэтажного офиса тебя переносят в буквально АДСКОЕ помещение, полное какой-то паранормальной х у й н и, становится скорее тошно, чем страшно.

А потому, желаю автору продолжать развивать успех своих проектов, рассказывающих об остросоциальных проблемах (The Closing Shift и Parasocial), ведь это у него получается очень хорошо.

Overall: I'd recommend CrossCode... to people that enjoy puzzles.

If you like twin-stick shooter combat, there is definitely plenty of that in CrossCode, and it's good, fun combat. 

However, the game has a LOT of puzzles. If I had to give numbers, I'd say the game is 60% to 70% puzzles. And the puzzles only grow in complexity as the game goes on and gives you more and more tools. And if you want to open the many, many chests for items to help you through the combat? Well, you'll be combing the environment for the one very specific way to get to them, which often involves another puzzle.

The story's good, but it is hurt a bit by the dungeons (the really big puzzle sections) taking up so much time, and messing up the story's pacing. It's hard to be happy when all you want is to continue the story after a major plot development, but you've spent an hour or more on nothing but puzzles (with very small amounts of combat in between puzzles). 

And if you're anything like me, that likes combat and story more than puzzles... you'll eventually give up and look up a guide to get you past the more elaborate puzzles, just so you can see how the story turns out. 

I know this review makes it seem like I'd give the game a big thumbs down, but everything (aside from the puzzles) kept me wanting to play, and got me through to the end of the story. I don't regret playing CrossCode for a moment.

[h1]Review after 100%[/h1]
Spoiler free

[h3]Gameplay:[/h3]
So I personally enjoyed the game but I feel like the gameplay is not for everyone. It is very fun and very grindy even after beating every available side quest the game still wants you to grind enemies to catchup. The combat arts felt very nice although a little confusing to keep track of what skills you have at the end game. The combat is very smooth once you get the hang of it. Also there is a LOT of puzzles in this game. I wouldn't be surprised if someone called it a puzzle game so if puzzles aren't your thing theres always google!

[h3]Story / World:[/h3]
The story is very engaging and I would consider it a dialogue heavy game. I wouldn't consider myself to be the biggest rpg player but I thoroughly enjoyed the dialogue and the characters especially grasshead. The areas especially autumns rise are very nostalgic bringing me back to a time when I was a kid again playing fiesta online for the first time. The level design I feel is the best part of the game which is hard to explain for this game but everything just works and everything is where you expect it to be. The aesthetic of the world and the story were amazing. I wouldn't say the story is super easy to follow and navigation for the main story means that you have to pay attention. You cannot skip the dialogue (well you can but its not recommended).

[h3]Graphics & Sound:[/h3]
For a game made in HTML5, the game is pixel arty and the performance was amazing and the soundtrack was quite a nice surprise. The music is actually good which I can't say for a lot of games. I kept it on the whole time and every soundtrack felt like the area I was in. I especially loved the soundtrack in once again autumns rise. That place is just beautiful and it's where my character lays after 100%ing the game.

[h3]Value:[/h3]
The game is very much worth the price. It has recently been going on sale for 70% so if you don't wanna buy it at full price wait for a sale! I personally think you should buy it directly from steam. The devs have quoted that they worked on the game for 7 years and it shows. Content is plentiful and most people will complete the game in 30-40 hours with a 100% around 50-80 hours.

[h3]Overall Thoughts:[/h3]
If you enjoy rpg/puzzle games this game is for you! I would recommend anybody to give the game at least a chance. I had a pleasant experience with the game and would relive it again for the first time if I could. For the achievements, there is a few missables so I would recommend researching beforehand and all the achievements aren't hard just grindy, but feel free to message me if you need help with an achievement since there isn't too much relevant information for specific achievements.

The cover art of this game is more enticing than anything you will likely find within. 6 hours in, and at best, you get to see a couple of shirtless guys. I don't know what I was expecting, but for my first gay visual novel, it wasn't something that rated lower than T for Teen. This "visual novel" plays it exceptionally safe, all the way to the very end. It's written content is a bit more explicit than the visual stuff, but not by very much. It's visual "Sexual Content" is always suggestive and never really shown. To add to all that, there's very few times you'll even be bothered by dialog options. 

I don't why there's negative reviews talking about "woke", as most everything these reviews complain about were minor foot notes in the overall story. There's a couple of times the characters ask if the other is feeling it, and they're very well placed and make sense. There's one case of the client they just met, confirming it would be fine to call him, he/him, as he walks in on crew conversing about not knowing what to call him. Hardly a pronoun off, by any means. (and I won't even get into the fact these two other negative reviews don't even know what "woke" means.)

As for the tentacles, and the organism - it's what I signed up for. Maybe it shocked others, but I was fully aware of the "surprise" before going into it, and it's right up my alley. However, I don't think there was enough there to satisfy anyone looking for a romantic cute story, or a fascinating dip into alien appendages. In trying to fulfill both, it didn't seem to do either very well. Maybe it's due to my aphantasia, but I feel completely let down there wasn't more erotic scenes to be had during this six hour run time. 

Final reason why this is getting a negative review, is because the credits trap you. I feel at no time is it alright, on a PC, to trap someone within your game with no clear exit... even the credits. I didn't consent to that. 😉 (others may disagree, and that's fine, this is more a comical quip I have about, than any serious reason to dislike the game as a whole)

I think if this visual novel had more time to cook on the art, and took more risks with it, or went stronger into dialog options, it could really be something special. The voice acting and art were 8/10, while the overall story was kinda mid (6/10 maybe?). Seeing DLC for this, at $15 is almost upsetting, as I feel initial story was incomplete as is.

盗版玩了三天，特来补票。
剧情很棒，虽然只玩了叶云裳线，我自己认为也是比较喜欢那种文静的女生的人，但云裳真的特别戳我。从第一周目完全不懂的萌新开始，我就选了叶云裳，虽然这可能是受到了b站上导流视频的影响。第一周目纯粹是瞎玩的，按照我那种认为强就可以改变一切的心理来玩，基本所有的行动点数都投入到了提升自己的六维点数上，也一直在搜集武功秘籍，人际关系，宗门向心力几乎没刷过，但当时忽略了四师兄的商店（男弟子房我第一周目就没点过），导致属性点都是练功场上随机刷出来的，和瑞声打根本打不过，结束时还很纳闷自己为什么触发不了叶云裳的相关剧情。
很不服气，楞冲了第二周目，目标就是把武林盟主给干死，其他如同上一周目，属性点高了很多，最后艰难残血打过瑞生（这时候还是不知道四师兄商店里可以买武功秘籍），到了相声双侠结局，玩完之后才意识到自己得看看攻略了，云裳剧情就是进不去。
看了攻略后才意识到自己错过了相当多的东西，第三周目准确触发了云裳剧情，玩到结缘时已经哭出来了，云裳和赵活一路上的生死相依患难与共让我意识到了自己之前玩这个游戏时的想法是多么错误，我前面都是一路朝着打败最终boss前进，却忽略了周围的人和事，最后的结局是神州旅人，这个结局其实我已经比较满意了。
第三周目结局时已经是凌晨四点了，但心还是静不下来，上床后刷视频时刷到了子夜寄君书，看完视频后联系着好结局，刷着视频哭了半个小时，一直睡不着，明明知道我已经打出云裳的好结局了，但心里还是难受，第一第二周目云裳结局估计很不好（我超级喜欢云裳，其他线的女主有点不想推了，感觉对不起云裳）到七点才迷糊了。
第四周目是就是为了补完西武林线结局，想看看最好的那个结局，最后也是如愿和云裳一起携手游江南，打完这个结局后，我愣了很久才意识到我是我，不是赵活，那种茫然感和错位感一直到第二天才消失，但到我发这篇评测时，我依旧有种不真实感，感觉这似乎是我的故事，但又不是我的故事。
我之前看其他小说时，每到结局就会特别难受，我还想了解他们之后的故事，不愿它就在这里划上句号，这篇故事依旧如此，我还想知道云裳和赵活在江南做了什么，云裳又做出什么闹心事让赵活给她擦屁股，“此生不得消停，到老圆满无憾”。但我知道这不太可能了，他们的故事已经结束了。
音乐方面更是顶中顶，我之前刚进游戏时听到主界面的曲子时只是感觉很清新，很悠远，但我知道这首曲子的内涵，知道名字是子夜寄君书后，我才真正听懂了曲子中的悲伤和淡淡遗憾。帐中梦守人我也很喜欢，听到后配上云裳在幽泉说的那些话，以及结缘时的对话，我总是想要哭出来。当云裳在锦香宫弹出变调后，我更是喜欢上了这首，它一扫原曲的哀愁和凄凉，反而是带给了我无比活泼和温馨的感觉，云裳得救后那种活泼感、对生的眷恋、对爱人的爱意一下子就体现了出来，和之前云裳的活泼调皮是截然相反的。
之前云裳的那种调皮总是带着淡淡的哀愁，大家都知道这个命不久矣的少女是在用这种方式留下自己在这个世上，在所有她在乎，在乎她的人的心中的最后的影子，后来的混世魔王叶云裳调皮过了头，但谁让她有一个能够宠她到老，爱她一辈子的好哥哥呢，历经千辛万苦，死了无数次，许多个be，才终于换来一个可以和心上人终生厮守，一辈子永不分离的美好结局，这就是偕老誓啊，无论经历过多少次风吹雨打，多少次痛苦挫折，我依旧在那个我做出同生共死，永不分离的承诺的地方等你。
非常感谢鸟熊带给我的这种体验，但这游戏的剧情分支实在是太复杂，能不能做一个枝状图来方便玩家来看到更多结局啊，在此提前谢谢啦。

The Cabin Factory is a spot-the-anomaly horror game set in a factory manufacturing spooky cabins for amusement parks and movie sets. However, due to a spate of reports that the cabins are actually haunted, the cabin factory has hired you to inspect each cabin, check whether it's haunted, and if it is haunted, run away before whatever poltergeist inhabiting it can catch you. 

It is absolutely terrifying, and I loved it. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3596647612

There is only one criteria for determining if a cabin is haunted. If something moves, the cabin is haunted. If nothing moves, the cabin is safe, however creepy it might be. Each cabin's layout is identical - even if its furnishings are not - forming a weird familiarity to the process of moving through the space. I could step in, sweep through my regular steps, checking whether the familiar things were moving, and then get caught up by something new. At multiple points, I found myself swaying from side to side, trying to decide if a painting's head was moving, or if it was just an optical illusion from the eyes. At other points, an object I'd dismissed as harmless started moving behind me. At still others, movement I'd thought was harmless would turn into something chasing me as I crashed helter-skelter into walls, doors, and furniture, trying to escape. The constant shifting of a nominally familiar space makes the game a deeply unnerving experience. Even in a mundane, safe cabin, the lack of true security leaves the heart pounding and the tension thick. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3596647815

Undergirding it all is the story of the cabin and the people inside it. While the cabins you are inspecting are recreations, they are recreations of an actual cabin. While the story itself is fairly basic horror fare, that there is a developing story and that the various people scattered around the house are trying to recreate it in their own, tormented way adds more to the experience than I would have believed was possible. I wasn't invested in their story, per se, but that these were more than wax figures made the cabin spookier. This is a game with a clear atmosphere and which lives and dies on its atmosphere, and oh, it lives. 

The Cabin Factory could well be one of the best horror games I've played in a while. It's short, understands what it is and how to make the most of its space, and doesn't overstay its welcome. It thrives in its simplicity, and leaves the player rattled.

[h3]💎 Всем доброго времени суток, в долине рудников Хориниса!
⠀⠀⠀⠀На связи — [url=steamcommunity.com/id/2o77x] [b]ム karhad[/b] [/url][/h3]

Сегодня расскажу о Gothic 1 — игре, с которой у многих началась любовь к «настоящим» ролевкам. Без лишних слов и пафоса — [b] только мрачный реализм, суровый юмор и невероятная атмосфера. [/b] Если вы слышали, что Gothic — это “игра с душой”, но не понимали, о чём речь, — сейчас разберёмся.

 [h3]⚔️ Под барьером: мир, где каждый шаг имеет цену [/h3]

Gothic 1 — экшен-RPG от немецкой студии Piranha Bytes, вышедшая в 2001 году. Действие происходит в долине рудников — [u] тюрьме под открытым небом, где преступников окружает магический барьер. [/u] Из этой западни не выбраться: внутри царит хаос, а власть поделена между тремя лагерями — Старым, Новым и Братством. Главный герой — безымянный заключённый, который должен выжить, обрести союзников и повлиять на судьбу всего мира.

На первый взгляд это классика старой школы: диалоги, фракции, нелинейные квесты, непростые схватки. [b] Но фишка Gothic — в ощущении живого мира. [/b] NPC не стоят на месте — они работают, едят, спят, реагируют на твои действия. [i] Мир не ждёт тебя — он живёт сам по себе. [/i] Это делает исследование невероятно захватывающим: ты действительно чувствуешь себя частью чего-то реального, пусть и грубого.

Боевая система проста, но требует точности. Здесь не получится “заспамить” удары — придётся учиться таймингу и внимательности. [u] Игра не стесняется быть сложной: нет маркеров, туториалов и подсказок. [/u] Тебе просто бросают фразу вроде “иди на север от ворот” — и вперёд, сам ищи дорогу. И в этом — её величайший шарм.

 [h3]💡 После сотен часов и перепрохождений [/h3]

Я возвращался к Gothic 1 не один раз. [i] Каждый новый заход — другое приключение. [/i] Вступаешь в другую фракцию — и мир уже реагирует иначе. Старые друзья становятся врагами, новые лица открываются с неожиданной стороны. [b] Эта реиграбельность и есть душа Gothic. [/b] Она не в “разветвлённых концовках”, а в том, как всё вокруг меняется в ответ на твои поступки.

Мир игры ощущается целостным, логичным и реалистичным. Даже спустя 20 лет он не разваливается, потому что создан с уважением к игроку. [u] Здесь нет чувства, что всё крутится вокруг тебя. [/u] Ты просто один из множества — и если хочешь выжить, придётся заслужить уважение. Это создаёт сильное ощущение погружения, особенно когда понимаешь, что каждый диалог, каждое действие имеет последствия.

Переигрывая Gothic, замечаешь, насколько он честен. Он не льстит, не даёт лишних наград, не делает скидок. Здесь можно проиграть из-за самоуверенности — и это нормально. [i] Мир не обязан быть справедливым, но он честен в своей логике. [/i] Именно за это фанаты до сих пор возвращаются в игру.

[h3]✨ Почему Gothic остаётся особенной и вызывает уважение [/h3]

• [b] Атмосфера [/b] — густая, мрачная тяжёлая, но невероятно достоверная и любимая, именно атмосфера заставляет заходить в игру снова и снова.
• [b] Свобода выбора [/b] — без искусственных “моральных шкал”, всё зависит от поступков и поведения с жителями колонии.
• [b] Живой мир [/b] — NPC живут, работают и реагируют на изменения, монстры патрулируют свои окрестности, а ключевые персонажи могут легко поменять о тебе мнение.
• [b] Сложность с характером [/b] — ошибки не прощаются, но и победы чувствуются по-настоящему.
• [b] Диалоги с личностью [/b] — ироничные, прямолинейные, порой даже философские. + отличная и душевная озвучка ГГ от Сергея Чорнишвили и других актёров озвучки студии Snowball Interactive. 
• [b] Музыка Кая Розенкранца [/b] — один из лучших саундтреков в RPG всех времен. Очень рад, что он будет создавать музыку для Ремейка игры(подробнее распишу в конце).
• [b] Фракции с историей [/b] — у каждого лагеря есть свои мотивы, система званий, обмундирование, логика и идеология.
• [b] Настоящая реиграбельность [/b] — не через концовки, а через опыт, который ты создаёшь для себя сам.

 [h3]💀 Слабые стороны(в основном для новичков) [/h3]

• [u] Управление [/u] — первое испытание любого новичка. С непривычки кажется неудобным, но к нему привыкаешь.
• [u] Графика [/u] — устарела, даже с патчами выглядит угловато, но дух игры перевешивает визуальные минусы.
• [u] Интерфейс [/u] — громоздкий и неочевидный; первые часы — борьба не с монстрами, а с меню.
• [u] Баги и скрипты [/u] — иногда квест может “застрять”, хотя фанатские патчи решают многое.
• [u] Темп [/u] — медленный старт, но после вживания становится естественным.

 [h3]⭐ Итог [/h3]

Gothic 1 — не просто игра, а проверка характера. Она заставляет думать, учиться и уважать игровой мир, а не ждать, что он будет тебя спасать. [b] Это игра для тех, кто устал от блестящих, но пустых RPG. [/b] Да, она старомодная, но зато настоящая.

⭐ [i] 9/10 — “Мир, который живёт без тебя, но ради таких, как ты.” [/i]

Если вы готовы к сложному началу и хотите почувствовать, каково это — быть частью по-настоящему живой истории, Gothic 1 подарит вам одно из самых запоминающихся приключений в жанре.

 [h3]🧭 Что попробовать после основного прохождения [/h3]

Если захотите продлить удовольствие — обязательно обратите внимание на фанатские модификации:
• [b] L’Hiver Edition [/b] — улучшает графику, баланс и добавляет новые детали мира.
• [b] Gothic 1: Returning [/b] — глубоко перерабатывает сюжет, добавляет квесты и персонажей.
• [b] The Story of Myrtana (История Миртаны) [/b] — масштабная модификация, фактически новая RPG во вселенной Gothic, созданная фанатами.

 [h3]🛠️ Взгляд в будущее — Gothic 1 Remake [/h3]

Сегодня над официальным ремейком Gothic работает студия Alkimia Interactive под крылом THQ Nordic. После выхода тестового демо фанаты активно делились обратной связью, и разработчики пообещали сохранить дух оригинала: ту же мрачность, иронию и хрупкий баланс между реализмом и фэнтези. [i] По свежим данным, ремейк идёт по пути “идейного переосмысления”, а не механического копирования. [/i] Это вселяет надежду: ведь главное — сохранить ту самую «душу Колонии», а не просто улучшить текстуры.

Игроки по всему миру, особенно старые готоманы, ждут ремейк с осторожным оптимизмом. Мы надеемся, что Alkimia Interactive сумеет не только воссоздать атмосферу, но и сделать её доступной для нового поколения.

Best-in-class city sim management game. I'm city game obsessive, from the days of Sim City 2000 to Cities Skylines and Manor Lords, I try them all and stick with the best ones. Farthest Frontier brings the goods. It's highly engaging, challenges you with raiders and wildlife as you develop your new city. The customization is excellent, from screen resolutions to UI scaling and optimization sliders to help the game perform best on your system. I LOVE UI scaling because it allows you to play on a TV from a few feet away. The game runs pretty smoothly at 5x speed on an RTX 4080 Super at 1080p, but definitely gets bogged down once you reach ~500 people or are on a large map with a few hundred citizens. I tend to play new cities rather than enduring at Tier IV so this hasn't been a huge problem, but it's worth noting. I also wish the game had a 12x speed like Manor Lords because I prefer to speed build cities and try different scenarios to see what works best and even at 5x, progress can be a little slow at times.

Raiders are my favorite part of this game. They scale up based on the size of your city, starting with 4-6 raiders causing trouble up to 100+ raiders with barricade busting forces laying waste to homes, markets and storage areas. I have played with raiders and wildlife set to maximum aggression because it keeps the game interesting between build outs. The looming threats force you to be mindful of city size and grid development, ensuring optimal routes are the focus of the game to avoid losing villagers.

In early access, the game was easier to play as a beginner because the upgrade tree was based on the base command center level (e.g., unlock specific buildings at Tier II, Tier III etc.) Shortly before launch, they added a tech tree which is massive and not super well organized. The UI scaling also doesn't seem to apply to the tech tree so you need to play at a lower resolution (1080p) on a 4K display in order to see what the different options are without squinting (again, from a few feet away.) I appreicate Manor Lords for their grouping of tech tree components. That all said, I have adapted to the tech tree and they have done a nice job of making it a choose-your-adventure style gameplay by allowing you to put knowledge points into what matters most to you, like mining over defenses. Once you have ~40 points in the tech tree, it becomes considerably harder to earn knowledge so you have to choose carefully because overinvesting in other areas can lead to a less fulfilling end game because knowledge point development speed ups were not prioritized early enough.

Improvements could be made to the way resources are populated on the map. If you choose a Medium size map, the resources are all much closer together and then quite spread out if you choose a Large map. It would be better (IMO) to keep the resource density of the Medium maps and just increase the amount of resources on the Large map. You have to travel great distances and it can take forever even on cobble road so it makes the Large map less enjoyable as a whole when resources are few and far between. Additionally, the game REQUIRES clay to develop the school, healer's house and other key game achievements to keep progressing. Unfortunately, there is no guarantee that clay will be on the map, so it forces you to add a Trading Post sooner in order to develop those buildings. I suspect this is due to some older decisions, when a Tier II Command Center made mining for clay and sand available. This is no longer default, and you have to unlock mining in the tech tree, even if you get the Tier II Command Center. This hiccup causes pain in the early development of your city and I can appreciate that clay may not appear on every map, but sand does and if one does, why not the other? Especially since you don't actually NEED sand to develop infrastructure in the same way that you do clay.

There are some UI issues that I experienced at 1920 x 1080, namely the confirmation screen (e.g., Do you want to delete this?) is off-screen and impossible to bring back into the game window. There was also some initial confusion around how to manage policies. I can access them by using the 'J' hotkey but outside of that, how do I access policies? It was very confusing until I figured out the right key to press and I don't see an on-screen element to click that brings up the policies screen.

In conclusion, I think you have to be someone who enjoys challenges if you want to excel at this game and I am, so I do. :) There is a "Pacifist Mode" that removes raiders and it took away the most enjoyable change agent in the game so I don't use it, but it may be of interest to others. You still have to survive so it's not exactly a sandbox free-for-all if you choose that mode.

I also want to commend the developers on an incredible feat. I have played Banished, Manor Lords, Town to City, Foundation, Cities Skylines I & II, all the Sim Cities, Two Point Hospital, Tropico etc. This game is the best out of all of them, by far. Farthest Frontier lets you get into the nitty gritty and manage hundreds of citizens at scale. It is glorious and pretty well balanced. I wish there were more decoration options, but you can build a nice city/base with the handful of existing options. Highly recommended, it's the best city builder of 2025, hands down.

It’s an okay city-builder, but it really doesn’t feel like a finished product. Steam "really" need an "okay" than just yes and no.

That’s the main reason is there is a lot of negatives, not because it’s bad, but because there are better and more complete options available right now. Most of the issues could be fixed later, but at release, it’s rough.

A lot of basic features are still missing or inconsistent. Windowed mode and “play in background” don’t work properly and sometimes just disappear from the settings menu, in a game with a lot of idle waiting, that matters. There are also no resolution settings at all, which feels bizarre in 2025.

The recent tech/upgrade rework also didn’t improve much. Most research choices fall into one of three categories:

* Pick the obvious gathering/crafting upgrade
* Avoid the pointless upgrade
* Unlock the next building that really should just have been tied to the Town Hall upgrade

There’s no real specialization, the system mostly just slows you down.

Some buildings feel like they are in the wrong tier entirely. The Healer’s Hut, for example, should be a basic early-game building (we’re talking herbal medicine here), but it’s stuck in a tier that makes early game unnecessarily punishing. On higher difficulty, one random wolf far away from its den can mean a villager bleeds out, because the healer is locked behind too many steps, no one can do anything.

The pacing is also strange. The game starts fast, then collapses into a very slow phase where gold income is weak, most buildings cost 100+ gold, and you basically wait. (Yes, you can bypass the gold problem by placing the smallest possible field just to unlock the Apiary and print honey → gold, but that feels like exploiting the design, not playing it. And you still not big enough village to make an decent production line)

Then when the production line is up and the children finaly grow up, you suddenly swim in gold and villagers, and the entire pace flips into a rush toward endgame. A lot of time feels like AFK idle, followed by instant acceleration from T2 and straight to T4.

Combat is also undercooked. You’re suggested to build walls early on, but they’re too expensive for that stage, so it’s more efficient to just rally the entire population and swarm attackers. There’s also no cheap early melee weapon like a wooden spear , you get bows early, but units still prefer melee unless they archer/hunter (you can "game this" by having a lot of hunter hunts that you fill up during an raid to get cheap non-gold archers). Metal production also comes in late in T2, which makes early defense feel clumsy and inconsistent. An "milita with spear" from the townhall where they just grab an stick would help a lot.

On harder map settings, the “challenge” often becomes staring at the trade screen more, especially when important resources like clay are missing and you end up trading honey for clay for half the game to you get out of the early production and decent production lines.

Overall:
If you push through the rough parts, it can be a decent city-builder. The atmosphere is good, the core loop is satisfying enough, and there’s potential here. But it is absolutely not finished, not well-balanced, and not well-tuned for pacing or play flow. If you’re okay with that, you may still enjoy it. If you want a polished city-builder right now, there are better choices.
