My original review for Tunic was positive, but I've decided that I shouldn't just say what I feel like I'm "supposed" to say about the game. This is MY review and I'm going to leave MY opinions.

[b] THIS IS A DARK SOULS GAME IN ZELDA DRAG [/b]. The Steam tags are not there to be pedantic. This is not a game like Cuphead or the N. Sane Trilogy where people used "like Dark Souls" as a synonym for "difficult." This [i] is [/i] a soulslike. The combat is Dark Souls, the going to where you previously died to pick up your stuff is Dark Souls, the stupid flasks that take four seconds to heal you is Dark Souls. If you love Dark Souls, great! I hate soulslikes. But as someone who loves Zelda games like a Link to the Past and was hoping for something like that, playing this game made me feel like I'd been tricked out of playing the game I actually paid for. This is made worse by the fact that whenever I asked people who recommended me the game what it was about, they'd always go "teehee, that's a spoiler!" Bug off.

The game is also obtuse by design. If you hate that feeling of "where do I go? what do I do? I feel underleveled for this area..." in Metroidvanias, avoid this game like the plague. Tunic [i] never [/i] stops to give you any kind of direction, and after you get your sword the invisible hand guiding you forward all but vanishes. You're supposed to piece everything together by finding pieces of the game's manual as collectibles on the map, and it (and all the ingame text) is written in runes. You [i] can [/i] piece some of it together through visuals, but you still need to find the appopriate pages for what you need. Even with the pages, I still couldn't figure out what to do half the time. There's a level up system, but how am I supposed to activate it? Apparently there's a piece of the manual hidden in the far corner of the map that explains it, but I can only imagine how helpful it does so when it can only do it in runes.

Overall I feel like this game is made for millenials wishing to relive the very specific experience of playing Zelda (or a similarly open game) before they could read, or playing a foreign game written entirely in another language, complete with Dark Souls type gameplay to "modernize" it. Neat concept, but I can't relate to the experience at all. Rather than immersed, the whole time I felt frustrated.

Something you should take note is that this game WILL kick your butt on your first few runs, and you will constantly be on edge as you'll never truly feel safe at any given moment. The game was intentionally designed to be vague and let players figure out how things are done for themselves. (For the most part, anyway.) Though this can either be a good or a bad thing depending on who you ask. Myself, I'd say I'm somewhere down the middle. While I appreciate the game not shoving tutorials in my face, it can lead to some parts being confusing and you're always second guessing whether you're doing something right or not. If you truly want to optimize everything you do, a wiki is practically a requirement.

Still, I admire the balls Klei had when they stuck to their guns and designed the game they way they did even if it might drive certain players away. That's not something you usually see from a lot of games nowadays. Sacrificing universal appeal for the sake of keeping the game cohesive.

If you haven't already, pick this game up. The lack of direction at the start my be daunting for newcomers, but once you get the hang of how the game works, it's satisfying as hell.

神。硬控我四个月成为我steam库里的Phantom了。文本大量管饱，we need Chinese但是我仍然强烈建议所有英文水平还可以的玩家体验英语原文，许多段落简直是艺术品的级别。作为一款键政模拟器，我觉得它最优秀的地方首先在于体现了一条真理，那就是在政治中永远应该是原则服从于实践而非实践必须为原则让步——我看见过太多由于违背了这条准则而遭到惨败的playthrough，and they deserved that defeat。很多事件，[spoiler] 无论是公事国事还是个人感情， [/spoiler]都无法有一个十全十美的结局——打的时候有时会感觉很煎熬很不敢迎接明日，但转念一想又有一种果然这才是生活啊的感觉。

想要重点夸赞suzerain的人物形象，我没买dlc所以就只就本体的来说一下。文案的笔力特别到位，序章寥寥勾勒三句话我直接做了[spoiler] 塔金·索尔 [/spoiler]四个月的深柜和狗，[spoiler] 唉索尔总统我们骄盛夺目的太阳啊，即使在我最喜欢的改革派路线中我的心里也永远有一座您的神龛 [/spoiler]彼得·维克顿和卢锡安·加拉德这俩活宝的化学反应特别有意思，他们各自也都是很有魅力的形象，玩到中局后我被他们牵动了许多心神[spoiler] 兄弟我爱你兄弟抱一下但是兄弟你怎么能做出那样的事？！彼得·维克顿写得真的如同艺术，燃尽、物质滥用、忠诚又过度奉献，微笑的铁假面下或许是长期的压力、抑郁和绝望——一定能够在有相似经历的人身上引发超强的共鸣。卢锡安或许是一位更典型的政治家，但正因如此他偶尔在冷静理性的表象之外露出冒进、野心和个人感情时才会现得如此intriguing。 [/spoiler]内阁的各位同僚们！你们的政治光谱超级多样、特别美丽，而且无论如何每一个人[spoiler] （是的，我知道你们中间颇有几个混蛋！） [/spoiler]至少都是才干过人，[spoiler] 给部门发钱真干活，[/spoiler]我爱死你们每一个人了，下一个四年咱们还要并肩同行好吗？出乎意料地，打过多周目尤其是多个结局后，越发令我叹服的居然是主角哥安东雷恩[spoiler] ——bro以45岁低龄当上索德兰总统，从做议员开始就屡创政坛年龄新低，这批真干活的阁臣包括彼得和卢锡安在内每个人都在自己最合适的位置上，可见其政治素养强如怪物。另外他肯定也有自己的骄傲——这个入疑似在面对索尔及其激推时很容易破防，而且也没有考虑过在不受欢迎的情况下下台。某种程度上，他和索尔真的有些互为半身的意味。不过最吸引我的地方在于安东雷恩真的是一个人味儿特别重的人，这样作为玩家的我们真的能意识到做一个政治家对一个*人*来说意味着什么——他感情丰富、常常自省；当选了就骄傲自豪，听到司机叫他总统先生就不由得微笑；有美酒好烟漂亮饭会美美享用，提到肥皂剧就想爽看；讨厌军队就讨厌了几十年，看见议员遗孤就悲伤得忘不了她们的眼睛。他能想到那个被所有人都认为是没有骨头的前司法部长一定也有自己的理由和难处；伦堡犯了战争罪对面都先拿枪指着他了，他还能惦记“这小伙子不比我儿子年纪更大”和“他们也是被不公正地要求为自己的国家去死”。打的周目多了以后我对安东雷恩几乎产生了一种尊敬，因为在诡异而艰难的时代里保持一颗柔软的心是一种非凡的勇气——如果我是索德兰的选民的话我大约真的会给安东雷恩投票的，不为了成就或者什么特别的观念之类，而是因为觉得如果是他的话，大约不会特别轻易地把谁当作可以牺牲的代价。至少对于我来说，作为主角哥的安东·雷恩也能有自己的倾向和坚持，实在是太好了。 [/spoiler]

好游戏。道理讲得清楚，故事合乎情理，感情细腻动人。我在里面除了胃痛的两难决定以外受的最大的苦是索德兰共和国那个抽象的破经济，但是转念一想现实中的经济建设也是如此抽象、诡异、困难和环环相扣，又感觉有点释然，毕竟我又不是个真的经济学家，而且打出synergy后发现其实设计确实是合理的。新玩家不想坐牢的话可以去贴吧找一下经济攻略——至少本体的攻略现在已经相当完备了；当然，如果你一定想尝试一下初心会把自己带到哪里，我对你的勇气表达深切的敬意，真的。

Severed Steel — шедевр инди-экшена, где отсутствие руки компенсируется избытком стволов.
Сюжет? Просыпаешься на свалке, без руки, но с жаждой мести. Вокруг — армия солдат, которые уверены, что ты — мусор. Их ошибка. Твоя задача — проложить путь к свободе через волны врагов, попутно выясняя, кто и зачем превратил тебя в живое оружие.
Геймплей — поэзия хаоса: [list]
[*]Движение — твоё главное оружие: бег по стенам, скольжение под пулями, сальто в прыжке. Здесь не стреляют — танцуют со смертью.
[*]Замедление времени дарит те секунды, чтобы прицелить выстрел в прыжке или уйти от ракеты. Чувствуешь себя богом рейва в мире, где пули — это ритм.
[*]Одна рука — не недостаток, а фича. Подобрал ствол — два выстрела, выбросил — взял новый. Арсенал от пистолетов до дробовиков, чья отдача подбрасывает в воздух, превращая перезарядку в рудимент игровой индустрии.
[*]Та самая пушка — «щёлк» и враг стал облаком красной пыли. Элегантно и без уборки.
[*]Враги — от пушечного мяса до ниндзя-невидимок и бронированных огнемётчиков.
[*]Саундтрек — электронный адреналин, вгоняющий в транс. После пары треков сам веришь, что вышел из мусорного контейнера ради мести.
[/list]
Что режет сталь, но не впечатление: [list]
[*]Достижения с требованием 30 S-рангов — тест на терпение, а не на мастерство.
[*]Герой молчит — возможно, потому, что слова бессильны перед таким геймплеем.
[/list]
Итог: Идеальный вечерний релакс: заменить пиво и дота-крипов на сальто под электронную музыку и дезинтеграцию солдат. Игра, где каждая секунда — вызов, а каждая победа — спектакль. Если ты искал игру, которая заставляет чувствовать себя живым — она перед тобой.

- All those laboratories are boring too. You just have to take 150 random ingredients with you and play two mini-games 30 times (depending on which branch you are researching, they are different)...
- Lack of self-sufficiency in the endgame. Do you want to focus only on running a restaurant from morning to night? You can't, because you have to go on a tour of the shops anyway, even though you can order from them, you still have to buy some ingredients directly from them 
- Of course, the RNG is so messed up that you may not have a certain ingredient you need in the store for 3-4 days because it won't be randomly selected. So cooking boils down to “whatever is in the fridge.”
- Winter is so damn boring and uninteresting that I just slept through half of it because there were no ingredients in the stores and I couldn't collect them myself - because it's winter and nothing grows (which is logical, of course).

And so... I could go on and on. But at the moment, the game isn't developed enough – it's in EA, so that's understandable. But maybe instead of focusing on what else can be borrowed from Stardew Valley (dating, farming, mining, hunting, housing,  pets, etc.), the team focused on how to improve and make the main features of the game more attractive – cooking and running a restaurant, perhaps?

I would not recommend this game at full price at all. However, with a Steam sale I would. Like others I purchased this game for $5 and I got my money's worth, unfortunately my ADD Husband disagrees and would not recommend this game even on sale. The main reason is lack of meaningful progression, this game can stagnate immediately if you figure it out quickly.

Building is the main reason to enjoy this game and the reason I play it, more building options would be amazing. The animals are adorable and I love to collect them all, although at this point only one animal is necessary for money making. 
My Husband has no interest in building and this game provides little more once he experienced it once. Farming makes little money but it expensive to set up and is a waste of time. I love farming in games so this was sad for me, there is also almost no uses for crops except to sell them so this makes it even worse. 

The world is empty and all the shops are far away from each other and most of them are boring (you cannot even enter the gas station). There is only one quest that allows the player to unlock a new item and I loved that, wish more quests had this feature. Maybe even locking some animals behind quests to make the town feel like it is growing with you. There is one high paying collection quest where it felt impossible to find the items without a guide but I did not hate it as it was at least unique. There are other side quests that can reoccur but they pay little and add little to the game. But I am glad they exist as it is the only thing connecting you to the town besides the shops.

There needs to be more do at low income and more to do late game when you have money. I felt like once I had money I spent it on horses and I was so excited to get a horse only for it to not be useful. I would love for horses to be able to pull items so I can take a horse to town instead of a vehicle, or at least a saddle bag so I can ride the horse to town to get one bag of food, just literally anything.

This games has lots of glitches it needs to work out. Expensive animals like my horses would die of starvation or dehydration even right next to food. Plants in a greenhouse (which had no buffs or improvements for the crops growing within for some reason) would occasionally show that it did not have water even if it was surrounded by sprinklers. Items to build would show as incomplete even if we gave it everything it needed to be complete. Driving is kinda annoying especially when pulling trailers. It was hard to connect in multiplayer but once joined it was fine.

Overall I had fun discovering things in this game, but its long term retention is low especially if building is not of any interest. I have put some hours into this game because I wanted to build and own every animal in this game, if you are like my Husband and you just want to make money in the most effective way this game is extremely short.

I just started this game 3 or 4 days ago and I must say I'm very impressed. It's great to see a different spin on the automation genre. I bought it during the Autumn sale and sat on it a little bit. Read a handful of reviews talking about building and belt placement being a pain. I have not experienced this at all. The building has been super easy and satisfying, both the production chains and the decorative/QoL fun stuff. I played Satisfactory starting on EA update 1. You want a game that was a pain in the ass to build in, that was it. This game, being only on EA update 2.2, is leaps and bounds ahead of that. Even without blueprints and trains this game is very fun and easy to play for hours on end. Automation is my favorite genre by far and I love seeing new things coming along. The voxel system brings a great experience that has been tried before and wasn't very successful. The galactic market is a fun addition, as is the requirement to buy items to use on the planet to progress. 

All in all I strongly recommend this game even at this early stage. I think the price is right for the amount of hours already available and it's only going to get better. Paradox being the publisher gives me enough confidence that this game will see 1.0 and beyond. Although I'm a little worried about their DLC tactics tbh. But there is potential there too. 

If you are on the fence, I say do it. If you love the genre this scratches the itch very well and adds the ability to terraform your heart out and make some truly amazing factories!

Overall rating: 7/10

This game scratches that factory building, logic scaling itch. It's a slightly less polished version of Satisfactory, but there are lot of mechanics I enjoy a lot more. The guide throughout the game is pretty good and helps steer you towards major objectives.

Thing I'd like to see over time:
Expanding the Galactic Market/Competition features. The trading/economy idea is fantastic and has huge potential if they introduce more complexity, but more importantly, competition. They have the rankings listed, but there's no real competition. Just the perception of it.

Physics! Making floating platforms is cool, but physics on buildings would be cooler.

Some kind of threat to deal with. Whether its economic threat/competition via the Galactic Market, or its another corporation trying to take over your planet's resources. This game has no sense of threat and therefore you don't have to consider layout as much.

Interplanetary travel. The size of the galaxy map is massive, but we can only use one planet for resources? Feels like a missed opportunity. I would even take a page from games like Factorio and have some resources only available on the other planets. Also another opportunity for threats (environmental)

A blueprint feature like the mod Duplicationer is a MUST. I don't think I would play this game without it. This game is all about scaling your economy. If I have to place down every single machine 1000 times to scale, it's not really fun, nor realistic.

There is no incentive at endgame to keep playing. I appreciate the progression and it feels smooth. But once you start shipping robots you end up saying "uh... now what?"

The ability to build/delete platforms and pipes larger than like 32 spaces... very limiting and tedious on a game that's spread out super far. Also doesn't lend itself to building at scale.

The game has enormous potential, but is badly held back by enemy/player fleet AI and other underlying systems. I really want to love this game, and feel strange leaving a negative review after so much time played, but hopefully it saves others a similar realization after already getting invested.

The cracks first started to show when I began to command a fleet rather than playing as a single ship. Want to issue a command to your squad of interceptors to prevent them from chasing an enemy ship too deep into enemy territory? That move command will be queued to the end of each ship's action list, meaning you have to manually clear the default intercept action if you want it to be followed. That behavior single-handedly prevents any RTS-style micromanagement, despite X4 being branded as playable like an RTS.

The real nail in the coffin for me though was realizing just how bad the enemy and player fleet AI actually is. Xenon destroyers are seemingly unstoppable killing machines when you first face them, even mowing through fleets of 20-40 ships with ease, but it's ok, because all you need to do is just hang back and wait. Eventually they'll fly head first into a base's guns, suiciding without a single shot fired. The same can be said for other factions - they're all just haphazardly throwing ships at each other in a piecemeal fashion. Occasionally a scripted event gives a brief illusion of something more tangible forming, but it quickly devolves back into the same nonsensical behavior, with cohesive fleets fanning out and suiciding into various structures, destroyers, etc rather than keeping formation and attacking viable targets at their optimal range.

The simulation itself really is such an impressive feat that you've got such a large world that can be played locally at such significant scale. It's just too bad that it quickly turns out to be all window dressing with very little depth due to the complete lack of functional AI. In my book, that single-handedly takes x4 from being a game, down to just being an impressive simulation.

I really want to recommend this game and like it more than I already do but there's just some issues it has that has yet to be fixed and really should. A good example are the companions you can find, which are these upgrades that follow you around, but they don't seem to do anything at all. The drunkleton is this dude who is supposed to collect bottles for you (the currency of this game) yet even if you have like 5 of them none of them will do anything. Companions float around and just kinda get stuck in ceiling corners and do nothing else. 

This game has all sorts of other bugs and problems that can ruin the game at anytime. Sometimes the game will just flat out freeze and you just gotta give it anywhere between 1-5 minutes because it'll sort itself out or you'll just have to force it to close if it never fixes itself. I've seen reports of the host generating a completely different level to what other players are seeing. Sometimes your left click or right click just won't work and the fix is to change active items and then change back and do it again, makes it really annoying when you're trying to drop a mine while getting chased and your window of opportunity is getting smaller. If this game didn't have these issues and was more polished and consistent then I would be more willing to recommend it for full price but until then try to grab this game on a sale.

What it does have going for it, though, is stuff I actually really enjoy. The game doesn't give you much to work with but with a little experimentation and creativity you'll start to learn that this game does not put an emphasis on combat but puts a massive emphasis on having the right tool for the right job. There are some melee weapons in the game made to be used for damage, but otherwise most of what you'll find will be tools and each tool has their intended use. A wrench is used to both repair Kletka as well as disarming traps. This makes it where it's far more effective to use said wrench to disarm a mine and use the mine to throw at an enemy. Rakes are good at clearing up slime and breaking down dead bodies, so you'll want to save them for those types of tasks, etc. This game gives you a reason to hold onto things like fire extinguishers, or having a pickaxe or two on standby when you eventually get a fleshmines map, and so on. 

This game has a charm to it and if it had more content, and especially more polish, then I could see it really taking off. Passives are far and few between, companions are broken in a bad way, and dying way too fast can really turn a lot of people away. If you can look past all that though this game really does feel like a gem. I just like running around, collecting resources, and taking care of my horrifying bio-mechanical elevator while I try not to die.

It's hard to put into words where exactly this game lies in terms of overall genre. You can easily call it an RPG and be on your way, or you could throw on 20 more tags of types and still be just as accurate, but both instances would be selling this game short of what it is and both are equally...insulting(?) in their own way.

Where the difficulty comes in labeling this game, describing it is not. This game is fun. Nothing else to say here because nothing else quite describes it well enough beyond that. It's just fun. Sure, there's some wishes and wants, some balancing and polishing, but for a single dev creating this entire game on their own, it's massively impressive and my biggest fear is that some game company snatches this talented individual up for a big pile of money and this game never sees completion. I'll say as a person burned more than a few times by EA games, this game being in EA for 2+ years now always has me nervous, but there's always something on the horizon content wise and they always deliver.

What makes this game so enjoyable is love of the craft. There's nothing 'randomly generated' in this game. This dev has (assumedly) made everything in it themselves. Placed every tree, flower, and fence post. In the era of procedural generation, it's a rare sight and to see it so lovingly done is a real treat. No, the graphics aren't groundbreaking but if you've read any of my reviews prior to this you'll know that it doesn't matter to me, and it shouldn't to you either. The graphics are part of this game's charm and if nothing else (more on that in a moment) they add to it with all the other stuff to do in this game. Not to snub procedural generation, there are areas on the map, such as 'hotspots' that appear nearly so, so the game maintains a slight air of 'randomness' to make the world interesting if you decide to park it somewhere to do something for a moment. Very well done, and subtly so.

Now for the meat and potatoes - the mechanics. This dev clearly is out to make a fun game before they make some groundbreaking story of an RPG. My ghasts would be utterly flabbered if I looked at their gaming history/library and movie collection didn't find a fantastic mix of fun genre classics like Streets of Rage, Smash Bros, Mario Party, and Skyrim, with a theatre of cult films like Matrix, Die Hard, Enter the Dragon and 300. This game nods to them all in very fun ways and I haven't played a game in a while where I did something and laughed out loud at the result. No spoilers, but there's nothing like building yourself to be a Hoplite and 300 kicking someone into next week, or shield smashing someone 'into the air' only for that phrase to actually mean 'into orbit'. 

The skills and talents all have something fun and useful. Some more than others, of course, but I haven't found one I didn't enjoy yet so much as 'didn't use as much as something else' instead. Which is a very good problem to have in a game, especially in the other more annoying era of gaming that is 'tiering'. Talents aren't permanent yet, so it allows you to enjoy everything and swap skills on a dime if you want to try something new. Can't say I'd enjoy that long term on a final release but for EA I'm super happy to experiment and bug report. 

The regions and environments are all superbly crafted and all have their own fun, unique 'thing' about them with nice little quests to do in each from surrounding npc villages and cities, each with their own factions and reputation. Think Skyrim, but simpler, and you definitely won't get your arms chopped off if you accidentally snag a potion out of a shop in front of the owner, you just may need to work back that guy's trust.

The mobs are fun, goblins tend to be everywhere and every time I thought I'd seen them all, some new kind of goblin shows up and makes me giggle (umm jetpack goblins are something I didn't know I needed). Still, they're nothing to truly brush off, my character is level 16 now and I still don't really know how to deal with boar riders, they scare the shit out of me.

For a constant work in progress, I'm thrilled and in awe at the amount of content already in this game, and seeing more coming all the time I find myself always excited to see this game pop up in my news feed about something. Yeah, there's things I'd like to see addressed because there's a lot of things you get notified about in the game that you actually can't do yet (talent points for tradeskills, for example) but the game also is pretty good about telling you about it too. There's a quest that's a WIP and when you do finally find the NPC when you chat it literally says, "bro, we're working on it, try again later" lol. At least I know it's not broken, ya know?

My only gripe isn't REALLY a gripe because I know it's probably just another WIP, but that's crafting. Nothing really SEEMS to be better than anything else other than aesthetic flair. One handers tend to cap out around 35ish 'damage' no matter the magical find or crafted materials you use thus far, Two handers about the same with the exception of a few finds that I have around 50 or 60. Damage seems to come from your skills which is great, but it gets a little boring to travel this massive world from city to city and the blacksmiths have varying cost of items that merely look different. I can buy a lute for 120 gold and it's the same performative boost (so it seems) as the lovely 'ash' lute I bought across the country from the  world famous bard for 6300 gold, just prettier.

Same with armor. Light, Medium, Heavy. Only restrictions seem to be movement and overall value, but I get my ass beat all the same and it's more about what do I want to look like over actual effectiveness. 

Again, I know it's a WIP but man was that an expensive learn, not that gold seems to be much of a problem.

All that to say, this is a brilliant game that I'm sure the average player of the RPG genre will thoroughly enjoy. I've had plenty of moments where I've found myself chuckling at the humor of the dialogue, laughing at the absurdity of some of the combat crap I've pulled off, and in pure awe of some of the simple but lovely mechanics of everything else that is in this game. There's so much to talk about in this game that the character limit for reviews just isn't enough. There's a very deep, very good crafting system. Inventory is fantastic and even has a search feature. Quests, factions, and rep are everything from straight and simple to deeply complex. Mounts and companions are unique and fun. The world map and travel is as quick or as deep as you'd like it to be. It's all good, there isn't anything more to say about it all.

Do yourself a favor and give it a try, it's one of those games where you keep telling yourself, 30 more mins and I'm good, only to find you've missed family dinner and are now eating cold potatoes from the fridge.

Civilization VII: A Disappointing Departure from the Norm
This review is based on my experience with the current state of Civilization VII, and unfortunately, it feels like a significant departure from the deep, intricate experiences the series is known for.

Core Gameplay Lacking Depth
Frankly, this game feels nothing like a Civ game. It is significantly slim in terms of technology, culture, and religious advancements. Instead of the carefully crafted, multi-layered strategy we've come to expect, Civ VII plays more like a short builder without real depth. It leans far more toward an action-focused strategy builder than the beautifully carved, expansive game we all miss. The fact there are only 3 eras is disappointing and makes the technology gameplay way too strong, especially in the modern era. The first planes just completely take over the game.

Unbalanced and Clunky Mechanics
I was very grateful that Humankind offered some competition in this genre, pushing the Civ team to make some adjustments, particularly to the warfare. However, a major issue I ran into involves the new era progression system.

One specific mechanic I truly disliked was tied to the era transition. After you progress to a new era, you can spend your achieved points on certain improvements. Within this menu is the option to transfer your capital city to another one. This transfer looks like an immense, unbalanced bonus if you figure out the precise effect.

Normally, upon advancing, all your cities are reduced to settlements, and you only maintain your capital as a full city. However, transferring your capital means:
1. Your previous capital stays a city
2. The selected city becomes the new capital city

This effectively grants you one additional starting city for the new era, which is a huge boost you have to figure out by yourself. It's a mechanic that feels completely unintuitive and breaks the balance of the transition.Another bug, in my opinion, is that if you annex a city, you have to choose between keeping the city and destroying it. So far, so good, but I was not successful in giving back a city to the original nation it belonged to. So if you keep the city and then in the peace negotiation give back the city, it just didn't happen. That way I increased my number of cities way too quickly and ended up with +10 cities over the normal cap. However, the negative effects were too small or not noticeable, which is bad balancing in my opinion.

Final Verdict:
Civilization VII is currently a shallow, action-oriented strategy game that lacks the intricate depth and polish expected of a flagship title in this franchise. The potential for a new direction is there, but the execution, particularly with the clunky cultural progression and unbalanced city mechanics, leaves the game feeling incomplete and unsatisfying.

I love this game, so this review will be LONG. I started my playthrough through Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengenace on July 9th, 2025. I write this review on October 21st, 2025. It has taken me nearly four months to finish both my playthroughs of the games different stories (or canons). Four months to have this game become perhaps one of my favourite JRPGS of all time, and definitely my favourite Megaten game. I'm sure many other players could have finished it faster, but I'm glad I got to really soak in and absorb every single part of this game. It has its many flaws, like all games do, and they can be pretty glaring at times. Even still, I implore you to give this game a shot. If you're a fan of JRPGs or Megaten in general, I know you won't regret it. 

For those who don't know Megaten, it's a VERY LONG series where colorful casts of characters fight in order to reshape a dying world in favour of different alignments. Law, Chaos, Neutral are the common three

And of course, with Vengeance being a rerelease of the original switch exclusive SMT V, there are a plethora of big changes that affect both canons. All these quality of life changes and new features bump up the game and make it the definitive experience. A short list of the most important changes are the following:
- New story path (the main selling point of the game)
- Innate skills, passives that add an entire extra level to demon customization and specialization
- Over forty new demons being added to the already expansive roster
- ABILITY TO SAVE ANYWHERE
- Virtual Trainer (rematch system against basically every boss)
- Aogami Husks (helps you get some abilities for fusion)
- Demon Haunt (a social area where you get to chat up your demons about their feelings on current events)
- Rails that allow you to shortcut through the map, or allow you to reach special pockets of land with treasure
- Sky view, gives you an aerial viewing of the surrounding location
- 89 NEW SONGS THAT ARE ALL BANGERS FROM START TO FINISH
- All original DLC are part of base game

Before anything else, I must address the music as a stand out part of this game. It is perfect. Perhaps one of the best videogame soundtracks I've had the pleasure of listening to. There is so much variety, so many different tunes with different motifs and moods and its just... perfect.  It's consumed my life and I find myself listening to it whenever I get a free moment. That vengeance credit theme just hits some kinda way... 

Same with the gameplay, which also deserves its own praise. The press turn combat system that was introduced in Nocturne is still one of my favourite JRPG battle systems ever. Earning an extra half-turn for exploiting a weakness. Losing some turns if you miss or get your attack nulled, or losing ALL turns if the enemies drains or repels your attack. And the best part is that the playing field is even for both parties. Sure, you can dumpster enemies if you play your cards right. But enemies, especially bosses, have their own way of rigging the system in their favor. One weakness exploit can lead into a full party wipe, which forces you to have concrete strategies for whatever you do. Combat can be both trivial at times, and near impossible at others if you allow it to be. 

AND THE DEMONS. THE DEMONS! THERE ARE SO MANY COOL DESIGNS AND ALL THE DEMONS ARE FROM DIFFERENT REGIONS AND RELIGIONS!!! Folklore fans always eat great with this series. I cannot do the designs enough justice, they are the bread and butter of Megaten.

Now onto my thoughts on the two different canons that this game has to offer. While I may like the new route more than the original, I believe both need to be played in order to have the perfect experience. I played both routes on the Hard difficulty, but there are easier difficulties if the game is too challenging (I believe this game shines when its hard)

[b]Canon of Creation:[/b]

Visually, its great. I love the many different locations of Da'at, that all feel oppressive yet free with their atmosphere. Knowing that you walk among the ruins of civilization makes for some scary thoughts. And the background music just completes it all.

Changing from a random encounter system (from previous entries) to the current overworld system where you can attack the enemies on your own terms takes a lot of frustration out of navigating the world (although Estoma, a skill for warding off enemies, is very pointless here). Fights can range in difficulty, depending on how prepared you are. If you're going into a fight blind, there is a decent chance you may get wiped in a turn or two. Some fights will just kick your ass regardless. But sometimes, the fights don't really pose any challenge to the player. There aren't many strong gimmicks when it comes to the main fights either, other than manipulating the Press Turn system.

Story, a focal point in most JRPGs, is just... alright? I'd say this is the biggest failing of the original game, sadly. That being said, I do like the story! Siding with different ideologies on how to reform the world is the coolest thing ever. However, the majority of characters that represent the different alignments feel more like tropes, and less like characters. Not only that, but the story offers so little time with some of them that you might feel indifferent when it comes time to pick sides. The ideas there are good, some set pieces like the [spoiler] Nahobino fights in the Empyrean [/spoiler] are phenomenal, and I think some characters like [spoiler] Abdiel [/spoiler] really shine above the rest. But the story ended and I just wished there was a bit more to it. Still, I enjoyed my time with this canon, and I think it deserves to be played just as much as CoV. I ended this canon with the Chaos ending.

[b]Canon of Vengeance:[/b]

Areas are the same, apart from the third area and accompanying dungeon being completely new in CoV. Can feel samey if you go through both stories back to back, but the new area [spoiler] Shinjuku [/spoiler] is probably my favourite in the whole for how gorgeous and ethereal it feels. Something about it is just so magical, despite it being filled with demons, I'd want to walk around it a little and soak in the atmosphere. [spoiler] Shakan [/spoiler], the new dungeon, is okay I guess. Very short and the 'gimmick' isn't very well used

Most gameplay notes from Canon of Creation are present here, although the intro of Guest characters was such a well-needed shakeup. Having your friends actually join and help in fights makes much more sense than just... NOT HELPING WHEN THEY EASILY CAN. Now you can fight hand in hand with your buddies, which made CoV stand way above CoC by itself (at least to me). Another note about the battles is the better used gimmicks within this route. A lot of fights in the original story could feel very similar, so having actual gimmicks made the battles feel so much more powerful ([spoiler] even if I hate some of them fuckkkkk Tiamat that fight was brutal [/spoiler])

Story is a huge improvement over the original, its way more character-centric and the chatacters are way better utilized. The tag-along of [spoiler] Yoko and Tao [/spoiler] throughout the middle of the story to provide commentary and moral dialogue may be annoying to some, but it feels quite nice to me. When things happened to the characters, I cared more. I wanted only the best for everyone. Characters like Yuzuru had so much more presence here, compared to CoC where he is sorta just... there. I think there are good aspects about the CoC story that are absent here, but that is why I believe both stories need to be played for the best experience. I ended this canon with the Law ending.

2023 Update:

First major concern a lot of people have about LOTRO - is it dead?

(Still) No. It still has a very healthy playerbase, big enough that the even the RP servers feel populated. So don't let your worries about population turn you away. The numbers online are not always accurate, so I'd be wary of trusting outside reporting.

This is a classic MMORPG. It's going to be familiar to anyone that has played Everquest, DAoC, WoW, etc. While it means you're not getting any particularly amazing new mechanics, the perk is that LOTRO has figured out how to get the best out of those systems. Leveling feels well-progressed, classes are (mostly) balanced, and there is a lot of variety even within the classes to provide lots of replay value and ways to mitigate strengths and weaknesses.

LOTRO might have the best soundtrack I've ever heard. I recommend turning off battle music and just enjoying the compositions. Bree, as well as the various Inns and Halls located therein, have some fantastic scores attached to them.

Let's be honest though - if you play LOTRO you're probably here because it's Lord of the Rings. And in that regard, you will not be disappointed. The game is steeped in the lore - books and films - and has little nods to it scattered everywhere that are rewarding for someone that is really into their Tolkien scholarship. This is not a LotR skin thrown over a MMORPG framework - this is Middle Earth proper. Even with dated graphics (updates are coming soon, as of this writing) it's still a joy to look at. If you're rolling through some place like the Shire, you'll be able to soak in that sleepy, bucolic atmosphere that the movies portrayed so well.

This is a great MMO experience, and I usually find MMOs tedious. Moreover, it's free - so it's a low-commit to try it out for yourself.

悪いが俺は強火のシリーズファンであり、どうしてもクソ長お気持ち表明にならざるを得ないので、最初に結論を書こう。
購入指標としてのレビューが読みたいなら冒頭部だけで十分だから安心してほしい。
「おすすめ」を選んだ理由は、俺自身が楽しめたからというだけだ。
万人におすすめするというわけではないし、できない。
「シリーズファンが、あくまでちょっと豪華なリマスターだと割り切って、セールを狙って買うなら」という但し書きがつく。
あまり他社作品と比べるべきではないかもしれないが、原作をリスペクトしつつリメイクとしての新たな価値の創造ができているあのバイオRE4が現在は定価約6000円だと考えると、本作は高くても定価5000円くらい、セールで3000円台が妥当な購入ラインだろう。
これからMGS3を初めて遊ぶという人は、悪いことは言わないからより原作に近いリマスターであろうMaster Collectionを選んだほうがいい。
これは、決してリメイクではない。

まず目を引くのが美しくなったグラフィックだ。
UE5で美しくリメイクされたジャングルは、原作を初めてプレイしたときの「とんでもない場所に放り出されてしまった」と圧倒された記憶を呼び覚ましてくれた。
各キャラクターもリアル寄りにデザイン変更され、原作のイメージを保ちつつも現代的な説得力を持った。
一見、名作が現代に美しく蘇ったように見える。
しかしその感動も長くは続かなかった。
美しいが、新しくはないのだ。
演出面は一切変更されていないため、現代水準のグラフィックに対して追い付いていない。
20年前では正解だった「技術的制約を隠すための短いカット割り」がそのまま流用されているため、映像の情報量が増した分だけその古さが際立つ。
調べてみたらキャラクターのアニメーションを作り直したそうだが……本当に？
少なくともカットシーンにおいては演技が新しくなっていないため、20年前のグラフィック向けのオーバーな動作が目立ってちぐはぐな印象を受けた。
オセロットの「革命的な」リロードなど一部は明らかに当時そのままを流用しており、最新グラフィックで人形劇をしているような滑稽さを覚えた。
さらに言うとグラフィック自体も、見れば見るほど粗が目立ってくる。
被写界深度表現のクオリティが異常に低かったり、レイトレーシングがなかったり、技術不足がどんどん露呈する。
極めつけはfpsが60キャップであり、それすらなんでもないシーンで突然カクつくなど最適化も十分にされていない。
おそらく本作最大の挑戦であったであろうグラフィックですら満足に達成できていないことは、本作が抱える問題を象徴している。
原作の良さを極力残そうとしたのだろうが、最新グラフィックの対としてあるべきだった表現のアップデートがなく、技術的な力不足によってかえって原作を毀損しているようにすら感じる。

ゲーム性に関しては、正直あまり褒められる部分がない。
面白いことは面白いが、そんなのMGS3を再現してるんだから当たり前だ。
まずTPS操作で遊べるNew Styleだが、これも一見新しいようで技術不足、開発経験不足が露呈している。
視野の狭さ、しゃがみや張り付きなどの操作方法の非洗練、入力に対するレスポンスの悪さなど、現代的な体験になっていない。
CQCやホールドアップなどのアクションの選択肢は据え置きなうえに、やたらのんびりしたモーションに変更されており、単に古いままなだけでなくより退屈な印象を与えてしまっている。
さらに肩越しTPS視点で撃つときの命中精度が異常に低く、結局昔からあった主観視点に切り替える必要があるのも、New Styleの無意味さを際立てる。
例えばこれがファンが作ったTPS操作Modなら、素晴らしい出来だと絶賛したかもしれない。
しかしこれは仮にも大企業が作った完全リメイクを謳うゲームの操作であり、褒める部分は見当たらない。
さらにゲーム体験もまるでアップデートされていない。
敵AIやレベルデザインが更新されていないため、結局古いゲームを遊んでいるだけなのだ。
一見現代的に美しくなったように見えるジャングルも、20年前のレベルデザインそのままであることがわかるとブロックの塊にしか見えなくなってくる。
一応New Styleで遊ぶと、ハンデとして敵のステータスが強化されるらしいが、これも調整不足が目立つ。
本当にステータスをいじっただけであり大部分は特に変化を感じられず、逆に原作では意図していないであろう場所での理不尽な発見が起こる場面すらある。
ボス戦も一切変更されておらず、TPS操作で遊ぶことがまったく考慮されていない。
ザ・フィアー、ジ・エンド、ザ・フューリー、といった「かくれんぼ」が重要な要素になっているボスは自由な視点が可能なTPSにおいて破綻している。
こんなことは言いたくなかったが、ザ・ボスとの「人生最高の10分間」すら、緊張感がなかった。
単純にシリーズファンだから解法がわかっているという以前に、ゲーム体験として現代的な価値がなくなっている。
本作で再会したボスたちの印象が終始「お前らバカかよ」だったのは、本当に残念に思う。
操作性の改善を試みUIも多少整理されたが、それに合わせてゲーム性が改良されていないため体験がアップデートされておらず、むしろ原作の価値を貶めてしまっている。
唯一満足できたのは各種ミニゲームや収集要素といったボリュームだが、それも単に原作にあったものをちゃんと収録したというだけだ。
隠しミニゲームの「ガイサベージ」を、アクションゲームを得意とするプラチナゲームスにリメイクしてもらったことは評価できる。
プレイ前後に異常に長いロードが入るという不便さはある（ゲームファイルを見たら別の実行ファイルとして分離されており、一度メインゲームを中断してガイサベージを起動するという訳わからん実装をしている）が、クリア後はセーブデータを取っておかなくてもいつでも遊べるのも嬉しい。
しかし、最も優れたリメイク部分は他社の功績という、実に残念な事実がそこに残るわけだが。

そして、ストーリー部分。
こちらに関しては、「原作再現」を忠実に行えている。
というか極一部の新録を除いて当時の音源をそのまま使っているので当たり前であるし、ストーリーの功績は当時の役者の皆様のものなんだが。
それはそれとして、美しいグラフィックで蘇るネイキッド・スネーク始まりの物語は、今見返しても心を揺さぶる力がある。
無線での時に緊張感のある、時に笑えるやり取りの数々も、再度の視聴に耐えうる素晴らしい出来だ。
これは「原作が持っていた素晴らしさを絶対に壊さない」という配慮が感じられ、ファンとしては嬉しく思う。
しかし同時に、どちらかというと遠慮されているようにも感じてしまった。
あまりにも原作を再現することに固執しすぎており、一切手を付けてはいけないと及び腰になっているのが手に取るようにわかるのだ。
なにも原作のストーリーを独自の解釈で破壊しろと言っているのではない。
原作をリスペクトしたうえで「リメイクだからこそできる」ファンサービスや世界観拡張のチャンスがあったのに、それをみすみす逃したのが問題だ。
例えば、後年MGSVで登場しスネークのミッションの裏で暗躍していたことが明らかになるスカルフェイスやXOFをほんの少しでも匂わせるとか。
原作において強烈な印象を残すもののあっさりと退場するコブラ部隊や、単なるMGS2のオマージュキャラクターに留まっていたライコフを掘り下げたりしてもよかったはずだ。
美しい思い出を美しいまま再現することはできている、それは認める。
少なくともストーリーに関しては「美化された思い出が美化されたまま蘇った」と感じることができた。
それに、余計な改変をしてしまったら猛烈な批判を受けるだろうという危惧も理解できる。
ほぼ唯一にして最大の変更点として、あの007シリーズのオマージュである印象的なオープニングを安っぽいテレビドラマのオープニングみたいにしたのは、俺も反応しかけた（冷静に見れば単に高解像度化するより新たに作ったほうが「価値」を創出できているので正しい判断だったと思う）。
しかしそういったリスクもひっくるめて、MGS3の「リメイク」に挑戦するという覚悟を示してもらいたかったと思う。
総じて新しさがなく、ガワが美しいだけで、20年前のゲームを猿真似しているだけなのだ。
まるで見てくれだけが良い偽物のように感じ、そこにシリーズが持っていた核心はないように見える。

ではその核心、言うなればMGSのGENEとはなんだろう？
ビッグボスの遺伝子の話ではなく、このシリーズが持つ根源的な設計思想だ。
それは「限界への挑戦」である、と俺は思っている。
そもそもMSX2の初代メタルギアが生まれたのも、大量の弾丸が飛び交う銃撃戦を描画するのが難しいというハードスペックの限界に対する挑戦からだった。
そうしてステルスアクションを発明し、その後も閉所、ジャングル、オープンワールドとステルスアクションの構造的限界に挑戦し続けた。
物語もMGS1以降は映画的な表現へ挑み、メタ表現や第4の壁の破壊、無線やカセットテープの収集で多層的に語られる物語など「ゲームだからこそ」の表現にも挑戦し続けた。
それは時に失敗することもあったが、メタルギアの名を冠するどの作品も、常に果敢な挑戦を続けていたことは疑うべくもない。
本作は、綻びは隠せていないものの「現代でも遊びやすい最新グラフィックのMGS3」を作ることはかろうじて達成できている。
大昔の自社エンジンで作られたゲームを最新のエンジンで再現するという、非常に手間のかかる難しい仕事をしたことも理解している。
しかし、もしそれが本作の挑戦であると言うのならば、やはりリメイクと呼ぶことはできない。
本作における挑戦は「残された遺産を模倣する」ことであり、しかもそれに成功していない。
そもそもの話、MGSを保存するという目的はすでにMaster Collectionで果たされているので、多大なコストと時間をかけて本作をわざわざ制作する意義すらなくなってしまう。
小島監督自身は過去に、MGSのテーマは「次の世代に遺すもの」であると語っている。
これが本当に、MGSを知らない若いゲーマーに受け継がれるべきものだろうか。
「かつての名作」ではなく「つまらないゲーム」として誤って記憶されはしないだろうか。
次の世代にGENEを受け継ぐうえで、そこにリスペクトは必要でも遠慮は必要ない。
今のKONAMIで働く若い開発者たちも、「愛国者達」が定めた設計図通りに製品を組み立てるのではなく、自分が面白いと思える新しいゲームを作りたかったはずだ。
そんな「これが現代におけるMGSの再解釈だ」と宣言するような作品を期待していた。
過去に囚われず、ゲームデザインの根幹に手を入れる覚悟や、物語の新たな側面を提示する勇気を見せてほしかった。
もちろんそれは決して簡単なことではなく、むしろ大失敗する可能性のほうが高いだろう。
そう、MGSVの根幹に手を入れ、新たな側面を提示しようとしたSurviveのように。
今のKONAMIが技術も経験も足りていないのは今回でわかったから、あれをもう一度見せられるくらいだったら、もう何もしないでいてくれたほうが本当はいいのかもしれない。
それでもなお「リメイクする」と宣言した以上、俺は「次世代MGSの始まりを告げるなにか」が見つけられることを期待していた。
だが、俺が見つけたのは「旧世代MGSに固執するあまり形骸化したなにか」だった。
MGS3のリメイクを謳いながら、最も重要な精神を次の世代に受け継がず、「賢者の遺産」を保存しようとするだけのプロジェクトに見えてしまう。
本作はまるで、ザ・ボスの理想を誤解し、自らが生み出したシステムに飲み込まれたゼロ少佐のようだ。
未来ではなく、過去に向けて作られている。

Nearly two months after release, there's still a gamebreaking bug of the game freezing hard if you tranquilize enemies during the jungle escape/escort part just before the final boss battle. My first two attempts ended with my needing to terminate the process via task manager after firing tranq shots at the pursuers. Another in the now long line of games I've labeled "spooky chores," where you do something that would be mind numbingly boring in any other context but add monsters to it. Jumping on top of something only delays the inevitable. You can technically sneak but a lot of streets and alleys are too small to sneak through if there's a monster nearby because you can't make enough distance. We figured maybe we're supposed to break the obvious glowing monster eggs when we see them, but hitting them even once destroys whatever you have equipped, so that's not viable.
If you manage to actually get shit done, you can still lose if you're out past 12:00 because the fog gets you. How do you know when it's close to 12:00 if you aren't already back in the store? Fuck you. How do you communicate it's time to come back to anyone that happens to still be out? Fuck you unless they're already within earshot of the proximity chat.
The concept is there but there are no mechanics to prop it up and make it into a full experience. It's possible we were just missing something but the only loading screen tip is that people can't hear you during loading screens, which is pretty obvious when their voices cut out during loading screens.
There needs to be more to the game to really make it worth playing, and some QOL like a purchasable upgrade for your crew to know what time it is or how many pizzas have left to be delivered, a map with your people on it, etc. Having the gameplay loop extend beyond "ok it's night 3 please die" would go a long way, with maybe a slower build up and incremental upgrades, or even the option to set up some defenses around the map.
The idea is there, but I do think it needs work.

It's a shame, theres so many things that arent great about the game that the things which are good about it are overshadowed, LMU could be a great simracer i could frequent a lot, but i end up growing frustrated every time i play, here's why;

## The Good
The online multiplayer works decently well. I’ve only gotten disconnected once in my entire time playing, and I could reconnect immediately. No major lag spikes or other issues to speak of. How your rank and safety rating change is explained in the post-game summary, which makes improving your racing relatively easy.    

The sounds are good. Cars sound authentic, and while some cars are a lot louder than others in the cockpit, it’s not a dealbreaker. The audio is immersive and well done.   

The FFB is decent, though maybe a bit overtuned in my experience. Curbs are extremely obvious, and so is locking or sliding. What the car is doing is pretty clear from the feedback alone.   

Graphics are serviceable and look up to date. There are some points I’ll touch on later, but overall, the visuals hold up with other games like LMU.

## The Bad
The tyre model is, in my experience, utterly terrible. Grip loss is hard to understand. Overdriving your tyres in any way makes your grip vanish completely. Locking your brakes is a guaranteed spin. Wheel-spinning out of corners usually ends in one too. Even compared to other games on the same engine, I don’t have nearly as many problems with the tyres as in LMU. I hate it, and I really hope that the developers will work on improving these tyres.

Flashing your brights is way too effective. Even with high beams being enabled by default, flashing your lights overpowers all other lights on track. Meaning someone 100 meters back can make the entire track in front of you flash, It’s completely unrealistic.

Also, flashing lights don’t seem to respect walls. If someone spams their flashers on a track with tight sections, you’ll see the flashes through walls. It’s hugely distracting and very annoying. 

## The Ugly
The game’s pricing structure is unclear at best and almost deceptive at worst. You end up paying over double the price just to get all the content they offer. Plus, there’s subscription nonsense in the game that isn’t visible on the store page before you buy. The developers basically want to charge you multiple times for content and features.

The RaceControl Pro and Pro+ subscriptions aren’t clearly explained before purchase. You’re led to believe you’re buying a complete game, but in reality, you’re only getting a fraction of it.

## The Summary
Despite decent audio, stable online play, and decent visuals, the game’s core systems, especially tire physics and lighting at night, are broken in ways that destroy my enjoyment of the game, combined with a misleading monetization model these issues make it impossible to recommend at full price, or any price, really.

[h1]Calling all platformer fans and cat lovers[/h1]

[b]Bubbles the Cat[/b], the debut game from [b]Team Cats & Bears[/b], is a single-button action platformer with the right amount of difficulty (not too easy and not too hard), clever level design, short levels and a smooth learning curve. There are 125 levels to play, divided in six worlds (five regular worlds and an extra hardcore world), unlockables and a pleasant soundtrack. 

[h1]Rewarding gameplay[/h1]

Most levels can be easily finished if you just want to rush to the exit, but the real challenge lies in completing each level with all cat food collected and in sub-par time, in a single run. The cat moves by himself and the only input needed is the jump button, but don’t be fooled – the game demands the right timing for jumps and there are a lot of power-ups that spice up the gameplay and are essential for beating levels. Each power-up grants you a new ability, from jumping higher to creating a small wall that will be needed to reach higher places, and much more. This game rewards curiosity, considering that you will need to explore a lot to find secret areas that contains more collectables; and creativity, as there’s usually more than one solution to 100% a level. 

[h1]Presentation and usability[/h1]

[b]Bubbles the Cat[/b] has very charming graphics, a great soundtrack, an intuitive interface, rebindable controls, Steam Cloud and full controller support. While I absolutely love this game’s crunchy pixels, the amount of detail makes some worlds a bit hard to read. What I mean is: some scenarios are too distracting, and certainly will cost you some lives until you’re familiar with them. In the end, this is not a huge issue, though, but sometimes less is more. 

[h1]Worth it?[/h1]

I’m having fun with [b]Bubbles the Cat[/b], and it’s certainly a great title to play in short bursts. I can fully recommend it full price if want to complete each goal every level (by finishing it in sub-par time and collecting all cat food), but if you just want to finish the game as quick as possible, wait for a sale. After all, you’ll get more from this game if you replay each level while trying to get all collectables and beating it in sub-par time.

[b]Pros[/b]:
* Fun in short bursts 
* Tight (and rebindable) controls
* Steam Cloud and full controller support
* Awesome pixel art and pleasant soundtrack
* Great amount of challenge for completionists

[b]Cons[/b]:
* Some worlds are too busy visual-wise
* Steam Overlay works partially (you can’t take screenshots for some reason)

This game is for a very particular type of person, someone who enjoys difficult games that require time and a lot of failure to learn and master. I thought I would be that type of person, but i feel this game loses something along the way, it stops becoming about learning or overcoming a challenge. For the first dozen hours I thought it was about that, but its not. I personally feel battle brothers is about failure, its about losing brothers, getting your face kicked in over and over again and learning you are not top of the food-chain. Full on dwarf fortress "losing is fun" style.
A lot of games can do this idea really well, Darkest Dungeon, Kenshi ect. But i feel battle brothers focuses on the wrong aspects of what makes those games fun. I love Kenshi because every time you fail or get beaten down you get stronger and learn, its really about overcoming a challenge and becoming a badass. In battle brothers when you get beaten down you really don't gain very much... you just rebuild and go to the next fight, knowing that all your work could be undone again due to nothing but bad RNG. You can learn little tricks here and there but eventually it all just comes down to how lucky you get. A lot of games have a dependence on RNG but i haven't seen many that rely on it quite as much as battle brothers does. I think there could be a case for this type of design if the game paid more respect to your time, but everything in this game takes so much work to setup and prepare for that it just sucks all the energy out of me. There are plenty of people who don't mind this type of thing and find a lot of enjoyment in this game but if your looking for something else this might not be a fun game for you.

[b]Bueno, experimenté Visage y sobreviví para contarlo.[/b]

Qué manera de transpirar y sufrir con este título. Fue pasarla muy mal constantemente y eso es algo re contra positivo para un juego de horror.

Visage está fuertemente inspirado en la famosa demo P.T. que suponía una nueva entrega de la saga Silent Hill, hasta que fue cancelada. Los chicos de SadSquare se ve que jugaron bastante la demo y en vez de quedarse de brazos cruzados decidieron ponerse manos a la obra para traernos este juego y no permitir que ese increíble adelanto muera del todo. Tenemos como escenario una casa enorme, repleta de habitaciones y contenido por ver y analizar. Y todo esto controlando al personaje en primera persona.

En la trama nos ponemos en los zapatos de Dwayne Anderson, un tipo... del cual no se sabe mucho al principio pero que, a medida que encuentra distintos objetos, va a ir conociendo a quienes vivieron en el pasado en ese mismo domicilio. Gente que encarnó diversos problemas, tanto mentales como paranormales, y todos tienen algo en común: parece que en algún momento conocieron al personaje el cual también tienen sus propios fantasmas. No les digo más, el resto se los dejo a ustedes.

En la casa podemos interactuar con prácticamente todo, desde puertas (obvio, sino no pasamos a ningún lado) hasta artículos de cocina, muebles, etc. Esto, siempre teniendo en cuenta el no quedarnos sin luz para que Dwayne no se vuelva loquito. Además, cada tanto habrá eventos paranormales aleatorios que te cambian totalmente el desarrollo de la partida. Puede pasar literalmente cualquier cosa, y todo es horrible. Y es indispensable explorar varias veces los mismos sectores o zonas porque a medida que avancemos, varios objetos irán cambiando de lugar o aparecerán otros que antes no estaban, atentis con eso.

También hay muchas referencias a juegos y películas que claramente inspiraron a esta entrega, como por ejemplo Silent Hill 4 (parece que la saga en sí inspiró completamente a Visage), Amnesia, Outlast, The Shining, The Ring. Casi todos los productos que ya conocen. Me gustó mucho también cómo implementaron los VHS y discos de vinilo para desbloquear zonas.

心情一言难尽，打完前两周目后我想一定要给这游戏打个好评，打完第三周目我犹豫了

以下内容涉及剧透
第三周目给人极度不爽感的原因就是“没苦硬吃”。我说实话，我在三周目基本没有看到角色的成长和发展。一二周目角色基本上都已经成长完毕了，大家的心结基本上解开，而且走向了完美的结局。作者在这个时候非要强行制造一个意外，让游戏进入三周目，然后让角色遭罪，玩家坐牢。
如果你能写好三周目也就算了，问题是三周目真的很难让人满意。如果这是一个以人物成长为中心的故事，那么我没看出三周目的存在有任何意义。三周目的故事脱离了玩家能够共情的日常，进入了一个“灾难片”的世界，而且角色基本上没有成长。有一个评论说的很好，如果说前两周目是记叙文，三周目突然变成议论文，而且空讲道理，他们喊着什么爱啊理解啊的就冲了上来，问就是因为灾难来了大家突然就开始珍惜现在了，显得之前的挣扎好像毫无意义。
如果作者认为这是一部科幻作品，那它是一部很烂的科幻。说实话作为科幻故事来说这个故事很俗套，而且其中很多解释非常强行[spoiler]（如果真的是男女主的努力导致了世界复原，波函数坍塌应该导致世界融合、波动消除才对，灾难反倒越来越严重这种设定真是没苦硬吃。如果男女主其实什么忙都没帮上，单纯只是男主妈和杰克选择了停止轮回，那这段剧情更是完全不知所云）[/spoiler]。是前面两周目细腻而富有感染力的描写、对于角色形象的刻画撑起了这个作品。

具体来说（涉及剧透！），一周目教我们逃避痛苦会带来误解，二周目教我们面对痛苦能够获得幸福，三周目作者沉浸在自己的艺术中，没有痛苦就主动创造痛苦。作者开启三周目的契机是小茜的失踪，但是二周目大家都已经走向了坦诚，说真的我没看出来小茜的家庭问题是二周目解决不了的，主角眼睁睁地看着小茜被父母带走这点我就无法理解，而且三周目一句灾难来了大家关系更好了就轻飘飘的解决了，更让人难以接受。结局男女主的分离也是受到很多人诟病的一点，我其实是能理解这个结局的，事情总会有遗憾，但是这种表达方式真的非常让人火大，好像作者故意要恶心玩家一下一样。写遗憾有很多种方法，比如简单的擦肩而过就很有感觉。你故意写男女主准备出门赴约，然后给特写镜头，最后镜头拉远，两人都在约会另一个陌生人，等于把玩家的期待值拉到最高然后一下子摔落。玩家愿意去接受痛苦，也不代表着愿意接受你这么刻意创造的痛苦。

其实这个游戏我整体来说是推荐的，作为视觉小说来说可以说很顶尖，我尤其喜欢对话时的沉默和留白，有一种此处无声胜有声的美感和真实感。角色的形象与人物关系刻画也很真实，前两个周目非常值得一玩。但正是前两个周目的出色让我期待一个好的结局，如果实在没有好的结局，至少把遗憾写得合理且有意义。所以我对于第三周目的表现过于失望，写了这篇基本上全是讲游戏缺点的评价。所以我决定还是把它算作差评。
[spoiler]好吧，也有一部分是因为我真的很不爽作者把妮可和马克给拆了，我真的很喜欢这对[/spoiler]

This just feels like the work of a student who's always aiming for a passing grade it has everything you’d expect but lacks any real insight or depth, coming across as a rushed job. Saints Row is honestly a mess. Who is the demographic for this? Am I just out of touch with whatever culture or age group this appeals to? Maybe I’m just getting old. It does have a surprisingly decent soundtrack, but having DMX tracks mixed in with the game’s tone just feels mismatched. Everything’s there on paper, but none of it really fits together.

The mechanics are outright weird, as if they were thrown in without any real thought about how they’d function or mesh cohesively. Everything feels disjointed. And seriously a QTE prompt for explosive objects? A simple red outline or glow isn’t enough? That’s just outright insulting to players’ intelligence.

On top of that, the characters aren’t likable or even hateable they’re just plain annoying. I stopped caring so much that I now browse online or do other tasks during cutscenes (since they keep playing even when you alt-tab). The gameplay, somehow, manages to be even worse. Side activities once a highlight of the series  are now reduced to meaningless chores: leave a rating and get attacked by a gang, pick up drugs, take pictures, or, unbelievably, go dumpster diving. There’s no creativity or charm here, especially compared to the hilarious and memorable side missions in Saints Row 2, which still stand out as some of my favourite gaming moments.

So why am I still recommending it? Honestly, if you can get it cheap, it’s still fun in a casual, turn your brain off kind of way. I’ve been rushing through the story and having fun with the missions each one at least feels different and occasionally delivers some entertaining, cinematic moments. It’s not all a dud. This isn’t Saints Row anymore, and it hasn’t been for a long time but whatever this version is, it’s at least worth a look when it’s on sale.

The Saints Row remake is a major disappointment and a far cry from what made the original series so beloved. Compared to other open-world games—and especially the earlier Saints Row titles—it feels uninspired, clunky, and stripped of the personality that once defined the franchise. The gameplay lacks polish, the story falls flat, and the humor that used to set the series apart feels forced and out of touch. From buggy performance to forgettable characters, it’s a remake that fails to capture the chaotic fun fans expected. Simply put, this version of Saints Row is best avoided at all costs.

Yes, it's a lot lilke Hearthstone, a game I enjoy immensely.

BUT ... the quality of life touches in Shadowverse just make this game so much nicer to play.

- Deck codes allow you to import an entire deck list instead of building it card by card.
- Replay mode lets you review your last 10 games.
- Story mode is more challenging and interesting than the Hearthstone tutorial.
- Daily rewards just for logging in.
- THREE quests every day.
- Rewards for reaching milestones in Ranked play.
- Special events with even more achievements and unique rewards.
- Prebuilt decks available for purchase, allowing you a 100 percent chance of getting certain cards.

HOWEVER ... I've now played enough of the game to see that the balance is very heavily skewed toward high-end-combo play. Most games between competitive decks are just a race to see who can get the big legendary combo off first, or to see if you can play your combo before the other guy draws the counter. All other turns are rendered trivial, so in a lot of cases it just boils down to a coin toss.

I'm not going to take back my positive review because I really do admire the foundation. And I recognize that other people do like this style of gameplay; it's just not for me. So while I'm going to uninstall it after saving this revised review, I still think it's worth a try for those who like CCGs. It's free, after all, and they are pretty generous with the cards, even though you'll never get enough free cards to be competitive.

Геймплей особенный: идёшь по горам, переправляешься через реки, следишь за весом груза — и вроде ничего особенного, но каждый шаг ощущается реально. Это почти как медитация в игре: ты успокаиваешься, погружаешься в мир, чувствуешь его детали.

Графика шикарная, а музыка просто завораживает. Иногда просто стоишь на холме, слушаешь дождь и песню, и кажется, что мир вокруг живёт своей жизнью.

Не скажу, что игра для всех — она медленная, иногда скучноватая, но если дать ей шанс, она реально зацепит. Это редкая игра, где чувствуешь эмоции и после того, как выключаешь компик.

В итоге: Death Stranding — странная, но красивая история о человечности. Она заставляет остановиться, подумать и почувствовать.

Most people today play Doom 2016, Doom Eternal, & Doom The Dark Ages. I'm old enough to have played all the Doom games, since the original 1993 release. 

[Doom The Dark Ages]

Its now 2025, the next highly coveted chapter, in the Slayers gut wrenching demon killing horror, is highly anticipated. That was until, Bethesda said, congrats, now there is a parrying mechanic, and we toned down the glory kills a bit. People said WTF? As the title of the game suggests, this is the dark ages, we used shields then, so I guess it fits? I got 26-hours into the game thus far, and I truly believe that they dropped the crap I didn't like in the previous 2 Doom games, but kept what I did like from them. 

DTDA still has arena battles as before, and the game will lock you into them, once you've crossed the trip wire threshold. But the previous games didn't have very large maps, so you felt like you were in tighter spaces. The maps in this game are so large, you feel like your playing an open world game, which I feel, is pretty cool. It takes what I like in an open world game, but gets rid of the unrelenting RPG elements, where you feel like you have to run all the NPC's lives, cause they could never take a crap without you guiding them. 

Some of the maps, I could tell they took ideas, from the forest maps in Halo 3. The game has a balance of natural Earthly style environments, and futuristic other worldly environments. Each map brings something new to experience, as such, I enjoy the map design, as much as I enjoy the gameplay. Is your horrorscope mars, you'll enjoy being there as well. I've never played a Doom game, that had this level of geometric complexity, when on Ultra Nightmare graphics levels.

Do you love platforming? You'll be doing some of that in DTDA, and your shield will help you to parcore in different areas. You use this sometimes to get where you are going, at other times, to access secrets. The game won't always be on foot however, sometimes you'll be flying a dragon called Sarate, who has a body mounted canon, which delivers hot death, to anyone in range. At other times, you'll be operating a giant mech called an Atlan, for which you will use to punch through barriers, and deliver the smackdown, to those pesky Titan class demons. 

I honestly didn't mind the parrying mechanic, I felt the gameplay aspect of that was fun. It was nice putting the enemy in a daze like their high on PCP, then going in for the finisher. Once you've upgraded your shield with the saw, now you get to slice into your enemy, while shooting a shotgun up their arse. There are multiple ways to reach 10 in the battles, and as you upgrade your weapons and capabilities, you can enjoy all the ways to kill a demon. Because lets be honest, your going to get payback for what they did to Daisy!

Who's that in my ear? Vega Omega, he's in my Slayer suit, telling me what my next objective is, so glad we have him, since were alone after the loss of Daisy. lol! Its not overdone however, so I don't mind. You get a lot more weapons in this game, some are great, some not so much. Some appear to be more for show, doing limited damage, others doing high damage, while looking the part, and their not even fully upgraded yet. My favorite weapon in the game, is the plasma rifle, called an Accelerator. Later I acquired the double barrel version, Cycler, which does double the damage, which equals double the fun. 

The ever popular combat shotgun, double barrel shotgun, rocket launcher, there all here, with some new new weapons added, like the shredder, impailer, the chainbolt. Nothing like launching a steel weighted heavy ball attached to a chain, into a demon to remind him your there. There are also multiple types of melee attacks you can choose from. As you progress through the game, new options will become available to you. In essence, you choose your method of melee attacks, not the game. 

Many people are sad, about the loss of Mick Gordan, who was famous for the awesome electric guitar shredding, that composed the music in Doom 2016. Unfortunately, due to contract agreements, and him getting screwed over, he got replaced by the time Doom Eternal was released, and the change in music style showed, and not for the better. In DTDA, they brought in Finishing Move, who's composers comprised of Brian Trifon and Brian Lee White. And while the music is no Mick Gordan, I actually really liked the music in the game, and probably the best were going to get these days.

The graphics are the best of any Doom game, IMO. Here's the thing though, in order to enjoy all the graphics setting's set to Ultra Nightmare on a 4K screen, you need a powerful computer, with at least an Nvidia 3080 GPU, and yes, RTX is required, as is the 580 driver. So, with that said, if your still rocking a GTX card, Bethesda says get out, RTX only club. Even if you only have a 1080P capable setup, your going to be lowering your graphics settings, cause if all your running is a 3060, 4060, 5060 GPU, you will not enjoy the FPS you get, and you'll hope and pray DLSS turned on, will save you. DTDA brings next gen graphics. 

I have an Intel 10870H 8-Core 16-Thread CPU, an Nvidia 3080 16GB-VRAM GPU, and 32GB of DDR4 PC3200-MHZ system RAM. Setting everything to Ultra Nightmare graphics levels on a 4K 144-HZ monitor, I was only getting 35-FPS. Turning on Adaptive Resolution, Present From Compute, and activating DLSS set to Ultra Performance, is what gained me between 60-FPS, to 95-FPS. The game looks amazing at these levels. If you can budget it, to gain 144-FPS, I would really recommend a modern system that has an Nvidia 4080 or 5080 GPU. Either that, or lower the graphics settings, or run a 1440P (AKA 2K) setup. 

Considering that my computer is 4-years old, I am plenty happy with the performance I'm getting, you just have to set your expectations to be reasonable, based on the machine you have. Getting 60-FPS is glass smooth, 75-FPS average is slick, and 80-FPS or above, is as smooth as an oil slick, so I'm happy! I love that there are lots of GPU settings to choose from. Thank goodness for the invention of DLSS with AI, cause 35-FPS is not going to cut it, its great for traditional film movies, but in video, that's chugging!

Speaking of which, the accessibility options are equally thorough, for which I appreciate! I won't go deeply into it, but I suffered a situation that partially disabled my left hand, which you need to move around in PC games. I was able to set those options up, as well as tune the difficulty setting, so I could actually enjoy the game. Previous Doom games didn't care about those with disabilities. I was happy to see, that DTDA was different, and allowed someone like me to play it.

Are you someone who appreciates the story lore of Doom? Worry not Doom fans, cause DTDA is loaded with story lore, for you to read, in the form of Codes pages. Do you have the physical copies of pas written Doom books? Well, there is more to strain your eyeballs on so enjoy. Speaking of story, DTDA takes place after Doom 64, and before the modern Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal games. Thus, it will fill in that juicy Slayer lore you crave. 

In conclusion: Is DTDA 100% classic Doom, NO! Is DTDA 100% modern Doom Eternal style, NO! DTDA is a game that I feel, falls in-between the classics & modern, combining elements of both genre's. Its got just about everything you would want from a modern Doom game. Some like the parrying mechanic, some don't, I however don't mind it at all, as it just adds to the overall gameplay of Doom. The dev's made the game challenging, but it can be only as challenging as you want it. I would 100% recommend DTDA, to any Doom fan. Now, attach those upgraded skins to your weapons, lets seek justice for Daisy!

➕The game has co-op, which seems to have been the focus of all open-world gameplay mechanics. Potentially, it should be the thing that makes any game 30-40% better, allowing you to regularly invite friends into battle to clear out the next section of the map, quests, and endgame world bosses. I played single-player, 'cos THE GAME'S REGIONAL PRICE IS WAY TOO HIGH.

Cons:
➖Now that this is another open-world game, events and activities are spread thinly across all maps. Fast travel points and supply nodes are a must, which becomes tiresome by the 5-7 hour mark of the 20-30-hour playthrough.
➖You have to travel between points of interest and tasks for a very long time, which becomes tiresome by the 5-10 hour mark because it's sooo booooooooooring... 
➖The same goes for ammo in the open world: it constantly needs to be replenished. And not from enemies or supply crates 99% of the time, as is the case in normal open-world games. Instead, you either go to your own designated, but terribly limited, resupply points or head back to your base. It's a very annoying and completely unnecessary fast-travel masturbation, making you moving back and forth every 10-20 minutes of gameplay or 5 minutes of intense combat.
➖Since we now have large, open maps, all the resources needed for crafting, leveling up, creating, and upgrading everything are scattered across them in respawning bits, and you have to run around collecting all this crap from all the open locations. Which also gets annoying around 8-10 hours.
➖Since we now have an open world, you need to take on world bosses multiple times, just like in an MMO, to have a certain chance of dropping the necessary items—from mutation factors to blueprints and resources for those blueprints.
➖Quests require you to change your exosuit into different setups before arriving at their destination, from light to heavy, with various items or upgrades installed. It's fun at first, but then it gets tiresome and boring.
➖Some quests require exosuit races, but the femto-particle reserves for the currently available parts aren't correctly calculated for them, and they deplete much faster than you can find refills along the way. No one tells you to upgrade and assemble an ultra-light and special set of exosuit parts.
➖Even in Story Mode, the game's open world and oddly tuned difficulty curve horribly unbalance the difficulty of its challenges, requiring you to replay battles 15-20 times after 5-8 hours of gameplay, tinkering with parts and tactics just to get through the boss. This isn't Story Mode, this is f0cking Hard Mode!
➖The balance of battles and weapons makes enemies feel like bullet sponges, even though you really want to swoop in and blow them all away with precision strikes.
➖I absolutely hate that the small jet engines, which drain stamina, drain it too quickly, making it impossible to gracefully maneuver around enemies on the ground, like in the first game. It's annoying.
➖The impact of hitting an enemy isn't always successful.
➖The absolutely disgusting wall turrets in the underground story complexes, which fire VERY frequently and push you VERY FAR away when hit by a beam. They force you to literally count the timing between shots down to the millisecond, ducking behind obstacles and trudging forward without getting pushed back. A fucking Sisyphean task, for God's sake. I'd forcibly send whoever came up with this idea to a resort in the Antarctic Sea in their underwear.
➖The transition point to one of the pre-final stages and battles is completely illogical, confusing you by throwing you into the quick-transition menu without clearly pointing you to the name of the next location.
➖Since it's an open world, there are plenty of places with randomly changing conditions—from dust storms to anomalies—but the game has seriously lost its visual style in terms of color combinations due to its shift toward pseudo-realism. Almost the entire world now looks very gray, formulaic, copied (procedurally generated), rather bland and bald, flat, and a couple of generations behind the current one in terms of visual quality. But the same can't be said for the exosuits—it's as if all the production money went into them. The environments are severely lacking in layering and density—bare rocks with low-resolution textures and a rough polygonal mesh, crudely placed objects, and other joys of life with sparse grass and undergrowth.
➖All this is further marred by the fact that the game runs on the Unreal Engine. As a result, we experience incredible lag when compiling shaders on the fly whenever something new appears on the screen — from an effect to an environmental element. Besides these, there are random bugs with flickering and underloading of objects, with flickering texture meshes on the floor, and with clipping through unloaded meshes. And if you update your drivers, change your video card, or reinstall the OS, the first time you load up, you have to patiently load to the level, wait 5-10 minutes for the game to compile the shaders in parallel with rendering, fly around a bit, exit the game, and then log back in as a normal person.
➖The female version of the main character uses the same rig as the male, making her look like a terriblly treated, hormone-deficient transsexual. So, to avoid the hassle of animating the two sexes differently, the developers simply gave them shared animations, and, as a result, shared shoulder and hip sizes. NPCs, including the antagonists, don't have this problem—they have feminine lower bodies, unlike the main character, and corresponding animations.
➖The English voice acting is very strange, with Ash constantly yelling into the microphone like his ass is being burned with turpentine, and Angel spends half the game struggling and crying.
➖The plot is pretty weak, in general terms. It's okay, but I wanted to see more character development and a much greater variety in the layering of events.

In short, I'm mostly disappointed. A good action game has been turned into a tedious grinder with an implicit emphasis on multiplayer. It's certainly playable in a pinch among cool games, but compared to what's been coming out this fall, it's too weak.
