Haven't touched this game in years but I saw the horrible reviews and just wanted to throw in my 2 cents. Yes, it was pretty buggy, and yes, they had some growing pains. But I have never played a looter shooter before or after this game that made you feel like such an incredible badass.

The story was interesting and brutal, and very sci-fi with the classic "the true monster is us" twist. But what really made this game stand out so much was the incredibly smooth combat. When you got your build going and found the right gear, you were a god: mowing down waves upon waves, surviving incredibly difficult battles and making yourself FEEL cool in the process. No one has nailed the "guns + powers" mechanics so well. Destiny 2 has NOTHING on this game, folks. Borderlands has better jokes but the vibe in this game was truly something special.

Sadly, I think after a couple of patches and updates the true game actually came through, but by then everyone had - justifiably - dumped on it for being so rushed, and so it landed with a thud. If it had been given 6 more months, I honestly believe we'd still be playing this game today, but the community never recovered.

In the end, though: it's still an AMAZING game. Absolutely still recommend picking it up and enjoying the story. Just know that when you reach the end, what was supposed to be a post-story end-game never really came together, the DLC was a dud, and the game has been abandoned, so don't expect anything to change. But it's still worth the price of admission for a fun-as-hell base game.

My expectations of this after Higurashi were impossibly high.
Maybe that's why it wasn't that surprising for me to realize that Umineko massively disappointed me.
But it's also really weird. I can see that the story is competently written (also suffering from the biggest issue of Higurashi - word bloat, especially during action scenes, with like a dozen scenes per chapter), I can't say I dislike it for some specific reason, but I just... don't vibe with it at all. 
I don't feel interested, I don't want to know what'll be next, I'm just waiting for it to be over.

There's a lot of competently written characters. Some you love, some you hate, it's great. But the story itself... well, I guess I can figure out one specific part of the story that I don't like - the amount of [spoiler]metanarrative[/spoiler] it uses 

Not only the whole original point of little "epilogues" after each chapter is completely lost and they are just straight up story elements now (why bother separating them into categories then, just to mess with Higurashi readers?), but they're also extremely on the nose when it comes to its dogshit tricks.

Example 1: The end of chapter 3. [spoiler]I know, I know, that was the whole point, to make Battler believe that Beatrice starts being good to just absolutely lose her biggest chance at victory at the last moment only to gloat how Battler (and, of course, the player behind them) are such morons that they expected this kind of anime trope to happen.[/spoiler] I know that was the whole point of the chapter, sure, but it also felt like such a pointless slap in the face of the player, considering how many stereotypes Higurashi used while playing them completely straight.

Example 2: End of chapter 4. Same shit, really, [spoiler]you're presented with a two hour long "battle"[/spoiler] that starts to feel cathartic to a degree, before you realize how ridiculous most of their arguments are (don't get me started about the [spoiler]small bombs[/spoiler]). 
Not only that, but these entire two hours are completely undermined in the literal next scene with [spoiler]Lambda and Bern (which are really hard to not treat as complete evil caricatures of Satoko and Rika) stating how all these arguments are just bullshit and are full of holes.[/spoiler] 

You have to continue the story somehow, I get it, and the whole separation into "questions" and "answers" was a joke even in Higurashi, but there should be another way to handle large section finishes without straight-up crossing over hours of your own writing just to continue the story. 

I don't know anymore. I suffered through 80 hours of this already (umipro). Maybe 10 of those hours felt like something Ryukishi wrote, The rest felt like his own extrapolated caricature that got told he can do no wrong and should not take any criticism or improve in any way after his first work got popular. 

I don't know if I want to continue if the Answers arc is just more of the same or just more ridiculousness while hoping that maybe 10% of that would feel like something worth reading. Maybe the way Ryukishi writes murder mysteries a-la danganronpa is just not for me.

Also fuck Ushiromiya Rosa. [spoiler]Truly the worst fucking parent in the history of fiction. Hurr durr single parent life is tough my ass.[/spoiler] Her, Ange, and Maria are probably the most well-written characters in this mess.

Then it starts to get so... damn... REPETITIVE. I almost quit the game multiple times, but kept going because was really interested in reaching the conclusion. In the end, a very worthy experience, although I won't condemn who goes after a walkthrough and set Reprises to Infinite just to avoid even more repetition (after all, I... errr... did it!). I very hesitantly recommend this game. The art is the best aspect of it, with fun gameplay and a decent story, but it just never really clicks. It's far too linear for a proper metroidvania, and the story throws a lot of Proper Nouns at you without really explaining it. It also cuts away from your main character quite frequently to tell the story from the perspective of other characters, which basically happens at random and is quite confusing. It gets a bit better with more of an emotional core near the end, but then it ends, with the story feeling extremely rushed and incomplete. I wish that this was a much bigger game with a whole world to explore, but it's a sort of awkward linear action-platformer that was turned into a subpar metroidvania.

All that said, I didn't dislike the game, I was just disappointed by it. If you are a big fan of metroidvanias and want something with great pixel art that's a quick experience, then I suppose I would recommend this. There's a lot of potential here, and I hope the devs are able to expand that in future games.

This seems to be a game primarily by artists. It looks beautiful, but so much of the crunch is lacking. It's also blatantly unfinished. I think it's insulting that they are charging $20 for what amounts to an unsatisfactory Act 1 and 2, with no Act 3 in sight. 

The best implemented mechanics are lifted from Megaman X and/or Zero. This is not inherently a bad thing, but when the only standout features of your game are not created by you, it casts a pall over the whole work. Several times I fell through platforms because their actual dimensions did not match the pixel art used for them. Someone on this dev team HATES i-frames. One of my deaths came from being cornered in a room with an enemy type that prevents you from rolling through them but also so large that I could not dash over him. He proceeded to stunlock me against a wall and kill me with zero recourse on my part. This is an egregious mistake in game design. Their solution to being unable to craft a tight mechanical experience? Make the game a cakewalk. As long as you play the game like a Metroidvania and do a modicum of exploration, you will rapidly outstrip most enemy encounters and the only challenge becomes pernicious enemy placement that impedes platforming (knocking you off ledges or small platforms) and the occasional deathtrap like I mentioned before. 

As for the story... "le religion bad" is probably the only thing I find more trite than "le corporation bad" and that's basically the whole thrust of this narrative. Maybe the planned ending would have saved it, but without any actual reveals I'm left to make my conclusions from what I actually have in front of me instead of a hypothetical finished game. The plot is extremely contrived and has no actual foreshadowing. The only reason you (the player) are waiting for a big reveal is your expectations built on meta-knowledge. All the heroes are virtuous, all the bad guys are scum. Then, about 60% of the way through, a switch flips and purely heroic characters receive a personality update that turns them into well-intentioned extremists who can't see that you represent a better way (allegedly). Their blind zealotry now gives you license to blast your way through them instead of acting like an adult and coordinating a response to the looming threat like you would want a hero to do if they were dealing with the characters from the beginning of the game. On the other hand, the "villain" receives no updates, he just continue to be mustache-twirling, hyper-cryptic a$$ hole from beginning to end, but the game wants to treat him like he has a point and is really sticking it to the zealots. Of course, we don't even know the truth because all that lore they dump on you in the beginning? Nothing. Zip. Nada. No real payoff for it, just hints and teases of unfulfilled plans.

Hard to beat for the price, highly recommend!

I've tried this game twice now, once at launch and just recently over about a week, and things just don't make sense.

1. Maths not mathing - a 50% damage reduction buff doesn't always reduce the incoming damage by 50%, it often reduces it by less. For example, I've seen 12 damage get cut to 8 but the 50% damage reduction buff is still used up. I assume this is because of how the damage equation is written but it feels like the game lying to me about what something does.

2. No respect for my time - The game spends so much time that could just be skipped over because it either A) adds nothing to the game or B) you heard this one many times before. 
Example for A: having to "drive" the stagecoach from the Field, to the Alter, then on to the Inn to spend your candles, pick you act and heroes. You're just watching the stagecoach drive between these places to go pick some options.
Example for B: Every time you start, you have to listen a little story bit for that act. Doesn't matter if you've tried and failed to finish act x 10 times in a row, you have to listen to the story bit again. Yes there are a few story bits for each act but after a few hours of play, I'm just over listening and want to get the next run up and going again.

3. What dose this buff/debuff do - There are a lot of buffs and debuffs in the game and not all of them are in the ALT window to explain what it does. Many times I look at a hero's ability, see a buff, look at the ALT screen and it's not there.

4. Healing and Damage - healing is now restricted to the target having HP at of below a percentage of their max hp, this is really not fun to interact with. DD1 let you heal whenever and enemies could regularly crit you for over 75% of your hero's max HP, so keeping people topped up made a lot of sense. Now, you can't do that. You have to sit and risk a big crit putting you on death's door because the game says no to healing minor wounds yet enemies can and will still crit your heroes for 75%, or more, of that hero's max hp. The occultist can heal over 50% of a hero's hp if he has three stacks of empowered buff and you get lucky on your rolls, but it can take two or three turns to get the occultist buffed properly. You can also land the heal, then get hit for the big crit and have all that effort essentially reset. I've had a character crit for 30 damage and their max hp is just 39.

What some might dismiss as only a lewd Yuri VN are missing out on what I consider an incredibly enjoyable and well-written story.  In fact, it may be placed among my favorites thus far (others including *Analogue: A Hate Story* and the *Fault* series, for reference). It's character and world building are simply fantastic. As expected, the growth of the main characters do a lot and the relationship form feels genuine and endearing. However, the side characters are just as well written and really give the world life. They are well defined without becoming generic tropes. Characters like Effie are lovable and make me laugh, yet there are just as great antagonists that you love to hate, and characters that are somewhere in between. 

The art is beautiful and befitting of the Victorian setting. Many backgrounds are given very distinct and almost noble looks while characters have a softer style yet with distinct coloring. Hearing the piano played in a classical style while reading in the befitting terminology of Victorian England did wonders to immersion. Though there are a few scenes where the author did mix some modern terminology as apparently the more accurate terms could be a bit... silly in comparison. So though they do stand out, it is understandable and very few at that.  That being said, the writing is still amazing and does well with descriptions and dialogue in a digestible manner. This is to say the VN allows the reader to immerse themselves while still leaving room to read between the lines and even some mystery. 

What have those particularly raunchy scenes themselves? Honestly they feel far less lewd in comparison and feel more in tune with the feelings of the characters. Though certainly spicy, they work far more as an amplification to the relationship/story rather than an out of place reward for the reader.

Rating: 10/10

Recommend? Very much so. I cannot stress on how great the writing is. Dialogue, exposition, world/character building. It is all just so good. So much so that I kind of wish I knew what happened with some other characters/plot lines but maybe that mystery is part of the appeal as well.

Pros:
+Genuine Dialogue
+Great Writing Overall
+Fantastic and Distinct Art
+Music and terminology suits the Victorian England Aesthetic
+Main and side characters feel well developed and unique.

Cons:
-A few modern words were thrown in (though it is understandable and very rare)
-The fates of some characters remain a mystery
-No male PNGs (for those that may want this)

Coming from a fan of Ashen, previous A44 game, it was the biggest pleasure playing their latest project.

The hate towards this game comes by 2 different kinds of people.
1. Radical monkey saying it is a woke DEI game
2. Jobless tryhards who think that if the game is similar to Dark Souls - it is bad because it is not Dark Souls.

The only so-called "woke" thing in this game is that we are playing a black female character that has zero to none muscles. How come these real gamers did not struggle playing Tomb Raider with a small woman as the MC? How come these real gamers did not struggle with playing as Ellie in The Last Of Us? Oh, she grew in the world of pain and is filled with hate? The main character here has the same type of struggle, seeking revenge and filled with hate and righteousness. 

Speaking of the second type of haters, it does not try to be Dark Souls, it has a biiiig pile of mechanics that make the game exceptionally fun to play. Think of Batman Arkham games, you can technically complete all Batman games by pressing leftclick, but it is not fun, fun comes from mixing up the strategies with ingame unnecessary mechanics. 

You can double jump, dash, use a rifle, a pistol, melee weapons with different animations for different purposes, grenades with different effects and you have A PET GOD that aids you in your journey. Different  "ultimate" abilites can be used for different playstyles, combinating the attack of this god with yours can grant you additional vampirism, stun effect and more. There more than plenty abilities for you to enjoy with the skill tree the game grants us.

Clingy movement? Have you seen your oh-so-cherished Dark Souls? IT IS THE SAME, LITERALLY, what does stand apart is the way story is present and how the characters are written.
It is common knowledge that story should be hidden and vague in this genre, here, the vagueness still exists, but the story is clear, understandable and has some very interesting twists that are being presented via visual storytelling like exploring temples, listening to villagers at the camp and talking to the God by your side. 

What I really enjoyed is the connection between the MC and the god. Some extremely enjoyable dialogues are presented mix with lurid, hilarious and personal topics. 

There is enough content in this game to chew on, more than 15 sidequests that are mostly "go kill the thing", but souls like games literally have the same thing. Unlike them, Flintlock mixes it up a bit, instead of destroying the army, you challenge a warrior for a duel, thus you have a bossfight. 

The world itself is extremely enjoyable to roam with sound design, and music standing out. A44 is really good at making you feel cozy at the safe spots and making you lock in outside of it. The game was rather challenging on the hard difficulty with bosses being menacing and truly hard to beat by the end of the game, even with nearly maxing out my character.

Please, do not listen to the hate, it is a great project, give this game a real chance.

A well deserved 7.5/10

Crystal Project, at core, is effectively "What if you took FF5 and brought it to modern day with all the qol and streamlining that entailed, but also expanded upon it with some MMO-inspired features"
Those MMO-inspired features being literally seeing your enemy's intent and upcoming actions, as well as being able to access a list of all their possible attacks while fighting them
It's a bit impressive to me that they manage to provide a challenge even despite giving you such powerful tools
And makes it all the more fun when certain enemies deny you the privilege of those tools
It is just incredibly elegant and I heavily recommend trying out the demo for a feel of what I mean.

Where it truly shines though, funnily enough, isn't even the classic turn based gameplay
The exploration.
The most interesting part of Crystal Project that makes it fairly unique by JRPG standards is the fact it is a 3D Voxel Platformer
And the entire world is constantly loaded
And you can achieve some VERY impressive things with the platforming if you are curious/stubborn enough 
It's EXTREMELY hard for me to go further into this without further spoilers, but again, the Demo demonstrates it exceptionally well.
VERY mild spoiler ahead...

To me, it's hilariously fitting from a meta perspective that you can actually bypass some of the Demo's restrictions and delve further into the game than "intended" just by... exploring and platforming enough.

And a lot of the time it just makes me wonder
"What the fuck."
"Surely the dev didn't actually intend for you to do this, right?"
But yes, the Demo is literally the first 10-20% of the game assuming you do it as intended and saves carry over to the actual game so please go play it.
If you like JRPGs, FFV or even just exploration and finding secrets in video games at all, please give it a shot.

Also, shoutout to the dev for having some INCREDIBLE assist and challenge options, as well as decent modding tools,
The Final Fantasy Project Overhaul in particular outright skips the middle man and turns the game into a full-on FF gameplay-wise while adding various story elements and cameos that make it feel like a genuinely impressive fangame and love letter to the older FFs.
I heavily recommend it for a second or third playthrough.

[h1]First 10 Hours Impressions[/h1]
________________________________________
[h2]The Short:[/h2]
After 10 hours, this game has really impressed me. The concept is fascinating, the art style captivating, and Ben Prunty’s soundtrack is phenomenal, it's something you can actively tune into, not just background noise. While I still stand by some of my initial impressions, I agree it could benefit from a slower pace. As a newcomer, it felt messy, with a lack of information that left me feeling out of control. Others may also struggle with the opposite, too much info at once. But as I’ve played more, I’m better at planning ahead and overcoming those early struggles.

[h2]The Long:[/h2]
[h3](And hyper-specific yap, please appreciate this team)[/h3]
[i]The first things I will say are that it’s impressive to see a small studio execute such a competent project. I’ve actively looked for ways to break this game, and yes, I’ve found some issues - but I went looking. The devs are very active, responsive, and clearly care a great deal about this. I’m really hoping it gets the recognition it deserves.[/i]

[h3]Art Direction and Visual Style[/h3]
I’m clearly smitten by the art direction here. It’s rare to see a dystopian sci-fi game that doesn’t stick to the same washed-out, bleak visuals I’m used to. The solarpunk angle is a refreshing departure. The game doesn’t swing too dark or go for pure optimism but lands somewhere in the middle. There’s hope, but it’s grounded. The art captures that balance perfectly, never losing its sense of atmosphere.

The tile map immediately stands out. Buildings have subtle animations that make the world feel alive. Each biome has a distinct look and feel, serving more than just aesthetic purposes. The way the environments are woven into gameplay mechanics is impressive. What you see directly influences how you build, manage resources, and handle challenges.

I find myself genuinely captivated by the vision the developers are presenting. The game rejects the tired, oppressive palettes that have become synonymous with the genre and leans into solarpunk, an emerging concept. It strikes a rare balance between hope and realism, avoiding the pitfalls of grim dystopia or unrealistic utopia. The tile map’s vibrancy and detail elevate the entire experience, making the world feel like an active participant in the story.

The visual details color shifts between tiles and the visuals that emerge during key story moments are deliberate and thoughtfully crafted, enhancing both the narrative and the overall atmosphere.

[h3]Narrative and Dialogue[/h3]
There were a few moments throughout the story and some of the narrative events where the dialogue and character reactions didn’t quite match how real people might speak or respond. At times, it felt a bit exaggerated, which created a bit of a disconnect with the otherwise grounded tone and themes of the game.

They remind me of Frostpunk, but taken further. These moments invest you in the lives of the people in your colony. They add depth and meaning to the experience, making the world feel more alive and personal. I’m excited to see how this mechanic evolves in future.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
One area for improvement is the game’s pacing of information delivery. It often swings between overwhelming with too many details while also leaving you underprepared for key challenges, especially impacting strategy and planning.

The game’s core mechanics are intriguing, and there’s a real sense of accomplishment when solving complex problems. However, there were moments when I felt unprepared for certain gameplay elements, which disrupted the flow. A more gradual introduction to mechanics would help players absorb information at a manageable pace, easing the learning curve, particularly for newcomers.

This is particularly evident when managing development and supply chains. For example, placing a water pump might seem straightforward, but overlooking production limits or the range of other structures can quickly lead to a softlock.

A small mistake can snowball into a problem you can’t recover from due to a lack of tools to address it. For instance, during my second playthrough, I placed a water pump in a location that seemed fine. However, I didn’t realize the pump’s finite production capacity would require it to be demolished eventually. When that happened, I had already built structures around it. The pump ended up out of range of my material waste storage and food production buildings, causing an unrecoverable situation.

The lack of any clear indication that demolished buildings would require waste storage left me stuck, and with only a limited number of prefabs left, recovery was impossible. Small missteps like this can disrupt the flow of the game, making it hard to get back on track. In contrast, games like Anno handle challenge progression well by gradually introducing mechanics and allowing players to recover from mistakes without significant setbacks.

[h3]UI and Feedback[/h3]
The UI could use some refinement to better communicate key information. While the art style adds to the game’s atmosphere, important gameplay details often feel unclear. For example, hovering over the demolish button doesn’t indicate that demolishing a building will leave waste behind, which requires another building to clear it. This lack of clarity can lead to mistakes, as mentioned earlier.

Character tooltips, while functional, could provide more depth. Traits often have generic descriptions that don’t offer actionable insights. Adding more context or feedback about how traits affect characters would make managing them feel more intuitive.

The influence system during narrative events also needs more clarity. It’s not always clear how influence is calculated or why you failed an influence check. Understanding these systems would help players feel more in control of their decisions.

The task management system could also be more engaging. Currently, it’s reduced to slapping the highest-level character onto a task, making it feel repetitive. Adding more layers of depth, like considering traits, skills, and past performance, would make this system more dynamic.

There are also occasional UI quirks, like buildings showing red icons even when they should be working fine. Toggling them off and on typically resolves this, but it’s a minor frustration.

[h3]Music and Sound[/h3]
Ben Prunty’s music is phenomenal here and I found myself actively tuning into it regularly. The music complements the art direction and enhances the emotional tone of the world. The sound design is minimalistic and purposeful, which I deeply appreciate. Nothing feels intrusive or grating.

The ambient sounds of the world are also subtle but effective, with soft winds and a faint electronic hum that fits the game’s setting perfectly. These sounds help make the environment feel alive without drawing attention to themselves.

The UI sounds are clean, with a satisfying, futuristic chirp when interacting with the interface. Each tile has its own subtle sound when clicked, adding another layer of immersion. Small details like the sound a completed building makes create a cohesive, polished experience.

[h3]Closing Thoughts[/h3]
In conclusion, this game shines with its charm, unique visuals, and seamless blend of art and mechanics. While it has its flaws, they’re far outweighed by its strengths, and I’m excited to see how it evolves.

I genuinely believe this will become a cornerstone title in the solarpunk genre. As someone who’s followed both Cyberpunk and Solarpunk, this is one of the few titles that has successfully merged technology and nature into a cohesive vision. It’s clear the devs are passionate about their creation, and I’m excited to see how it evolves in future updates.

Pros:
No major bugs (only one cut-off button).
Nice art style.
Interesting approach with a turn-based city builder.
Character editor is fun.


Cons:
The game asks you to make decisions before you even know what they’re about, which feels wrong.

The balancing is off: building space is tight due to the tile system. I often had to place multiple buildings because others were out of range, not because there was actual demand.

The UI looks cool but doesn’t work well for me. The UI color palette is too close to the background, so elements blend in. Also, the dialog “button” is a tiny triangle—please just let me left-click to skip dialogs, especially when there’s no choice to make.

The character art style doesn’t match the rest of the game. It feels like it comes from an asset pack and doesn’t fit.


Feedback:
It feels like the developers’ focus is off. There’s a lot of emphasis on short character scenes, while city-builder features and polishing are lacking.

For example, I sometimes struggle to distinguish buildings. An option to overlay icons would help. There are icons in the building menu, but they’re not really explained or self-explanatory. Also, why do I need multiple clicks to remove demolished buildings—even when I placed a building specifically for that?

On the other hand, it seems a lot of dev time went into the story building scenes and the possibility to make decisions, but those decisions don’t feel very meaningful.

Another odd thing is how limited th buildings supply and storages are. The groundwater pump’s supply runs out very quickly, but you can just remove it and build a new one.

Why is the recommended age 16? From what I’ve seen, it could be 6 or 12. xD

I’m an academic and generally fine in English, but I still had to look up some words. The language can be quite difficult—especially for non-native speakers. The dialogs are fine, but the game would be much more accessible if you supported additional languages.


Recommendation:
If you like city builders, you can give it a try.

However, I fear this game might stall in Early Access. Sales seem low, and considering the team size and how long this version took, I’m not sure it makes financial sense to continue development.

Would I buy it again? Not at this price.
Will I play it again? Probably yes—but I’ll wait for the next 2–3 major updates (hopefully they arrive).

Id love to see some sort of unique ability or trait for each frame, eg activate a shield, teleport/jump a short distance, unique wierd weapons. 2. The cooldowns on abilities feel a bit long, particularly with enemies coming constantly. I think it would be easier to manage them if some enemies dropped cooldown reducing items, if enemies came in waves, or if there was a way to temporarily escape from enemies while your abilities cool down. 
3. I enjoy a good simple top down shooter, and I understand if it is out of scope, but I think a bit more of a story to string the missions together would be nice. I don't need 4k cutscenes or anything, but some recurrent NPCs talking about the missions and occasionally showing up as allies in missions would liven up things a bit.
4. I think more mission types would be nice, particularly some without infinite enemies, or where you can avoid/disable the reinforcements. Throw in a heavily defended radio relay to destroy, scanners to avoid, or a mini boss to defeat that will disable reinforcements. 
5. I want bigger railguns, give me a mech or a tank with a ridiculous spinal mount railgun that has to run and hide while the big gun is recharging.

La carte est vaste, variée et propose plusieurs biomes intéressants. Qu’il s’agisse de progresser dans la quête principale ou de dénicher des coffres cachés, on se retrouve souvent à chercher le bon chemin, ce qui renforce le plaisir de l’exploration. L’alchimie générale fonctionne très bien et parcourir la map est vraiment agréable.

❌ Points négatifs :

🧳 Inventaire frustrant
L’inventaire se remplit extrêmement vite d’armes secondaires inutiles, obtenues toutes les trois secondes sur les ennemis. La plupart doivent être jetées manuellement une par une. Un PNJ permet plus tard de détruire les armes en masse, mais sans vraie récompense à la clé.
De plus, pas de revente possible, ce qui est dommage. Cela reste un défaut mineur mais entraîne des sessions de tri un peu pénibles pour les joueurs maniaques.

📍 Téléportation mal pensée
Deux systèmes coexistent :

Des PNJ répartis sur la carte qui activent des points de téléportation fixes (OK).

Les points de sauvegarde, qui ne permettent que de faire un aller-retour entre le château et la salle du trône, sans pouvoir choisir librement son point de retour. Résultat : on doit souvent faire un détour inutile. On finit par s’y habituer, mais ce n’est vraiment pas pratique.

🎯 Conclusion :

Un excellent metroidvania, avec un gameplay fun, une bonne difficulté et une exploration plaisante. Quelques défauts dans la gestion de l’inventaire et de la téléportation, mais rien qui gâche réellement l’expérience globale.

👉 Je recommande chaudement, surtout aux amateurs du genre.

👍 Note personnelle : 8/10

I'm going to try to leave some constructive criticism because I was drawn to the concept and the art of this game and I think those two things are pretty good. I genuinely think it's super cute. Unfortunately, that's where the good things end. I'll leave a list of things that are a bit frustrating when playing.

The big:
- There's very little content. I unlocked everything in the entire game within about one day of owning it. 
For an "incremental afk game" that you're supposed to leave on all the time to me feels like there's not enough to do.

- The's effectively no game design. Getting new washers and dryers is arbitrary because the most money you get is from returning the clothes to the customers (which makes sense logically) / the ironing board (which makes less sense) and it trivializes how much you get from the washers and dryers, even the higher tiered ones (which cost much more than the ironing board). No clue why the washers and dryers give you money either since only your employees are interacting with them. Unlocking new washers and dryers at the beginning of the game is also extremely punishing for no reason. Your only panda worker until you save $13,000 is extremely slow and will be limited to about 3 washers and dryers and you have to buy 5 of a set to get unlock the next tier. Anything more no matter how efficiently you place them for pathing they won't be used. The vending machines don't make any sense whatsoever and buying one is extremely punishing and stops your character from moving and making more money (the only thing to do in the game) for a very long time and barely compensates you for it no matter how expensive the vending machine is.

- The pandas are lifeless, especially the "customers" if you can even call them that. For starters random pandas that look exactly like yours fill the street in front of you just walking / running back and forth which is great. The thing that doesn't make sense is A. they don't interact with your shop or any other shop they just walk in one direction and then despawn when they're off screen and B. none of them are wearing clothes? When I bought the game and saw the pandas running around on the Steam store page I thought the customers would be interacting with the laundromat like a typical one (where I live anyway) and you would serve them and make them happy, but it's only your employees. The laundry is just in an unlimited pile and the only limit is how fast your pandas can take it out of the basket and put it in a washer.

- The art is 100% cute, but there's hardly any of it. The most interesting looking part of the game is the street and you can't interact with it or the pandas walking around in any way and a lot of it is often obscured by clouds. The washer and dryers are cute, but they're all the same of two models that have been recolored and I think in the buy menu the washers and dryers are actually backwards for the front load models.

The small and annoying:

- There is guaranteed at least one game breaking bug in the game where your panda will get stuck on a washer, dryer, or ironing board and won't be able to move at all if you place them in the wrong spot. You sometimes won't know if your spot is bad for quite awhile so if you get up after placing one in the wrong place your panda could be stuck for hours.

- There's only one place to get and return clothes and the location of them for trying to set up an aesthetically pleasing shop is kind of bad. It's also terrible for pathing.

- Your first panda has some pretty serious ADHD. This is harder to figure out about or care after you get more, but watching the first and slowest guy is very annoying. He will walk all the way across the map to put clothes in a dryer that is nowhere near the washer they just came out of. The way that he queues tasks seems to be strictly in order of when they get done, including the dryers and ironing boards somehow. Instead of choosing a dryer or ironing board that's available the game logic seems to pick the one that was done with its task first.

- I think it says there are 10 tracks on the Steam store page but at most I heard one or two, so I'm not sure if you have to buy the additional game sound track to hear them in the game in the game or something.

- Pathing simply does not function well. No matter how you set up your washers and dryers your panda will choose an absolutely absurd route to take most of the time. If you pay any attention to the game and you want to make things a little better or easier for him it just won't work. Don't bother trying.

- The decorations are sparse and kind of uninteresting. I haven't bought a few of them but most of them have no function whatsoever, which would be fine if there was more to do in the game. I was hoping that the laundry baskets would help my panda somehow or make taking things out of the dryer faster, but they just sit there on top of the dryer.

- The lack of interaction at all with the customers / the pandas in the street made me sad. I was thinking the vending machines were for them or something, but they just walk. Lots of little things like that in the game don't really make any sense to me.

- The camera movement is not good. It's extremely slow and feels kind of buggy, especially with the mouse.

TL;DR: Iron Oath and Crosstails had a baby: this game. But it inherited all the worst characteristics of both parents. Go play either parent game instead, or any other hundreds of better TRPGs instead.

- Demo was removed

I’ve been a gamer since the early 90’s and to date, the Lunar series is my pick for the best RPGs of all time – not something I say lightly.  These games are a masterclass in character development, music, and storytelling.  It’s so easy to get attached to these characters and they’ve never fully left my mind since the first time I played the series back in 1999 and 2000.

That said, the games follow the traditional formula of JRPGs started in the first Dragon Quest games, so you likely won’t find anything particularly innovative in terms of gameplay here.  These games would largely appeal to those who like JRPGs, anime, or just a good story.  If, like me, you fall into all 3 of those categories, then these are a no brainer to buy.

The crown jewel of this collection has to be Lunar 2, which at the time of writing this review sees its first release in a quarter century.  I’m not sure what the legal situation was surrounding the game, but it was definitely on the verge of fading into obscurity, so GungHo deserves a lot of praise for saving it.  It’s a shame it was locked away for so long because it is one of the best examples of a video game sequel I’ve ever played.  It not only justifies its existence in the lore, but meaningfully expands and enhances the original, ups the stakes and most importantly, respects your time with having played the first (references, original plot points logically flowing into the next installment, etc.)  Think Terminator 2 if you’re a movie fan – it’s that good.

I presume they were forced to redub the cutscenes likely because of that legal situation.  The new dub is good, but the original dub was phenomenal.  The absence of Jenny Stigile’s singing and John Truitt’s Ghaleon is most noticeable.  When you play these, I’d highly recommend checking out the original cutscenes on YouTube and see if you agree.  John has one of the best evil laughs I’ve ever heard – it stayed in my head for 25 years!  There’s also a few of the more subtle elements removed from the scenes like the ticking clock when Ghaelon is introduced and the sad piano theme in one of the final cutscenes that I don’t know why they cut as they added to the overall feeling and filled in the empty space.

All that aside, it’s such a joy to be able to play these games again after so long – I can’t recommend them enough!

我们至少是四个人一起玩，各司其职，我负责运营和规划，朋友负责科研制作，另外两个朋友都负责钓鱼，只钓鱼从早钓到晚。每次赶海回来，他们都会带着非常夸张的一船货物回来，因此这里就不得不说游戏的一个机制：游戏的晚上时间段是无限的，不会自己结束，除非睡觉，其次游戏没有耐力，因此，肝一点的话，其实第一天就能靠钓鱼，直接收入百万（这是我们后知后觉的东西）。差不多我们四个人天天疯狂肝，每天都是收益最大化，提前准备节日等，冬季还没过，我们游戏内容就已经打完了。等待未来的继续更新吧。

差评仅对于新出的罗马小镇，罗马地图的任务系统完全打破了前两张地图的基础，但是朋友，完全没有的任务指引（包括哪里有任务，以及任务道具可以在哪里获得，甚至部分任务刷新都需要结束当日），可能为了避免跳出地图而设置到处都是的空气墙（前两张地图完全没有，所看即所及），任务的奖励居然只有新的地区解锁或者对功能的补全（比如种子店先解锁水壶和锄具，要再完成任务才能解锁种子购买），而当我解锁店铺之后，我甚至一直找不到购买商品的地方只能去买种子（这里还要批评居然需要两一个半锄头才能开辟一整块田，以及一桶水壶甚至不够浇灌一半的田的同时水井的位置又恰好在所有田中最远）。而且在解锁店铺之后我还需要将免费送的收银台打包来避免每天的额外消费。而且矿石和野花（香料）的设定弊端完全没有修正，本身就小的背包栏位却需要装各种各样的物品，而且这些物品还只能一个一个的拾取和丢弃，更重要的是我在费时费力的收集并花费高价购买相关的设施之后，他所获得的利润甚至不如我直接购买酒或者钓鱼（钓的鱼也只能一个一个拿而且背包小也是老问题了），导致这个事务的存在就是为了成就（以及罗马地图的费时任务）。在相较于之前的游玩体验中，罗马小镇对我的反馈几乎全是负面的，我费心费力的工作只为了获得我前两张图一开始就有的功能而几乎没有任何的额外收获，地图设置各种各样的拐角以及空气墙又导致我每次找一个任务或者交易地点都要更长的时间。
总之，如果没有绝对的闲情雅致或者一起玩的朋友，不要选罗马地图（甚至挡位都只有三个，难道出第四张图的话我居然需要把我之前的努力删掉一份吗？）

[h1] 요하네 더 스파이어.환일의 요하네로 즐기는 매우 순한맛의 슬더스 [/h1]

환일의 요하네 - NUMAZU in the MIRAGE - 는 인티크리에이츠에서 나온  환일의 요하네-BLAZE in the DEEPBLUE-와 같이 비슷한 시기에 나온 요하네 IP의 게임이다. 인티크리에이츠에서 나온 게임이 액션/메트로배니아 장르의 게임이 었다면 Bexide에서 만든 이 게임은 로그라이트/덱빌딩 게임이다. 

게임은 요하네의 친구들이 갑자기 몸이 안좋아지는데 이를 통해 거울 세계를 들어가면서 원인을 알게되고 그에 따른 스토리를 해결해나간다는 이야기이다. 게임은 더빙이 기본적으로 되어있긴 한데, 초반 인트로 때에는 풀더빙이 되어있으면서, 정작 메인스토리 넘어갈 때는 더빙이 안되어있었던게 아쉬웠다. 그래도 생각했던 것보다 스토리 전개가 탄탄해서 좋았던 게임이었는데, 원래 이 게임이 한글지원을 안해서 그냥 영어로 스토리를 보고 있었는데. 25년 한글날에 한글패치가 추가되었다. 그래서 좀 더 스토리에 집중할 수 있었고, 원래 이 게임을 구매하려고 했다가 한글 미지원이라 게임 구매를 꺼렸던 사람들은 이번에 구매하면 될 것 같다. 

게임은 기본적으로 노멀난이도이고 게임은 장르에서 가장 유명한 게임인 슬레이 더 스파이어의 하위난이도 모드라고 생각하면된다. 그래서 해당 장르를 잘하는 사람들에게는 게임이 많이 쉽다고 느낄 것이다. 근데 노멀난이도가 최고 높은 난이도이고 나머지인 이지랑 베리이지모드는 게임의 난이도를 더  쉽게 만들어주기 때문에 로그라이트 덱 빌딩이 처음인 유저들은 입문용으로 플레이하기 적당하다고 생각한다. 아마 장르 고수분들은 그닥 흥미를 못느낄 수도 있을 법 한데 슬더스의 승천난이도 같이 게임을 어렵게 하는 요소가 전혀 없기 때문에 어려운 것을 찾는 분들에게는 추천하는 게임은 아니지만 정말 가벼운 난이도라 머리식힘용으로 혹은 킬링타임용으로 정말 즐기기 괜찮은 게임이라고 생각한다.

총 4라운드로 진행되며, 3라운드까지는 그냥 일반적인 플레이고 4라운드에서 최종보스전을 진행하는데 4라운드에는 휴식처 한 곳 그리고 갈랫길로 상점과 보물상자 이후 엘리트몹 그 후 휴식처를 지나 최종보스전을 진행하게 된다.
게임은 처음에 밸런스모드로 진행을 하게 되지만 이후에 파워모드가 추가되는데, 요하네가 사용하게 되는 덱 풀이 바뀌게 된다. 밸런스는 방어형 카드들도 꽤 많이 나오고, 파워타입은 좀 더 공격적인 카드들이 많이 나온다. 그래서 두 플레이 모드를 진행해보고 자기가 더 재밌는 빌드를 세울 곳이 어디인지 판단하고 게임을 진행하면 되는데, 생각보다 캐주얼한 난이도임에도 불구하고 장르 특징을 정말 잘 녹여놔서 베리이지로 플레이해도 그 난이도의 맛이 있었고, 노멀난이도에서도 재미를 느낄 수 있었다.

빡센 덱빌딩 게임을 찾는다면 그렇게 추천하는 게임은 아니지만 간단하게 덱빌딩 게임을 즐기고 싶은 분들 혹은 러브리아브 요하네 IP를 좋아하는 사람들에겐 괜찮은 게임이 아닌가라는 생각이든다. 아마 IP 팬 중에 이러한 로그라이트/덱빌딩 게임에 익숙한 사람이 많지 않을 것을 대비해서 난이도를 쉽게 낸거 같은데 그 쉬운 난이도에서도 요하네 만의 맛을 잘 녹여놓았기 때문에 간단하게 덱빌딩 게임을 즐긴다면 괜찮은 선택지가 되지 않을까란 생각이든다.' 무엇보다도 이제 한글 지원도 되니까 더 재밌게 플레이할 수 있지 않을까라는 생각이든다.

여담) 도전과제는 그냥 묵묵히 플레이하면 다 할 수 있는데, 문제가 되는것이 모든 의뢰 1회씩 해보기 인데 이게 RNG라 운이 나쁘면 정말 오래해야할 수도 있다. 토론창 보니까 100시간을 했는데도 의뢰 하나가 안나와서 100% 못했다는 사람도 나오더라... 필자는 버거 10회, 치카카드 3회가 죽어도 안나오다가 막판에 두개가 한꺼번에 떠서 이번에 100% 달성할 수 있었다. RNG이므로 도과 100% 달성시간...자신의 운을 시험해보자....

Hyperbeat is a rhythm game masterpiece. From start to finish, I was transfixed by every aspect - from music to gameplay to even story (!).

The soundtrack is all original, and it's fantastic enough that I want to listen to it even out of game (please let me buy it!). It's a collection of 20 tracks, organised into 4 "chapters" with 5 songs each. They're all electronic music (sorry for being vague, genre nerds) and each has a different vibe that reflects the character the chart represents.

The game nails the other key ingredient, the rhythm gameplay. This is not another one of the 4 button rhythm games that has you tapping and holding buttons to the beat. Instead, it controls similarly to a rail shooter like Space Harrier or Star Fox - Rez might be the most relevant comparison here, given the similar vibe - flying through abstract tunnel environments. 

Hyperbeat's equivalent of the stream of notes dropping down from the top of the screen takes the form of circular targets streaming down the tunnel towards and reaching your screen in time to the beat. You tend to stay on the outer edge of the tunnel unless you need to cross suddenly from one side to another, making it almost reminsicent of Tempest and its descendents (I think mostly of Space Giraffe in this regard). I'm also reminded of the way osu! plays and in fact one of the preferred control methods to play that game, tablet, is also supported here.

Where the genius of Hyperbeat really stands out to me is scoring. Many rhythm games stick to taps and hold notes, which is not in itself a bad thing. However, as a casual enjoyer of rhythm games with an absolute lack of rhythm, I tend towards the lower difficulties, and these are often unengaging because the solution to making a song easier to play through tends to be just having fewer notes. This leads to sections requiring very few button presses and really disrupts the process of getting into a flow state, which is where I think good rhythm games really shine (and even games which aren't technically rhythm games but heavily incorporate music into the gameplay, such as Rez).

Hyperbeat avoids falling prey to this issue by having different types of notes. One kind scores you based on how close to the center you fly through it, one kind scores based on your timing of a swipe or button press, one kind based on both accuracy and timing, and some notes award the full points value just by flying through them. There also sustain (hold) versions of these. The more strictly scored notes tend to show up in higher quantity on the harder songs and higher difficulties.

This allows even the easiest songs to feel rhythmic and engaging, without the awkward breaks between notes of a traditional button-tapping kind of rhythm game, as all you need to do is touch the notes to be scored and rewarded with a satisfying hit sound to the beat of the song.

The game also supports the creation of custom beatmaps and while I haven't yet played any, I'd love to see the community grow so that the great gameplay can be leveraged for more and more songs.

To my surprise, I enjoyed the story, which definitely isn't at the top of my list of expecations when buying a rhythm game. Since it's short and sweet, I won't delve into it and spoil anything, but it's a bit of a vague and open to interpration kind of story with an uplifting message (at least, I thought so). There are a handful of characters which each have their own particular way of speaking and I thoroughly enjoyed finding out about each character. Though dialogue is voiced entirely by text to speech, it didn't detract from the game for me. If anything, it enhanced the "weird PS2 game you've never heard of" vibe.

All in all, this is a must-have for even the most casual of rhythm game players. It's worth checking out even if you're not interested in rhythm games typically, but like playing weird and experimental stuff like Rez,

명작 퍼즐 게임 시리즈인 "모뉴먼트 밸리 시리즈" 의 3번째 작품이자, 같은 시리즈 내 이전 작품들과 비교해 다양한 기믹을 넣으려는 시도가 보이는 작품.

Monument Valley 3 는 착시를 기반으로 한 시각적 연출과 퍼즐들을 기반으로 하는 모뉴먼트 밸리 시리즈의 세 번째 게임으로, 비주얼 면에서는 절대로 실망시킨 적이 없는 시리즈의 최신 작품답게 여전히 시각적 면모가 뛰어난 게임이다. 1편과 2편 모두 해 본 사람이라면 알겠지만, 2편으로 넘어오면서 더 화사하고 다양한 색채를 사용해서 플레이어가 화면을 보는 맛을 더 높여 주었는데, 3편 또한 시각적 면에서 한 번 더 발전한 면을 보인다. 2편과 다르게 살짝 더 긴 컷씬들을 넣어 놓아서 화면을 감상하는 재미가 올라갔고, 게임의 배경이 바다를 떠돌아다니며 등대를 수리하는 스토리인 만큼, "정화되지 않은 바다" 와 "배가 다니기 안전한 바다" 가 붉은색 / 흰색 + 검은색 그리고 파란색 / 초록색으로 확연한 차이를 보여서 색감 면에서는 2편만큼 만족스러웠다. 특히 게임의 후반부에는 바다가 아니라 밀밭이 나오면서 이와 관련된 퍼즐 기믹 및 이동 애니메이션이 나오는데, 해당 스테이지가 정말 아름답게 표현되어 있어서 마음에 들었다. 시각적인 면 말고도 퍼즐 관련 기믹도 조금 더 늘어났는데, 이전 문장에서 적은 밀밭 관련 기믹 말고도 메인 기믹 중 하나로 나오는 건 바로 바다 위를 항해하는 배 관련 기믹이다. 전작에서 볼 수 있었던 토템이 이번에는 작은 돛단배 형태로 나오며, 주인공이 이 위에 탑승하면 터치 & 드래그 형식으로 배를 조작할 수 있다. 게임의 테마가 착시인 만큼, 배의 위치를 오묘하게 배치하면 기하학적으로 불가능한 이동 경로를 만들어 낼 수도 있고, 아무래도 이전 작품에서는 보이지 않았던 새로운 기믹인 만큼 이와 관련된 시각적 연출들을 보는 맛이 있었다. 다만 이 드래그 형식의 조작이 생각보다 그리 편하지는 않았는데, 방향키가 아닌 화면 홀드 + 드래그 방식은 모바일 게임에서 더 많이 사용하는 조작인 만큼, PC로 이 조작을 행하는 게 어색하게 느껴졌으며 조작이 원하는 대로 되지 않는 순간도 종종 발생하였다. 그래도 게임이 고도의 컨트롤을 요구하는 게임은 아닌 만큼, 여기서 느낀 불쾌감은 그리 크지 않았으며 게임에 대한 몰입을 방해하지는 않았다.

시각적인 면에 대해서는 극찬을 남겼지만, 퍼즐의 퀄리티 및 스토리 면에서는 비주얼만큼 발전하였다고 보기에는 애매하다. 전자의 경우, 당연히 퍼즐을 플레이어에게 보여주는 형태는 아름답지만, 퍼즐의 난이도는 오히려 이전 작들보다 더 내려갔다고 생각한다. 물론 모뉴먼트 밸리 시리즈가 고난이도의 퍼즐로 승부하는 게임 시리즈는 아니지만, 1편의 마지막 스테이지는 어느 정도는 생각을 해야 해결할 수 있었으며, 해당 게임의 추가 스테이지 또한 마지막 부분에는 약간은 어려운 부분들이 있었다. 반면에 이번 게임에서는 마지막까지 생각을 요구하는 스테이지는 나오지 않았고, 그저 "어 이거 그냥 물 흐르듯이 너무 자연스레 진행되는데?" 라는 생각이 더 많이 들었다. 후자의 경우, 스토리가 별로라는 건 아니며, 오히려 몇몇 스토리 위주 게임들보다는 기승전결이 완벽하고 주인공에게 닥치는 위기와 고난의 극복 - 부서진 등대를 복원하면서 스승과의 이별을 받아들이고 바다를 더 안전한 곳으로 만들어 가는 모습 - 은 스토리 내 안정적으로 녹아 들어갔다. 다만 1편에서 결말을 통해 주인공의 서사를 확실하게 자리잡고 플레이어에게 충격을 주는 결말이나, 2편에서 (스토리의 충격은 덜 하더라도) 나름 자녀가 성장하는 이야기를 밝은 톤으로 그려냈다면, 이번 작품의 경우 스토리의 퀄리티에는 문제가 없었으나 이야기의 흐름이 몇몇 부분에서는 너무 작위적으로 느껴져서 개인적인 취향과는 별로 맞지 않았다. 물론, 모뉴먼트 밸리 1편이 스토리 편에서는 너무 고점을 찍어서 이후 나온 같은 시리즈의 다른 작품들이 이보다 더 흥미로운 스토리를 낼 수 없었다는 생각이 들었기에, 스토리 관련에서 불만을 느꼈음에도 이 게임에 비추천을 남길 정도라는 생각은 들지 않았다. 사실 퍼즐의 퀄리티나 스토리보다 더 큰 의아함을 느낀 건 가격인데, 이전 게임들도 가격 대비 플레이타임이 좋은 게임은 아니었으나, 이번 작품의 경우 가격이 거의 2배가 올랐음에도 플레이타임은 거의 비슷하기 때문이다. 물론 12월 3일에 무료 컨텐츠 추가 관련 공지를 하였으며 이를 통해 가격 상승이 납득이 될 수 있다는 행복회로를 돌릴 수도 있으나, 이전 작품들 모두 추가 업데이트를 통해 여러 개의 스테이지가 추가되었음에도 불구하고 플레이타임이 크게 늘어나지 않았다는 걸 생각하면, 그렇게까지 획기적인 업데이트가 되지는 않을 것이라고 생각한다.


결론적으로, 모뉴먼트 밸리 시리즈의 이전 작품들과 거의 비슷한 맛 + 약간의 이색적인 조미료를 쳐 놓은 맛을 지니고 있으며, 파격적인 발전을 보이는 게임은 아니지만 나처럼 해당 시리즈에 애정이 있으며 전작들을 재미있게 해 왔다면, 이번 작품에서도 화면을 바라보며 잔잔하게 눈과 마음을 힐링할 수 있기에 추천. 플레이타임의 경우 이전 작들처럼 1.5 ~ 2 시간이면 모든 퍼즐을 해결할 수 있기에, 가격 대비 플레이타임은 많이 아쉬운 게임이다. 만약 구매를 할 것이라면, 할인을 할 때 1편부터 3편까지 묶어 놓은 콜렉션 번들을 구매해서 돈을 조금이라도 더 절약할 수 있도록 하자.

여담) 스팀 업적의 경우 대부분 스테이지 진행만 해도 딸 수 있지만, 3편의 경우 1편과 2편과는 다르게 스테이지를 완료해도 초기화 되지 않는 요소들이 있기에 실수로 놓친다면 게임 초기화를 해야 딸 수 있는 업적들이 존재한다. 이렇게 놓칠 수 있는 업적 모두 3번째 스테이지에 존재하며, 스팀 가이드에 이러한 업적 관련 가이드가 있으니 업적 100% 를 좋아한다면 가이드를 보면서 따는 걸 권장한다.

[스토리]

황폐한 도시 속 “ICEY”는 천천히 문을 열고 길을 나선다. 왜 도심이 이토록 폐허가 되었는지도, 자신이 어디로 향하고 있는지도 모른 채, 그저 발걸음을 옮기는 소녀는 의문의 로봇들과 조우한다. 모습을 드러낸 정체불명의 로봇들은 이유도 없이 소녀를 향해 공격을 퍼붓는다. 이에 질세라 ICEY도 검을 휘두르며 차가운 고철 덩어리들을 하나씩 베어넘긴다. 소녀는 계속해서 조우하는 로봇들을 처치하며 안개가 옅게 낀 숲을 돌파한다. 

사방이 독극물로 가득 찬 호수와 낭떠러지로 둘러싸인 위험한 구역을 지나며, 계속해서 전진하는 ICEY. 그 끝에서 그녀는 다리 위에서 인간형 로봇과 대면한다. 양 팔이 총으로 개조된 그 로봇은 처음 마주했던 소형 로봇들과는 비교할 수 없을 만큼 강력하게 공격을 퍼붓기 시작한다. ICEY는 물러서지 않고 검을 휘둘렀고, 전세가 기울었는지 로봇은 공격을 멈추고 짙은 구름이 깔린 밤하늘로 도망치듯 날아가 버린다.

ICEY가 조심스레 다리를 건너려던 찰나, 갑작스레 나타난 인간형 로봇의 기습 공격에 의해 다리를 파괴한다. 그렇게 ICEY는 칠흑같은 어둠속으로 떨어지게 되는데..

장점

[b]반발 심리를 잘 이용한 메타픽션 요소[/b]

필자가 이전에 플레이해본 메타픽션 게임은 OneShot이 유일하다. 다만 두 작품을 모두 즐겨본 입장에서 느낀 점은, 메타픽션적 장치를 활용했다는 공통점에도 불구하고 플레이 방식에서 미묘한 차이가 존재한다는 것이다. OneShot에서는 플레이어가 "니코"라는 캐릭터와 함께 문제를 해결하며 협력 관계를 형성한다. 플레이어와 니코는 서로 의논하고 공감하며, 마치 한 팀처럼 행동하는 느낌이 강하다. 반면 ICEY에서는 플레이어블 캐릭터인 "ICEY"가 따로 존재하고, 상호작용의 대상은 "내레이터"라는 제3의 존재다.

이 차이로 인해 두 게임이 주는 감정적 경험이 완전히 달라진다. OneShot이 협동과 공감을 통해 서사를 완성한다면, ICEY는 명령과 반항의 대립을 중심으로 전개된다. 내레이터의 일방적인 지시를 따르거나, 반대로 무시하고 거부하는 플레이가 가능하다는 점이 ICEY만의 독특한 재미 포인트다. 특히 반항적인 선택을 할 때마다 내레이터가 격한 반응을 보이거나 멘트를 던지는 구간들은, 플레이어가 게임의 틀을 벗어났다는 느낌을 극대화시킨다.

내레이터에게 반항하는 행동들은 대부분 도전과제의 형태로 구현되어 있다. 낭떠러지로 일부러 떨어지기, 숨겨진 방을 찾아내기, 처치해야 할 보스를 죽이지 않고 방치하기 등, 상상 이상의 방식들이 존재한다. 이러한 시스템 덕분에 ICEY의 진짜 매력은 단순한 클리어보다, 도전과제를 100% 달성하며 메타 구조를 해체해 나가는 과정에 있다. 결국 이 게임의 모든 재미를 온전히 느끼고 싶다면 도전과제 올클리어를 목표로 하는 플레이가 가장 이상적이다.

다만 행동의 단추가 반항이라 그런지, 내레이터의 대부분 반응들이 짜증 섞인 투거나, 계속해서 불평하는 톤이라 호불호가 갈리기 쉽다. 실제로 후기들을 보면 “중2병스럽다”, “징징거려서 귀가 아프다”는 의견이 적지 않다. 필자는 오히려 그 과장된 반응이 우스꽝스럽고 재미있게 느껴졌지만, 누군가에게는 불쾌하거나 피곤하게 다가올 수도 있다.

여담으로 필자의 경우는 한 유저분의 한글 패치 덕분에 편안하게 게임을 진행했는데, 해당 패치의 보이스가 일본어로 자동 설정이 되어 있어 일본어로 진행했다. 내레이터의 일본어 성우는 "시모노 히로"로, 최근 극장판으로도 흥행한 귀멸의 칼날의 "젠이츠" 역으로 유명한 성우다. 덕분에 연기력은 두말할 필요 없이 훌륭했고, 몰입감있게 잘 즐길 수 있었다. 아마 애니메이션을 열심히 본다면 징징거리는 내레이터의 목소리에서 젠이츠의 느낌을 확 받을 수 있을 것이다. (필자가 그랬음..)

단점

[b]1. 밋밋한 액션, 답답한 조작감[/b]

해당 게임의 기본적인 흐름은 내레이터의 안내에 따라 다음 구역으로 향하며, 최종 목적지까지 도달하면서 마주하는 적들과 전투를 진행하며 결국 최종 장소에 존재하는 해당 챕터의 보스를 잡는 것이다. 최종 목적지에 도달하기 전까지 숨겨진 장소를 찾으며 보물 상자를 찾거나, 이스터에그를 찾는 것 또한 부가적인 목표라고 할 수 있다.

때문에 해당 게임의 핵심이 아무리 내레이터와의 메타픽션적인 상호작용이라고 할지라도, 전투가 게임의 전반적인 비중에 있어서 결코 적은 비율을 갖고 있지는 않다. 애초에 게임 내 시스템 자체에서도 커맨드를 이용한 화려하고 스타일리시한 전투를 할 수 있도록 지원하고 있으며, 강화 시스템도 있는 걸 보면 게임의 제 2의 재미 요소로써 전투를 선택했다고 봐도 무방하다.

다만 전투 파트만 뜯어놓고 본다면 불쾌한 요소가 상당히 많으며 깊이가 굉장히 얕다. 일반적인 필드에서는 일 대 다 전투가 굉장히 빈번하게 이뤄지는데, 피격을 한 번 당해서 공중에 뜨면 연달아 피격당하는 일이 잦다. 이 때문에 초반에 돌연사가 굉장히 빈번하다. 피격 이후 캐릭터가 땅에 떨어지면 일어나는 모션을 취하는데, 이때 무적이 적용되어 있지도 않아 일어나다가 또 얻어맞고 허망하게 죽는 경우도 다수있다.

피격 부분에서의 문제점도 있지만 몬스터의 공격 모션이 거의 없다시피 하는 점도 문제다. 보통은 몬스터가 공격하기 전에 준비 모션이 잠깐이라도 존재하는데 그런 게 전혀 없다. 때문에 공격을 회피와 카운터로 반응하기가 굉장히 어려워 별도의 커맨드 없이 그냥 딜찍누로 잡는 게 가장 편하고 재밌다고 느꼈다. 

다행히 회피 카운터, 혹은 적에게 공격을 어느 정도 누적시킨 경우에 할 수 있는 QTE 공격을 통해 일부 HP와 쉴드 회복이 가능하긴 하다. 그렇다 보니 전투 자체의 난이도가 그렇게 높게 느껴지지는 않았으나, 똑같은 상황을 계속 느끼다 보니 너무 불쾌하고 큰 단점으로 느껴졌다. 그래도 이 부분은 스탠딩 때 약간의 무적이라도 묻혀주면 약간의 개선이 되지 않을까 싶다.

[b]2. 없는 것만 못한 세계관 설정[/b]

게임을 진행하면서 이스터 에그를 하나씩 찾다 보면, 마치 숨겨진 진실을 암시하듯 웅장한 시나리오가 출력되는 장면을 빈번하게 확인할 수 있다. 시나리오는 ‘신자’, ‘유다’, ‘계획’과 같은 거창한 단어들을 반복적으로 사용하며, 마치 성서의 계시록을 연상시키는 난해한 문장들로 구성되어 있다. 얼핏 보면 스토리의 핵심적인 진실에 접근하기 위한 단서처럼 느껴지지만, 문제는 문장들이 뭘 의미하는지 전혀 이해할 수 없다는 점이다. 이해가 되지 않으니 흥미를 느끼기도, 비판하기도 어렵다.

더 큰 문제는 이 시나리오가 연속적으로 제시되지도 않는다는 것이다. 도전과제를 하나씩 클리어할 때마다 짧은 단락 형태로 노출되다 보니, 이전에 봤던 내용이 무엇이었는지 기억조차 나지 않는다. 결국 이야기를 이해하기는커녕, 시나리오끼리 따로 노는 짧은 설정 모음집처럼 느껴진다. 사실 설정 모음집이라 표현하는 것도 후한 평가고, 오히려 GPT가 임의로 생성한 문장들을 나열해둔 듯한 인상을 준다.

어떤 면에서는 프롬소프트웨어의 스토리텔링처럼 모든 것이 불분명하고 상징적으로만 제시되는 점이 비슷하다고 볼 수도 있다. 하지만 프롬의 작품들은 촘촘히 설계된 세계관과 정교한 떡밥 회수 구조를 기반으로 하기 때문에, 이해는 어렵지만 설득력은 있는 서사로 완성된다. 반면 ICEY는 그런 기반이 전혀 없는 상태에서 갑작스럽게 난해한 키워드만 쏟아내는 느낌에 가깝다. 차라리 이런 연출들을 과감히 삭제해 서사의 통일성을 유지하고, 중2병스러운 오글거림에서 벗어나게 만드는 편이 훨씬 나았을 것이다.


[가격]

정가 13,000원. 필자의 경우 60% 할인된 5,200원에 구매했다. 결론부터 말하자면, 한 번쯤은 해볼 만한 게임이라는 생각은 들지만, 개인적으로는 정가에 구매하기에는 다소 부담스러운 작품이다. 물론 독특한 게임성을 이유로 정가에 구매한다고 하면 어쩔 수 없지만.. 메타픽션 요소에서 더 상위호환적인 모습을 보여준 One Shot보다도 가격이 높아 아쉽긴 매한가지. 더군다나 엔딩만 빠르게 본다고 가정할 경우 2시간 이내에도 클리어가 가능하며, 게임의 재미를 느끼며 도전과제를 전부 달성하더라도 3~4시간 내에 모든 도전과제를 올클리어할 수 있을 정도로 플레이타임이 굉장히 짧고 굵다. 이런 점에서 정가에 구매 시 가성비 면에서는 다소 아쉬움이 남는다.

그래서 개인적으로는 할인할 때 구매하는 걸 추천한다. 체감상 ICEY는 할인 주기가 비교적 짧은 편이라, 급한 게 아니라면 여유롭게 구매해도 괜찮을 듯 싶다. 게임에 관심이 생겼다면 찜목록에 등록해 두었다가 만족하는 가격이 됐을 때 구매하면 좋을 것 같다. 참고로, 리뷰를 작성하는 10월 22일 기준 ICEY의 최저가는 65% 할인된 4,550원이다. 할인 타이밍을 잘 노려, 부담 없는 가격으로 라이브러리에 담아보길 추천한다.


[도전과제]

난이도 - 下
필요 회차 - 1회차+

도전과제 올클리어 난이도는 매우 쉬운 편이다. 다만 일일히 찾으면서 진행을 하기에는 시간이 오래 걸리기 때문에, 개인적으로 빠른 진행을 원한다면 공략을 보면서 진행하는 걸 추천한다. 게임이 출시된 지 꽤 오랜 시간이 지난 만큼, 잘 정리가 된 공략들이 많아 시간을 굉장히 단축할 수 있다.

도전과제는 크게 챕터별 보스 퇴치, 이스터에그, 엔딩 클리어의 세 가지 종류로 나뉜다. 개인적으로 추천하는 루트는 내레이터의 안내대로 플레이하며 노멀 엔딩을 본 뒤, 각 챕터에 숨겨진 이스터에그 도전과제까지 정복한 이후, 마지막으로 히든 엔딩을 보는 것이다. 아쉽게도 한국어로 된 가이드는 존재하지 않지만, 업적 클리어를 위해 복잡한 과정은 없기 때문에 가이드로도 충분히 클리어가 가능하다. 필자의 경우 스팀 커뮤니티의 두 유저,[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=852330775]"Frostbyte"[/url]와 [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=805364372]"KOS-MOS"[/url]가 작성한 가이드를 참고해 쉽게 이스터에그 업적들을 모두 클리어할 수 있었다.

참고로 초반 튜토리얼 파트의 업적을 놓쳐 곤란을 겪을 수도 있는데, 이럴 때는 메인 화면의 설정 메뉴에서 기존 게임 데이터를 초기화한 후 새로 시작하면 튜토리얼부터 다시 진행할 수 있다. 단, 혹시 모를 상황에 대비해 기존 데이터를 미리 백업해두는 것을 권장한다. [strike]사람 일은 또 모르는 거니깐..[/strike]

전반적으로 플레이 타임도 짧고, 도전과제 올클리어의 난이도도 높지 않다 보니 필자처럼 도전과제 올클리어를 즐기는 게이머라면 가볍게 도전해보기 좋은 작품이다.


[총평]

[b]액션 게임의 탈을 쓰고 있는 2D 메타픽션 게임[/b]

작년 겨울 세일 때 구매해두고 한동안 창고에 넣어뒀다가, 짧게 즐기기 좋은 게임이라는 평이 떠올라 꺼내 플레이하게 된 작품이다. 스팀 평가도 매우 긍정적이고, 상점 페이지에 걸린 ICEY의 일러스트가 예뻐서 구매했는데, 막상 인게임에서는 ICEY의 이미지가 등장하지 않아 약간 아쉬웠다. 메타픽션적인 요소가 있다고 해서 처음에는 One Shot처럼 ICEY와 직접 소통하는 구조일 거라 생각했는데, 예상과 달리 내레이터랑 소통할 줄이야..

개인적으로 게임을 플레이하면서 전반적인 구성에서 매트로배니아 장르처럼 느껴졌다. 내레이터의 안내 시스템을 제거하고, 화면 우측 상단에 미니맵만 상시 제공한다면 현재 구조 그대로도 충분히 매트로배니아로 재편이 가능해 보인다. 커맨드 기반의 화려한 액션과 맵을 탐색하며 밝혀나가는 재미에 힘을 준 매트로배니아 장르였다면 올해 3월에 플레이했던 페르시아의 왕자와 유사한 플레이 경험을 줬을 것 같다. 도전과제를 클리어하는 과정에서, 개발 기간이 무려 10년이라는 시간이 소요되었다는 사실을 언급했는데, 이런 긴 개발 기간 동안 모종의 이유로 장르의 방향성이 바뀌었을 가능성도 엿보였다.

OneShot 이후로 오랜만에 만족스럽게 즐긴 메타픽션 게임이라 전반적으로 만족스럽지만, 호불호가 갈릴 여지가 있는 작품임에는 확실하다. 자신이 메타픽션적 연출과 이스터 에그를 좋아한다면, 한 번쯤 플레이해볼 가치가 충분한 게임이라 생각한다.


[추천/비추천 게이머 유형]

추천 게이머 유형
1. 메타픽션 요소를 선호하는 게이머
2. 킬링 타임용 게임을 찾고 있는 게이머
3. 빠른 속도의 콤보 액션을 좋아하는 게이머

비추천 게이머 유형
1. 순수한 액션 중심 게임을 원하는 게이머
2. 깊이감이 있는 메타픽션을 기대하는 게이머
3. 다회차를 선호하지 않는 게이머

[h1]8.5/10   赛博十字绣[/h1]
[b]+++恰到好处的难度，顺畅的填色体验
+++清脆的音效，舒缓的音乐
+++以上两条1+1＞2的解压组合
---有点短不够玩，期待新作🥰[/b]

     前几天我在玩这款游戏的时候，我的一个朋友偶然经过然后看了一会儿，等我填完一个区域使其恢复原色的时候，他说了一句：“这不就是赛博十字绣吗。”我思考了一下，还真是。“十字绣”给我的感觉和这款游戏带给我的是一致的——[b]专注、疗愈、静心[/b]，因此也就拿来当了标题。[spoiler]当然我其实没真的做过十字绣，这只是我的个人印象:D[/spoiler]

     买这个游戏是在9月，但真正爱上它是在前一段的期中周。那时候每天都挺忙的，人也比较烦躁，做事时很难静下心来。在偶然的一次休息时间，我决定玩点小游戏放松一下，找来找去后，我打开了本作。

     因为在这之前我也玩过几次，所以操作已是驾轻就熟，游玩时基本不用动脑，靠着直觉即可完成。伴着清脆悦耳的嗒嗒声和舒缓的BGM，我的大脑逐渐放空，生活琐事已是身外物，我要做的只有点击鼠标，将我心中的杂念化为颜料泼洒在这幅名为《Netherlandish Proverbs》的画卷之上。填完几个区域，我也就差不多平静下来了。于是关掉游戏，再去用生活填充刚刚腾出空来的大脑。

     在这之后，每次我觉得有些烦躁的时候都会打开本作，将躁动填在画作之中。一般来说，填两三个区域我也就能静下心来了，相当好用，百试百灵。

     综上，本作我觉得拿来放松解压非常棒，每次游玩都仿佛经历了一次冥想，而且价格也不贵。我已经推荐给了我的好几位朋友，反响也都不错。新作马上要上线了，到时候整一个备战期末！XD

Proverbs is a mosaic puzzle game, which is effectively a Sudoku/nonogram/minesweeper type number grid puzzle. It's very chill, it's got a fun aesthetic, the lute MIDI-style tunes give good vibes, some of the proverbs you reveal are funny and silly, and it plays perfectly on Steam Deck if you just want to wind down at the end of the day with some low stress logic puzzling. My only real issue was for some reason it seemed to be a bit stubborn about Steam Cloud sync at times, so just keep an eye on that if you're playing on multiple devices.

If you get the good brain chemicals from number puzzling, Proverbs is an easy recommendation.

A deeply moving gem of a game.

I discovered the demo of this game as part of the upcoming Endix Expo (https://endix-expo.com/), a virtual game expo that will run from the 28th-30th of November 2025. I was so moved by the demo that I bought the full game right away.

While playing this game I was so moved by the story of this little child who is so unjustly treated, because of the small mindedness, bitterness and anger of the people around them. These people are angry of the child's parents, who also do not want to keep or raise the poor child. So the child is abandoned by everyone else but the player.

Thus starts this deeply moving and very sad story, which nevertheless offers some glimmers of hope of kindness and generosity in a few upstanding and brave people, despite the bitterness and pettiness of most of the adults around them.

Thus, this is also a story about standing up for what is right and kind, even when almost everyone around you disagree with you, to the point that they will hate you for it. In real life this is not easy.

In the game, you can explain the situation to the child as gently and kindly as possible, in terms they can hopefully understand and make sense of, to maybe prevent them from becoming as angry and bitter over the horrible way they are treated when they grow up.

This is the core of the story, and during playing this game, I so much wanted to help the little child, make them feel loved and understood by one adult, and show them that it is possible to trust and love some select people. 

Cooking nutritious food for the child, buying them a few modest gifts for their birthday, Christmas and other celebrations, feeding them, repairing their clothes, supporting them emotionally, reading for them, providing a little bit of fun and playing and enjoyment, and try to protect them from the abuse they unfortunately experience in school and the terrible abandonment from the institutions that should protect a child, such as the school, the local community, the church, their own family, felt really important and made the game deeply moving for me.

It is a short story and it is told in simple terms so that everyone can understand it and play it. It is also very sad to know that the experiences of this child happened to real people, for the same reasons as the child in the game, and that these people, even as adults, were abused and ostracized and let down by their families, communities and even their nations. Just because they had the wrong parents.

The follow-up to this game will be out on the 20th of November 2025, but only on mobile, and in an alternative time setting (1990s instead of the 1950s). This game made me want to help the little child so much that I really want to play the second game to try and give the child more help and hope, and maybe a happier ending.

This game's mechanics and balance are everything I wish pokemon generation 3 was. I wish old school pokemon games worked on this game's mechanics. A lot of this review goes off what the wiki says, which in some ways is out of date, but it doesn't feel out of date for the parts I really liked.

Here's standard pokemon fare.
- Lots of cool creatures.
- Type system which includes a same-type-attack-bonus
- Held items / berries which can automatically consume on certain events
- Health, Speed, Attack, sp Atk, Defense, and Sp Defense

And now for the great design choices this game makes.
- The game's kind of hard. Not super hard, but I found myself frequently making tactical choices I wouldn't make in pokemon.
- Your mons each have a mana bar instead of a finite use count per move, and each move consumes that mana bar, called "special points" in this game.
- This means bosses in this game can run out of mana, which causes them to rest for a turn to regain 50%. You can use this mechanic to predict switching opportunities. This is an example of a tactical choice you don't get to make in pokemon.
- Hospitals are connected to a teleporter network.
- No stat-affecting natures. Awesome. Hated that damn mechanic. Any mon of a species will have predictible stats in line with its base stats. You don't need to worry about finding a mon who's indtended role is glass cannon but it has a 10% debuff to its main attack stat and a 10% buff to its irrelevant attack stat.
- There is a sort of IV / EV system, and it's good.  EVs are manually chosen by the player.
This makes it super easy to evaulate a Coromon's base stats and priortize which stats to level as you earn "potential points", which work like Pokemon's EV system.

Here's how EVs work here; its a separate exp bar which goes up along with your regular exp bar. When it gets full you get a few (for me it's always 3) points you can directly apply to a stat. It doesn't go toward modifying the base stat, it modifies the stat directly as you see on your screen. So +3 to attack in this fashion will raise your attack stat from 20->23, but your Coromon may have a base attack stat of 108. The base stat is not what is being modified here. Each stat may be increased in this way a maximum of 60 times.

Each coromon has a potential which ranges from 1 to 21. A coromon with 1 potential will gain 66 extra stat points throughout its life. A coromon with 21 (perfect) will have 121 extra stat points.

What if your mon has a low potential and you want to use it in your main party full-time? There is a machine in the game which can be used once per mon to increase its potential, and you'll collect any points you missed out on. There is also a machine to reset potential points for re-allocation and both are "priced right". You don't want to spam them on a ton of mons, save 'em for the ones you like, but the game gives enough money to make good decisions. I'm pricing this in at time of writing my max level mon is 25 in the area just after the first main boss.

I had no problem save-scumming this machine and getting a particular mon up to 18-19 potential easily. If the potential point reward is an even spread along the range, there is basically no difference between a mon with 18 potential and a mon with 21. 10 points maximum. Each run took about 3- 4 minutes. I reliably hit 18-19 potential after a few tries. It's not bad.

If you want to know much an impact on the mon's performance and potential tactics this makes, then you can understand the stats with a simple equation which you can find on the wiki. You as the player only need to know that the base damage of an attack before modifiers scales on (roughtly) 2xlevel * power * ratio of your attack vs their defense .

1. So a Coromon double your level would do roughly double your damage even if your attack stat was the same as it.
2. If you see a move with a power of 80, it will do double the damage as a move with power 40.
3. if your attack stat is double their defense stat you will have a 2x multiplier to damage. If it's half of their defense stat then it's 0.5x . 

Some examples of building a mon around this.
- What if your favorite mon in your party has a low base special def stat? Use some of your 110-120 points to effectively it and now you've reduced the damage he takes by half aginst a mon which would otherwise have had a 2x attack / defense ratio.
- The mana (sp) bar can only take 26 of extra points, so you can build a mon around using heavy-hitting attacks. So 26 allows the mon to use more powerful attacks (doubling the damage there) which frees the other points to bolster defense or health.
- There is a move in the game which restores 15% health, and another 15% if you had a status ailment. So you can allocated those potential points to bolster health in an impactful way beacuse it increases the flat amount of HP healed by this move. Then you can max SP and build a durable, sustainable casting mon easily.

And if you're an old school pokemon player, it's super easy to plan your team without a ton of grinding involved. Barely any effort on my part to put together a team that was "good enough" on the potential front, and I know I'm not wasting time leveling up a bad mon. You don't need to worry about getting to the end of the game and dealing with some enigmatic NPC who gives you a vauge answer on your mon's potential before throwing it away and farming a new one from scratch.

Also the potential of a mon is reflected in its color, so "shiny" mon are also perfect mon by definition. Remember how fun it was catching a shiny pokemon and it having a garbage IV? Doesn't happen here.

One more nice thing about this mechanic; The mana bar makes farming for a "good enough" mon very simple because the game gives you back some mana at the end of a fight. No need to return to town just to refill a PP gauge when trolling for an under-leveled mon. It's another thing this game does which minimizes grind.

So far I'm loving it.

Sinopse: Em Coromon, você assume o papel de um jovem pesquisador recém-contratado pela Lux Solis, uma organização de pesquisa tecnológica dedicada ao estudo das misteriosas criaturas conhecidas como Coromon. Logo após começar sua jornada, você descobre que uma força sombria ameaça o equilíbrio do mundo, e cabe a você — junto de seus Coromon — investigar ruínas antigas, enfrentar titãs poderosos e impedir que essa energia maligna se espalhe.

Durante sua aventura, você poderá capturar e treinar mais de 100 espécies de Coromon, personalizar seu personagem, resolver quebra-cabeças, e participar de batalhas táticas por turnos que exigem estratégia e preparo.

Avaliação: Muito Bom. Que surpresa boa, joguinho extremamente divertido e bem-humorado. Ótimo design das criaturas, uma história que foge do padrão do gênero, músicas bem trabalhadas, bons puzzles, customização de personagem bem interessante, visual em pixel art muito caprichado e variação de cenários rica.

A gameplay tem algumas singularidades, por exemplo: temos 2 barras de experiência, uma funciona normalmente como um level up e a outra barra toda vez que ela enche o jogo nos dá a liberdade de distribuir 3 pontos de stats em qualquer atributo. Outra boa diferença fica no sistema de energia dos golpes. Ao invés do tradicional PP que limita a quantidade de vezes que podemos usar um mesmo golpe, aqui é uma barra de energia única pra todos os 4 golpes. Quando ela acaba, descansamos 1 turno pra encher metade da barra. Temos 13 tipagens de criaturas com o sistema tradicional de pedra-papel-tesoura.

A campanha tem uma boa variação de atividades e cenários, com alguns momentos mais focados em batalhas, em conversas, em puzzles, em ações, em descobertas de segredos e muito mais. A dificuldade é bem personalizável, tendo até o famoso modo nuzlocke que "mata" um monstrinho pra sempre se ele cair em batalha. Uma pena que a campanha é muito curtinha, deu pra terminar ela com apenas 15 horas. Fiquei com um gostinho de "quero mais", sinto que o final faltou um peso um pouco maior, algum acontecimento mais surpreendente.

Recomendo bastante Coromon pra todo fã de Pokémon, ele não possui o mesmo charme da famosa franquia porém tem sua própria personalidade e diversão.

which had no difficulty and classes that all played/felt the same. A large portion of time in EW i had almost fallen asleep multiple times and outright refused to do my weekly Alliance raid because EW raids were a walking sim, since the mechanics gave you 3-5 working days before ending cast.

Apart from Zeromus EX, actually the most enjoyable fight i ever did even tho the difficulty of it felt like 'normal' difficulty shadowbringers and before.

This game pleasantly surprised me, and I think it deserves a recommendation because I would've bought this sooner if I had a better idea of what it was from the Steam page. First of all, it isn't just a sandbox, it's kind of an open world adventure with a storyline, actual progression, and abilities to unlock and stats to upgrade, which are all right up my alley. Additionally, it's an inspiring example of how we can combat a major societal problem throughout the world in that many indigenous languages are dying off due to the lack of economic opportunities within their communities with their language or relating to their culture. I'm not sure what specific elements are based in New Caledonian legends or mythology, but the voice actors appear to be from New Caledonia and speak either their indigenous language, French, or both. I think that is an excellent way of supporting indigenous communities in the face of their cultures and languages dying out. Honestly, it's worth purchasing for that simple fact alone. 

That being said, it was also a fun game. I loved messing around with the central mechanic as part of the MC's powers, and flying around as a bird or racing through the water as a dolphin was a good amount of fun on its own. The story and world-building felt very reminiscent of the kinds of fantastical stories that are often a part of indigenous mythologies, which I liked a lot, although the storytelling had some odd moments when visualized in the game itself. They were interesting moments, because the same thing in the context of a legend wouldn't be as strange, but having it visualized before me with the cartoonish art style made me somewhat uncomfortable, but not enough to change my opinion of it. The romance between the adolescent MC and an NPC also seemed somewhat strange to me, but I think they were going for a sweet story and I can get behind that. The gameplay was also good, and I really appreciated some of the more light-hearted aspects of the game, like the musical sequences and the fact that you could poop on command as a bird. I've been on the receiving end of that enough to suspect that real birds are fairly intentional with it as well.

Overall, I enjoyed my time playing. There were some highlights and some low points, but I think this game is worth your time and it's a great example of how games can work to treat a major societal issue.

Plain Sight is one of those wonderfully strange ideas that deserved far more love than it ever got. Imagine robot ninjas leaping through the void of space, dueling each other with katanas and exploding into bursts of digital light; that’s the game in a nutshell. It’s fast, clever and stylishly minimalist, but like so many great indie experiments from its era, it ultimately fell victim to time and obscurity.

At its heart, Plain Sight is a multiplayer arena brawler built around a brilliant mechanic: every time you destroy an opponent you gain energy, but you can only bank that energy (and your score) by self-destructing. It turns every match into a risky dance of greed and timing, where survival and success are constantly at odds. It’s one of those rare systems that’s easy to understand but endlessly tense to master.

The movement is exhilarating: double jumps, gravity shifts and midair flips make every arena feel like a playground for chaos. The cel-shaded visuals and crisp soundtrack add to the sense of kinetic style. Unfortunately, the fun relies entirely on having other players to fight, and that’s where Plain Sight now falters. With the servers long deserted, what remains is a haunting shell of what once was; you can jump, you can move, but there’s no one left to explode.

Even so, Plain Sight deserves to be remembered. It captured the essence of creative multiplayer design: simple mechanics, deep risk–reward and a unique identity. If you can gather a few friends for LAN play, it’s still an absolute blast.

Alone, it’s a ghost of a great idea. Together, it was lightning in a bottle.

Peppa Pig: World Adventures, developed by Petoons Studio and published by Outright Games Ltd., is a colorful, gentle, and highly accessible children’s adventure game that faithfully brings the beloved television series to life. Designed specifically for very young players, it serves as an interactive episode of Peppa’s world, where exploration and play are prioritized over challenge or complexity. The game continues the formula established by My Friend Peppa Pig, expanding its scope with a global theme that sends Peppa and her friends on a journey to visit famous locations around the world. It is an experience crafted with clear intent—to delight preschool-aged children, encourage basic interactivity, and immerse them in the cheerful, pastel-colored universe they know from television.

The premise is as simple and inviting as it sounds. Players join Peppa and her family as they travel to several countries, including the United States, France, Italy, Spain, Germany, and Australia, among others. Each destination features a handful of short activities that highlight the culture of the place in a child-friendly way—making pizza in Italy, playing soccer in Spain, building a skyscraper in New York, or dancing under the Eiffel Tower in Paris. The gameplay is extremely straightforward: players move left or right, press a button to interact, and engage in short, whimsical tasks. There are no complex controls, no fail states, and no time pressures, which ensures that even the youngest of players can navigate the experience without frustration. Every interaction, from jumping in puddles to taking pictures, is designed to evoke curiosity and joy, reinforcing the sense of play that defines Peppa Pig’s world.

Visually, the game perfectly captures the aesthetic of the TV show. The art style is vibrant, simple, and instantly recognizable, with character designs, color palettes, and animations that replicate the cartoon almost exactly. This consistency allows children to feel immediately comfortable, as though they are stepping directly into an episode. The world is bright and friendly, full of smiling characters, clean lines, and the kind of gentle humor that defines Peppa Pig’s charm. The voice acting is similarly authentic, featuring familiar tones and cheerful dialogue that align with the series’ atmosphere. The sound design, from the peppy music to the signature snorts and giggles, creates a sense of warmth and familiarity. For fans of the show, it’s as close as one can get to interacting with an actual episode, and for parents, it feels like a safe and wholesome experience for their children.

The structure of the game reflects its focus on exploration rather than progression. There are no traditional levels or competitive elements. Instead, players move freely between destinations, complete small objectives, and collect souvenirs to decorate their home. The house customization feature adds a small layer of creativity, allowing players to personalize Peppa’s environment as they complete activities around the world. It’s a simple but effective incentive, giving a sense of purpose to each trip. The pacing is relaxed, and the lack of urgency makes it an ideal game for quiet, low-stress play sessions. Children can wander at their own pace, enjoy the cheerful visuals, and interact with their favorite characters without fear of losing or doing something “wrong.” It’s this accessibility that makes Peppa Pig: World Adventures so effective as an introduction to gaming.

While the game succeeds beautifully in appealing to its target audience, it naturally has limitations when viewed through a broader lens. The simplicity that makes it perfect for preschoolers also means there’s little here for older children or adults to engage with. The activities, while charming, can become repetitive, as most interactions boil down to pressing a single button or watching short animated sequences. The world-tour concept, though delightful, doesn’t expand much beyond a handful of interactions per destination, and the overall experience can be completed in just a couple of hours. There are minor technical hiccups as well, such as long loading times between areas and occasional animation glitches, though these issues are minor and rarely disrupt gameplay. It’s also worth noting that, while the game is easy to navigate, very young children may still benefit from parental guidance during transitions between areas or when starting new activities.

Despite these limitations, Peppa Pig: World Adventures delivers precisely what it sets out to provide—a safe, educational, and joyful digital playground for young fans of Peppa Pig. It’s not about mastery or competition but about discovery, empathy, and the simple pleasures of play. Children will find delight in traveling to new places, meeting familiar faces, and taking part in gentle adventures that celebrate imagination and curiosity. Parents, in turn, will appreciate the game’s wholesome tone and intuitive controls that allow their children to play independently with minimal frustration. It’s a rare example of a game that understands its audience completely and tailors every aspect of its design to them.

Ultimately, Peppa Pig: World Adventures is a charming and thoughtful continuation of the Peppa Pig video game series, one that embraces the spirit of the show and transforms it into a relaxed, interactive experience. It’s a perfect entry point for young children taking their first steps into gaming, offering a world that is safe, colorful, and consistently positive. While older players will find little depth or replay value, the game’s simple joy and authenticity make it an ideal gift for Peppa’s youngest fans. With its gentle humor, bright visuals, and global sense of adventure, it succeeds not as a complex game but as a heartwarming journey that brings Peppa Pig’s world to life in the most faithful and endearing way possible.
