A Riot conseguiu fazer aqui um jogo melhor do que o próprio LoL kkkkk. Se você curte RPG por turno, vai se apaixonar! A história é cativante do começo ao fim, os personagens são super carismáticos e cada campeão mantém sua dublagem original — o que deixa tudo ainda mais imersivo e nostálgico para quem já joga o “lolzinho”.

Fico muito feliz por ter jogado esse título, porque além de ser uma experiência incrível, pude conhecer melhor a personalidade e o background de cada campeão.

O único ponto que me incomodou foi o mapa. Às vezes ele marca um objetivo em uma área muito ampla e, quando você chega lá, ainda precisa ficar procurando exatamente onde interagir. Pode ser um pouco frustrante, mas nada que estrague a experiência.

No geral: jogo praticamente perfeito. História, gameplay, ambientação e personagens — tudo no ponto. Recomendo demais!

Sinopse: Ruined King: A League of Legends Story acompanha um grupo improvável de campeões: Miss Fortune, Illaoi, Braum, Yasuo, Ahri e o misterioso Pyke. Eles se unem para investigar a névoa negra que ameaça Águas de Sentina. Ao seguirem as pistas, eles descobrem que a ruína tem origem na sombria Ilha das Sombras, onde precisam enfrentar forças antigas e impedir que a corrupção se espalhe pelo mundo.

Avaliação: Muito Bom. Eu tinha uma certa expectativa de jogar esse jogo desde o lançamento e acabou sendo uma experiência acima do que eu esperava. Pra quem já conhece os personagens por jogar League of Legends torna o jogo ainda melhor, mas não é um impeditivo pra iniciar no universo do jogo.

Cada um dos 6 personagens possui características bem únicas, com habilidades de batalha e de exploração. O sistema de batalha usa o "Lane System" que consiste entre 3 linhas pra usar habilidades. Uma dessas linhas faz o golpe ser aplicado mais rápido porém com menos dano, a linha do meio é o padrão e a terceira linha torna o golpe mais demorado porém mais poderoso. E no meio dessas escolhas temos os buffs e debuffs dos ambientes que influenciam onde o personagem está nessas linhas.

Os personagens são bem trabalhados com um destaque sensacional pra dublagem PT-BR, algo muito raro de se ver em jogos do gênero. Cada um tem o seu propósito bem claro e bem explorado durante a campanha. A narrativa funciona muito bem, contando com cutscenes que possuem uma arte bem interessante. A atmosfera é um ponto bem trabalhado também, com uma trilha sonora que se encaixa nos momentos certos.

Os defeitos que encontrei foram alguns bugs técnicos chatos que incomodavam na gameplay, nos menus que são um pouco confusos e na falta de teleportes mais acessíveis, onde ocasionavam momentos chatos de backtracking sem recompensa. Poderiam ter encaixado mais personagens do universo da franquia no jogo, poucos aparecem.

yes I would recommend this game.......but it may depend on some factors. Do not compare this to doom or doom 2. Rise of the Triad came sort of like an offshoot of Wolfenstein 3D, but with huge advancements in mechanics.

I discovered Rise of the Triad in a bundle of shareware I got when I bought Duke Nukem 3D. The shareware alone was almost like a full game. I think in total it was like a dozen or more levels. Then Later I got Dark War which was a full 4 act game. But what is truly unique here, is that the shareware has completely different levels, it runs like a running up to the main game. And you can play The Hunt Begins and Dark War separately.

I immersed myself in this game for hours at a time with the lights out. It was great. And now that they took the entire game and made it work in 4K without losing what made it great in the beginning.

But back in the mid to late 90s, it was sorta awful, but it was because back them mouselook was rather primitive and not smooth. Once ROTT got the OpenGL treatment of the early 2000s, it was so much more fluid today. Unfortunately only Quake and Quake II has really good mouselook for the time.

The singleplayer is where it's at.Long expansive levels, traps, interesting enemies. And it has the best in-game music ever made. The Multiplayer is what is lacking. With bullet weapons and rocket/fire weapons, its extremely lopsided, and more modes than anyone can wrap their heads around. All these years, I wish this game had a cooperative like Doom and Doom 2 do. But overall if you can take this as a cult gem from nostolgia, your in the right train of thought.

Co k tomuto počinu říci? Hned ze začátku jsem byl silně zklamán, po přechodu ze spellforce 1 mi ani nádherná grafika hry nedokázala nahradit zážitek z herních mechanik prvního dílu. Nedokážu ale říci, že bych si hru neužil, postupem hry jsem si na to zvykl a zklamání postupem času opadlo.

+ Hra kombinuje rpg žánr se "strategií".

+ soundtrack

+ archieventy

+ hra nabízí režim kampaně v coop režimu a ten bych doporučil využít, vaše parta hrdinů se při rpg kampani rozdělí na půl a při budovačce se jeden stará o tábor, zatím, co druhý ovládá hrdiny. Funguje to překvapivě skvěle a je to pak i větší zábava.

Rpg systém - průměr, každé povolání má hrstku aktivních a pasivních schopností, které jdou až 3x vylepšit, vaše postava může kombinovat 2 stromy a jeden je fixní. Boj - průměr, i ve spellforce 1 měli postavy více bojových animací a doprovodných soundefektů, navíc zde byla ještě navíc mechanika staggeru, schází zde bojové povely, jako: neutíkej bezhlavě přes půl mapy za tím scoutem.

Příběh - nijak extra zajímavý, zbytečně přetažený za vlasy, ale stravitelný - průměr, mohu ale pochválit backstory vašich doprovodných hrdinů.

Budovačky? Průměr, máte mapu vytyčenou sektory, můžete hrát za lidi, elfy, nebo orky (ale co si budeme, většinu kampaně hrajete za lidi), budovy nijak extra neřešíte, bum, bum, pila, bum bum kamenolom a už to jede. Armáda je prostá, prostě spamujete jednotky a doufáte, že přetlačíte nepřítele, který je otravnější, než svítiplyn. Strategie? Neřešte, na tu není čas, vemte hrdiny, zaberte, co nejvíce můžete a pak jen doufejte, že to stačí. Obrané budovy jsou k smíchu, absolutní ztráta surovin a pracovní síly.

Rpg scénáře mě bavili nejvíce i přes průměrnou paletu průměrných nepřátel.

『Romancing SaGa -Minstrel Song- Remastered』は、フリーシナリオ構造に基づく非線形型のロールプレイングゲームです。プレイヤーは八名の主人公から一人を選択し、オープンワールドを探索します。イベントは特定のストーリールートではなく、場所や時間に応じて発生します。

探索は好奇心に応える設計となっており、街や荒野にはクエスト、隠されたスキル、希少な戦闘が存在します。進行はマーカーによる誘導がなく、自由度が高い反面、新規プレイヤーには混乱を招く可能性があります。目標管理はプレイヤー自身に委ねられています。

戦闘はターン制で、フォーメーションと武器スタイルが重要要素です。キャラクターは戦闘中の能力使用を通じて新たな技を習得します。このランダム性は一貫性に欠ける場合がありますが、自然な成長を促進します。敵の強さはプレイヤーに合わせて上昇し、全域で高い緊張感を維持します。

キャラクタービルドは装備やクラスによる役割分担を重視します。装備変更により性能が迅速に変化します。回復手段が限定されているため、リソース管理が重要です。パーティ全体の相性は個々の火力よりも影響力が高くなります。

リマスター版では、ビジュアルが強化され、モデルの鮮明化やライティング改善が施されています。利便性向上として、地図上のマーカー改善や移動速度向上が追加されています。音楽はアレンジを伴いながらも、ボス戦を強調する構成を維持しています。

ストーリーはモジュール型で提供され、各地域が独立した対立構造を持ちます。大規模な物語要素も存在しますが、発見順が断片的となる場合があります。この設計により、複数回のプレイが推奨されます。

本作はシステムの奥深さと探索の自由度を求めるプレイヤーを主な対象としています。初心者には不透明に感じられる可能性がありますが、実験的なRPG構造を好むユーザーにとっては、高いリプレイ性と戦術的な挑戦が提供されます。

Today, after starting a new save this weekend, I finally beat Romancing SaGa Minstrel Song. I bought it in 2023 for the Switch, got to the final boss, couldn't beat him, and gave up. But today I did it. I really think I'll remember it as one of my favorite games, and yet I don't think I could recommend it to anyone unless I know for a fact they'd be comfortable with what is effectively a 20+ hour puzzle box. Because that's what this game was.

You get to pick between 8 characters with virtually no idea who any of them are, "tutorials" are walls of text that randomly pop up only after you encounter the new mechanic (or presented by these little twerps that call you a rookie in every town no matter how late in the game you are), the game literally tells you to keep multiple saves in case you mess up (because you can mess up BAD), the whole game has a "time" limit, there is no main quest until the very end of the game so you're flying by the seat of your pants and holding on by the skin of your teeth trying to figure out what the heck is going on, and that final boss was a bastard. It's a game where the main character is a plaything of the gods strung along by fate and the whims of you the player (I'm not being philosophical on that one. The game asks you your real name and sex for story reasons). But God knows it felt good to finally beat it. It's a gorgeous game, serene even. Yet it's still comfortable punching you in the gut and telling you that you failed so badly that you should probably start a new save. There's even a section in your quest log for failed quests. Even then, I only beat the game as one of the 8 playable characters.

Minstrel Song is completely comfortable being itself and the main mind behind the franchise doesn't beat around the bush when he talks about his games in interviews. The whole SaGa franchise is like this. These games are weird and you may love one game in the franchise only to hate the next. But if this is your thing, you're not going to get the SaGa experience from any other gaming franchise. For what it's worth, I hope you reading this love this game the way I did.

玩愚人船的时候我非常幸福却又止不住流泪，会有很多人来夸奖，分析愚人船的方方面面，而我只想表达一个酷儿玩到愚人船时的感受。
这个世界充满了需要解释、证明和辩护的瞬间，而在另一个酷儿个体面前，许多核心的痛苦和挣扎是“不言自明”的。我们不需要寒暄客套，创伤共鸣能让我们迅速感知，理解彼此，“能与我感同身受的往往只有那些经历过相似痛苦的人。”。酷儿经历往往不被主流历史、文学或家庭叙事所记载。这种被抹去、被忽略的经历本身就是一种深重的痛苦，我也不能确定简中互联网是否能接受这份作品，但是愚人船毫无疑问为酷儿群体提供了一种强大的疗愈——当一部作品，以细腻、真挚的方式呈现你的身份、你的痛苦和你的爱时。
几个月前玩完第一章demo后，某个深夜里我少有的回忆起了那个夜晚。那个夜晚我看到了站在你床前的阎王，他看了我一眼，我害怕地把头缩进了被子，如果那个时候我要是勇敢一点冲出去打断他对你的审判，事情会不会发生改变？我和提莫西一样没有在外人面前因为你的离去而流泪，和韦德一样在许多年之后才感受到你的离去而带来的巨大悲伤。我现在已经变得很勇敢了妈妈，不再因为一个人去买晚饭害怕楼道里的黑暗而狂奔，不再因为害怕拒绝而把你织的红色米老鼠毛衣送给别人.。虽然我的情感防御机制还在起效，愚人船提供了一个安全的、间接的空间，让我重新连接到那份压抑的爱。就当做是一场预先演习吧，因为我对你的哀悼还未完成。

年末的艺术礼物，体验过demo后心心念念一直期盼它发售，作者有很优秀的艺术审美和文学素养，虽然只有一个人但是游戏制作比很多解密游戏都要成熟，音效搭配画面产生的精神冲击很强，再次体验第一章有种心脏漏风的冷感，让我想起了每次开药等待时候坐在病人堆里的紧张和不安。
“生者是深渊，死者是太阳” 整个游戏的文本构成了一篇文笔深厚优秀的散文，想看作者更多的文学创作。

第二章体验完成再次编辑，整个游戏艺术表现手法和文字都更加的成熟和震撼人心，在人生中一路跌跌撞撞走到现在真的能感受到每个小故事和文字承载的情感意义，如果过去的人生是无边际的痛苦，今天我将选择和一切和解。
“害怕战争，害怕暴力，害怕危险，害怕爱人离开自己，当这一切全都发生，你就将不再害怕一切”
如果无法共鸣到第二章的痛苦和情感，恭喜你是这个空洞虚伪世界的幸运儿，又或许是像作者说的——
”有这样一种逃亡的方式：
就是对除了自我之外的一切置若罔闻。
明哲保身，专注过好自己的生活。”

最后，希望作者健康幸福，活得自由
也希望人们能懂得珍惜还存活的时间，珍惜身边人陪伴你的每一天，或许会和某些人分别在未来到来之前。

TLDR
A solid sidescroller/farming-game. It's not "excellent" at either genre, but I also think it's "slightly above average" at both types of gameplay. The atmosphere of the farm is incredibly relaxing, so if you just want something to chill out with, I'd highly recommend it. The caveat is that you have to enjoy action-sidescrollers, since a large percent of the playtime is spent exploring instead of farming.

If you want more info on the two sides of the gameplay, read below:

FARMING
Honestly, the farming is more atmospheric than anything. Many of the early-year and end-of-year tasks are deliberately-repetitive QTEs or simple chores. It's not as bad as it sounds, as it can be quite relaxing. There's also *some* strategy during the daily upkeep, but not a ton. Unlike Rune Factory/Stardew, you can't choose a variety of crops, or customize your farm's landscape. You manage one field of rice a year (years are 12 days). All you grow is rice.

It's honestly a fairly detailed/realistic rice-growing sim, where the rice has different needs during its various growth phases. However, if you're looking to be creative, then it might not be for you. Every year the goal is just to replicate the optimal fertilizer/temperature/water levels needed for each growth-phase. There's definitely depth to it, but it's undeniably a very restrictive farming system. Not specifically good or bad, but it's important to know that it's restrictive.

ACTION-SIDESCROLLER
This is the bulk of the game, so you better enjoy it. I personally find it quite fun, but I have an affinity for platformers. It's a sidescrolling beat-em-up with fighting-game combat. Sort of similar to Smash Bros, except that enemies can die from damage.

Thankfully, your variety of moves/specials actually DO matter, so it's not purely button-mashing. The goal is to finish exploring before nighttime, so the player is motivated to fight quickly and efficiently, which makes the game more interesting than it would be otherwise. You also have a grapple-hook, which can be used on walls AND enemies. It's quite fun to play around with, and is very important to doing well in combat. This makes the fighting just a little bit more unique.

this game's badass...but i wish i liked it more than i did. i think it's mainly because of the scoring system.

shady knight is a stylish action game in theory, but maybe not so much in practice. to get an sss rank (the highest rank), you must meet a certain score requirement. in the early levels, there are so few enemies that reaching that requirement is sort of a puzzle; you need to kill every enemy in the map by incorporating as many different high-scoring actions as you can. as scoring isn't communicated to you super well, this kind of ends up being trial and error until you figure out the right combination of actions that gets you the sss rank. then there's a sweet spot in the second quarter of the game where you still need to keep action diversity in mind to get an sss rank, but getting a perfect run (all kills, no damage, no falls) will do most of the work. in the back half of the game, there are so many enemies in each level that a perfect run will almost certainly give you an sss rank no matter what actions you take, so instead of going for style, you go for safety, playing as conservatively as possible; there's no time requirement (which i think there should be), so you can and probably should just play evasively and opportunistically. when the style system encourages you to play cautiously and defensively rather than, you know, stylishly, something has gone very wrong!

the game is also frustratingly inconsistent, which would not be such a big deal if getting hit didn't mean resetting the level if you want an sss rank. this is partially because the game depends on physics for a lot of things, and the slightest deviation can result in very different outcomes when physics are in play. but that's the nature of the beast, and it's the least of the game's problems in terms of inconsistency. for example, using your grapple on an enemy that's standing on the edge of a platform while you are off of the platform is SUPPOSED to pull the enemy off the platform as it pulls you back on. it's extremely finnicky, though, and aside from enemies that are statically positioned on edges and waiting for you to do this to them, i found it rarely worked. knocking enemies off of ledges, in general, is a whole can of worms. in a Kick Game like this one, you'd expect kicking enemies off of ledges to be something you do frequently. the scoring system should discourage you from overly relying on this (although really that should probably be level design's job). but what ACTUALLY stops you from kicking enemies off of ledges is that a significant number of enemies, especially later in the game, will just jump or teleport back onto the ledge when kicked off. the worst are the shielded enemies. some enemies will arbitrarily have a barrier around them that allows them to ignore non-unblockable attacks (you can also use fire, which is not always available or convenient), which really limits the ways you can approach an encounter until the barriers are broken. it feels like the game is afraid of the tools that it has given you and does stuff like this to keep them in check.

the game has other issues; enemy variety is very limited. there's one environment that is used for the whole game. this doesn't completely absolve the issues, but this is a solo dev game, and sometimes concessions have to be made to keep scope in check.

but...like...this game's badass. there is so much cool shit you CAN do in this game, when the game has not discouraged you from doing it. it is so fun to improvise. it is so fun to launch an enemy, kick them further up, finish them off by throwing a sword at them, air dash into the sword and then use the height you gained to do a slam attack that launches another enemy, which you then enemy step off of to slam it into the ground and then you kick it to slam it into the ground again. the core of the game is so solid. shady knight's inspirations are clear, but i don't think there are any other stylish action games quite like it; the best game like shady knight is shady knight. i really hope lessons can be learned from it, by its developer or by someone else, so that a game like shady knight that is better than shady knight can be made, because there is SO much potential here.

商店兑换推荐：
    1.皮肤：大部分比原版好看，角色卡牌需要重新升级，只能用钻石买，每天限量且卖的随机，感觉钻石优先买完。

组牌
    图鉴：卡牌信息查询，卡牌升级，卡牌皮肤选择，卡牌组合修改
    卡牌组合：卡牌组合必须60张，每个等阶必须有10张，新购买的卡牌需要修改卡牌组合，加入进来，不会自动添加，新开战斗处可以选择已保存的卡牌组合
    新手组牌常见几个思路：
    1.单一大哥（高攻高防，大哥硬刚直推）
    2.群体大哥（群体buff，都硬，倒下一个还有一个）
    3.召唤流（多召唤物加上阵buff，耗死对方）
    4.群杀点杀（直接干掉对方辅助，群杀清场）
    5.毒杀（一换一直接干掉对方大哥）
    6.以上多个思路组合
    几个通用核心辅助：
    摄政王，额外释放同列技能
    救世者，死亡后复活首个己方卡牌
    圣女，己方上阵获得经验（召唤物有效）

卡牌升级：
    原始卡牌为1级，注意新皮肤和原卡牌需分别升级，卡牌专用碎片不足时可以用通用碎片替代
    100金币20碎片升2级，攻击+1，卡面动态效果
    500金币40碎片升3级，生命+1（2级攻击+1效果会消失），卡面动态效果提升
    1000金币100碎片升4级，攻击+1，生命+1（不和低级效果叠加），卡面动态效果提升

名词解释
    行：左中右3张牌视为同一行
    列：上下2张牌视为一列，右为前列，左为后列
    攻击次序：我方从右上开始，右下，中上，中下，左上，左下依次进行，对方先左上，同我方次序呈镜像
    营地：每局中战斗前强化卡牌的环节，地图移动后执行地图事件后，回到营地进入下一轮
    地图事件：包括火堆（无战斗，回复玩家1生命），叹号（随机事件，有可能随机出战斗或火堆），剑（一般战斗），红色剑（高难战斗），按照路线从左到右进行，无尽头
    体力：营地中，使用手牌消耗3体力，刷新手牌消耗1体力
    解散：营地中，撤回场上卡牌，回复1点体力（2级卡牌回2点，3级卡牌回3点）
    锁定：营地中，长按手牌锁定该手牌，刷新时保留，仅刷新其他手牌
    准备开始时：战斗结束后进入营地界面
    准备结束时：地图移动后
    获得：永久获得加成
    增益：仅下一场（营地中）/当前战斗（战斗中）临时获得加成
    上阵：卡牌进场，召唤的卡牌进场也有效
    升级：当前卡牌升级时（仅获得经验未达到升级不触发）
    战斗前：整场战斗开始后
    攻击前：当前卡牌攻击前

技能相关装备说明
    恶魔之手：装备后卡牌对对方卡牌造成即死效果
    真视之石：本身无效果，混沌部落部分卡牌技能有关联效果

I was 15, running around my school in Iran, showing my classmates the trailers for Final Fantasy XV. It made me proud to be a gamer (and future game designer). “This is what games are! Do you see why I’m so passionate about this now?”

Now I’m 27. A whole decade later, I finally played it. I’d been scared — scared it wouldn’t live up to what I saw back then. The reviews weren’t perfect, and that haunted me. But somehow, after all this time, it [i]exceeded[/i] my expectations — and that might surprise most people.

This game is genius. Absolute genius — maybe even in ways the developers never intended. Maybe that’s copium. Maybe it’s truth. But either way, FFXV is about something bigger than itself: the beauty of life and its inevitable passing. It’s that one last road trip with the boys. The side quests you hated doing at the time — fetching tomatoes, running errands — somehow become the sweetest memories when it’s all over.

“I’m a king, goddammit!” you think, "why am I fetching tomatoes for you?". But that’s the point — you had the privilege of knowing normalcy. Like capital-L [i]Life[/i] itself, the small, mundane things end up meaning the most. By the end, you find yourself missing the early hours — the stupid fetch quests, the campfires, the jokes and banter with your brothers. What you wouldn’t give for one more night under the stars with them.

People wanted another [i]Witcher 3[/i] — a world bursting with content, where every random joe on every corner had a deep story to tell. But FFXV isn’t that kind of game, and Life isn't that kind of experience. Its emptiness [i]is the point.[/i] Life isn’t packed with meaning at every turn; it’s quiet, awkward, sometimes tedious. And then one day you look back and realize — that was it. That was life itself.

You don’t remember the massive battles. You remember your brothers. The drives. The fireside laughter. The homemade meals. And somewhere along the way, it stops feeling like a game. It feels like a memory.

Maybe I’m coping. Maybe I’m seeing something that isn’t there. But I’d rather believe it was intentional — that the tedium, the melancholy, the silence — all of it was designed to make you feel the weight of time. And if you play the game with this perspective, it would reach into the depths of your soul and impact you in a way that no other game has.

Final Fantasy XV is messy, beautiful, and painfully human. As I fight back tears, all I want to say is: Ignis, Gladio, Prompto — thank you for living this life with me. You guys... are the best.

It absolutely breaks my heart to choose "not recommended" because it is very obvious that a LOT of love and effort went into this game, moreso than most any other game you will probably ever encounter.

My reason is very simple yet very complicated; it's just not thematically a good sequel.

TLDR; Off the high of the success of the previous game, I feel that Uchikoshi wanted to do something bigger and more complicated, and the end product greatly suffered by coming out very convoluted. It's also much more linear than the first game which is unfortunate because I felt that AIS1's non-linearality was the first game's biggest strong point. One of the reveals near the ending forced me to reexamine everything I've done up to that point in an overly complicated way that felt a bit like a slap in the face for the time and effort I had put into it prior. The game's writing feels like it expects you to voluntarily replay it from the beginning to fully understand what's been going on the whole time, but with your brain so already overloaded with information, the overall experience just felt exhausting to me. It attempted to explain things clearly to me and did an OK job, but I still just felt overwhelmed and bitter by the end of it all.

If you want to play an AI Somnium game, I strongly feel you either have to choose between playing this one *or* the first one - AIS2 feels uninterested in keeping major plotpoints from the first game brought into the second. Playing both side-by-side was just not a good experience for me, and if I could choose to go back in time and decide that the first game was enough for me, I wish I could.

If you are curious about which of the two I would personally recommend you choose, I would choose AI: The Somnium Files (AIS1).

AIS1 felt very welcoming to a casual player, lacking the complicated math and word puzzles of AIS2. You could argue AIS1 was "too easy", but I don't feel like a game like it *needed* a lot of gameplay; it was a visual novel first-and-foremost, and I found it welcoming to just about anyone. To AIS2's defense, it has an option to lower puzzle difficulty, but as an experienced gamer in other genres it feels like a humiliation ritual to actually lower the difficulty myself, haha...

The end takeaway message of AIS1 felt uplifting and solid, while the end takeaway message of AIS2 I have been struggling for days to interpret - I keep coming back to the conclusion that the writer is sincerely trying to promote a nihilistic philosophical message that goes beyond just the game plot, and I don't want to believe that, but I feel he may have done a clumsy job making what any positive takeaway should've been as more clear. It also retroactively feels like an insult to AIS1's gameplay direction in seemingly being about trying to achieve the best ending. Am I just stupid? I have mixed feelings about this game. On one hand, it gets many things right; the voice-acting (I played with Japanese dub), the artstyle, the sound-design, it is all very on-point. You are playing a few episodes of the old UFO Robo Grendizer, and you can tell the game designers are people who loved the show.

That being said, this game is a bloody rip-off.

I have 15 hours on this. That is 15 hours with like half of them spent running around looking for collectibles. The actual game is like 8 hours? Maybe 10? With 0 replayability. No New Game+, no new difficulty, no Boss Rush mode. Super bane-bones. If it was like 15-20 euros (which is how much I paid on a discount) I'd say it is alright - but 40 euros?! On top of other DLC?! Hell no! Wait for a discount.


Most easter-eggs are useless by the way. You get nothing for getting everything. No concept art (which I usually do not care much for) which...how cool would it be, to get concept art of Grendizer and all the Saucer Beasts?! But no. No unlockables. Not even achievements. Not even acknowledgement from the characters! Pointless. Just get what you need to unlock the alternate skins for Grendizer (if you even care) and ignore everything else. Do NOT bother looking around for every last Tori Gate or Gren-Diner and such.

There are some stages where you play as Koji in his TFO (Terrestrial Flying Object). Those are basically just very cheap, very basic arcade space-shooters. The game even lets you skip them, on your FIRST playthrough. That is how little they matter.

In-between missions, you have a small hub; the ranch and the lab. They are pointless and just waste your time. Nobody has much to say. A simple menu would've sufficed, with actual cut-scenes in-between. Heck, how cool would it be if we had proper animation? This is a game catered to ANIME fans. We would 100% watch some original footage. We'd consider ourselves lucky too. We get to play Grendizer AND watch new episodes of Grendizer, over 40 years later? Yes please! But no.

So....what IS good? The gameplay. If you've played Transformers: Devastation on the Playstation....it is very similar. You cannot dock on the Spazer unfortunately, and you do not get any of the other Spazers either. Would've been nice if it could've been included in finishers, or if you could fly around the stages - but no. Only in cutscenes and on rail-roaded space-shooter sections. But fighting on-ground is pretty great. Dodge, block, roll, weave and hit hard. Use all of Grendizer's arsenal (but again, no Spazers); Shoulder Boomerangs, Hand Beam, Screw Punch, Screw-Cruser Punch, Gravity Storm, everything is there! And the voice-actors will hammily shout the names of your attacks every single time. It is great.

Ultimately, this game has its heart in the right place - but it does not do enough to warrant its price. It just needed....more. More hours, more story, more fanservice, more variety. You can't go in this expecting something spectacular. This won't change anyone's minds. This is only for Grendizer fans, and Super Robot anime fans in general.

So if you want this....get it on a discount. anywhere from 10 to 20 euros is a fair price. You will have a few hours of fun, indulge your nostalgia....then uninstall and probably never touch it again. Which is fine. But I wish we got something more for the King of Space, and for non-Gundam mecha games in general. Alas.

You cycle through random letter tiles like Scrabble and place them on a board. Select a tile from the board, then adjacent ones to form word combos. Thus it's fairly open-ended as you plan the board for giant combos. The game ends when your board is filled, and you can't form anymore words. Games can last anywhere between 20 minutes to hours. 

There are different game modes and even leaderboards where you can upload to or watch other players' games on the workshop. There's even a spellchecker.  Can be played with mouse-only if you choose. 

I recommend this game to anyone looking for word games or puzzle games.

This is a deceptively simple game. The graphics are simple and it doesn't take long to get the hang of it but there is a lot of strategy involved in letter placement to enable you to find the best words. As the game goes on it gets more complex, with letter tiles with various special effects, which adds to the enjoyment.

You can choose different game lengths, starting at half an hour, and there are two extra modes: infinite and survival.

Highly recommended.

先说我个人的路线喜好，美咲＞明日香＝真白＞莉佳
美咲线，个人觉得是最好的一条线，也是在剧情上最完整的一条，和男主的小时候的剧情冲突，和同伴的天赋方面的冲突，都是塑造的最好的。竞技比赛有不完美的才是人之常情，也有失利后的夺冠，是最正确，最完整的一条。而且hcg也比其他的多，甚至是其他三条线一起的数量。

真白线，比较废萌的一条线，但是架不住真白的人设啊，谁不喜欢孤僻傲娇猫猫，和男主的感情塑造也很好，打完只想求多几个hcg和剧情，还好后面还有ex1

明日香线，官方钦定的女主线，非常传统王道的一条线，但是剧情上缺少和晶也的冲突，和男主之间的塑造还是有点自然而然了，没有和美咲互相救赎的冲突，也没用和真白之间约定信任的冲突，导致故事性少了一点。但是后半部写的真的太好了，特别是空竞的演出，非常的热血，非常的无敌，在我个人路线排名直接超过真白一点了。虽然还有很多坑没填，但是绝对是官方的标准结局，适合放到最后一条线打，或者只打一条线的玩家打，我就是放到最后一条线打的，观感非常好

莉佳线，纯纯是路人女主了，也是我第一条通的线，导致没啥记忆点了，但是剧情上还是合格的。感情塑造也非常的甜

整体而言，个人认为绝对是称得上完美的galgame，美术和人设都非常的顶级，而且接近两百张的cg绝对是gal里的3a，再加上每章结尾都有播片，op和ed也有两三个。音乐和BGM也非常的抓耳，op和ed也非常符合作品主题，已经在循环了。剧情和演出不用说，空竞这一个优秀的设定非常的完整全面，空竞的演出也非常的热血，给我打泪目了。在视觉小说方面，最重要的文案脚本也不错，基本都通俗易懂且合适，不用来回阅读，不像现在的二游文案跟阅读题一样，需要反复看几遍的谜语人。

仰望天空，注视天空，享受天空，答案就在那里。非常的nb，非常的无敌。还想要更多的剧情，要更多的hcg，还有我的未萌线，葵姐线。

[h1] 我心中最完美的galgame [/h1]
本篇虚构了一个不存在的运动--flying circus，同时以男主小时候退出空竞为切入口开展故事，男主并非什么都会的龙傲天，而是心态时不时崩溃的普通人（其实还是很厉害的）。

[h1]一款杰出的视觉小说[/h1]


在正式的评价前，我得声明，这是我2025年玩到过最棒的游戏，没有之一，它的美术、配音（全程沉浸感超高的韩配）和剧情（3条主要故事，18条支线故事），绝对支撑得起92元的售价。


本作有三位女主，萨妮「Sani」、娜莫「Namo」、基薇「Kiwi」，各自的故事线个性鲜明。而作为作家“路过的狗”的最新力作，剧情更是完美继承了他独特的创作风格。[u]轻松的故事与严肃的剧情相衔接，伏笔与爆点不断，[/u]而作为主要故事线的Sani线（教授线）更是拥有跌宕起伏、震撼人心的剧情。


如果你有意愿入手这款游戏，我想我这有几处你会很好奇的重点。
[olist]
	[*]本游戏三条主角线独立，故事线没有分支，故事采用了“路过的狗”经典的单支叙事，从头到尾，任何对话选项不影响最终剧情发展。
	[*]本游戏是HE。虽然中后期剧情沉重，但三条线都是彻彻底底的HE。作者甚至巧妙的规避掉了此类型剧情中常见的问题与漏洞，带来完美快乐的故事。即便首次游玩会觉得内心不平，但仔细了解剧情后终究能明白其饱含的爱意。
	[*]我强烈建议以Namo、Kiwi、Sani线的顺序进行游戏，至少以Namo线打头。
[/olist]

首先，剧情、立绘和配音都是顶中顶。虽然我是furry控，但是我自己口味本身吃的很开，人设这方面对我来说自然也是加分点，而且我也得说如果不是因为在bilibili上看到了这游戏的PV，看到主角三人的人设，我可能就不会入手了。
Taleshop自己也提及这样的不完全furry的人设是为了平衡两面受众，甚至作家“路过的狗”在一开始给出的便是更加偏向兽人的设定，现在这样也算是无可奈何的为大众考虑吧。
在三条支线中，Sani线给我的感触和震撼最深，Kiwi其次，而Namo线确实有点平淡了。但是我恰恰喜欢Namo线更多，因为给人一种“就像是明天会发生的事情一样”，对吧？
然后关于游戏的广播剧我也是听完了前两集，EP1讲的是刚刚收养基薇后的故事，EP2讲的是Namo[spoiler]喝了神秘药水变成小孩[/spoiler]的故事，也都是很有趣的，可以去韩国游戏平台stove上购买，130多块。

It’s incredible how much - or almost everything - can be achieved with so little, or almost nothing. I discovered Faith through a nearly four-and-a-half-hour YouTube video by Wendigoon titled “The Game too Scary for 3D - The Hidden Story of FAITH: The Unholy Trinity.” I found the game extremely intriguing and, something I rarely do, I managed to stop watching before being spoiled, saving the experience to enjoy it firsthand.

Faith is, without a doubt, a unique game. Its aesthetic is deliberately minimalist and experimental, the cutscenes are extraordinary, and there are literally only two gameplay mechanics - walking and showing the cross to the devil. The game is unapologetically itself, and somehow manages to terrify using what little it has, in ways many AAA games can’t.

The graphics are inspired by 8-bit Atari games, with restrained, minimal pixel art. Yet, through the clever use of color, lighting, shadow, and contrast, the game achieves a remarkable visual delicacy. There’s something fascinating in how the omission of reality - having to imagine the pixel art - intertwines with terror. Nothing scares us more than what’s left unseen. It may sound almost comical, but there were moments when I trembled and got chills over just 20 pixels - more than with high-resolution monsters in typical AAA games.

Another highlight is the cutscenes. They are unbelievable. Airdorf, the creator of Faith, developed them using rotoscoping - manually drawing over live-action footage, frame by frame. This innovative approach gives the animations a unique and disturbing style that perfectly matches the retro aesthetic. Watching the original footage behind the cutscenes is highly recommended: https://youtu.be/CcJIE9kjoQo?si=bTxn439wJqkL5OS8
 and https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4tjjaexTUeQ

The music is another standout. Inspired by retro 8-bit compositions, it doesn’t sacrifice quality - the tracks are rooted in classical music and create a supernatural, oppressive atmosphere. Some sections opt for complete silence, making the environment even more anxious and terrifying. The characters’ voiceovers, produced with voice simulators, distort the vocals in a retro style, enhancing the unsettling effect.

The story is rich and compelling. Without spoiling too much, it explores the occult, the supernatural, and the Church. You play as John Ward, a priest returning to a house where an exorcism went terribly wrong - his first exorcism, in fact. The three chapters follow John’s growth as a priest, as a person, and in his courage and faith.

Something I particularly appreciate is how the game doesn’t take an anti-faith or anti-church stance. It could have easily gone the agnostic or atheist route, considering the typical gamer demographic, but Faith remains serious and respectful, portraying John’s faith and charisma in a mature and spiritually grounded way.

There are some issues with the game itself, but they become almost irrelevant in light of its overall strength - though they are worth mentioning. I think the gameplay, while minimalist, could have explored additional avenues instead of relying on just two mechanics, one of which is the most basic of all videogame mechanics: movement. The theme of doing a lot with very little is something I greatly admire and talk about often, but even without adding much more, the game could have experimented with additional gameplay elements that enhanced immersion - not “cross power-ups with God’s blessing level 2!” style mechanics, but subtle, thoughtful interactions.

A good example is a mechanic introduced in Chapter 3 that replaced another. Even though it was just a substitution, it brought a significant innovation to the gameplay: it was completely terrifying and oppressive, ranking among the most frightening moments I’ve ever experienced in a videogame. (SPOILER: I’m talking about the camera mechanic in the New Haven Apartment Complex.)

There are also aspects of the boss fights that can become frustrating - and here we start touching on real game design issues. At times, there are few visual cues or prompts for upcoming moves, making it difficult to read or anticipate enemy patterns. This can be frustrating, but it doesn’t overshadow the brilliance of the overall experience.

Faith is truly a once-in-a-lifetime game, and I sincerely hope new chapters continue John Ward’s story. A film adaptation is also currently in the works. The evolution from Chapters 1 to 3 is remarkable, showing clear growth and maturity in Airdorf’s design, which excites me even more about the potential continuation of the game. I highly recommend it, and I genuinely believe the saga has a bright future ahead.

After finishing this review, I'll request a refund, 

Why? Because this feels like a movie production game made without passion for either movie production or game development.

In real life, the movie production business has both very iconic visuals (think of the classic studios with their gates, soundstages, etc.) and some rather unique business processes. (E.g., the importance of stars, negotiations with agents and talent that can involve anything from billing order on the poster to a revenue share agreement, etc.) To make things even more interesting, all of this changed greatly over time, in terms of both technology and business model. 

None of that is in this game. What you get instead is a generic management sim: Build rooms inside of a pre-made building. If you run out of space, buy another pre-made building to build rooms in. None of this looks even remotely what a real studio complex with soundstages would look like, cast and crew are simply hired as employees on your payroll, and the whole production process is just a generic "let employees work on task" game loop without any attempt to address the specifics of the business the game purports to simulate. In short: The movie production theming is just sloppy window dressing. This could easily be re-skinned into just about any other kind of basic business sim without changing any of the underlying game mechanics. 

On the gameplay side, there is a noticeable lack of polish: The translation is poor and often confusing, character names are frequently nonsensical, the tutorial is glitchy, the UI doesn't give access to important information (e.g., room temperature has an effect on employee morale, but there's no way to way to check the current temperature of a room or how much it is affected by any heaters or A/C units you place in there), flavor texts for events feel flat and generic as if created by an LLM. 

I could maybe forgive some of that, if it were an Early Access title, but this is supposed to be a full release. The complete lack of polish and care for both gameplay and subject matter makes me think that the aim wasn't to release a quality game but rather to make a quick buck. 

Not recommended, will refund.

[EDIT: Shortly after  writing this, I came across a glowing Steam review of this game that had all the hallmarks of being written by an LLM and which praised a bunch of features that do not actually exist in the game at all. I wrote a comment underneath that review pointing this out,  and shortly afterwards, the comments underneath that review were turned off. I'm not going to engage in any speculation as to who might be responsible for that fake positive review, but as a potential buyer you should be aware that not all reviews for this title are genuine.]

The game take place on Caribbean in 1905. We play as a professional diver who, due to tragic accident, was forced to leave his ship (Thalassa) to recover ashore. During our absence, Thalassa sank under mysterious circumstances, and now is up to us to discover its fate.

Honestly, the story is quite good, believable, and tragic, not to mention the twists and turns. You're sure, that you've figured it out, but then something comes along that throws the whole puzzle off course.

Unfortunately, the developers squandered the potential of a single, crucial event occurring in the prologue. The scene there could have had a much greater impact on the player if, instead of rushing things, they had developed the plot and its introduction much more slowly. In its current form, it merely "impacts" rather than “shocks”.

✅[list]
[*] UI is well designed, user-friendly and readable. Map updates automatically every time you push the plot forward or find an important tool.

[*] Good graphics. Underwater environment is mesmerizing and well designed. Locations were created with great care, personalized and give the impression that someone really lived there, rather than just being a background for the story.

[*] Quite good detective story. Every time I thought that I find decisive clue, new facts changed everything. The side stories are neatly woven into the main plot and complement it perfectly.

[*] Mysteries - in-game name for a detective mode. Collect clues and infos, then place them on mind-map to create leads. These can be main – essential for gameplay and pushing plot forward, and side – additional info about NPCs or conflicts between them.

[*] Great voice acting. Not only the regional accents that match the character design, but also the fact that the voice actors put a lot of effort into their work and based on the dialogues, you can easily determine the emotions that a given NPC is experiencing at a given moment.

[*] All sounds are appropriately muffled, with reverberation appropriate for locations deep underwater. 

[*] Music is quite minimalistic. In few moments when it can be heard, it’s a variation of piano&violin, always sorrowful and melancholic.
[/list]

😐
     Unskippable cutscenes; most likely introduced to mask loading screens.

❌[list]
[*] Voices are very quiet and in-game options weren’t really able to improve it. Needed to changed Windows settings for it.

[*] MC is mute and you can’t hear his responses – only NPCs reaction to it. Pity, considering that system similar to Firewatch would provide greater engagement for player.

[*] Unfortunately it’s one of “those” games that introduce full crew of NPCs but don’t allow the player to form any meaningful connections with them. For me it’ll always be a wasted potential – how can you expect player to care about them if you didn’t give him any chance to grow fond of them.

[*] Visualizations cannot be skipped or sped up. Automatic interaction animations are frustratingly slow. 

[*] One of the achievements does not make any sense while another is basically a hit-and-miss.
[/list]

I very much expected to like this, but it turns out the description of the game is deceptive from its very first sentence "Thalassa is a single player, first person psychological drama set in 1905." Well that sounds nifty! 1905 is an interesting era; a decade before WW1, and at the height of the Imperial world built during the Victorian era. 

But it turns out the only thing "1905" in this game is what the developers think 1905 looks like. There's no historical accuracy, and it turns out it's an alternate universe situation - which is fine, but point that out! 

It's not even clear why the developers went for putting the game in the era they did, since it doesn't appear to matter, because right away they introduce what are essentially scuba divers with underwater radios and handheld audio players (that also work underwater). They should have just made the game contemporary, or if they wanted it to be an "era game", pop it into the 80s or something.

The game is also full of cringey writing, and every character acts/talks/reacts in an incredibly anachronistic manner. It's set in 1905, but everyone acts like they were born in 2005. 

The developers and writers of the game also appear to not realise that things degrade underwater. You're walking around the sunken remains of your former vessel and all of the materials are in fine condition, except they float around underwater. Have the devs ever submerged paper in water for any length of time? They might be surprised to see the results! 

I had my fill of it after an hour. I didn't get to the emotional or sorrowful bits, but to be honest, if the devs/writers handling of human emotional complexity is as bad as their handling of history, materiality and narrative, I can't imagine I'm missing much.

While I really fancy the art style, characters, and basic game play, I do not have the nerve to recommend this game to my friends.

It comes down to the main aspect of the actual fights (at least I perceived so), resets.
The resets itself seems to be ubiquitous in fighting games, but in Skullgirls it's the prominent part of the game play.
This game comes with multiple measures to punish longer combos, which inevitably encourage the intentional dropping of the combo.
The simplest form is high/low, which seems to be not so bad.
Of course you can add the grab with the cost of heavier damage fall down, 33/33/33 seems still manageable.
And there's also cross ups to all of this, it's A LITERAL DICE at this point.
Did I forget mention that some characters can do this airborne(albeit without low so a bit fewer options)?

The worst part is that not all characters have a tool to properly punish every reset, which I think nullifies the whole defense of the resets.
If the opponent cannot punish high, you can just do high cross ups.
If the opponent cannot punish you airborne, do whatever you want, but in the air.
It's like RPS but the opponent's fingers are glued together.
Getting blocked is the worst you can expect and it is not punishing at all, as you dropped that combo because finishing off is not worth it anyway.


I love the nuance of neutral game and that is the main reason I want to fight real people and not bots.
But 90% of actual battle is indistinguishable from training mode.
For me this game feels like just a glorified combo showoff contest equipped with QTE.
And that did not click for me.

To be honest, I'd better off getting infinite combo'd.
Because then you can't force me to flip a coin (sometimes it's 1d6) and insist that is "engaging" or "interactive" in some way.

Just git gud?
Pick characters who compliment each others?
Yeah, fair enough.
To be honest mere existence of peacock is more than enough reason for me to not recommend.

A silly little stealth massacre game about the joy of christmas/

Christmas Massacre is about a mentally ill man who was abused as a child who takes on the role of santa claus to dole out what he believe to be justice during the holiday season.  Each level has you navigating a small area where you need to kill all the people without being seen.  Technically, being seen doesn't matter, as it doesn't impact your score, but when a character sees you or a dead body, they run for the door, and you lose if they make it there.

There are a lot of stages to go through, and you learn new killing skills as you progress (like, 2).  These skills make the game easier, but generally reduce the score you can obtain.  You don't need to get a high score to progress, but you will need it to get all the trophies.

This is NOT a serious game, and it isn't really about anything at all, but it is a fun little massacre simulator with a truley retro aesthetic.  If you want to kill people with a little stealth gameplay, then this is a fun little romp.  If you want something to sink your teeth into, look somewhere else.

I wanted to like this game. I love Lovecraft inspired games, especially ones that focus on the psychological side like Dredge. Call of the Sea has a great art-style. But that's where the positives end. The puzzles are all really simple or just plain finicky. A bunch of them require you to have all of the hints possible, which are incredibly easy to miss because the UI symbol for them is so small and you have to be looking right at them (plus they often look exactly the same as other things in the area that are completely non-interactive).  The voice acting is also amateurish at best, I know it's a small team but plenty of other indie games have been able to absolutely nail voice acting. There are only two voiced characters, so it really should have been better. And the main character just talks to herself throughout the game, usually for no reason at all. Her reactions are also very counterintuitive to what's happening around her, like reacting with mild amusement when she's on a scary ship at night in a thunderstorm. The story is boring AF and no one is likeable or interesting. When you're not actively solving puzzles, you're just picking up photographs and reading journals, which is were 90% of the story is told. Again, really uninterestingly. The aesthetic of this game is excellent, it had so much potential. But it is just not a very good indie game. Maybe if it came out in 2010, it might have been less underwhelming. But since this came out in 2020, during the golden age of indies that we're still currently living in, it is mediocre at best. Oh and this game has the most BS achievement I've ever seen: Fawning Developers. It requires you to purchase all of the publishers other games to get the achievement. I've never had an achievement make me physically angry before.

Do you know how gutted I was to finally get my hands on Salt and Sacrifice, only to discover I don't like it?
I don't know what it is. It feels like what I enjoyed about the first game was ground down like the rough edges of a project. It's techncially more refined, technically better balanced - but it feels like it lacks... *something* I liked more.
Why do so many weapons feel so bad? The magic system I loved in one is gone, replaced with... something very different, and something that just feels *weak* and bad. It feels like it's entirely balanced around the PvP, so all the spells can't be anything too crazy or too strong, but now I feel like I'm throwing magic throwing knives at a boss for no damage.
Why exactly is a Vanguard weapon (sword and shields, scale mostly with strength), have a random wind weapon in it that scales with dex? You can't even make proper use of that without investing heavily into a stat that doesn't benefit the Vanguards at all.

The bosses all feel... Weak? Some are just annoying, the "Pulling instant attacks out of their ass" kind, but they're never that hard? None of the main-line bosses are. The monster-hunter like mages go from being easy to "Holy shit, what were they thinking?" Yeah, the vampire mage is an awesome idea. Shame the fight boils down to him spamming endless combos that send it across the small arena you're relegated to and it stunlocks and juggles insanely hard.
Shame the huge mech boss made of wood that looks AWESOME is "I just have to expect that at any moment it can pull out its strongest attack with 0 wind up that does 80% of my HP and it combos into and out of anything."
It's a lot of that in the end game.

I really, really wanted to enjoy this game. I don't even mind it's a weird monster hunter dark souls like, but I don't really feel like it plays to the strengths of monster hunter, or even really dark souls. For all of the weirdness and quirks I loved about the first game, some of that charm is gone in this one. The music is still good most of the time, sometimes it feels a bit... I don't want to say bad? I don't think it is, but it just seems odd.
Some of the atmospheric tracks are wonderful. Bol Gerahn has one of my favourite tracks.
I think a lot of the story is interesting, I love how grim a lot of this game can feel. I really enjoy the setting in general, I enjoy some of the lore implications I've found in this game and how it ties into the world of Salt and (x).

Hell, I love some of the changes actually. Ranged weapons being more limited, but actually being useful is nice? Something any build can have? Axes for strength, knives or bows for dex, staves that use some kind of powder as a catalyst for an arcane reaction for... arcane builds. It's cool, I like it.
But then you have things like the bombs. So many of them are just. Weak and bad, to be honest. Why do we have holy water jars that scale with convinction, when Bombs give you strength for unlocking, and then it does *bad* damage and has a terrible scaling? What about the jars of water that inflict the feeling of drowning in the deep sea just... being shit? i feel like there's a lot of that in this game.
I don't like some of the areas. Some enemies are just annoying to fight. Some areas just feel awful, like the area added in Traitor's Tomb. Some of the areas I just, can't get down. I cannot navigate them well for the life of me, I CANNOT commit them to memory and I do not know why.

There's more I want to say about this game, but I just don't know how.
I don't think it's bad to experiment. It's good to, actually. Stagnation is how you get games that feel samey and boring and repetitive. Experimentation might not always hit the mark, but you'll still learn something along the way, and that might inform the direction of your next project. 
I wish I liked where this experiment landed. But I did not.

I’m going to be honest, I didn’t really know what to expect during the first 30 minutes of playing. Once I got used to how everything was laid out and what I should be doing, I actually started to enjoy it a lot.

I agree with much of what people are saying in the negative reviews:

The UI/UX is a bit rough and confusing, even for me as a communication designer.

Some of the stats are hard to understand and don’t clearly explain what they do.

There’s no real tutorial, and honestly, I needed some hand-holding in the beginning. If I hadn’t figured everything out soon after, I probably would’ve refunded the game.

Now, for what I do like about the game:

The complexity of the classes.

The variety of ways to finish a run is great. I usually have a particular playstyle in games like this (I’m a sucker for healing classes), and this game fills that void.

A huge selection of upgrades post-run — though I’ll admit, there are way too many things to consider, and it’s a bit confusing figuring out where everything is. Also, why is it all numbered? lol

I think this is a wonderfully sad little story about a family torn apart by religious beliefs and their own singular tragedies. It's beautifully written, and has some excellent art both of the drawn and photographic variety, and wonderful music. The static image of the angel statue that the family has in their home is honestly gorgeous, and I'd even buy it as a print if I could. I also love the design of each of our main characters as like biblically accurate angels with their eyes closed most of the time until near the end, but I don't want to spoil the ending. (I will just say it's not a happy one.)

However, I would be amiss to not point out that this is one, just a half hour long, and two, doesn't have any broader "gameplay" so to speak. It's just "tap spacebar and read", but for something like this, and only for about a dollar, I'd say that's more than fine, and it was an overall positive experience for me. It's like reading a short horror story. So if you're looking for something a bit more interactive, this isn't for you. As the description says, it's a kinetic novel, not a visual novel.

TL;DR: If you're looking for a sad little tragedy to read and have a half hour of time to spare, this is something that I'd love to recommend.

Platform 8, ou ８番のりば ([i]hachi-ban noriba[/i]), est le second jeu de Kotake Create, reprenant peu ou prou le concept de The Exit 8, qui avait connu ses petits instants de gloire en ligne. Cette fois, on se retrouve dans une rame de métro plutôt que dans un couloir sans fin. Le réalisme des lieux, des publicités jusqu’à la texture de la moquette des banquettes, nous plonge à nouveau dans un état de malaise insidieux.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3598393179
Cet espace irréel joue avec notre perception et nous demande cette fois de nous confronter aux anomalies pour passer aux rames suivantes. Allant toujours vers l’avant, le joueur doit interpréter les signes et déjouer les pièges sur sa route. Platform 8 se joue plus rapidement que The Exit 8 : les obstacles sont plus simples à franchir et il est moins nécessaire de scruter chaque détail pour repérer les anomalies. Ce second jeu relève davantage de l’expérience horrifique là où le côté [i]puzzle game[/i] d’Exit 8 se montrait plus affirmé.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3598393352
J’aurais tendance à recommander plutôt The Exit 8 s’il fallait faire un choix. Néanmoins, je vous conseille de vous procurer le pack regroupant les deux titres, disponible sur Steam à prix réduit, pour une plongée sans retenue dans ces espaces liminaires où le réel côtoie l’indicible.

Stronghold Legends - это, в первую очередь, мое детство. Это моя память. И как минимум из-за этого я не могу поставить игре оценку ниже, чем "рекомендую".

У игры очень атмосферный сеттинг и в целом достаточно уютная энергетика. Свою роль в этом играет как приятный визуальный стиль, так и юмор, свойственный всей серии игр Stronghold.

При этом существуют также весомые минусы. Прежде всего, это баланс. Фракция короля Артура значительно слабее фракций Зла и Холода, которые, в отличие от своих "добрых" коллег, обладают сильными мифическими юнитами. Справедливости ради, надо сказать, что у Артура есть рыцари Круглого стола, но их мало, и без коней они медлительны (а кони под ними очень быстро погибают от вражеских стрел). Кроме того, их спецспособности восстанавливаются очень долго.

Миссии в кампании тоже неоднозначны. Кампании Артура и Дитриха могут вызвать в нескольких местах затруднения, в то время как кампания Влада Дракулы, несмотря на свой официальный сложный статус, является самой легкой, поскольку игроку в ней дается доступ к мифическим войскам, а компьютерным оппонентам нет.

В заключение можно сделать следующий вывод. Игру могу порекомендовать тем, кто хочет вспомнить былые времена. Steam-версия работает стабильно (по крайней мере, у меня) и в наличии имеется поддержка русского языка. Новым игрокам я данный проект посоветовать не могу, так как у игры очень высокий порог вхождения.

In [i]The Average Everyday Adventures of Samantha Browne[/i] you play as Samantha, a college student who lives alone in a dorm. She gets hungry and decides that the best thing is some oatmeal. However, she also has severe social anxiety that will encumber her trip to the kitchen and back. It is up to you to try to make the correct decisions and keep Samantha's anxiety level to a minimum.

This game is a visual novel meaning that it is mostly story-driven and much of the game is just reading. You make choices along the way that dictates Samantha's actions during the course of the story.

As I understand it, the main purpose of this game is to show what it is like for a person to have social anxiety. I admit that I am not an expert on this topic. Although I have certainly had times in my own past where I had difficulty interacting with others or getting nervous over relatively minor things, I have never been diagnosed with any sort of disorder.

To start off with the positive aspects of this game, I thought that the artwork was pretty good. Although not necessarily detailed, it looks good and helps to tell the story. 

However, I thought the writing in this game was weak. As a shorter visual novel, there was not much room for any character development. As such, Samantha came off as a rather unlikable character who gets angry and apparently hates the few people she encounters for no real reason. There is a sort of implication that being spiteful is just part of having social anxiety, which I doubt to be true. There are ten or so endings in this game, but there is not a lot of variation between them. Even though you can achieve 100% completion in under an hour, it still felt like a chore to complete.

Despite the nice art, I thought the main character was rather unsympathetic. Since the story revolves around her, I feel that I cannot recommend this game. Still, it is short so if you are curious enough it might be worth a play.

Leider nicht mehr das was man sich wünscht.

Um es jetze schon zu erwähnen, kann ich den SWORD ART ONLINE Fractured Daydream trotzdem empfehlen, aber auch nur für bestimmte Spieler.

Ich weiss nicht was ich genau sagen soll. Zum einen Teil ist es jetze kein schlechtes Spiel aber zum anderen nicht mal gut. 

Fange ich mal so an. 
Fractured Daydream ist eher ein Live Service Game und konzentriert sich auch nur auf dem Multiplayer, der auch größtenteils nicht aktiv gespielt wird. Zumindestens hatte ich nicht so viel Erfolg. Durch viele gute Freunde konnten wir aber das Spiel gut nutzen. Spielerisch ist das Spiel richtig bombe und macht auch viel bock. Steuerung ist sehr gut und fühlt sich verdammt gut an. Die Story ist unterhaltsam und kann ich weiter empfehlen.
Es gibt auch eine Story die man nur für sich spielen kann und auch paar Nebenquest aber die sind leider nicht so wie in den Vorgängern von SAO. In Fractured Daydream ist es so. Man startet einzelne Missionen die man spielen möchte übers Hauptmenü.
Ich finde es nicht so geil weil man eher aus die Story und den spielerischen Spaß raus gezogen wird.

Es gibt noch mehr zu erzählen aber komme ich mal zum kurzen Fazit.
So an sich kann ich das Spiel empfehlen aber nicht zum voll Preis. Wer nur die ca 20 Stunden Kampagne sowie paar Nebenquest aus ist, sollte auf einen Sale warten. Der Multiplayer ist leider nicht aktiv, da werden leider keine schöne Runden zusammen kommen.

[h1]👩🏽‍🦱短評️👨🏽‍💻[/h1]
　2人協力専用パズル。[b]1人購入すればフレンドパスも付いてくる[/b]ので、割高とは感じない。セールでは結構な割引も期待できる。初回のプレー時間は9.6時間と、協力専用にしては短くはない。

　エージェントとハッカーとして、互いの技能を生かし、意思疎通で情報を交換しながら、障害を突破するゲームプレー。[b]戦闘は一切ない[/b]ので、それを求める人にはお勧めしない。

　パズルは斬新で且つ種類も豊富。最後まで飽きることはなかった。ここは高く評価できる。
　しかし問題も少なからずあって、不満を募らせることもあった。緊張感のあるストーリーとの兼ね合いもあるのだが、[b]制限時間が厳しく[/b]、ゆっくり解かせてくれない。何度も時間オーバーでやり直しを食らうと、興醒めしてしまう。
　この手のゲームは、初見の2人で遊ぶのが最も新鮮だが、それが悪い方に転じて「そもそも何をすればよいのか？」と見当もつかないことが多い。それに、相手がやろうとしていることが想像できず、助けようにも不可能でもどかしくなる。また両者が、「ここは相手がやるべき仕事」と思って、実は自分にもやる事があったという勘違いもある。
　あまりにも難しい場合には、双方の同意でヒントを参照できる。一応の救済策にはなっているが、達成感は削がれる。クリアしたが、結局よくわからなかったパズルもある。

　これは他のレビューにもあるが、[b]自分がもたついて相手をイライラさせてしまう[/b]ことがあった。これは2人専用ゲームには必ず付き纏う問題だが、殊にこのゲームには強く現れている。本当に面白くなるのは、相手が何をやっているか想像がつく2回目のプレーではなかろうか。

　グラフィックは特に言及する必要はなく、世界観はスタイライズド調でバタくさい。音楽はサスペンス調で良い。
　[b]同期のバグが散見[/b]され、相手が伝えた情報が使えない事がある。またクラアント側がフリーズした事があった。チェックポイントはこまめに入るが、先の不具合では大きくやり直しとなった。なにかおかしいと思ったら、ゲームを立て直した方が良さそう。

　この手の2人専用ゲームは、数は少ないが徐々に増えてきているので、それだからといって評価はしない。協力パズルはとても面白いが、相手がしくじっても寛大でいられるならおすすめできる。

闪4的剧情仍然继承闪轨系列的低水准，叙事结构也是照抄闪2这种垃圾作品，但不像闪2完全一场空，这部至少是把轨迹帝国篇的剧情写出了一个不尽人意的结尾，玩家们在吃完闪轨4部的屎之后总算可以向新篇章的轨迹迈进了至少没有拖到闪5闪6继续折磨玩家，也算是功德一件了，因此还是给个好评。
具体的优点：最重要的就是把钢之至宝，七器相克，宰相和结社各自目的这些闪轨最重要的主线讲完了，还在对战马克邦时进一步揭露塞姆利亚整体世界观，真结局后的隐藏剧情也让盟主的设定露出冰山一角，在轨迹主线推进方面算是不错的一部作品。其次战斗是闪轨前几代的全面升级，拥有轨迹系列最多的可控人物，最终真结局决战能操作三十号人，更有罗赛二姐光剑分校长这种超强角色可以玩，同时加强了闪轨偏弱的魔法系统，削弱了破防收益和神气合一里疾风，战斗再也不是3保1让黎恩复读里疾风或大锤破防疾风阵灌死，战略性有明显的强化。最后就是这代前作卖情怀非常到位，序章就直接可控艾丝蒂尔和罗伊德，中间游击士支援科老人物的戏份也不少，真结局大团圆包饺子，结局cg空零碧老人物全部出场，可以说非常尊重从fc一路玩到闪4的轨迹老玩家，值得很多游戏公司学习。
缺点：最严重的问题就是主线剧本水准和叙事结构相比前作闪3不进反退，咚虽然极其脑残但至少给玩家留下想象空间，而闪4前期救黎恩，各地下副本重新集结七班成员这种非常水的情节占据了50%以上的剧情量，中期更是充斥着毫无意义的友方npc与主角团切磋考验环节，都是系列第四部了真不知道为什么还要搞迷宫提升战力/切磋彰显意志这种闪2就应该处理完的桥段，好不容易熬到后期进入相克主线，七姐这个碧轨就塑造逼格的老人物像来自杀一样，还要让杜芭莉负责骂醒250年的不死者，最后刚弃暗投明就给大少一剑捅死，这段完全是编剧机械降神让武艺巅峰察觉不到大少隐身强行被捅死，非常地不知所谓。最后最大的剧情败笔就是闪轨的所有反派在闪4都洗白了，乔治小王子亚里沙爹这些三流反派就安排被地精脑控，铁血之子这些二流反派就设计成被宰相裹挟身不由己，最后你以为编剧把仇恨都集中在宰相这个反派上了正想报闪3大仇的时候编剧直接告诉你原来宰相也是好人！全tm怪伊修麦格。这段就非常搞笑了，伊修麦格和诅咒基本就是编剧认奥斯本为爹不得已空降下来的背锅垃圾桶，强行按头告诉玩家闪轨系列的主角原来是奥斯本，他扮演鲁鲁修一样的角色，黎恩七班这些主角反而扮演卡莲甚至扇要这种什么真相都不明白的二流配角，玩家代入的黎恩和个小丑一样被宰相玩弄于股掌之间，正义性也被宰相毛了，真不知道为什么全是好人就一个伊修麦格是反派还要强行互打4部。主线信息也是一律不知只能靠水镜放ppt结社执行者说台词强行往玩家脑子里灌，说真的这个主线换成黎恩单挑伊修麦格30次旁边放个水镜解说设定和前情提要都行。
人物塑造方面也是非常差劲，主线强相关人物就黎恩一个算塑造的还可以，男二克洛莫名其妙装逼还混到三次复活和个傻卵一样，白兔终极牺牲化剑根本没看出有什么剧情上的意义，武力强的队友分校长光剑罗赛二姐的作用就是砍个盐之桩，正面打宰相0出力，智力强的队友缪洁纯智障棋手只会摇人和神风突击，奥瓜铺垫了5部的老角色只会开那个破船像开出租车一样把七班载到不同的地方，支线队友旧七班全是伪人，除了二少全部删掉也没影响，新七班只有黑兔塑造确实不错，协力者瑟蕾奴和杜芭莉倒是塑造还可以，就是戏份太少，20个常驻队友大概只有4~5个正常人，带着这些虫豸能玩好jrpg吗？反派的人物塑造也很差，大少只会偷袭正面一碰就碎，小王子魔怔b还和前作杀人狂夏莉组cp看着恶心，奥斯本全程谜语最后莫名其妙洗白，作为反派不如怀斯曼一根毛，最后就一个马克邦观感还行，但这人纯打架还非常有礼貌从不恶心人应该也不算反派。
一想到下一部创轨还要在我最爱的克州主场被托尔兹七班十几个伪人继续折磨一部就恶心，如果法社能活到闪轨重制的时候，拜托把新七班旧七班全部删除只留黎恩黑兔别写什么学生教官了，直接改为宰相直属特务在内战执行任务过程中发现至宝真相反抗宰相，其他主线设定和七班以外的支线人物留着，最后把宰相写成类似怀斯曼的利用至宝野心家别搞那些脑残转世诅咒的话，我觉得应该会做出来一部不错的jrpg。

Игра 100 из 10, очень советую любителям Journey, Abzu и других игр в подобной стилистике и повествовании. Концепция простая, появляешься в локации, решаешь головоломки и открывается путь к новому месту. Но что мне особенно нравится, так это динамика происходящего. Управление приятное и простое.

Многие пазлы решаются интуитивно, нет особой необходимости ломать на них голову. В игре также отличная атмосфера: музыка, дизайн локаций, стиль игры. Я как любитель покататься на роликах или поиграть во что то быстрое и плавное как Mirror's Edge кайфанула от прохождения этой игры. Проходит кстати становится еще веселее на хардкоре, обычная сложность ощущается слишком простой, но это чисто мои предпочтения. История тоже отличная, я в конце аж прослезилась, всем советую.

Единственное к чему могу придраться так это к русской локализации. Я для разнообразия переключилась на русский и там немного грустно. Вместо нейтральных слов типо "сканировать, взаимодействовать, изучить, осмотреть" используются слова "взаимодействие, изучение". Я не первый день играю в игры в русском дубляже, такой перевод словно был сделан гугл переводчиком, а не реальным переводчиком.

The game is solid, though I can't help but feel sad that I didn't love it as much as I expected. The atmosphere, sound design, and visuals were a consistent treat throughout, but the gameplay just felt a little hollow. The Mario Galaxy-esc gravity mechanics were SUPER cool at certain moments but it seriously felt underutilized, as orbiting a planet often felt optional and something you'd mostly do if you got lost. Maybe I'm just burnt out from the Horizon games, but the AAA-style lore data logs were thoroughly disinteresting and only caused me to disconnect from the story. The bosses though were a great highlight, even if the game's overall structure was very repetitive. Overall though, I'd still recommend it if the visuals interest you and it's on a deep discount.

The entire experience feels like a gentle fairy tale — very pure, very kind, almost like King’s Ranking. The story follows a classic isekai setup, with simple dialogue (lots of kana, few kanji), so even playing in English feels like reading comprehension practice. It’s childlike in tone, filled with animated cutscenes, but that’s also part of its charm.

The art style is what attracts most people — that “Miyazaki-but-not-quite” look. Compared to the first game, the Ghibli feeling is a bit weaker (mostly due to how some 3D elements are rendered differently from the characters), yet it’s still gorgeous overall. Screenshots from this game should honestly be printable posters.

Gameplay-wise, it’s a huge improvement over the first game.
Combat went from slow, turn-based to fluid real-time action — it’s like jumping from classic Final Fantasy to something closer to Monster Hunter-lite. Town-building and a small real-time strategy mode were added too. They aren’t mandatory unless you're aiming for all achievements, but developing your kingdom early helps a lot with side quests.

Speaking of side quests: there are many. Most are just “collect this” or “go talk to that person,” but midgame fast-travel makes them painless. The DLC introduces Dream Dungeon, a roguelike mode that’s actually fun… until you forget the game doesn’t let you save inside and lose hours of progress. (Yes, it happened to me. Twice. On Expert.)

In general:

Beautiful visuals and music ✅

Easy to get into, great for JRPG newcomers ✅

Adults should start on at least Hard, otherwise the combat becomes too easy ✅

Even if the story doesn’t leave a deep emotional scar the way other JRPGs might, the overall package — visuals, music, combat, town building, exploration — makes it a delightful and well-rounded game, especially at a discount.

Also: after finishing the main story, don’t quit.
Load the save with the asterisk — extra content awaits.

The first few times i played this game it had me feeling conflicted, I wanted to love it so bad but the learning curve was a major wall in getting into it. I saw other people creating so many awesome builds, and it's not like i didn't already have experience with other park building games, but somehow i kept hitting walls and not understanding how people were getting the results they had. But after 72h in game i wanna say i finally get it and i love it for what it can be once you get the hang of it, so here is my extremely honest bullet point list of what to expect and some tips:

[h3] The Cons [/h3]

- The path system is by far the most frustrating part of the game. It's not that its bad, once you get a hang of it you can make really nice looking things, but it's extremely janky and you're going to spend a major amount of time just trying to figure it out and fix it. God forbid you want to place an exhibit in the middle of a pre-existing path. Even if you used  the grid system, you might run into the issue of wanting to fit a few exhibits next to each other, and then having to fight with a path that's creating random gaps. and don't get me started on the words "obstructed" and "terrain too uneven". The pathing system is trying to prevent clipping and guest flow issues, but in the end you end up restricted from placing paths in certain places, you still experience clipping, and now you have a weirdly shaped path where you could clearly connect it. 

- The work zones are honestly something i still need to learn more about, but it's allot of micromanaging and when your parks start getting bigger it becomes harder and harder to manage.

- whenever you're playing the campaign, you don't have access to certain tools which would make learning the game much better. in any case, i feel like if you like this game, campaign is more of a secondary way to play the game, rather than the main feature.

- Not having the ability to scale objects like you can in jurassic world evolution 3 and prehistoric kingdom is dumb. At the very least i'd expect the decals and letters to be scalable, one thing i really enjoy creating in a park game, is the ability to create custom signs and information plaques. instead, the fonts themselves have a set size that cannot be changed, and it limits you to what you can do. it also takes away the functionality of the shapes.

-The UI scale in the game is just off. you can scale it yourself, but it doesn't really fix the issue, i know it is hard to find the right balance between being able to see your objects well enough and being able to see your working space too, but it took me a while for me to get over having only 30% of my screen to work with. i think maybe if the background was a bit more transparent, for example, or it was just placed a little differently and was a bit smaller, it would be much easier. I have used game engines like unity, or editing software like the ones form adobe for example, it's not like having only a small area to work with is the end of the world, but it's the fact that it's a game and the tool boxes aren't neatly arranged in a way that allows your eyes to rest and focus on the contained area of the screen dedicated to the workspace.

- Fences are tricky too, but have more margin for work around's, the one thing i do wish they would allow for is to build a fence within a fence and not have it flag the animal as escaping every time it goes in. Awhile back i wanted to include a pool for a tiger in a campaign enclosure, that had some glass  so people could watch the tiger do deep dives. this is when i learned that objects in this game don't have collision, so unless you use the terrain tools or the fences, you  aren't able to place water anywhere. i thought no problem, i'll use the fences and make a little ramp so it can climb in. turns out even though the tiger cannot physically escape and attack anyone, as soon as it goes in the water, everyone panics because it's gotten out. 

[h3] The Pros [/h3]

- The animals are adorable and complex, they really manage to make them feel alive without too many repetitive animation loops. I particularly love placing cameras in their enclosures and just watching them go. The also really got it right with all the enrichment items. I LOVE watching the little guys just go for it and have fun.

- The fact that it sometimes is more like a game engine than a game is a huge plus if you're into making extremely detailed stuff, the terrain tools are really powerful and easy to work with, i love the fact you can just make a tunnel under a habitat and place a path in it, being able to build vertically both up and down is huge. And the modular building system is incredible. You can really spend hours just creating a single shop, placing every item and decor, and it be a functional store is crazy.

- If you like, you can fully ignore the aesthetic side of things because the management aspect of the game is extremely complex and detailed. There is always something going on.

- And even if you want to make things aesthetic but don't like to build them yourself, there is a massive community of talented people that just post their builds for free in the community workshop. it takes two seconds to install in your game, and then you can just freely place them around. You even Have fully functional, pre-made parks to download that you can either just enjoy, or use as a base.

- Once you get a hang of all the shortcuts, tricks and systems in the game, it actually becomes really easy to make whatever you want. For me one thing i always find myself making is custom fences. I you ARE into custom builds, you can just open a sandbox flat game, and start making and saving blueprints. Don't be fooled into looking at an item in this game and think it only have one purpose. You can really combine every single thing into making something new and grouping it. Then just copy paste it a few times in your chosen game save and voila! Extremely satisfying.
- Because of the game's complexity, there is allot more to it than you'd previously imagine. I really like being able to experience the game from a visitor's perspective, the fact you can watch the cameras in their habitats, all the little details they've put into the visitor behavior. They're not things i personally am constantly paying attention to, but when i do, it breathes a little bit more life into the game.

[h1] Tips and Final Thoughts [/h1]

Overall, if you like being creative, you love animals, you just want to spend a few hours making something cozy and creative, and you have the patience or interest to learn some advanced piece by piece construction tools, and you like pouring hours of labor into making something look fantastic, or just care about the tycoon aspect of it, then i recommend you get this game especially now that it's on sale so often. My biggest tips are to watch some tutorial videos on it, and for the love of everything you care about, when you first start playing the game, try to memorize the keyboard shortcuts for the building tools and play around with the path grid on/off system.  [u] i repeat, learn the grid on/off path system [/u] it's your biggest friend and the best way to make paths look normal. There are a bunch of guides online, which should be a part of the game tutorial but it isn't. You place a path on a grid first, and then connext and round out whatever is left after turning off the grid by placing and deleting corners. use -= and [] for adjusting the path without having to move your mouse, and use CTRL if your path keeps clipping somewhere you don't like. hold down SHIFT to adjust path height and you can hold and drag your mouse to create slopes. Lastly, do yourself a favor and try out some mods after you've learned to work with the game well enough. They're free, and extremely useful. 

Hope this helps

Well, that concludes my final run of the Mimimi stealth games. I was going to put the genre to bed for a while after completing Shadow Tactics (my favourite), but after picking this one up in a recent sale, I decided to play through it first.
This is a trickier game for me to review compared to the others. While it’s definitely the easiest game they’ve made, and certainly starts off far too easy, it has provided some of the most fun I’ve had in this genre. In the missions from mid-game onwards, they manage to balance a healthy challenge with a wide variety of emergent and static options that provide flexibility, regardless of who you have in your crew and which path you have taken. This is the first of their games where you get to choose the order of many of the missions and the members of your team (although this is locked for some missions and sequences), with higher XP awarded when choosing underutilised crew members, which encourages you to experiment with different combinations of team members. They’ve obviously put an endless amount of thought and effort into designing and playtesting these missions, which are varied and more ambitious than what they have attempted previously.
They’ve got an amazing team of designers and artists who have produced beautiful and engaging locations. The animations and models are perfectly suited to the environments, which provide a charming, fantastical alternative Caribbean pirate world.
Unlike their other games, Shadow Gambit seemed pitched to a very young audience, based on some elements of the chosen style, characters, and dialogue. I must admit that I skipped an enormous amount of dialogue, as the writing was mediocre, too great in volume, and I didn’t care much for the stories of the crew. This detracted from what was otherwise an outstanding game.
All that said, this is probably one of the best games of this genre, and they went out on a high note in terms of gameplay and design.

Got Kitara to play with my significant other in local co-op, mainly "because Kitara has cute cats in it". In the end, both of us had mixed feelings:

- The graphics are appropriate, but really dated---not that much of a problem for us. The soundtrack isn't exactly bad, but as stereotypical as what you'd expect from the screenshots.

- Combat is fun and somewhat reminiscent of the earlier Cat Quest installments. Mechanics are nicely balanced in that each new item imparts a strong feeling of progress.

- The story is somewhat bland and short. Perhaps that's also partly an issue of the German translation, which has little heart or wit to it. Last but not least, the ending is unsatisfying: The final dungeon is short, the final boss is unspectacular and the final cutscene doesn't actually resolve anything.

- The game world feels small and half-finished. There are just four dungeons, each with but one or two tiny screens and a few enemies. There are no puzzles, nor crossroads or even the traditional levers for doors. At places, the overworld seems to allot entrances for further dungeons, but there is nothing there. One of the ending regions, in particular, features an eye-catching, glowing portal that just leads nowhere.

- The farming mechanics are boring. It's always the same steps: Buy seeds, plow fields, drop seeds, water seedlings, harvest crops. Rinse and repeat. No plants require special treatment or placing. Luckily, farming isn't necessary apart from a few side quests and a few (mostly useless) consumables---earning money by farming enemy drops is much faster.

- Local co-op is a disappointing experience: There is no split screen, so both players need to work close to one another---this is annoying when shopping or farming, for example. Furthermore, the co-op player isn't acknowledged in cutscenes, they also can't talk to NPCs (except for shopping) and thus they can't hand in quests. There also seems to be a bias for enemy drops to end up in the main player's inventory. Finally, there is little incentive to work together (i.e. there is but one healing skill for cooperative play). For the most part, the co-op player just deals extra damage and provides extra inventory space.
